title: Reject `--param` and `--job-variable` values without `=` in `prefect deployment run`
body:
closes #24034

This PR makes `prefect deployment run` reject `--param` and `--job-variable` values that do not have the form `key=value`, instead of silently sending an empty string.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`load_json_key_values` wrapped `spec.partition("=")` in `try`/`except ValueError` to report `Invalid ... option ... Expected format 'key=value'.`, but `partition` never raises, so the error branch could not run. A value without `=` such as `--param name` produced `{"name": ""}`, and `--param =5` produced a parameter with an empty key. The function now checks the separator and the key that `partition` returns and exits with the intended message, so the check applies to both `--param` and `--job-variable`. Values that contain `=` (for example `url=a=b`) and explicit empty values (`name=`) are parsed as before.

Reproduced on `main` against an ephemeral server with a deployment that takes a `name` parameter:

```
$ prefect deployment run my-flow/my-deployment --param name
Created flow run 'honorable-kagu'.
└── Parameters: {'name': ''}
```

With the change:

```
$ prefect deployment run my-flow/my-deployment --param name
Invalid parameter option 'name'. Expected format 'key=value'.
$ prefect deployment run my-flow/my-deployment --job-variable name
Invalid job variable option 'name'. Expected format 'key=value'.
```

Both exit with code 1 and create no flow run. `--param name=Ada` still creates a run with `{'name': 'Ada'}`.

Tests:

- `tests/cli/test_utilities.py`: `load_json_key_values` keeps parsing JSON, plain strings, values containing `=` and empty values, and rejects `name`, `=value` and an empty string.
- `tests/cli/deployment/test_deployment_cli.py`: `deployment run` with `--param name` and `--job-variable name` exits with code 1, prints the error, and creates no flow run.

The new tests fail on `main` (5 failures) and pass with the change. I ran `pytest tests/cli/deployment/test_deployment_run.py tests/cli/deployment/test_deployment_cli.py::TestDeploymentRun tests/cli/test_utilities.py` (88 passed) on Python 3.14, and `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.15.19, as pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) and `codespell` on the changed files.

No documentation change: the CLI help is unchanged and the error message already describes the expected format.

</details>

title: Support non-root users in the official Docker image
body:
closes #6888

This PR adds a non-root `prefect` user (UID 1001, primary GID 0, home `/home/prefect`) to the official image and documents how to run the image as non-root and with a read-only root filesystem. The default user is still root, and no global `PREFECT_HOME` is set, so existing images and anything mounted at `/root/.prefect` behave as before.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `Dockerfile`:
  - `useradd --uid 1001 --gid 0` runs only when the base image has neither a `prefect` user nor a UID 1001 account, so custom `BASE_IMAGE`s that already have one still build. In that case the existing account's home gets the group-0 permissions instead (`/` and `/root` are skipped).
  - `/opt/prefect` and the user's home are set to group 0 with `chmod g=u`, so arbitrary UIDs in group 0 (the OpenShift convention) can write there too.
  - `--user 1001` / `--user prefect` gets `HOME=/home/prefect` from `/etc/passwd`, so the default `~/.prefect` is writable without extra flags.
  - The `prefect-conda` stage now puts `/opt/conda/envs/prefect/bin` on `PATH` via `ENV`. Before, the env was only activated through `/root/.bashrc`, so non-root users couldn't find `prefect`.
- `.github/workflows/python-tests.yaml`: the Docker image check also runs the image as `--user 1001`. It asserts `HOME=/home/prefect` is writable and runs `prefect version` and `prefect config view`.
- `docs/v3/how-to-guides/self-hosted/server-docker.mdx`: new "Run as a non-root user" section covering `--user 1001`, `--read-only --tmpfs /tmp` with `PREFECT_HOME`, and arbitrary UIDs (where `HOME` is `/`). The server examples set `PREFECT_UI_STATIC_DIRECTORY` to a writable path. Without it, a non-root server cannot copy the UI bundles into site-packages and serves no UI.
- I didn't add a `USER` instruction, because switching the default user would break existing images and derived Dockerfiles that rely on root (e.g. `apt-get` in downstream builds or the runtime `EXTRA_PIP_PACKAGES` install).

**Testing:** CI covers the non-root contract through the Docker image check above. I also built the default and conda images locally and ran:
- Default root: flow completes, `HOME=/root`.
- `--user 1001`: `uid=1001(prefect)`, `HOME=/home/prefect`, flow completes.
- `--user 1001 --read-only --tmpfs /tmp -e PREFECT_HOME=/tmp/.prefect`: flow completes.
- `--user 12345:0`: writes to group-0 directories succeed; with `PREFECT_HOME` set, the flow completes.
- Conda image as `--user 1001`: `prefect version` and a flow both succeed.
- Base images that already have a `prefect` user, or a UID 1001 account: both build, and that account's home is group-writable.
- Each docs `prefect server start` example as written: `/api/health` is `true`, `/` and `/v2/` return 200, and the logs show no errors.
</details>

--- docs/v3/how-to-guides/self-hosted/server-docker.mdx (+36/-0)
@@ -38,6 +38,42 @@ prefect dashboard open
 
 For more information, see the Docker topic about [Networking using the host network](https://docs.docker.com/network/network-tutorial-host/).
 
+## Run as a non-root user
+
+The image runs as root by default. To run as the built-in `prefect` user, use `--user 1001` (or `--user prefect`):
+
+```bash
+docker run --rm --user 1001 -p 4200:4200 \
+  -e PREFECT_UI_STATIC_DIRECTORY=/tmp/prefect-ui \
+  prefecthq/prefect:3-latest prefect server start --host 0.0.0.0
+```
+
+This user has primary group 0 and home `/home/prefect`, so the default Prefect home, `~/.prefect`, is writable.
+Both `/home/prefect` and `/opt/prefect` are writable by group 0, including arbitrary user IDs in that group.
+Root continues to use `/root/.prefect`.
+
+Set `PREFECT_UI_STATIC_DIRECTORY` to a writable directory so the server can prepare both UI bundles. The server creates separate `v1` and `v2` subdirectories there instead of writing to the installed package directory.
+
+For a read-only root filesystem, provide writable temporary storage with `--tmpfs /tmp` and set `PREFECT_HOME` to a directory there:
+
+```bash
+docker run --rm --user 1001 --read-only --tmpfs /tmp \
+  -e PREFECT_HOME=/tmp/.prefect -p 4200:4200 \
+  -e PREFECT_UI_STATIC_DIRECTORY=/tmp/prefect-ui \
+  prefecthq/prefect:3-latest prefect server start --host 0.0.0.0
+```
+
+For an arbitrary UID without an `/etc/passwd` entry, `HOME` defaults to `/`. Set `PREFECT_HOME` explicitly to a writable directory even without `--read-only`:
+
+```bash
+docker run --rm --user 12345:0 --read-only --tmpfs /tmp \
+  -e PREFECT_HOME=/tmp/.prefect -p 4200:4200 \
+  -e PREFECT_UI_STATIC_DIRECTORY=/tmp/prefect-ui \
+  prefecthq/prefect:3-latest prefect server start --host 0.0.0.0
+```
+
+Data in `/tmp` is ephemeral. To persist server data, mount a writable volume and set `PREFECT_HOME` to that location instead. Ensure the volume permissions allow your container user to write to it.
+
 ## Further reading
 
 - [How to scale self-hosted Prefect](/v3/advanced/self-hosted)

title: docs: document legacy prefect-agent pool handling in CLI AGENTS.md
body:
This PR adds one contract to `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`. The contract tells agents that `prefect-agent` work pools are legacy and that workers cannot poll them. CLI commands must filter or redirect these pools, and must not suggest agent commands.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "**`prefect-agent` work pools are legacy and unpollable.** Prefect 3 removed agents (and commands like `prefect agent start` / `prefect deployment build`), and `worker start` rejects these pools, yet the server still auto-creates `default-agent-pool` with this type when a queue is created without a pool. Pool pickers, worker-type lists, and next-step hints must filter or redirect `prefect-agent` pools (see `_prompts.py`, `_worker_utils.py`, `work-queue create`) — never suggest agent commands or `prefect worker start` for them."
Non-obvious evidence: The server makes `default-agent-pool` with type `prefect-agent` in `server/models/work_queues.py`. This is far from the CLI code. Before #24014, `work-queue create` told users to run `prefect worker start` against this pool, and `worker start` told users to run the removed `prefect agent start`. `cli/deploy/_core.py` still tells users to use the removed `prefect deployment build`. So this mistake happens again and again.
Cross-cutting scope: All CLI commands that select pools, list worker types, or print next steps: `_prompts.py`, `_worker_utils.py`, `worker.py`, `work_queue.py`, `deploy/_core.py`.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule applies to many CLI modules. A comment in one module does not help an agent who writes a new command or a new hint in a different module.
Durability: The server keeps the `prefect-agent` type and the default agent pool for backward compatibility. The rule stays valid while these exist.
Counter-evidence checked: `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/workers/AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md` (no mention of `prefect-agent` pools); the comment in `work_queue.py` explains only the local fallback; `tests/cli/test_work_queues.py` and `tests/cli/test_worker.py` test only these two commands.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Files changed in the triggering push (f7f20d7..a328ffc)</summary>

- `docs/contribute/styles-practices.mdx`
- `src/prefect/cli/work_queue.py`
- `src/prefect/cli/worker.py`
- `tests/cli/test_work_queues.py`
- `tests/cli/test_worker.py`

</details>

title: Store text files with LF line endings
body:
This PR makes Git store and check out text files with LF line endings, so a commit from Windows cannot add CRLF line endings.

- Adds a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`. Git converts CRLF to LF when a file is staged, and checks out LF on every platform. The four binary extensions in the repo (`ico`, `jpg`, `png`, `ttf`) are marked `binary`.
- Adds the `mixed-line-ending` pre-commit hook with `--fix=lf`. `static-analysis.yaml` runs pre-commit on all files, so CI fails on a CRLF file.
- Converts the two `prefect-kv.svg` files from CRLF to LF. These are the only CRLF files in the repo, and their content is unchanged.

The change affects only repository config and two images, so there are no new tests or docs.

## Rollout caveats

- `no-op: git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol shows no change to the two SVGs`
- `watch: open PRs from Windows contributors may fail the pre-commit check until they rebase onto main and run git add --renormalize .`

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

A contributor PR came in with Windows line endings. The same `.gitattributes` and hook are going into fastmcp, fastmcp-ts, prefect-collection-registry, prefect-helm, and marvin. `text=auto` alone would check out CRLF on Windows. `eol=lf` keeps shell scripts and Dockerfiles working in a Windows checkout.

</details>

title: Fix `ReactiveTriggers` stop race during startup
body:
This PR fixes a race in `ReactiveTriggers` that made `test_trigger_round_tripping[trigger1]` fail on main ([failed run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/44767938742)).

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Failure:** At teardown, the ephemeral server lifespan calls `ReactiveTriggers.stop()`. `stop()` fails with `AssertionError: Reactive triggers not started`.

**Root cause:** `ReactiveTriggers.start()` sets `consumer_task` only after `triggers.consumer()` finishes setup. That setup calls `reconcile_automations(force=True)`, which reads from the database and can be slow under load. If the server shuts down before that setup completes, `consumer_task` is still `None`, so `stop()` fails.

**Fix:**
- `ReactiveTriggers.start()` now sets `consumer_task` at once. The task does the handler setup and the consumer loop together (`_consume`). `stop()` can now cancel a service that is still loading automations.
- `triggers.consumer()` now does the initial `reconcile_automations(force=True)` inside its `try/finally`. If setup is interrupted, the `listen_for_automation_changes` task is cancelled and does not leak.

**Tests:** I added `test_reactive_triggers_service_can_stop_while_loading_automations`. It blocks `reconcile_automations`, calls `stop()` during startup, and asserts that the change listener is cancelled. The test fails without the fix and passes 20/20 times with the fix. `tests/events/server/triggers`, `tests/events/client/test_automations_server_compatibility.py`, and `tests/server/services/test_service_subsets.py` pass.
</details>

title: Refresh the Python and UI dependency lockfiles
body:
This PR moves several dependencies to newer releases in `uv.lock`, `ui/package-lock.json`, and `ui-v2/package-lock.json`. It changes no source code.

npm:

- vite 8.3.4 → 8.3.8 in ui and ui-v2. The `vite` range floor in both `package.json` files moves to `^8.3.8` so a regenerated lock can't resolve an older 8.3 patch.
- ui-v2: seroval 1.6.12 → 1.8.2 and seroval-plugins 1.6.11 → 1.8.0. `solid-js` 1.x, which `@tanstack/react-query-devtools` depends on, requires `seroval ~1.6`, so new `overrides` entries lift that range.
- ui: jsdom 25.0.1 → 31.0.1. `@prefecthq/vue-compositions` declares `jsdom ^25` but doesn't import it from its built package, so an override lifts the range.
- es-toolkit, `@ungap/structured-clone`, ajv, bundle-name, tldts, and enhanced-resolve move within their existing ranges.

`uv.lock`:

- requests 2.33.0 → 2.34.2, grpcio 1.84.0 → 1.85.3, httplib2 0.32.0 → 0.32.1, google-cloud-storage 3.7.0 → 3.17.1, platformdirs 4.5.1 → 4.14.8, tomlkit 0.14.0 → 0.15.2, asgiref 3.11.0 → 3.13.0, coverage 7.13.1 → 7.17.3, and soupsieve 4.1.1 → 4.1.3. tomli drops out of the lock because nothing needs it on Python 3.11+.

Locally, ui builds and passes vitest, ui-v2 builds and passes vitest, and `tests/utilities` and `tests/cli` pass.

title: Stop pointing users at removed `prefect agent start` for `prefect-agent` pools
body:
closes #24013

This PR changes two CLI messages so that users who have a `prefect-agent` typed work pool get a correct next step. Before, `prefect work-queue create` told users to run `prefect worker start`, and `prefect worker start` then told users to run `prefect agent start`. That command does not exist in Prefect 3.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `prefect worker start` on a `prefect-agent` pool: the error now says that agents were removed in Prefect 3. It tells users to create a work pool with a worker type, and it links to the [upgrade guide](https://www.prefect.io/docs/v3/how-to-guides/migrate/upgrade-agents-to-workers).
- `prefect worker start --type prefect-agent`: this now has a separate error. It says `prefect-agent` is not a worker type and tells users to remove `--type` or pass a worker type.
- `prefect work-queue create`: the command now reads the work pool type before it creates the queue. If the type is `prefect-agent` (for example, the `default-agent-pool` that you get when you do not give `--pool`), the output does not suggest `prefect worker start`. It shows how to create a typed work pool and a work queue in that pool. For all other pool types, the output suggests `prefect worker start` as before. The suggested recreate command keeps any `--limit`/`--priority`, the inspect command now includes `-p <pool>`, and queue and pool names in generated commands are single-quoted for POSIX shells.
- The old `test_start_with_prefect_agent_type` test was nested inside another test function, so pytest did not run it. It is now a module-level test that uses a real `prefect-agent` pool.
- `docs/contribute/styles-practices.mdx`: the work queue output example now shows the current `prefect worker start` output.
- The default work pool type does not change (out of scope for the issue).

Example output:

```
$ prefect work-queue create testq
Created work queue with properties:
    name - 'testq'
    work pool - 'default-agent-pool'
    id - faf898df-cd9a-4a1f-bd28-cf8007f9f80a
    concurrency limit - None
Workers cannot poll 'default-agent-pool' because it is a 'prefect-agent' typed work pool.
To pick up flow runs, create the work queue in a work pool with a worker type:
    prefect work-pool create '<WORK POOL NAME>' --type process
    prefect work-queue create 'testq' -p '<WORK POOL NAME>'

Inspect the work queue:
    prefect work-queue inspect 'testq' -p 'default-agent-pool'
```

</details>

title: Edit RRule schedules in the ui-v2 schedule dialog
body:
Related to #6741 (piece 2; builder landed in #24009)

This PR replaces the "RRule schedules are unsupported" stub in the deployment schedule dialog with a real form built on `RRuleBuilder`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `rrule-schedule-form.tsx`: active toggle, inline builder, timezone, parameter overrides, create (POST) / update (PATCH) through the existing hooks, with `schedule: { rrule, timezone }`. Rules always serialize with `DTSTART;TZID=`. The dialog closes only when the save succeeds; on failure, edits are kept.
- Rules the builder can't represent stay read-only (summary, "can only be edited in code", docs link, collapsed "Show rule"). Save still updates Active and Parameter Overrides, sending a PATCH without `schedule` so the rule is never rewritten.
- New rule default: daily at 09:00, starting today.
- Changing the timezone keeps the wall-clock time.
- `RRuleBuilder` gains an optional validity callback so an invalid draft disables Save.
- No upcoming-runs preview in the dialog (dropped per maintainer review); the deployment page already lists upcoming runs after saving.

Tests: form tests (create/update payloads, overrides, invalid draft, failure keeps edits, metadata-only update for unsupported rules). Stories cover create, supported edit, and unsupported, checked in light and dark mode.

title: Use route names as OpenAPI operation IDs
body:
closes #6754

This PR makes the server's OpenAPI `operationId`s use the endpoint function name in place of FastAPI's generated ID (for example `create_flow_flows__post` becomes `create_flow`). This is the approach agreed on in the issue thread.

<details>

- `create_api_app` now passes `generate_unique_id_function=lambda route: route.name` by default. A `generate_unique_id_function` supplied through `fast_api_app_kwargs` still takes precedence.
- Six route names were used twice, so those routes get explicit IDs:
  - Work-pool-scoped queue routes: `create_work_pool_queue`, `read_work_pool_queue`, `read_work_pool_queues`, `update_work_pool_queue`, `delete_work_pool_queue`.
  - `/automations/templates/validate`: `validate_automation_template`.
  - The Python function names do not change.
- FastAPI builds anonymous request-body schema names from the operation ID, so those names get shorter too (for example `Body_read_flow_runs_flow_runs_filter_post` becomes `Body_read_flow_runs`).
- Regenerated files:
  - `docs/v3/api-ref/rest-api/server/schema.json`, via `just generate-openapi`.
  - `ui-v2/src/api/prefect.ts`, via `npm run service-sync`.
  - The ui-v2 type aliases that reference those body schemas, updated to match.
- REST API doc pages are keyed by `method path`, so they are not affected. Request paths and payloads do not change.
- New test: `test_openapi_operation_ids_use_route_names` checks that every operation ID is unique and equals either the route name or its explicit override.
- Tests run:
  - `tests/server/api/test_server.py`: 98 passed, 4 skipped.
  - ui-v2 tests and build: passed.

</details>

title: Add RRule schedule builder component to ui-v2
body:
Related to #6741 (piece 1 of 2; the issue stays open). Supersedes #24008

this PR adds a Google Calendar style `RRuleBuilder` component and an rrule ↔ form mapper under `ui-v2/src/components/ui/rrule-builder/`. It is not wired into the schedule dialog yet; `rrule-schedule-form.tsx` is unchanged. The follow-up PR wires it in with an upcoming-runs preview.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- Copy and layout follow Google Calendar's custom recurrence: "Repeat every [N] [day/week/month/year]" (pluralized), single-letter weekday chips, one monthly dropdown derived from the start date ("Monthly on day 19" / "Monthly on the third Thursday" / "last"; changing the start date updates a matching selection), annual summary, and Ends radios (Never / On date).
- Supports FREQ daily/weekly/monthly/yearly, INTERVAL, BYDAY, BYMONTHDAY, BYSETPOS, yearly month+day, a time of day and UNTIL. `COUNT` is not offered, since the [docs](https://www.prefect.io/docs/v3/concepts/schedules#rrule) say Prefect doesn't support it.
- Always serializes `DTSTART;TZID=<tz>:...`. UNTIL is written as the end date's local 23:59:59 wall-clock digits with `Z`, matching `RRuleSchedule.to_rrule()`, which relabels UNTIL with the schedule timezone via `.replace(tzinfo=...)`.
- Fields use the shared `Form`/`FormField` primitives with per-field validation messages; only fields the current frequency uses are validated.
- No raw-text editing in the UI. Rules the builder can't express (HOURLY/MINUTELY, COUNT, EXDATE/RDATE, multiple rules, BYWEEKNO/BYYEARDAY, yearly BYMONTHDAY without BYMONTH, multiple times, missing DTSTART, mismatched TZID) show a `toText()` summary, "This schedule can only be edited in code.", a link to the [RRule schedule docs](https://www.prefect.io/docs/v3/concepts/schedules#rrule), the reason, and a collapsed read-only "Show rule".
- Uses the existing `rrule` dependency; no new packages.

Testing: vitest covers mapper round trips, unsupported detection, and component interactions (frequency switching with cleared unused fields, monthly start-date sync, docs link). Locally, mapper output was checked with server `RRuleSchedule.get_dates()` for near-midnight times in Asia/Kathmandu and America/Chicago: the last run lands on the chosen end date. Stories checked in Storybook, light and dark.

Note for the preview PR: JS `rrule` interprets UNTIL differently from the server, so a client-side preview must account for that at the end date.
</details>

title: Reduce state cross-products in orchestration rule tests
body:
This PR reduces the state cross-products in the orchestration rule tests. The touched tests go from 1,226 to 58. Apart from one test-isolation fix (below), only test parametrization changes. There are no changes to `src/`.

The rules in these tests use `FROM_STATES = TO_STATES = ALL_ORCHESTRATION_STATES`. The only inputs that take different code paths are a `None` or non-`None` state on each side of the transition. The tests now use a small set of representative transitions (`REPRESENTATIVE_TRANSITIONS` in `test_rules.py`).

| Change | Tests | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| c4 | `TestNullRejection` (fizzle, abort, no-state) | 342 | 6 |
| c5 | `TestBaseOrchestrationRule` (nested, complex nested, #6177 regression, initial/proposed validity) | 310 | 14 |
| c6 | `TestOrchestrationContext::test_contexts_validate_proposed_states` | 200 | 8 |
| c7 | `TestBaseUniversalTransform` (all, nullified, errored) | 190 | 6 |
| c8 | `TestTransitionsFromTerminalStatesRule::test_does_not_block_transitions_from_non_terminal_states` | 108 | 12 |
| c9 | `TestPreventPendingTransitions::test_all_other_transitions_are_accepted` | 76 | 12 |
| | **Total** | **1,226** | **58** |

File totals (`uv run pytest <file> --collect-only -q | tail -1`): `test_rules.py` 1,095 → 87, `test_core_policy.py` 530 → 370.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Difference from the audit spec (c9).** #23962 merged after the audit. It adds `COMPLETED` to `PreventPendingTransitions.FROM_STATES` and to the test's `banned_states`. Because of this, COMPLETED → PENDING is now aborted and `test_banned_transitions_are_aborted` covers it. This PR does not put it in the accepted list. That is why c9 starts at 76 (not 77) and ends at 12 (not 13). The accepted list has a comment that cites #9447 and #7116.

**Removed helpers.** `CANONICAL_STATES` and the `all_transitions`, `terminal_transitions` and `active_transitions` class attributes are no longer used, so this PR removes them. `itertools.product` is no longer used in `test_rules.py`, so this PR removes that import too.

**Coverage.** The coverage report is identical before and after for each file, including the missing lines and partial branches:

```
uv run pytest tests/server/orchestration/test_rules.py tests/server/orchestration/test_core_policy.py -n4 \
  --cov=prefect.server.orchestration --cov=prefect.server.models --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing
```

| Before | 4286 | 1927 | 1478 | 185 | 49% |
| After | 4286 | 1927 | 1478 | 185 | 49% |

Before: 1,623 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed. After: 455 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed (SQLite, run locally).

Tracked in OSS-8499 (part of OSS-8493).
</details>

title: docs: document how to verify integration dependency floors
body:
This PR corrects the integration testing guidance. Tests against the local Prefect checkout can pass even if an integration does not work with the minimum Prefect release declared in its package metadata.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: src/integrations/AGENTS.md  
Proposed text: Explain when integration tests use the local checkout and when to test against the exact published Prefect minimum with the local override disabled.  
Non-obvious evidence: The dependency table advertises a published minimum, but the separate uv sources table selects the checkout for normal integration tests. The test workflow does not test this minimum, and the existing guidance incorrectly says the default is PyPI.

title: Fix flaky logs subscriber setup-cancellation test
body:
This PR fixes the flaky test `test_subscriber_closes_socket_when_setup_is_cancelled` in `tests/logging/test_logs_subscriber.py`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Failure:** [Unit tests run on main](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/44578881857) (python 3.15, postgres 14) failed with `assert log_recorder.connections == 1` (`0 == 1`).

**Root cause:** The test cancelled `subscriber.__aenter__()` with a 0.5 second wall-clock timeout. The timeout covers `check_server_version`, the TCP connect, and the websocket handshake. On the CI runner, the event loop was blocked for 0.92 seconds (asyncio slow-callback warning in the log). The timeout fired before the client sent the HTTP upgrade request, so the server logged `opening handshake failed` and never counted the connection. The test did not exercise the "cancelled mid-handshake" path that it is meant to test.

**Fix:** The patched `recv` sets an `asyncio.Event` when setup is waiting for the auth response. The test runs `__aenter__()` in a task, waits for that event, and then cancels the task. Cancellation now always occurs after the socket is open, and the test does not depend on timing. The assertions do not change.

**Verification:** The test passed 30 of 30 runs locally (both parametrizations). The full module passed with `-n4`. Pre-commit hooks passed.

</details>

diff:
--- tests/logging/test_logs_subscriber.py (+11/-3)
@@ -822,7 +822,10 @@ async def test_subscriber_closes_socket_when_setup_is_cancelled(
     context that fails to enter is never exited by its caller."""
     log_puppeteer.token = token
 
+    waiting_for_auth = asyncio.Event()
+
     async def never_respond(self: ClientConnection, *args: object, **kwargs: object):
+        waiting_for_auth.set()
         await asyncio.Event().wait()
 
     monkeypatch.setattr(ClientConnection, "recv", never_respond)
@@ -831,9 +834,14 @@ async def never_respond(self: ClientConnection, *args: object, **kwargs: object)
         filter=LogFilter(level=LogFilterLevel(ge_=logging.INFO)),
         reconnection_attempts=0,
     )
-    with pytest.raises(TimeoutError):
-        async with asyncio.timeout(0.5):
-            await subscriber.__aenter__()
+    # Cancel only once the handshake has completed and setup is blocked waiting
+    # for the auth response; a wall-clock timeout can fire before the socket
+    # opens on a slow runner.
+    setup = asyncio.create_task(subscriber.__aenter__())
+    await waiting_for_auth.wait()
+    setup.cancel()
+    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+        await setup
 
     assert log_recorder.connections == 1
     assert subscriber._connect.connection.state is WebsocketState.CLOSED

title: docs: clarify tmpchdir process-wide scope
body:
This PR clarifies that `tmpchdir` changes the working directory for the entire process. It gives callers a way to avoid relative path conflicts when work overlaps.

Audited all nine commits in [2574680482..125543d334](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/compare/2574680482812f0c82ee0cb123ef67b73d9b367b...125543d334df8cb9e6b08e757fb090c6b31151ed).

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: src/prefect/utilities/filesystem/AGENTS.md  
Proposed text: Clarify which callers the lock serializes. For concurrent work that needs different base directories, use explicit paths or set the working directory of the subprocess.  
Non-obvious evidence: The current guidance and the docstring say that other threads block. The lock test checks acquisition of the lock only. A local probe confirmed that a separate thread and a separate async task still resolve relative paths against the temporary working directory.  
Cross-cutting scope: Applies to relative path resolution in concurrent callers, including the CLI, deployment steps, and runner code.  
Why not code comment/docstring: Callers need this guidance when choosing between a process-wide directory change, explicit paths, and a subprocess working directory.  
Durability: The working directory has process-wide scope, independent of how the helper serializes callers.  
Counter-evidence checked: The `tmpchdir` implementation and docstring, its filesystem tests, CLI and async test callers, and existing filesystem and parent AGENTS.md guidance.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Files changed in the triggering push</summary>

- `src/prefect/utilities/dockerutils.py`
- `tests/utilities/test_dockerutils.py`

</details>

### Checklist

- [x] Documentation-only change to agent guidance.
- [x] Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Filesystem tests passed on Linux (34 passed, 5 Windows-only skips). A separate probe verified relative path resolution from another thread and an async task.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/dfa843ba65de4a4eb39d16bfcd620648
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/dfa843ba65de4a4eb39d16bfcd620648?variant=devin
author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
diff:
--- src/prefect/utilities/filesystem/AGENTS.md (+2/-1)
@@ -9,9 +9,10 @@ Path normalization, file filtering compatible with `.gitignore`/`.prefectignore`
 ## Entry Points
 
 - `filter_files(root, ignore_patterns, include_dirs=True, *, as_posix=False) -> set[str]` — return the set of included paths under `root` according to pathspec patterns. Returned paths are relative to `root` and use platform-native separators by default. Callers comparing against `Path.as_posix()` must opt in with `as_posix=True`. Used to build `shutil.copytree`'s `ignore` callback.
-- `tmpchdir(path)` — context manager that `chdir`s into `path` and restores the previous cwd on exit. Guarded by the reentrant module-level `chdir_lock`: contexts nest within one thread, and other threads block until the outermost context exits.
+- `tmpchdir(path)` — changes the working directory and restores it on exit. Contexts nest on the same thread and serialize across threads that call `tmpchdir`.
 - `get_open_file_limit() -> int` — platform-specific maximum open-file count, with a conservative Windows default.
 
 ## Pitfalls
 
+- **`tmpchdir` changes the working directory for the entire process.** Other threads and async tasks can resolve relative paths against the temporary directory while the context is open. Use explicit paths or a subprocess `cwd` when concurrent work needs different base directories.
 - **`filter_files` with `include_dirs=True` (the default) always includes all ancestor directories of matched files**, even if those directories weren't directly matched by the ignore patterns. This ensures `shutil.copytree`'s `ignore_func` doesn't skip directories containing files that should be copied. Side effect: callers expecting only pathspec-matched entries will receive additional directory paths. The parent-dir expansion does NOT run when `include_dirs=False`.

title: Retire PR auto-labeling workflows
body:
### Overview

This PR retires the two `pull_request_target` auto-labeling workflows ahead of the GitHub Actions policy change taking effect December 2, rather than requesting a policy exception.

Removed:

- `.github/workflows/labeler.yml` (`actions/labeler` — applied `plan`, `docs`, `migration`, `upstream dependency`, `2.x`, `ui` from changed files/base branch)
- `.github/workflows/copy-linked-issue-labels.yml` (`michalvankodev/copy-issue-labels` — copied labels from linked issues)
- `.github/labeler.yml` (labeler configuration, now unused)

Kept: all GitHub labels and `.github/release.yml`.

### Dependency check

Verified before removal:

- **No required-check dependency.** The only ruleset applying to `main` (org-level "Protect default branch") has no `required_status_checks` rule; the effective branch rules are `non_fast_forward`, `pull_request` (1 approval), `deletion`, and `required_linear_history`. Neither workflow gate merges.
- **No workflow dependencies.** No `workflow_run` trigger references these workflows (`notify-on-failure`, `devin-fix-flaky-tests`, `api-compatibility-comment` watch other workflows).
- **Release notes.** `.github/release.yml` and `scripts/prepare_integration_release_notes.py` consume PR labels at release time, but the labels themselves remain; only automatic application is removed. The script also falls back to title-based categorization.
- **Label-triggered workflows.** `integration-package-tests.yaml` reacts to the `labeled` event and the `test-all-integrations`/`integrations` labels, which are applied manually and unaffected. `stale.yml` uses `status:*` labels, unrelated.

The only impact is triage and release-note labeling.

### Maintainer note

Going forward, maintainers should apply labels manually before merge where appropriate:

- `plan` on plan-only PRs (excluded from release notes)
- `docs` on documentation changes (categorized under Documentation 📓)
- `upstream dependency` on requirements changes (categorized under Integrations & Dependencies 🤝)

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request removes functionality that requires no tests (workflow/config deletion only).
- [x] No user-facing behavior change; no documentation updates needed.

title: Reset the logs subscriber retry budget after a successful reconnect
body:
Closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23984

This PR resets the logs subscriber's failure count after each successful reconnect. A separate count limits clean closes when clean-close reconnection is enabled. Both the log and event subscribers raise the connection error when either retry limit is exhausted.

<details>
<summary>Test results and retry behavior</summary>

With a budget of two retries, the regression test fails on the third disconnect before the fix. With the fix, it receives a log after four reconnects. The clean-close test confirms that a second clean close raises when the budget is one.

A regression test for each subscriber confirms that an abnormal receive failure followed by a clean close during the reconnect ping raises `ConnectionClosedOK` when the retry limit is one.

All 105 logs, events, and flow-run subscriber tests passed. Pre-commit and Pyright also passed.

As with the event subscriber, the logs subscriber keeps retrying if the server accepts each reconnect and then disconnects abnormally.

</details>

Linear tracking: [OSS-8494](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/OSS-8494/logs-subscriber-gives-up-after-transient-reconnects-because-retry)

- [x] This pull request references the related GitHub issue.
- [x] This pull request includes regression tests.
- [x] The subscriber docstrings describe how the retry limit applies.

title: docs: document safe redirect search params in routes AGENTS.md
body:
this PR adds a short rule to `ui-v2/src/routes/AGENTS.md`: a search param that becomes a navigation target should be declared as `z.string().refine(isSafeRedirectPath).optional().catch(undefined)`. This follows #23980. The section's existing example, `redirect: z.string().optional()`, is the pattern that allows an open redirect.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: ui-v2/src/routes/AGENTS.md
Proposed text: In the "Search Parameters" section, one paragraph saying that a search param used as a navigation target (e.g. `redirectTo` on `/login`) should be `z.string().refine(isSafeRedirectPath).optional().catch(undefined)`. A plain `z.string()` lets `//host` or `https://...` values redirect off-origin. Without `.catch(undefined)`, a rejected value raises a search-validation error when it should fall back to the default.
Non-obvious evidence: The section's only example is `redirect: z.string().optional()`, which accepts off-origin values. The `.catch(undefined)` requirement is mentioned only in the `isSafeRedirectPath` docstring and only for the login route. Nothing in the routes layer tells authors of new routes to use the helper.
Cross-cutting scope: Any TanStack route whose search param ends up in `navigate`/`redirect`/`<Navigate>`. `/login` (`redirectTo`) and `/blocks/catalog/$slug/create` (`redirect`) both do this today.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule applies to routes that do not exist yet. The docstring on `isSafeRedirectPath` is only read by someone who already knows to use it. The routes AGENTS.md is where agents look for search-param conventions.
Durability: Open-redirect protection and the TanStack search-validation fallback behavior don't depend on this PR. They stay relevant for every new route that accepts a return URL.

title: Vacuum terminal flow runs that have no end_time
body:
closes #23981

This PR changes the flow run vacuum so that it also deletes old terminal flow runs that have no `end_time`. For these runs, the vacuum uses `state_timestamp` to measure age.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Before #20369 (3.6.14), `SetEndTime` set `end_time` only when the run had a `start_time`. Runs that went to a terminal state without running (for example, Scheduled → Cancelled) kept `end_time = NULL`. The old eligibility filter required `end_time IS NOT NULL`, so the vacuum never deleted these runs, their logs, their artifacts, or their subflows.

The new filter is:

```python
sa.or_(
    db.FlowRun.end_time < retention_cutoff,
    sa.and_(
        db.FlowRun.end_time.is_(None),
        db.FlowRun.state_timestamp < retention_cutoff,
    ),
)
```

`state_timestamp` is set on every state transition, so for a terminal run it is the time that the run entered its terminal state. Both columns have indexes. I used a fallback in the vacuum instead of a backfill migration, so there is no large data update on `flow_run` during upgrade.

Tests:
- `test_preserves_terminal_run_without_end_time` is replaced. The old test did not keep `end_time` NULL, because `SetEndTime` sets it at creation time.
- New tests simulate legacy rows (`start_time`/`end_time` NULL) for all terminal states, and make sure that recent legacy rows are kept.
- The new tests fail without the fix. `tests/server/services/test_db_vacuum.py` passes on SQLite and PostgreSQL.

The database maintenance docs are updated.
</details>

title: Accept only same-origin paths in the UI v2 login redirect
body:
Related to #15512

The UI v2 login route reads a `redirectTo` search param and sends the user there after login. If the user is already logged in, the route sends them there immediately. The route schema accepted any string. TanStack Router keeps the current values on the same origin, because the app passes them as `to`. But that safety comes from router internals, not from our code.

This change hardens the path check in the login route:

- `isSafeRedirectPath` in `ui-v2/src/utils/safe-redirect.ts` accepts a value only if it starts with `/` and stays on the same origin after URL parsing. URL parsing applies browser rules, so `/\evil.example` and values with tabs or newlines are rejected. A value that does not parse is rejected and does not throw.
- The login search schema uses `z.string().refine(isSafeRedirectPath).optional().catch(undefined)`. A rejected value becomes `undefined`, so the user goes to `/dashboard` and the login page still renders.
- The value that the root auth guard sets (`location.href`, for example `/flows?x=1`) still passes, so users return to the page they asked for.

Tests: unit tests for accepted and rejected values, and two Playwright tests in `e2e/auth/login.spec.ts` for an external URL and a `//` URL.

### Checklist

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
  - Small fix; no separate issue.
- [x] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.
  - No docs change: the login page behaves the same for normal links.
- [x] If this pull request removes docs files, it includes redirect settings in `mint.json`.
- [x] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings.

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

A review of the login route asked how `redirectTo` gets its value and where it can send a user. Only the root auth guard sets it, and all three consumers pass it to the router as `to`. A first version used `new URL` without a try/catch. Values such as `//[` then made the schema throw, and Zod's `.catch` does not absorb a throw inside `.refine`, so the route showed its error page. The final version returns `false` instead.

</details>

title: Keep workers alive when cancelling a run hits an API error
body:
closes #23972

this PR stops API errors in `BaseWorker._cancel_run` from crashing the worker.

<details>

### Problem

The cancellation observer starts `_cancel_run` in the worker's `_runs_task_group`. `_cancel_run` only catches `ObjectNotFound`, so a 502/504 or timeout from `read_flow_run`, from `resolve_for_flow_run` (which reads the deployment), or from `set_flow_run_state` escapes the task, cancels the task group and stops the worker along with every run it supervises.

### Changes

`_cancel_run` now wraps the existing body (moved unchanged into `_cancel_pending_run`) and logs any `Exception` as `Failed to cancel flow run <id>` instead of raising. Moving the body keeps the existing tests that call `_cancel_run` as they are and avoids re-indenting it. `BaseException`s such as cancellation still propagate.

### Tests

`test_worker_survives_api_error_while_cancelling_run` in `tests/workers/test_base_worker.py`, parametrized over the three calls above. In the `set_flow_run_state` case `kill_infrastructure` has already succeeded. All three fail on `main` with `httpx.HTTPStatusError: HTTP 502` and pass with the change.

```
uv run pytest tests/workers/test_base_worker.py -k TestWorkerCancellationHandling   # 14 passed
uv run pytest tests/workers -n 4                                                    # 273 passed, 1 skipped
uv run pre-commit run --files src/prefect/workers/base.py tests/workers/test_base_worker.py   # clean
```

The reproduction script in the issue prints `worker crashed: HTTPStatusError('502 Bad Gateway')` on `main` and `worker exited cleanly` with this change.

### Not changed

- A cancellation that fails this way is not retried: the observer has already claimed the dispatch, and it only releases the claim when `on_cancelling` raises synchronously. Before this change the worker crashed instead, so the request was lost either way. Re-registering the run with the observer on failure would allow a retry in polling mode; I left it out to keep this focused, and I'm happy to add it if you'd like.
- `Runner._cancel_run` has a similar unguarded `read_flow_run`; it's a separate code path.

</details>

title: docs: document GitRepository credential redaction rule in runner AGENTS.md
body:
This PR adds a short "GitRepository Credential Redaction" section to `src/prefect/runner/AGENTS.md`. The section states that any URL or git stderr from `GitRepository` that goes to logs, `repr`, or exception messages must go through `strip_auth_from_url` / `strip_auth_from_urls_in_text`. It also states that redaction is display-only: `__eq__` and `to_pull_step()` keep the raw `_url`.

Audited range: `73a37b22c25007e7b3ce63f4f678f2a378722d9b..d0b2ae04d709e51034f57501538f29499f8f0e19`. The later commit (#23967) removes dead code only. No AGENTS.md text refers to the removed helpers, so it needs no change.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/runner/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: New 3-line section "GitRepository Credential Redaction". `_url` can contain credentials and `_repository_url_with_credentials` adds them. URLs and git stderr that go to logs, `repr`, or exceptions must use `strip_auth_from_url` / `strip_auth_from_urls_in_text` (`prefect._internal.urls`). Redaction is display-only: equality and `to_pull_step()` keep the raw `_url`.
Non-obvious evidence: The helpers are applied one call site at a time, so a new log line or error message can skip them. This has happened more than once: #18845 (clone failure), #22196 (clone stderr), and #23969 (clone debug log and `__repr__`). The display-only exception, where `to_pull_step()` and `__eq__` keep the raw URL, is not documented anywhere.
Cross-cutting scope: Applies to every output path of `GitRepository` (clone, pull, existing-repo URL mismatch errors, `repr`) and to the shared helpers in `prefect._internal.urls`. It does not apply to one function only.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule applies to future call sites that do not exist yet, and it spans the whole class. Agents read AGENTS.md before they change `runner/storage.py`. It sits next to the existing "GitRepository Input Validation" security section.
Durability: The rule stays valid while `GitRepository` takes URLs that can contain credentials. It does not depend on the triggering diff.
Counter-evidence checked: `storage.py` call sites and docstrings (no class-level note about redaction), `prefect._internal.urls` docstrings, `tests/runner/test_storage.py`, `src/prefect/runner/AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` (the Logging section covers only API key obfuscation through `get_logger`), and all AGENTS.md files searched for `strip_auth` and credentials (none found).

--- src/prefect/runner/AGENTS.md (+4/-0)
@@ -124,6 +124,10 @@ This matters because `get_directory` typically calls `shutil.copytree(..., dirs_
 
 These validations exist to prevent git argument injection. Do not bypass them when constructing `GitRepository` programmatically.
 
+## GitRepository Credential Redaction
+
+`GitRepository._url` may embed credentials (`https://user:token@host/...`), and `_repository_url_with_credentials` adds them from `credentials`. Any URL or git stderr that reaches logs, `repr`, or exception messages must go through `strip_auth_from_url` / `strip_auth_from_urls_in_text` (`prefect._internal.urls`); missed call sites have leaked tokens more than once. Redaction is display-only: equality checks and `to_pull_step()` keep the raw `_url`.
+
 ## GitRepository Concurrent Pull Protection
 
 `GitRepository.pull_code()` serializes concurrent calls via a `FileLock` (`prefect.locking._filelock`). The lock file sits adjacent to the destination: `destination.parent / (destination.name + ".lock")`. Stale locks from crashed processes are recovered automatically via PID check. Tests that broadly monkeypatch `pathlib.Path.exists` must account for this lock file being created next to the destination.

title: Run the TLA+ model check on Amazon Corretto 21
body:
The TLA+ workflow installed Eclipse Temurin 21, whose newest release, 21.0.13+9, is affected by CVE-2026-114938, a heap overflow in the JDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder. Temurin has not published a fixed build. Amazon Corretto 21.0.13.1.2 includes the fix, and `actions/setup-java` installs it with `distribution: corretto`.

The job reads only the pinned TLA+ tools jar and the model files in the checkout, so the exposure was low. The change keeps CI off an affected JDK without waiting for a Temurin release.

I ran the target model check locally on `amazoncorretto:21` (JDK 21.0.13.1) with the pinned `tla2tools.jar` 1.7.4. It completed with no errors: 244,765 states generated and 55,915 distinct. This PR changes the workflow file, so the TLA+ model check runs here on Corretto too.

title: Strip credentials from repository URL in `GitRepository` clone debug log
body:
closes #23968

this PR applies `strip_auth_from_url` to the `Cloning repository %s` DEBUG log line in `GitRepository._clone_repo`, so tokens embedded in the repository URL (e.g. `https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/...`, the pattern the docs recommend for the Prefect Cloud GitHub App) are no longer written to process logs when `PREFECT_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`. `GitRepository.__repr__` is sanitized the same way.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The failure path already sanitized the URL; this was the only remaining log of the raw `self._url`.
- The URL actually passed to `git clone` is unchanged.
- Verified with the repro from the issue: before the fix the token appears 3 times (once per retry); after, the line reads `Cloning repository https://127.0.0.1:9/owner/repo.git`.
- Added tests for the sanitized debug log and `__repr__`; both fail without the fix.

</details>

title: Remove unreachable branch and unused internal helpers
body:
This PR removes code that is never run. It does not change behavior. All removed names are in private `_internal` modules or behind `if False`.

<details>
<summary>Evidence for each removal</summary>

To find callers, `git grep -w <name>` was run across `src/` (this includes `src/integrations/`), `tests/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `benches/`, `integration-tests/` and `compat-tests/`. "No callers" means that only the definition was found.

1. **`task_engine.py`: the `if False and txn.is_committed(): txn.read()` branch in `run_generator_task_sync` and `run_generator_task_async`.** The `False and ...` condition is always false, so only the `else` body runs. #13820 (2024-06) added this branch as a placeholder. The `else` body is now dedented and its content is the same (`git diff -w` shows only 8 deleted lines). The sync and async paths are changed in the same way.
2. **`_internal/concurrency/event_loop.py::run_coroutine_in_loop_from_async`**: no callers. Its last user was removed in #13593 (2024-05, "Remove old task runners and futures modules"). The `Coroutine` and `get_running_loop` imports were then unused, so they are also removed.
3. **`_internal/pydantic/v2_schema.py::has_v2_type_as_param`**: no callers since #12210 (2024-03). `is_v2_type` and `is_v2_model` are still used and are kept.
4. **`_internal/ast_utils.py::find_task_functions_in_file`**: never called. Its sibling `find_flow_functions_in_file` is used by `cli/_prompts.py` and is kept.
5. **`_internal/versioning.py::SimpleVersionInfo`**: never constructed. Since #17966, `deployments/runner.py` builds a plain `VersionInfo(type="prefect:simple")`. Nothing finds subclasses through a registry or `__subclasses__`. The `VersionType.SIMPLE` enum value is kept.

Found with `vulture` and `deptry`, then checked by hand. Items that look unused but are reached in other ways are not in this PR: the `render_swagger` mkdocs entry point, `jinja2-humanize-extension` (loaded by its name as a string), `aiosqlite` (loaded through the SQLAlchemy URL) and `click`.

**Tests:** `pre-commit` passes on the changed files. The generator tests in `tests/test_task_engine.py` (30 passed). `tests/_internal/{concurrency,pydantic,schemas}` and the tests that import `versioning` or `ast_utils` (989 passed).
</details>

title: Retry run-deployment actions when the database is unreachable
body:
closes #23964

this PR makes a `run-deployment` automation action survive a brief database outage instead of failing after one attempt.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- **Server**: `is_client_retryable_exception` now treats `socket.gaierror` and `ConnectionRefusedError` as retryable, so the API answers 503 instead of 500 when asyncpg can't resolve or reach the database host. asyncpg raises these unwrapped from the pool connect, the same way it raises `PostgresConnectionError` (added in #23741). Other `OSError`s still give 500. The client then retries with its normal backoff.
- **Actions**: `RunDeployment.command` calls `response.raise_for_status()` on a 5xx. The error is no longer turned into a final `ActionFailed`, so the consumer doesn't ack and the broker redelivers the message. `create_flow_run` already sends `triggered_action.idempotency_key()`, so a redelivery can't create a second run. 4xx responses still raise `ActionFailed` like before. Other `DeploymentCommandAction`/`ExternalDataAction` subclasses keep the `>= 300` check, since the ticket doesn't cover whether retrying them is safe.

**Tests**
- `test_retryable_exception_handler` covers the two new exceptions (503), and a new test checks that other `OSError`s are not retryable.
- `test_server_errors_are_redelivered_without_duplicate_runs`: the first `create_flow_run` creates the run but returns 503. The handler raises, and the redelivered message ends with exactly one flow run. This test fails without the fix.

**Repro**: I ran the issue's script against a Postgres URL with a refused port. Before the fix: `[500]`, and the handler returned, so the message was acked. After the fix: `[503, 503]` from the client's retries, and the handler raised, so the message would be redelivered.

</details>

title: fix(prefect-redis): keep unprocessed entries when trimming streams
body:
closes #23963

This PR stops `_trim_stream_to_lowest_delivered_id` from deleting stream entries that a consumer group has not processed. It also logs a warning when an entry is lost.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Changes in `prefect_redis/messaging.py`:

- **Pending entries:** A group's trim floor is now its oldest pending entry (from the `XPENDING` summary) when the group has pending entries. Otherwise, the floor is its `last-delivered-id`. Before this change, the trim could delete an entry that failed in a handler before `XAUTOCLAIM` retried it. If the `XPENDING` call fails, the trim is skipped.
- **ID comparison:** The new `_parse_stream_id` compares IDs as `(ms, seq)` tuples. Before, `min()` compared strings, so `"1000-10"` was lower than `"1000-2"`.
- **Deleted pending entries:** `process_pending_messages` reads the third element of the `XAUTOCLAIM` reply (Redis 7.0+). It logs a WARNING with the stream, the group and the deleted IDs. It does this before the `if not claimed_messages: break` check. Redis has already removed these IDs from the PEL, so the consumer does not ack them.
- **Skipped groups (cases 4 and 5 in the issue):** The trim still skips groups whose consumers are all idle past `trim_idle_threshold`, and groups at `0-0`. The skip rules do not change. If you change them, an abandoned group can pin the stream again (#18606). A maintainer must decide that. Now, when the trim skips such a group and the group has pending entries or a lag that is not 0, the trim logs a WARNING (before it was a DEBUG line only).

A side effect: when a group has an entry that stays pending, that entry now holds the floor until the entry is acked or sent to the DLQ (after `max_retries`). Before, the trim deleted the entry.

Tests: new real-Redis tests for pending entries, numeric ID order, the `XAUTOCLAIM` deleted-ID warning, and the skipped-group warning (warn and no-warn cases). `test_trimming_skips_idle_consumer_groups` now also checks the warning.

I also ran the reporter's script on Redis 8.10.3. Rows 2, 2b and 3 now lose no entries. Rows 1 and 4 lose the same entries as before, and the trim now logs a WARNING for each.
</details>

title: Prevent stale workers from moving completed flow runs to `Pending`
body:
closes #23961

This PR adds `StateType.COMPLETED` to `PreventPendingTransitions.FROM_STATES`. The server now aborts a `Completed -> Pending` proposal for a flow run.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Before this change, the server accepted `Completed -> Pending` when the completed state had no persisted result data. `HandleFlowTerminalStateTransitions` only rejects this transition when the result is persisted, and `PreventPendingTransitions` did not include `COMPLETED`. Thus, a worker with a stale copy of a flow run (from an earlier poll) could propose `Pending()` and submit a run that another worker had already completed.

The server orchestrates the transition on the locked flow-run row, so a fix in the server closes the race. A re-fetch in the worker would not close it.

Behavior that does not change:
- Reruns of deployed runs go through `Scheduled` (for example `AwaitingRetry`), then `Pending`.
- Reruns of ad hoc runs go directly to `Running`.
- `force=True` uses `MinimalFlowPolicy`, which does not include `PreventPendingTransitions`. The ad hoc infrastructure retries in `workers/base.py` and `workers/process.py` use `force=True`, so they continue to work.
- `BaseWorker._propose_pending_state` already handles `Abort`, so the stale worker skips the run.

`Failed`/`Crashed -> Pending` are not changed. The issue only covers `Completed`.

Tests:
- `TestPreventPendingTransitions` now includes `COMPLETED -> PENDING` in the aborted transitions.
- A new API test (`test_stale_pending_proposal_for_completed_flow_run_is_aborted`) runs the full policy: `Pending -> Running -> Completed` (no data), then `Pending` is aborted and the run stays `COMPLETED`. A rerun through `Scheduled -> Pending` is still accepted. This test fails on `main`.
- These suites pass locally: `tests/server/orchestration/test_core_policy.py`, `tests/server/models/test_flow_run_states.py`, `tests/server/orchestration/api/test_flow_runs.py`, `tests/workers/test_base_worker.py`, `tests/workers/test_process_worker.py`, `tests/runner/`.

The generated API reference (`docs/v3/api-ref/python/`) will update from the docstring when the docs are regenerated.
</details>

title: Document `RemoteFileSystem` settings with an example
body:
closes #6286

This PR explains how to use the `settings` field of the `RemoteFileSystem` block. Before this change, the field description was only "Additional settings to pass through to fsspec." No example showed how to pass connection options.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The `settings` field description now says that the values go to the fsspec implementation for the base path's protocol as keyword arguments. It links to the built-in and other known fsspec implementations. It also says that the values are stored as plain text and are not obfuscated, so users must not store credentials there. The UI block form shows this description.
- The `settings` field now has an `examples` value: `{"client_kwargs": {"endpoint_url": "http://localhost:9000"}}`.
- The `RemoteFileSystem` docstring has a new paragraph about `settings`. The paragraph says that external implementations must be installed (for example, `s3fs` for `s3://` paths). It tells users to supply credentials through the environment or a dedicated block, such as `SMB` or `S3Bucket` from `prefect-aws`. The `SMB` block was added in [#6344](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/6344) and covers the Samba case from the issue.
- The docstring has a second example that connects to an S3-compatible service, such as MinIO. The example reads credentials from the standard AWS environment variables.
- A new test makes sure that `settings` are sent to the fsspec file system (`storage_options`).

The changes do not modify runtime behavior. Because the field description changed, the block schema checksum for `RemoteFileSystem` changes too. This is the same as for other field description updates.

</details>

title: Start the suspension observer early for MicroVM deployments that pull code
body:
Related to CLOUD-6128

#23947 made `prefect.engine` and `flow_engine._run_flow_from_runtime_entrypoint` start the flow run suspension observer before they load the flow run and the flow. In a Lambda MicroVM, that cut the time from the runtime entrypoint to the Running proposal from 1.44 s to 1.15 s at p50 (16 runs on each side of the merge commit).

The prefect-aws MicroVM supervisor has two paths. A deployment with an entrypoint goes through `_run_flow_from_runtime_entrypoint`, so it already gets the early start. A deployment with no entrypoint, which is the case when it has pull steps, runs the supervisor's own copy of the `prefect.engine` sequence. That copy still starts the observer late, so those runs still wait for it before Running.

`execute_flow_run` now starts the observer as soon as it has the flow run ID, the same way `prefect.engine` does. It stops the observer after `load_flow_run` if the run has no deployment. We have not measured this path; we expect about the same saving, because it runs the same steps.

prefect-aws supports Prefect 3.8.4 and later, and those versions have no `prestart_flow_run_suspension_observer`. The supervisor imports it under `try`/`except ImportError` and falls back to a context manager that starts nothing, so on older Prefect the engine starts its own observer as before. The engine contract test pins the function's signature, so a rename or signature change in Prefect fails that test instead of falling back silently.

`scripts/generate_integration_package_tests_matrix.py` now lists `_flow_run_suspension.py` among the core files prefect-aws uses, so a change to it runs the prefect-aws tests.

Considered and rejected: raising prefect-aws's Prefect floor to the release that carries #23947. The fallback costs a few lines and keeps prefect-aws installable with older Prefect versions.

## Rollout caveats

- `no-op: MicroVM runs with an entrypoint, and runs on a Prefect version without #23947, take the same path as before`

title: Fix flaky `test_keeps_polling_while_setup_hangs` observer test
body:
This PR fixes a flaky test: `tests/test_observers.py::TestObserverRecovery::test_keeps_polling_while_setup_hangs`.

It failed on `main` in [Unit tests run 43973504965](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/43973504965) (python 3.14, group 7) with `assert stream.abandoned == 0` / `assert 1 == 0`.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

The test set `SETUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to `0.2`. Then it waited for polling to report the signal and asserted that the hanging setup was not abandoned yet. This is a race between a 0.2s wall-clock deadline and the poll loop. In the CI log, the event loop stalled for 0.526s (`Executing <Task ... _connect()> took 0.526 seconds`). The setup deadline expired before the assertion ran, so `abandoned` was already `1`.

I reproduced the failure on every run by adding a `time.sleep(0.5)` after the second setup attempt starts.

The fix removes the wall-clock race. The test now:
- sets `SETUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to a large value, so the deadline does not expire by itself,
- wraps `asyncio.timeout` to capture the `asyncio.Timeout` for the setup,
- after it asserts polling delivery, expires that deadline with `Timeout.reschedule(loop.time())`.

The real timeout path in `ObservationDelivery._connect` still runs (`TimeoutError` is caught and logged as "failed to reconnect"). Only the time when it fires is controlled by the test. No source code changes.

Verification:
- Passes with the injected 0.5s stall (it failed before the fix).
- 60/60 passes with `--flake-finder --flake-runs=30 -n 4`.
- `tests/test_observers.py`: 76 passed with `-n 6`.
</details>

title: Start the flow run suspension observer before the engine loads the flow
body:
Related to CLOUD-6126

Before the engine proposes Running for a deployment flow run, it starts the flow run suspension observer and waits until the observer has a client, an events subscription, and a first read of the flow run. In a Lambda MicroVM that wait was 0.43 s at the median, out of 0.55 s from `run_flow` starting to the Running proposal. The process entry points already know the flow run ID while they spend that same stretch loading the flow run and the flow.

`prefect.engine` and `flow_engine._run_flow_from_runtime_entrypoint` now start the observer as soon as they have the flow run ID. The engine uses that observer for its flow run instead of starting another, and it still waits for the observer to be ready before it proposes Running. The engine and the observer share one `FlowRunSuspensionRequest`, so a suspension that arrives while the flow loads raises `Pause` at the first orchestration boundary, as it does today.

Decisions:

- A run without a deployment never used an observer. The entry points stop it right after `load_flow_run`, cancelling its first read if that read has not finished.
- An inline subflow keeps its parent's request and starts its own observer, as before.
- With no `PREFECT_API_URL`, nothing starts early. The ephemeral server that `get_client` starts is not safe to start from two threads at once.

Considered and rejected: starting the observer only after `load_flow_run`, once `deployment_id` is known. It avoids the extra connection for runs without a deployment but gives up the overlap with that read. Also rejected: dropping the readiness wait, which would let the engine propose Running over a suspension it has not seen.

This touches the same module as #23274, which changes how the async engine waits for the observer. Whichever merges second needs a rebase.

## Rollout caveats

- `no-op: flows called directly, and entry points run with no API URL, take the same path as before`
- `watch: debug log "Flow run suspension observer exited with an exception". The observer now runs during flow loading, so a rise points at an early start that fails`
- `rollback: revert this PR; no settings or stored data change`

title: docs: fix dead and chained redirects, CLI page titles and stale links
body:
Fixes the docs-side errors from the Nov 2026 SEMrush crawl of `www.prefect.io/docs`.

## What changed

**`docs/docs.json` redirects**
- 86 redirects pointed at a page that no longer exists (18 distinct dead targets, e.g. `/v3/develop/task-caching` → `/v3/how-to-guides/workflows/cache-workflow-results`) or at another redirect (e.g. `/latest/concepts/flows` → `/v3/develop/write-flows` → `/v3/how-to-guides/workflows/write-and-run`). Each now points at its final page, checked against the live site.
- New rules for URLs that 404 today: `/v3/concepts/logs`, `/v3/automate/incidents`, `/v3/deploy/control-plane/hybrid-architecture`, `/v3/integrations`, `/v3/how-to-guides/workflows/cache-workflow-results`, `/ui/notifications`, and the `/3.0rc` prefix.
- Redirects to `/v3/api-ref/python` and `/v3/api-ref/rest-api/server/flows` are left alone: those are nav groups that land on their first page.

**CLI reference (`docs/v3/api-ref/cli/*`, `scripts/templates/docs_template.jinja`)**
- Pages had `title: " "`, so they rendered an empty `<title>` and a `BreadcrumbList` item with no name (26 structured-data errors). The title is now the command name and the duplicate H1 is dropped, in the 40 pages and in the generator template.

**Broken image**
- `integrations/prefect-aws/ecs-worker/manual-deployment`: the work pool screenshot used `src={"/images/..."}`, which skips the `/docs` base path and 404s. It now uses a plain string like the other images.

**Stale links**
- Integration pages, release notes and five docstrings linked to `/docs/latest/...` or `/docs/3.0/...` URLs, and to the `prefect.io` apex. They now link straight to the live page. The matching generated API reference pages are updated by hand to match the docstrings.

## Judgment calls worth a look
- There is no incidents page any more, so incidents URLs go to `/v3/concepts/automations`.
- `/v3/deploy/control-plane/hybrid-architecture` goes to `/v3/concepts/workers`.
- The retired big-data and visualize-flow-structure pages go to `/v3/concepts/flows`.

## Not verified
- I did not run `scripts/generate_cli_docs.py`; the template edit was made to produce the same output as the hand-edited pages.
- No Mintlify preview build was run locally.

## Not in this PR
- Duplicate `<title>` tags across the generated Python API reference (402 pages share titles like `events - Prefect`) and duplicate meta descriptions on a few REST API pages. Both need generator or OpenAPI changes.

title: Keep flow run state change events within the related resource maximum
body:
closes #19064

this PR keeps the server's flow run state change events within `PREFECT_SERVER_EVENTS_MAXIMUM_RELATED_RESOURCES`. `flow_run_state_change_event` relates one `prefect.tag.*` resource per tag of the run, its flow and its deployment, besides the flow, deployment, work queue, work pool, parent task run and creator. Once that passed the maximum (100 by default), the `Event` failed validation and every state change of the run returned 500, starting with `create_flow_run_from_deployment`.

`_flow_run_related_resources_from_orm` now leaves out the tags that don't fit and logs a warning, the server-side counterpart of #22835. Tags come after the run's other resources and the creator is added after the cut, so only tags are dropped unless the maximum is set below the number of those resources. The tags stored on the deployment and the flow run don't change. The tradeoff is that an automation matching a dropped tag doesn't see it on these events; the flow run events reference now says so.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `test_instrumenting_a_flow_run_with_more_tags_than_an_event_can_relate` fails on `main` with `ValidationError: The maximum number of related resources is 5` and passes with this change.
- Ran here: `tests/server/orchestration/test_flow_run_instrumentation_policies.py` (37 passed on SQLite), pre-commit on the changed files, and pyright (`pyrightconfig-ci.json`) on the changed Python files. Postgres and the rest of the suite are left to CI.
- Out of scope: client-side events that also relate one resource per tag (worker and flow engine events, the runner's `prefect.runner.cancelled-flow-run`) still go past the maximum with that many tags.

</details>

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jsdom/jsdom (jsdom)</summary>

### [`v31.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/jsdom/jsdom/releases/tag/v31.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jsdom/jsdom/compare/v30.1.3...v31.0.0)

#### Breaking changes

- Changed the optional canvas and image decoding backend from `canvas` to `@napi-rs/canvas`. Install `@napi-rs/canvas` v1.0.13 or later in the v1.x series alongside jsdom; installing `canvas` alone no longer enables this support. The new backend provides prebuilt Skia binaries on supported platforms, and rendering and encoded image bytes can differ. Projects using native canvas objects or custom font registration should follow the [canvas migration guidance](https://redirect.github.com/jsdom/jsdom/blob/v31.0.0/README.md#canvas-support). Added WebP serialization through `canvas.toDataURL()` and `canvas.toBlob()`. Fixed image loading to wait for decoding before firing `load`, discard obsolete source requests, avoid refetching when dimensions change, and prevent failed images from drawing stale contents. Fixed canvas context and serialization behavior, including unsupported context types, read-only `ctx.canvas`, image-drawing exceptions, MIME type and quality normalization, and asynchronous `null` results from `canvas.toBlob()` for empty canvases or encoding failures. ([@​Brooooooklyn](https://redirect.github.com/Brooooooklyn))
- Changed CSS parsing, selector matching, and computed styles to use a new integrated implementation, with substantially expanded support and faster selector queries and repeated style reads. This includes cascade layers, nesting, `@scope`, custom-property substitution and registration through `@property` and `CSS.registerProperty()`, typed `attr()`, conditional `if()`, shadow-tree styling with `:host`, `::slotted()`, and `::part()`, pseudo-element computed styles, and constructable stylesheets with `document.adoptedStyleSheets` and `shadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets`. Fixed numerous cascade, shorthand, serialization, and default-style issues; computed declarations now stay live across DOM and stylesheet changes. CSS serialization and computed values can differ from previous releases.
- Changed HTML and XML parsing to pause at blocking scripts until their required resources are ready. The `JSDOM` constructor, `JSDOM.fromURL()`, and `JSDOM.fromFile()` can now return partially parsed documents. Wait for `DOMContentLoaded` for the finished tree, or the window's `l

### Release Notes

<summary>astral-sh/uv (ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv)</summary>

### [`v0.13.8`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0138)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/compare/0.13.7...0.13.8)

Released on 2026-11-12.

##### Python

- Add CPython 3.16.0a2 ([#​23211](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23211))
- Update managed CPython 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, and 3.15 builds to include pip 26.3, zlib 1.4, and Expat 2.10.0 ([#​23211](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23211))
- Update GraalPy 3.13.0 to build 25.5.5 ([#​23088](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23088))

##### Preview features

- Install wheel variants from local paths, direct URLs, and Git repositories in platform-specific resolutions ([#​22720](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22720), [#​22722](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22722), [#​22724](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22724))
- Detect x86-64 microarchitecture levels and AArch64 architecture versions when selecting wheel variants ([#​22832](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22832), [#​22949](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22949))
- Detect Google TPUs up when selecting wheel variants ([#​23066](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23066), [#​23121](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23121))
- Fix CPU detection for wheel variants on macOS with GraalPy ([#​23089](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23089))
- Report quarantined packages in `uv audit` when index URLs differ only in redacted query values ([#​23129](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23129))

##### Performance

- Avoid duplicate environment builds when concurrent `uvx` or `uv run --with` invocations need the same environment ([#​23123](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/23123))

More information #### Details ##### Summary Matching a selector that puts a general-sibling combinator inside `:has()`, such as `div:has(a ~ b)`, against untrusted HTML runs in O(n²) time in the number of sibling elements. A single small document with a few thousand siblings ties the process up for a minute of CPU, so an application that runs a fixed selector of this shape over HTML it doesn't control can be stalled by one request. `:has` is powerful, but much in the same way poor regular expressions can be crafted to cause catastrophic backtracking with greedy capturing, has can be used to create non-ideal scenarios that can cause large portions of the tree to be evaluated for one or many elements if not used thoughtfully. This behavior is not exclusive to Soup Sieve, but browsers make note of these potential performance issues themselves: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Selectors/:has#performance_considerations. With all of that said, there is room for improvements that can in some cases greatly improve performance. ##### Details `:has(a ~ b)` asks "does this element contain an `a` that has a later sibling `b`?". When no `b` is present, soupsieve can't short-circuit, and it answers the question with a nested scan: `match_future_child` walks every candidate `a` under the scope, and for each one the general-sibling branch of `match_future_relations` walks all of that `a`'s following siblings looking for `b`. With n siblings that is (n-1) + (n-2) + ... + 1 comparisons, i.e. O(n²). The adjacent-sibling form `div:has(a + b)` stays linear, because its branch checks only the one immediately following sibling per candidate.
