title: Don't count resuming a blocking pause as a new flow run attempt
body:
closes #23838

this PR makes resuming a blocking pause (`pause_flow_run()` / `wait_for_input` without `reschedule`) continue the current attempt instead of incrementing `run_count`, so a flow with `retries` that paused once is still retried when it fails.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Problem.** The resume endpoint proposes `Running()` directly from a blocking `Paused` state. `IncrementFlowRunCount` skips the increment only when `empirical_policy.resuming` is already set, but `HandleResumingPausedFlows` set that flag in `after_transition`, after the global transforms had already incremented the count. A `retries=1` flow that paused and resumed therefore reached its first failure with `run_count == 2`, and `RetryFailedFlows` accepted `Failed` instead of `AwaitingRetry`. The flag then stayed set on the `Running` run.

**Fix.**
- `IncrementFlowRunCount` no longer counts `Running` when the initial state is a blocking pause and the run has already started an attempt (`run_count > 0`). It sits under the same `api-version >= 0.8.4` gate as the existing `resuming` check, and since it's a global transform it also covers forced `Paused -> Running` transitions.
- `HandleResumingPausedFlows.after_transition` sets `resuming=True` only when the run leaves the pause for a scheduled state, which is the `suspend_flow_run` path (`Scheduled("Resuming")`) that consumes it on the next `Running`. Previously it also set the flag on `Running`, `Cancelling` and final states, where nothing consumed it; on a `Running` run it made the next attempt (for example after `AwaitingRetry` on SIGTERM) skip its increment.

Edge cases:
- A run forced into a blocking pause before it ever ran (`run_count == 0`) still counts its first `Running`.
- Reschedule-style pauses are unchanged.
- Clients with API version below 0.8.4 keep the old counting.

**Tests.**
- `TestResumeFlowrun::test_resuming_blocking_pause_keeps_run_count_and_retries`: pause, resume through `POST /flow_runs/{id}/resume`, then fail; `run_count` stays 1 and the failure is rejected into `AwaitingRetry`.
- `TestResumeFlowrun::test_attempt_after_resuming_blocking_pause_is_counted`: resumed blocking pause, then `AwaitingRetry`, `Pending`, `Running`; `run_count == 2` and `resuming` is cleared.
- `TestResumeFlowrun::test_resuming_blocking_pause_before_first_run_counts_the_run`: forced blocking pause before the first run, resume, then a second attempt; counts 1 then 2.
- `TestPausingRules` (global policy): blocking resume doesn't increment; `run_count == 0`, reschedule-style pause and API version 0.8.3 still increment.
- `TestResumingFlows::test_does_not_mark_flow_run_as_resuming_when_blocking_pause_resumes`; `test_marks_flow_run_as_resuming_upon_leaving_paused_state` now uses the reschedule path (`Scheduled("Resuming")`), which is the case that sets the flag.
- `TestSetFlowRunState::test_pauses_fire_again_after_blocking_pause_is_rescheduled`: the expected count after two attempts changes from 3 to 2; the old value

title: Keep workers alive when reading the deployment fails before submission
body:
closes #23835

this PR stops errors from the pre-submission deployment check in `BaseWorker._submit_run` from crashing the worker, and releases the `--limit` slot when a run is cancelled because its deployment was deleted.

<details>

### Problem

`_submit_run` runs inside the worker's `_runs_task_group`. Since #17313 it calls `client.read_deployment()` before proposing `Pending`, and only catches `ObjectNotFound`. A 502/504, 401 or timeout on that request escapes the task, cancels the task group and the worker process exits (the same stack as #16977), taking every other run it supervises with it.

The `ObjectNotFound` branch cancels the run and returns without `_release_limit_slot`, so with `--limit N` every run whose deployment was deleted keeps a slot forever. After N of them the worker stops submitting.

### Changes

The deployment check moves into `_check_deployment_before_submission`, which returns whether the run can be submitted:

- `ObjectNotFound`: the run is cancelled as before. If the cancel request itself fails, the error is logged and the run stays `Scheduled`, so the next poll tries again.
- Any other error: logged on the flow run logger and the run stays `Scheduled` for the next poll. This is what the worker already does when proposing `Pending` fails (`_propose_pending_state`).

When the check returns `False`, `_submit_run` releases the limit slot and clears the submission bookkeeping. That cleanup now runs after the cancel request finishes. Before, the run was removed from `_submitting_flow_run_ids` before the cancel was sent, so a poll landing in between could pick it up again.

I kept the guard around the deployment check instead of wrapping all of `_submit_run` in `try/except`. After `_propose_pending_state` succeeds, the run is `Pending` and its slot can belong to `_submit_run_and_capture_errors`, so "release the slot and retry on the next poll" would be wrong there.

### Tests

Added to `tests/workers/test_base_worker.py`, all four fail on `main`:

- `test_worker_survives_error_reading_deployment_before_submission`: a 502 from `read_deployment` no longer escapes the worker context; the slot is released, `run()` is not called, and the run is still `Scheduled`.
- `test_worker_resubmits_run_after_error_reading_deployment`: once the API recovers, the next poll submits the same run.
- `test_worker_releases_limit_slot_when_deployment_was_deleted`: with `limit=1`, the cancelled run gives its slot back and the next healthy run is submitted.
- `test_worker_survives_error_cancelling_run_of_deleted_deployment`: if marking the orphaned run cancelled fails with a 502, the worker keeps running, the slot is released and the run stays `Scheduled`; the next poll cancels it.

`uv run pytest tests/workers` passes (270 passed, 1 skipped), and pre-commit is clean on the changed files.

### Not changed

`_cancel_run` has a similar shape (`read_flow_run` only handles `ObjectNotFound`). It is a different code path, so I left it for a separate chan

title: Keep row index in `INPUTS` cache key for zero-column DataFrames
body:
closes #23831

This PR changes the `INPUTS` DataFrame transform so that a DataFrame with no columns keeps its row index in the cache key.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The DataFrame transform in `cache_policies.py` reduces a frame to its column names and its column Series. Each Series carries the row index. A frame with no columns has no Series, so every zero-column frame becomes `([], [])`. Frames with different row counts or different `Index`/`MultiIndex` labels get the same key, and a task returns a stale cached result.

The fix:
- When the frame has no columns, the transform returns `(columns, [], df.index)`.
- When the frame has columns, the payload does not change. Existing cache keys for these frames stay the same.
- The new zero-column payload has three elements, so new keys do not match the old collided `([], [])` keys.

The transform is now a module-level `_stable_dataframe` function. It is still registered only when pandas is already imported.

Tests:
- Row count, `Index` label, and `MultiIndex` label changes cause a new execution. A copy of the same frame is a cache hit. A result persisted under the old collided key is not reused.
- The key for a frame with columns is the same as before.
- Keys for zero-column frames are stable across processes.

</details>

title: Fix flaky UI E2E tests reading stale default task run names
body:
This PR fixes a flaky test in the UI v2 E2E suite. The E2E helper `ui-v2/e2e/helpers/run_flows.py` could return a task run's default name before its custom name was saved.

Failing run on main: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/42663686114 (`runs-task-runs.spec.ts` › "displays task runs with name, state, and breadcrumb links")

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

The task engine creates a task run with a default name (`simple_task-488`) and renames it to the custom `task_run_name` afterwards (`_set_custom_task_run_name`). The server stores that rename asynchronously. `get_task_runs_for_flow` stopped polling as soon as *any* task run existed. That meant it could return the old default name, which never shows up in the UI. The test then waited for text that would never appear.

The failed run's trace confirms this: the helper returned `simple_task-488` and, on the retry, `simple_task-788`. The task-runs list on the page showed only renamed runs (`e2e-runs-tr-task-44d07dd2`, `e2e-runs-tr-task-8a884417`).

Fix: the helper already knows each scenario's custom names, since it sets them. `get_task_runs_for_flow` now takes `expected_names` and polls until all of those names come back from the API. If they never appear, it raises a `RuntimeError` instead of returning stale names, so setup fails with a clear error. The `parent-child` scenario now uses the same helper instead of its own polling loop, which only waited for a task run to exist.

</details>

Verification (local server + Vite dev server):
- All three scenarios (`simple-task`, `flow-with-tasks`, `parent-child`) return the custom names. An unknown flow run raises the new error.
- `npx playwright test e2e/runs/runs-task-runs.spec.ts e2e/flow-runs/task-run-detail.spec.ts --workers=1 --repeat-each=5` → 30 passed.
- `ruff format --check` passes. `ruff check` reports one BLE001 error on this file's existing `except Exception` line in `main()`, which this PR doesn't touch.

title: Document ClassVar annotations for custom block metadata
body:
Related to #17529

This PR documents how to type custom block metadata with `ClassVar`, as requested in the issue discussion. Plain `str` annotations can leave the block name and slug at their inherited defaults. The example shows the working annotations and their output, and notes that unannotated overrides also work.

<details>
<summary>Validation and scope</summary>

- Reproduced the plain-annotation behavior on main (`b0479c0`) with Pydantic 2.14.1.
- Executed all three runnable Python examples on the page, respecting its existing `notest` directives.
- Asserted that the new example returns the custom name and slug and that only `bucket` is a model field.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed.
- Vale: zero errors, warnings, or suggestions on the edited page.

This addresses the requested documentation workaround; it does not change the underlying Pydantic behavior or claim to resolve the runtime bug.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex drafted the documentation and ran the local checks.
</details>
author: ashutosh8021
diff:
--- docs/v3/advanced/custom-blocks.mdx (+24/-1)
@@ -132,6 +132,29 @@ Available metadata fields include:
 | `_description`     | Short description of block type. Defaults to docstring, if provided.                                                                         |
 | `_code_example`    | Short code snippet shown in UI for how to load/use block type. Defaults to first example provided in the docstring of the class, if provided. |
 
+These metadata attributes are class variables. If you add type annotations, use `ClassVar` to preserve that behavior:
+
+```python
+from typing import ClassVar
+
+from prefect.blocks.core import Block
+
+
+class StorageLocation(Block):
+    bucket: str
+
+    _block_type_name: ClassVar[str] = "Storage Location"
+    _block_type_slug: ClassVar[str] = "storage-location"
+
+
+location = StorageLocation(bucket="reports")
+print(location.get_block_type_name())  # Storage Location
+print(location.get_block_type_slug())  # storage-location
+```
+
+A plain annotation such as `_block_type_name: str = "Storage Location"` does not preserve the inherited class variable and can leave the metadata at its default value.
+You can also override these attributes without type annotations, for example `_block_type_name = "Storage Location"`.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pixijs-userland/pixi-viewport (pixi-viewport)</summary>

### [`v7.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pixijs-userland/pixi-viewport/releases/tag/7.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pixijs-userland/pixi-viewport/compare/6.0.3...7.0.0)

Tested with pixi.js v8.22. This release fixes many long-standing bugs. Some of those fixes change behavior that apps may rely on, so this is a major version.

Breaking changes:

- Built-in plugins always run in their default order (drag, pinch, wheel, follow, mouse-edges, edge-scroll, decelerate, animate, bounce, snap-zoom, clamp-zoom, snap, clamp), whatever order you add them in. Previously, each call moved that plugin to the end of a list shared by every viewport, so `viewport.clamp().drag()` ran drag after clamp. User plugins added with `viewport.plugins.add()` still go at the end unless you pass an index.
- `clamp()` with no options no longer clamps. `false` for `left`, `right`, `top`, or `bottom` now means "don't clamp this side" (it was treated as 0).
- `drag-start` and `drag-end` report the pointer's screen position in `screen`.

New:

- `viewport.edgeScroll()` scrolls when the mouse is near the screen edges, with `speed` in screen pixels per second. It replaces `mouseEdges()`, which is deprecated but unchanged.
- `drag({ disableOneFingerDrag: true })` ignores one-finger touch drags so the page can scroll.
- `clampZoom({ keepAspectRatio: false })` clamps one axis at a time, for zooming along a single axis.
- `wheel({ trackpadPinch: true, trackpadPinchSpeed: 2.5 })` speeds up trackpad pinch zooming without changing mouse wheel zooming. The default (`1`) keeps the current speed, which is slow for a pinch.
- `new Viewport({ ignoreWheelFromOtherElements: true })` ignores wheel events that bubble up from other elements, such as HTML overlays.
- A pixi object inside the viewport can call `stopPropagation()` on its `wheel` event to keep the viewport from zooming. With `passiveWheel: false`, the page doesn't scroll either.
- `getVisibleBounds()` takes an optional `Rectangle` to write into, and the default hit area no longer allocates a new one every frame.
- The event types (`DragEvent`, `MovedEvent`, `ZoomedEvent`, and others) are exported.
- A new demo site: a playground with presets and a live code panel, plus examples for embedding a viewport in a scrolling page and for overlays. The API docs are generated wi

title: fix parallel tasks failing when using kwargs
body:
<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://www.prefect.io/docs/contribute/index
-->

<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
<!-- Whether or not AI tools helped draft this PR, you are responsible for understanding the change, keeping it scoped, validating it locally, and explaining the approach. -->
<!-- Maintainers may close PRs that appear low-effort, likely AI-generated, and substantially far from the expected implementation. -->

Consider this example which raises an error:

```py
from prefect import flow, task


@task
def fetch_customer_ids():
    return [101, 102, 103]


@task
def sync_customer(**kwargs):
    customer_id = kwargs["customer_id"]
    destination = kwargs["destination"]

    return f"Synced customer {customer_id} to {destination}"


@flow
def nightly_customer_sync():
    customer_ids = fetch_customer_ids.submit()

    # Expected: one sync task per customer.
    # Actual: raises MappingMissingIterable.
    return sync_customer.map(
        customer_id=customer_ids,
        destination="salesforce",
    ).result()


nightly_customer_sync()
```

This happens because the top-level futures are resolved before expanding `kwargs`. There is no iterable to map over.

title: Preserve tuple and non-string key types in `hash_objects`
body:
closes #23817

This PR makes the JSON path of `hash_objects` keep the difference between tuples and lists, and between non-string dict keys and their string forms. Before this change, `task_input_hash` and the `Inputs` cache policy produced the same key for `(1, 2, 3)` and `[1, 2, 3]`, and for `{1: "a"}` and `{"1": "a"}`, so a task could return a stale cached result.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- A new helper, `_tag_json_lossy_types`, walks each arg and kwarg value and reports whether it found a tuple or a dict with a non-string key.
- If it finds neither, `hash_objects` hashes the untagged `(args, kwargs)` exactly as before. Hashes for JSON-native inputs (block schema checksums and most existing cache keys) do not change, including str-keyed dicts that happen to use the tag names.
- If it finds either, the tagged payload is hashed with a `\x00` prefix. JSON output can never start with that byte, so a tagged hash can't collide with an untagged one. Tagging works like this:
  - A tuple becomes `{"__tuple__": [...]}`.
  - A dict with a non-string key (`int`, `float`, `bool`, `None`) becomes `{"__dict__": [[key, value], ...]}`, sorted by each key's JSON encoding so insertion order doesn't matter.
  - Inside a tagged payload, a str-keyed dict whose only key is `__tuple__` or `__dict__` is escaped into the `__dict__` form, so real values can't collide with tags.
  - Other key types (for example tuple keys) raise `TypeError`, so the existing cloudpickle fallback still runs.
- Cache keys for inputs that contain tuples or non-string keys change, so those cached results miss once.
- `utilities/hashing.py` moves to `utilities/hashing/__init__.py` (same import path), with an `AGENTS.md` that documents these contracts, as `utilities/AGENTS.md` asks once a module gains invariants like these.
- Not in scope:
  - `JSONSerializer` round-trip behavior for `result_serializer="json"`, which the issue notes as a documented limitation.
  - Tuples nested inside Pydantic models or dataclasses. `prefect_json_object_encoder` dumps these in JSON mode, the same as on `main`.

Tests: unit tests in `tests/utilities/test_hashing.py` cover type distinctions, insertion-order independence, unchanged hashes for JSON-native inputs (including ones that use tag names), the fallback for unsupported keys, and self-referential containers. An end-to-end test in `tests/test_tasks.py` runs a `task_input_hash` task with a tuple and then a list.

CI note: `tests/server/schemas/test_schedules.py::TestIntervalScheduleDaylightSavingsTime::test_interval_schedule_always_has_the_right_offset` fails in the Python 3.13+ server jobs with `TimeZoneNotFoundError: 'US/Pacific'`. It fails the same way on other open PRs running on the `ubuntu-26.04` runner image and has nothing to do with this change.
</details>

+# hashing
+
+Stable hashing of strings, files, and arbitrary Python objects.
+
+## Purpose & Scope
+
+`stable_hash`, `file_hash`, and `hash_objects`. `hash_objects` produces the cache keys for `task_input_hash` and the `Inputs`/`FlowParameters` cache policies, and the checksums for block schemas (`Block._calculate_schema_checksum`).
+
+## Entry Points
+
+- `hash_objects(*args, hash_algo=..., raise_on_failure=False, **kwargs)` — hash via JSON (`JSONSerializer`, `sort_keys=True`), falling back to cloudpickle of the original objects when JSON fails.
+
+## Contracts
+
+- **Hashes of JSON-native inputs must not change.** Block schema checksums are persisted server-side and compared against client-computed values, so inputs made only of str-keyed dicts, lists, and scalars must keep serializing to the same JSON. +- **JSON-lossy types are tagged before serializing.** When a tuple or non-str-key dict is present, tuples become `{"__tuple__": [...]}` and dicts with non-str keys (`int`, `float`, `bool`, `None`) become `{"__dict__": [[key, value], ...]}`, sorted by each key's JSON encoding. The tagged JSON is hashed with a `\x00` prefix, which JSON output can never start with, so tagged hashes can't collide with untagged ones. Within a tagged payload, a str-keyed dict whose only key is `__tuple__` or `__dict__` is escaped into the `__dict__` form so real values can't collide with tags. +- Tagging only walks dicts, lists, and tuples. Containers nested inside objects handled by `prefect_json_object_encoder` (Pydantic models, dataclasses) are serialized by Pydantic in JSON mode and are not tagged.

+import hashlib
+import json
+from functools import partial
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Callable, Optional, Union
+
+import cloudpickle  # type: ignore  # no stubs available
+
+from prefect.exceptions import HashError
+from prefect.serializers import JSONSerializer
+
+_md5 = partial(hashlib.md5, usedforsecurity=False)
+
+_TUPLE_TAG = "__tuple__"
+_DICT_TAG = "__dict__"
+_JSON_KEY_TYPES = (str, int, float, bool, type(None))
+# JSON payloads always start with `[`, so prefixed tagged payloads can never
+# collide with untagged ones
+_TAGGED_PAYLOAD_PREFIX = b"\x00"
+
+
+def _tag_json_lossy_types(obj: Any) -> tuple[Any, bool]:
+    """
+    Recursively tag tuples and dicts with non-string keys so that values JSON would
+    otherwise conflate (e.g. `(1, 2)` and `[1, 2]`, `{1: "a"}` and `{"1": "a"}`)
+    serialize differently.
+
+    Returns the tagged value and whether any tuple or non-string-key dict was found.
+    """
+    if isinstance(obj, tuple):
+        items = [_tag_json_lossy_types(item) for item in obj]
+        return {_TUPLE_TAG: [item for item, _ in items]}, True
+    if isinstance(obj, list):
+        items = [_tag_json_lossy_types(item) for item in obj]
+        return [item for item, _ in items], any(lossy for _, lossy in items)
+    if isinstance(obj, dict):
+        if all(isinstance(key, str) for key in obj):
+            tagged = {key: _tag_json_lossy_types(value) for key, value in obj.items()}
+            lossy = any(lossy for _, lossy in tagged.values())
+            if len(obj) == 1 and next(iter(obj)) in (_TUPLE_TAG, _DICT_TAG):
+                # Escape dicts that look like tags so they can't collide with them
+                return {_DICT_TAG: [[key, v] for key, (v, _) in tagged.items()]}, lossy
+            return {key: v for key, (v, _) in tagged.items()}, lossy
+        for key in obj:
+            if not isinstance(key, _JSON_KEY_TYPES):
+                raise TypeError(
+                    f"keys must be str, int, float, bool or None, not {type(key).__name__}"
+                )
+        # Sorted by each key's JSON encoding so the result is independent of
+        # insertion order, matching `sort_keys=True` for string-keyed dicts
+        items = sorted(obj.items(), key=lambda item: json.dumps(item[0]))
+        return {
+            _DICT_TAG: [[key, _tag_json_lossy_types(value)[0]] for key, value in items]
+        }, True
+    return obj, False
+
+
+def stable_hash(*args: Union[str, bytes], hash_algo: Callable[..., Any] = _md5) -> str:
+    """Given some arguments, produces a stable 64-bit hash of their contents.
+
+    Supports bytes and strings. Strings will be UTF-8 encoded.
+
+    Args:
+        *args: Items to include in the hash.
+        hash_algo: Hash algorithm from hashlib to use.
+
+    Returns:
+        A hex hash.
+    """
+    h = hash_algo()
+    for a in args:
+        if isinstance(a, str):
+            a = a.encode()
+        h.update(a)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def file_hash(path: str, hash_algo: Callable[..., Any] = _md5) -> str:
+    """Given a path to a file, produces a stable hash of the file contents.
+
+    Args:
+        path (str): the path to a file
+        hash_algo: Hash algorithm from hashlib to use.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: a hash of the file contents
+    """
+    contents = Path(path).read_bytes()
+    return stable_hash(contents, hash_algo=hash_algo)
+
+
+def hash_objects(
+    *args: Any,
+    hash_algo: Callable[..., Any] = _md5,
+    raise_on_failure: bool = False,
+    **kwargs: Any,
+) -> Optional[str]:
+    """
+    Attempt to hash objects by dumping to JSON or serializing with cloudpickle.
+
+    Args:
+        *args: Positional arguments to hash
+        hash_algo: Hash algorithm to use
+        raise_on_failure: If True, raise exceptions instead of returning None
+        **kwargs: Keyword arguments to hash
+
+    Returns:
+        A hash string or None if hashing failed
+
+    Raises:
+        HashError: If objects cannot be hashed and raise_on_failure is True
+    """
+    json_error = None
+    pickle_error = None
+
+    try:
+        serializer = JSONSerializer(dumps_kwargs={"sort_keys": True})
+        tagged_args = [_tag_json_lossy_types(arg) for arg in args]
+        tagged_kwargs = {
+            key: _tag_json_lossy_types(value) for key, value in kwargs.items()
+        }
+        lossy = any(lossy for _, lossy in tagged_args) or any(
+            lossy for _, lossy in tagged_kwargs.values()
+        )
+        if not lossy:
+            # Keep hashes for JSON-native inputs identical to previous releases
+            return stable_hash(serializer.dumps((args, kwargs)), hash_algo=hash_algo)
+        payload = (
+            [arg for arg, _ in tagged_args],
+            {key: value for key, (value, _) in tagged_kwargs.items()},
+        )
+        return stable_hash(
+            _TAGGED_PAYLOAD_PREFIX, serializer.dumps(payload), hash_algo=hash_algo
+        )
+    except Exception as e:
+        json_error = str(e)
+
+    try:
+        return stable_hash(cloudpickle.dumps((args, kwargs)), hash_algo=hash_algo)  # type: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]
+    except Exception as e:
+        pickle_error = str(e)
+
+    if raise_on_failure:
+        msg = (
+            "Unable to create hash - objects could not be serialized.\n"
+            f"  JSON error: {json_error}\n"
+            f"  Pickle error: {pickle_error}"
+        )
+        raise HashError(msg)
+
+    return None

title: Raise when `RemoteFileSystem.put_directory(overwrite=False)` hits an existing file
body:
closes #23815

This PR makes `RemoteFileSystem.put_directory` and `aput_directory` raise `FileExistsError` when `overwrite=False` and a file already exists at the destination. Before this change, the code called `put_file` without arguments when `overwrite=False`. That call always overwrites the file.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- A new private helper `RemoteFileSystem._put_file` holds the upload logic for the sync and async methods.
- When `overwrite=False`, the helper calls `self.filesystem.exists()` before the upload. This check works with all fsspec backends. The `mode="error"` value that the issue suggests does not exist in fsspec (fsspec uses `mode="create"`), and backends such as `adlfs` do not use `mode`.
- The `SMB` block passed `overwrite=False` only as a workaround: fsspec's SMB implementation sends extra keyword arguments to `smbclient.open_file`, which does not accept `overwrite` (refer to 552e1b6f92). With this fix, that workaround would make SMB redeploys fail. Thus `SMB` now uses the default `overwrite=True`, and `_put_file` does not send the `overwrite` keyword for `smb://` paths. This is the same `smb://` special case that `awrite_path` has.
- Tests: memory filesystem tests for the sync and async paths, which fail on `main`. Also an `SMB` test (it runs only when `fsspec[smb]` is installed) which makes sure that `put_directory` uploads without `overwrite` and does not raise.

</details>

title: Skip fetching a pinned commit that the clone already contains
body:
closes #23813

This PR changes `GitRepository._clone_repo` so that it only runs `git fetch origin <commit_sha>` when the commit is not in the new clone.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Before this change, `_clone_repo` always ran `git fetch origin <commit_sha>` after `git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout`. Git cannot fetch an abbreviated SHA from a remote. Thus a short `commit_sha` (for example `1234567`) failed with exit code 128.

The clone usually contains the commit already. Now `_clone_repo` uses the existing `_has_commit()` check (`git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}`), which also resolves short SHAs. It fetches only when the commit is missing. This is the same check that `pull_code` uses for an existing checkout.

Tests:
- `test_clone_repo_with_commit_sha` is now parametrized: no fetch when the commit is present, fetch when it is missing.
- New `test_pull_code_clones_and_checks_out_short_sha` clones a real local repository with a 7-character SHA and checks the checked-out commit. This test fails without the fix.

</details>

title: Keep `Annotated[T, Field(description=...)]` descriptions in flow parameter schemas
body:
closes #23808

this PR makes the flow parameter schema take a parameter's description from the `Field`s in its `Annotated` type, merged the way pydantic merges them, as it already does for a `Field` default since #19281, instead of passing `description=None`, which overrode the description in `Annotated` when pydantic merged the two.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `process_v2_params` only looked at a `Field` default and the docstring, so for `x: Annotated[int, Field(description=...)]` it built the field with `description=None`. Pydantic merges that field with the `Field` in `Annotated`, the explicit `None` wins, and the description never reached the schema or the run form in the UI.
- The description now comes from the `Field` default, then from the `Field`s in `Annotated`, then from the docstring. Before, a docstring entry beat the `Annotated` description while it lost to a `Field` default.
- The `Field`s in `Annotated` are merged with `FieldInfo.from_annotation`, so a later `Field` wins as in a pydantic model, also when it sets `description=None` or `""` to clear an earlier description (e.g. one from a type alias). `FieldInfo.merge_field_infos` is deprecated since pydantic 2.12; `from_annotation` gives the same description as a model field on pydantic 2.10.1, 2.11.10, 2.12.5, 2.13.5 and 2.14.1.
- Kept from #19281: an empty description falls back to the docstring, and a `Field` default only takes over when it has a description.
- If pydantic can't merge the `Field`s in `Annotated` (e.g. `default` with `default_factory`), no description is taken from them, so `generate_parameter_schema` still falls back to `Any` for that parameter instead of raising.
- The lookup runs after the `*args`/`**kwargs` wrapping, so a `Field` in their annotation keeps describing each value (`items`/`additionalProperties`), as before.
- Unchanged: `title` (always the parameter name, as with a `Field` default), the other `Field` settings in `Annotated` (`ge`, `examples`, `json_schema_extra` already reached the schema), and `process_v1_params`, which #19281 didn't touch either.
- Repro and context: #23808; review follow-up in the comments below.

Tests:
- new `test_process_v2_params_with_annotated_fieldinfo` and `test_process_v2_params_with_annotated_fieldinfo_uses_last_description` in `tests/_internal/schemas/test_v2_schema.py`, next to the tests from #19281, and `test_flow_with_annotated_field_description` in `tests/utilities/test_callables.py`, which checks the whole schema: the `Annotated` description, the docstring when `Annotated` has none (with `ge` kept) or when a later `Field` clears it, and a `Field` default winning over `Annotated`; all 3 fail on `main` and pass with this change
- new `test_process_v2_params_with_annotated_fieldinfo_later_field_clears_description` (a later `Field` with `None` or `""`, with and without a docstring), which failed on the first commit of this PR, and `test_flow_with_annotated_fields_pydantic_cannot_merge` for the `Any` fal

title: Show the script error from `prefect deploy` and `prefect flow serve` for flows that fail to load
body:
closes #23806

this PR makes `prefect deploy` and `prefect flow serve` handle `ScriptError` the way `prefect block register` does: print the script's traceback and exit with the script error, instead of letting it reach `with_cli_exception_handling`, which prints Prefect's own frames and ends with `An exception occurred.`. Follow-up to #23773.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- Since #23773, a script that fails to import behind a non-`def` entrypoint raises its `ScriptError` from `load_flow_from_entrypoint` instead of `ValueError: Could not find object`. Neither command caught it, so the output became the chained traceback plus `An exception occurred.`. A syntax error in the flow file already went that way, with a regular `def` entrypoint too.
- The traceback goes through `print_verbatim` because it carries the user's source lines, which `console.print` would parse as Rich markup; the message goes through `exit_with_error`, which already disables markup.
- `exception_traceback(exc.user_exc)` is the same call `prefect block register` makes, so it also keeps the two `<frozen importlib...>` frames from `exec_module`; I left `ScriptError`'s trimming alone to keep this to the CLI.
- `ValueError` and `MissingFlowError` handling is unchanged, and a `def` entrypoint with a missing dependency still deploys with the placeholder flow.
- Repro and context: #23806

Tests:
- new `test_deploy_reports_script_error_for_non_def_entrypoint` in `tests/cli/test_deploy.py` and `test_flow_serve_cli_reports_script_error_for_non_def_entrypoint` in `tests/cli/test_flow.py` run the commands on an entrypoint assigned from `with_options()` in a script that fails to import; both fail on `main` (the `ScriptError` propagates) and pass with this change
- passing locally (Linux, Python 3.12): `tests/cli/test_deploy.py` (221 passed), `tests/cli/test_flow.py` (13 passed), `tests/cli/test_utilities.py` (8 passed) and `tests/test_flows.py` (415 passed, 11 skipped, 2 xfailed)

</details>

title: Fix broken examples in the store-flow-code guide
body:
Fixes six defects across four examples in `docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployments/store-flow-code.mdx` that make them fail when copied:

- **Bitbucket, `bb_private_repo_credentials_block.py`**: `flow.from_source(source=source, ...)` passes a name that is never defined; the block is assigned to `github_repo` a few lines up. Changed to `source=github_repo`, as the sibling `bb_private_repo_secret_block.py` already does. pyflakes on the old snippet: `undefined name 'source'`.
- **S3, `s3_block.py`**: missing comma after `work_pool_name="my-work-pool"` before `job_variables=...`. The old snippet fails to parse (`SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?`).
- **GCS, `gcs_block.py`**: imports `GCSBucket` from `prefect_gcp`, but the package exports `GcsBucket` (`src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/__init__.py:3`, class at `cloud_storage.py:1068`); `GCSBucket` appears nowhere in the repo, so the snippet fails at its first import. Renamed in the import, the `.load` call and the commented constructor.
- **GCS `prefect.yaml`**, three fixes in one block:
  - `prefect_gcp.deployment.steps.push_to_gcs` / `pull_from_gcs` -> `prefect_gcp.deployments.steps...`. The module is `prefect_gcp/deployments/steps.py` (`push_to_gcs` at line 34, `pull_from_gcs` at line 139); there is no `prefect_gcp.deployment` package.
  - The pull step read `folder: '{{ pull_code.folder }}'`, its own output, inside itself. Changed to `'{{ push_code.folder }}'`, the value `push_to_gcs` returns (`steps.py:133-136`) and the same reference the S3 example uses.
  - The fields under `- name: my-gcs-deployment` were indented two spaces deeper than `name`, so the block was not valid YAML (`mapping values are not allowed here`). Re-indented to match the S3 block.

Docs only; no behavior change, so no tests or issue (small fix).

How it was checked: extracted each snippet from the old and new file. Old Bitbucket snippet: pyflakes reports the undefined name; new one is clean. Old S3 snippet: `ast.parse` raises the SyntaxError above; new one parses. The `GcsBucket` name was checked against the package source (prefect-gcp was not installed). Old GCS YAML block: `yaml.safe_load` raises the error above; new one loads, with `version`, `tags` and the rest under the deployment. The docs site was not built locally.

title: Reserve hosted test API server port before starting uvicorn
body:
this PR fixes a port race in the `hosted_api_server` test fixture behind [this main failure](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/42274482367) (group 15, py3.12/postgres:14: 22 failed + 1 error).

On Unix, the fixture now binds a `127.0.0.1:0` socket itself and passes it to uvicorn with `--fd` (via `pass_fds`). Windows keeps the existing `--host/--port` path.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

Before this change, `hosted_api_server` got a port from `unused_tcp_port_factory()`, which binds port 0 and then closes the socket right away. uvicorn only bound that port later, after the subprocess had started. That port is reserved only within one process, so a second xdist worker starting its own hosted server could be given the same port in between. When that happened:

- this worker's uvicorn failed to bind and exited;
- the fixture's `/health` loop got a 200 from the **other worker's** server, so it yielded that URL anyway.

From then on, every hosted-API request from the affected worker went to another worker's database (`prefect_tests_gwN`), while in-process `session` and ephemeral clients still used its own. That other worker's `clear_db` and migration tests wiped and disconnected data in the middle of these tests. That fits the CI evidence:

- every failure was on a single worker (`gw2`), starting at the same point and running to the end of the session;
- hosted-API calls failed with 404s and `ObjectNotFound` for objects that had just been created;
- Postgres logged FK violations (`flow_run.flow_id`, `worker.work_pool_id`, `deployment.flow_id`) and duplicate `uq_work_pool__name`;
- `bulk_delete` deleted 0 of the rows the test had inserted through `session`;
- the hosted server's connection was killed by `pg_terminate_backend` from a migration test, and at the end `DROP DATABASE prefect_tests_gw0` reported another session still connected.

When the fixture binds the socket itself and hands it to uvicorn, nothing else can take the port between choosing it and serving on it.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Testing</summary>

- New test `TestHostedApiServerPortAllocation::test_hosted_api_server_is_not_shadowed_by_server_on_probed_port`. It starts a decoy HTTP server on the port the factory returns, runs the real fixture, and checks that `/api/hello` returns the Prefect response. Without the fix it fails (`assert 'other' == '👋'`). With the fix it passed 20/20 runs.
- `tests/testing/test_fixtures.py -n 4`: passed.
- Hosted-API heavy modules (`test_bulk_operations.py`, `test_prefect_client.py`) with `-n 6 --dist worksteal`: 295 passed.
- pre-commit (ruff check/format, codespell) passes on the changed files.
</details>

title: docs: document form button type pitfall in ui-v2 components AGENTS.md
body:
this PR adds a one-line pitfall to the Forms section of `ui-v2/src/components/AGENTS.md`: non-submit `Button`s inside a form must set `type="button"`, because `@/components/ui/button` renders a native `<button>` with no default `type`, so clicking one submits the enclosing form.

This bug has now shipped and been fixed twice in ui-v2: #22325 (schema form "Add item" button) and #23776 (automation trigger "Format" button submitting the wizard).

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `ui-v2/src/components/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "Non-submit `Button`s inside a form (format, add item, etc.) must set `type="button"` — `@/components/ui/button` renders a native `<button>` with no default `type`, so clicks submit the enclosing form (including whole wizard forms)"
Non-obvious evidence: the shared `Button` (`ui/button/button.tsx`) renders `asChild ? Slot : "button"` without a `type` default, so it reads like a plain action button. The bug was reintroduced in two separate components (#22325, #23776), each time only caught after it shipped.
Cross-cutting scope: any component in `ui-v2/src/components` that puts auxiliary buttons (format, add/remove item, toggles) inside a `react-hook-form` `Form`, including `Stepper` wizards and schema forms.
Why not code comment/docstring: the failure happens at call sites spread across many components, not in `Button` itself. The Forms section of the components AGENTS.md is where agents look before building a form.
Durability: this follows from how HTML forms and the shared `Button` work, not from either triggering fix, so it holds for as long as forms use this `Button`.
Counter-evidence checked: `ui-v2/AGENTS.md`, `ui-v2/src/components/AGENTS.md` (Forms and Schema Forms sections) and the other ui-v2 AGENTS.md files have no guidance on button `type`. `ui/button/button.tsx` has no comment or default about it. About 39 call sites already set `type="button"`, but nothing says it is required.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Files changed in the triggering push</summary>

title: Document reserved event name prefixes
body:
The events docs say event names can be anything, and their examples use `prefect-cloud.` names. Nothing on those pages says the `prefect.` and `prefect-cloud.` prefixes are reserved for events Prefect emits, or that Prefect Cloud drops client-sent events named `prefect-cloud.*` without returning an error. A custom event that uses that prefix disappears with no signal to the sender.

This states the rule once, in the events API reference's namespace conventions, and points to it from the events concept page and the custom event grammar guide. The concept page's note repeats the drop behavior because that page is where people choose event names.

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

The API reference already marked both namespaces as reserved, but the concept and guide pages, where people choose event names, said names were free-form. The drop behavior was undocumented anywhere.

title: Fix `visit_collection` for `defaultdict`, `Counter`, `deque`, and `frozenset`
body:
closes #23793

this PR fixes how `visit_collection` handles several stdlib containers, so task futures nested in them are resolved and recorded as upstream `task_inputs`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- **`defaultdict`**: rebuilt with `type(mapping)(mapping.default_factory, items)`. Before, the list of pairs was passed as the default factory, which raised `TypeError: first argument must be callable or None`.
- **`Counter`**: rebuilt with `type(mapping)(dict(items))`. Before, `Counter(items)` counted the `(key, value)` tuples, so the data was silently wrong.
- **`deque` / `frozenset`**: now handled in the sequence branch, so their items are visited. A rebuilt `deque` keeps its `maxlen`.
- Collections are still returned unchanged (same object) when nothing inside them changed.
- Updated the "Supported types" list in the docstring.

Tests:
- Added `frozenset`, `deque`, `defaultdict`, and `Counter` cases to the existing parametrized visit/transform tests, plus tests that `default_factory`, the `Counter` type, and `deque.maxlen` are preserved, and that the same object comes back when nothing changed. The new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- `test_task_inputs_populated_with_upstream_futures_in_stdlib_containers` checks that futures inside a `defaultdict` and a `deque` are resolved and appear in `task_run.task_inputs`.
</details>

title: fix(prefect-redis): keep messages published while a publisher flush is in flight
body:
closes #23791

this PR fixes `prefect_redis.messaging.Publisher._publish_current_batch` silently dropping a message that `publish_data` appends while a flush is awaiting `Cache.without_duplicates`. The flush now takes ownership of the batch (`batch, self._batch = self._batch, []`) before its first `await`, and flushes are serialized with an `asyncio.Lock` so the periodic, `batch_size`-triggered, and `__aexit__` flushes can't interleave and reorder messages.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- Previously the flush passed `self._batch` by reference to `without_duplicates` and then called `self._batch.clear()` after the round-trip, discarding anything appended in the meantime. `create_event_publisher()` always deduplicates by `id`, so every event on `/api/events/in` was exposed to this during normal Redis round-trips.
- If `without_duplicates` raises, the swapped-out batch is put back at the front of `self._batch`, preserving the existing behavior where the batch is retained (and `__aexit__` forgets its dedup markers on failure).
- Behavior on `xadd` failure is unchanged (dedup markers for `to_publish` are forgotten and the error propagates). Re-queueing on publish failure / periodic task resilience during Redis outages is tracked separately in #22478 and intentionally left out of scope.
- Regression test pauses *after* the dedup pipeline has read the batch (inside the Redis call, as the issue notes is required), publishes a second message, then releases. It fails on `main` (`['first']`) and passes here (`['first', 'second']`); its exact ordering assertion also covers the flush lock.
- Added a test that a failed dedup check retains the batch for the next flush.

Validation (Redis 7.4 on `localhost:6379`):
- Repro from the issue: `published 2 messages, stream has 1: ['first']` before, `stream has 2: ['first', 'second']` after.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -n4` in `src/integrations/prefect-redis`: 255 passed, 3 skipped.
- `pre-commit run` on changed files passes.

</details>

title: fix parent transactions committing after child commit failure
body:
<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://www.prefect.io/docs/contribute/index
-->

<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
<!-- Whether or not AI tools helped draft this PR, you are responsible for understanding the change, keeping it scoped, validating it locally, and explaining the approach. -->
<!-- Maintainers may close PRs that appear low-effort, likely AI-generated, and substantially far from the expected implementation. -->


  The customer has no invoice, but rerunning the workflow reports that billing was already processed.

```py
from pathlib import Path
from prefect import flow, task
from prefect.transactions import transaction

INVOICE = Path("invoice-2026-11-06.txt")


@task(persist_result=False)
def create_invoice():
    INVOICE.write_text("Customer: Acme\nAmount due: $100\n")
    print("Invoice created")


@create_invoice.on_commit
def notify_billing(txn):
    # Simulate the billing service being unavailable.
    raise ConnectionError("Billing service unavailable")


@create_invoice.on_rollback
def delete_invoice(txn):
    INVOICE.unlink()
    print("Invoice deleted during rollback")


@flow
def daily_billing():
    with transaction(key="daily-billing-2026-11-06") as txn:
        if txn.is_committed():
            print("Billing already processed; skipping")
            return

        create_invoice()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    daily_billing()
    print(f"Invoice exists: {INVOICE.exists()}")

    daily_billing()
    print(f"Invoice exists: {INVOICE.exists()}")
```

Output:
```
  Invoice created
  ... ConnectionError: Billing service unavailable
  Invoice deleted during rollback
  ... Finished in state Completed()
  Invoice exists: False

  Billing already processed; skipping
  ... Finished in state Completed()
  Invoice exists: False
```

Fixed by allowing the parent to roll back if a child fails to commit.

title: Bump oauthlib from 4.0.0 to 4.0.1
body:
Bumps [oauthlib](https://github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib) from 4.0.0 to 4.0.1.
Release notes

Sourced from oauthlib's releases.

4.0.1

Security

  • CVE-2026-49272 / GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc: The device code flow token endpoint did not validate the device_code parameter. A request with a known client_id and a bogus device_code could obtain a bearer token. DeviceCodeGrant.validate_token_request now calls DeviceCodeGrant.validate_device_code(), which rejects missing or unknown device codes (invalid_request / invalid_grant) and delegates the code's authorization status to the new RequestValidator.validate_device_code() hook, per RFC 8628 Section 3.5. (cherry-picked from #954)

Upgrade note for device flow integrators

Custom RequestValidator implementations using the device flow must now implement validate_device_code(client_id, code, request). Return one of the DeviceCodeGrant.DEVICE_CODE_* statuses for known codes, or None for an unknown code. When returning AUTHORIZED, the validator must also populate request.user and request.scopes from the stored authorization.

title: Fix `RemoteFileSystem` uploading all files when ignore file excludes everything
body:
closes #23785

This PR makes `RemoteFileSystem.put_directory()` and `aput_directory()` upload zero files when the ignore file excludes every entry.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Before this change, both methods checked the truthiness of `included_files`. When `filter_files()` returned an empty set, the methods skipped the exclusion check and uploaded all files. This is the same result as when no ignore file is given.

Now both methods check `included_files is not None`. An empty set excludes all files. `None` (no ignore file) still uploads all files.

`LocalFileSystem` is not affected, because its ignore function does not check truthiness.

Tests: a new test in `tests/test_filesystems.py` runs in sync and async modes. It writes `*` to the ignore file and asserts that the upload count is `0` and that the destination is empty. The test fails before the fix and passes after it.
</details>

title: Stop flow run heartbeats before proposing a terminal state
body:
The heartbeat thread checked `flow_run.state` before each heartbeat, but the engine updates that state only after the server answers its terminal state proposal, and the server timestamps the terminal state when it accepts it. A heartbeat that came due during that round trip occurred after `Completed`, so the zombie flow automation (`after: prefect.flow-run.heartbeat`, `expect: prefect.flow-run.*`) waited for an event that never came and crashed or alerted on a run that had finished normally. Both timelines in #21932 show a heartbeat 25 ms and 148 ms after `Completed`. The server change in #23445 could not prevent this, because the trigger evaluated those events correctly. Now `set_state` stops the heartbeat thread before it proposes a terminal state, and the thread checks for a stop and emits under one lock, so no heartbeat is mid-emit when the proposal goes out.

The heartbeat thread also waits on its stop event instead of sleeping in one-second steps. Stopping it, and the sync engine's join on exit, could otherwise wait up to a second at the end of every flow run.

Closes #21932

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

- The stop lives in `set_state` so it covers every terminal proposal made while heartbeats run. In practice that is `handle_success`, including generator flows. `handle_exception`, `handle_timeout`, and `handle_crash` already run after the heartbeat context exits.
- `set_state` takes a lock instead of joining the thread, because the async engine avoids blocking its event loop on the thread. Taking the lock waits for at most one `emit_event` call, which only queues the event.
- Exiting the heartbeat context now also takes the lock, so the async engine, which does not join the thread, cannot have a heartbeat mid-emit when it proposes `Failed` after an exception.
- When a returned `Failed` state is retried, heartbeats stop for the retry delay and restart when the engine enters the next attempt. A raised exception already behaved this way.
- The fix is client-side, so it reaches users when they upgrade `prefect` on the machines that run flows. Heartbeats use the client's clock and the terminal state uses the server's, so clock skew between the two can still order them wrong. This change closes the round-trip window, which is much wider than typical NTP skew.
- The tests set a 50 ms heartbeat interval and hold the terminal state's response until the heartbeat thread emits, or for 250 ms. Without the stop in `set_state`, both the sync and async tests fail with a heartbeat about 40 ms after `Completed`. With it, no heartbeat can be emitted during the hold, so the passing result doesn't depend on timing.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

A user reported in #21932 that the zombie flow automation still fired on completed runs after #23445. Their timeline, and the original reporter's, both show the last heartbeat occurring after `Completed`, which the server-side fix doesn't cover. Reading the engine showed why the

title: Log pull step failures to the API in the workspace resolver
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23782

This PR makes the workspace resolver send pull step failures to the flow run logs in the API.

#22432 sent pull step progress logs to the API, but a failed step only wrote its error to stderr. In short-lived infrastructure (for example, a Kubernetes pod), stderr is lost, so the flow run logs showed `Executing deployment step: git_clone` with no cause.

`prepare_workspace` now catches `StepExecutionError` from `run_steps`, logs the cause message (for example, the `git_clone` exit code and git stderr tail) at `ERROR` level with the flow run logger, and raises the error again. This is the same behavior as `load_flow_from_flow_run` in `flows.py`. The structured error payload and stderr traceback do not change.

- `test_pull_step_logs_are_sent_to_the_api_when_a_step_fails` now asserts that the step's error message is in the API logs at `ERROR` level. This assertion failed before the fix.

title: fix: keep automations loaded while the triggers service reloads them
body:
closes #23777

This PR makes the triggers service keep its automation cache full while it reloads automations from the database.

Before this change, `reconcile_automations` cleared the cache and then awaited the database read in `load_automations`. `automation_changed` did the same for one automation on `automation__updated`: it called `forget_automation` and then awaited `read_automation`. The event consumer runs on the same event loop and `find_interested_triggers` does not take `_automations_lock`. Thus an event evaluated during the read found no triggers and did not fire.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `load_automations` now reads and validates all automations first. Then it clears the cache and loads the new automations with no `await` between these steps. Evaluations see the old cache or the new cache, never an empty or partial cache. The restore-on-failure logic moves from `reconcile_automations` into `load_automations`, around the swap.
- `automation_changed` now awaits `read_automation` before it calls `forget_automation` and `load_automation`.
- New regression tests in `tests/events/server/triggers/test_service_changes.py` hold the database read of `reconcile_automations` and of `automation_changed`, and examine that `find_interested_triggers` still finds the trigger during the read. Both tests fail on `main`.
- `test_reconcile_automations_reloads_when_snapshot_changes` no longer asserts that the cache is empty after a mocked `load_automations`, because `reconcile_automations` does not clear the cache now.
- The reproduction script in the issue now prints `fires during a reload:  True`.

</details>

+class HeldRead:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.reading = asyncio.Event()
+        self.release = asyncio.Event()

+def hold_automations_session_read(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, method: str, call: int
+) -> HeldRead:
+    """Makes the triggers service's `call`-th `session.<method>(...)` wait until the
+    test releases it, as a slow database query would"""
+    held = HeldRead()
+    calls = 0
+
+    @asynccontextmanager

+

+                calls += 1
+                if calls == call:

+                    await held.release.wait()

title: Surface import errors when the placeholder flow fallback cannot find a non-`def` entrypoint
body:
closes #23769

This PR changes `load_flow_from_entrypoint` so that it re-raises the original `ScriptError` when the placeholder flow fallback (`safe_load_flow_from_entrypoint`) raises. Before, the fallback raised `ValueError: Could not find object ...` for entrypoints that are not a top-level `def` or class (for example `etl_daily = etl.with_options(...)`). `prefect deploy` and `Flow.from_source` then showed only that message, and the real import error was lost.

<details>

- An exception from the fallback now has the same result as a `None` result: the original `ScriptError` is raised.
- `def` entrypoints still load as placeholder flows. There is no change.
- `safe_load_flow_from_entrypoint` still raises `ValueError` for a missing object (`test_flow_not_found`).
- With `use_placeholder_flow=False` (runtime), there is no change.

Output of the repro from the issue with this change:

```
$ prefect deploy --name daily
...
prefect.exceptions.ScriptError: Script at 'flows.py' encountered an exception: ModuleNotFoundError("No module named 'some_dependency_not_installed'")

$ prefect deploy --name plain
...
        $ prefect deployment run 'etl/plain'
```

New tests in `tests/test_flows.py::TestLoadFlowFromEntrypoint` cover `.with_options()`, `flow(...)(fn)`, annotated assignment, re-export, and a `KeyError` from `os.environ` at import time. They fail on `main` and pass with this change.

title: Remove a failed script from `sys.modules` in `load_script_as_module`
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23770

This PR makes `load_script_as_module` remove the module entry from `sys.modules` when the script raises an exception. This is the same behavior as the Python import system.

Before this change, the half-run module stayed in `sys.modules`. A later `import` of that name in the same process got the half-run module, and the error changed from the original exception to `ImportError: cannot import name ...`. This occurs when one process loads many entrypoints, for example `prefect deploy --all`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The cleanup removes the entry only if `sys.modules[module_name]` is still the module that this call created. Thus, the cleanup does not remove a module that the script put in `sys.modules` itself.
- The registration in `sys.modules`, the execution, and the cleanup occur under `_get_sys_path_lock()`. Thus a concurrent loader of the same name cannot register its module between the identity check and the `del`. The execution was already under this lock, so concurrency does not change.
- The cleanup runs for every `BaseException` (for example `SystemExit`), as the import system does. The function still wraps only an `Exception` in `ScriptError`.
- A script that loads successfully keeps its `sys.modules` entry, as before (#16458).
- New tests in `tests/utilities/test_importtools.py`:
  - a failed script is not in `sys.modules`, and a second script that imports it gets the original `ModuleNotFoundError`;
  - a failed script that uses the `__prefect_loader_<hash>__` fallback name leaves no entry, and the earlier successful module with the same file name keeps its entry;
  - a script that calls `sys.exit` leaves no entry.
- `tests/utilities/test_importtools.py` and the entrypoint / `from_source` tests in `tests/test_flows.py` pass.

Repro output from the issue, with the fix:

```
helpers.py: ModuleNotFoundError("No module named 'some_dependency_not_installed'")
  'helpers' in sys.modules: False
flows.py: ModuleNotFoundError("No module named 'some_dependency_not_installed'")
  'helpers' in sys.modules: False
```

</details>

title: Let `*` match an empty string in `prefect deploy --name` patterns
body:
closes #23768

This PR makes `*` in a `prefect deploy --name` pattern match an empty string. Before, `etl*` did not select `etl`, and `*etl*` did not select a name that starts or ends with `etl`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`_parse_name_from_pattern` changed `*` to `.*` with `re.escape(...).replace(r"\*", ".*")`. Then it did `.replace("*", ".*")` again on the result, so each `*` became `..*`. That regex needs at least one character.

The fix compiles the converted pattern one time, for the flow part and for the deployment part.

The new test `test_pattern_deploy_wildcard_matches_empty_string` uses the deployments `test-name`, `test-name-backfill` and `dont-deploy-me`. It has patterns where `*` matches an empty string at the start, at the end, and on both sides of `/`. All 6 cases fail on `main` and pass with this change. The other `TestDeployPattern` tests still pass.

Names matched by a `flow/deployment` pattern now keep the flow prefix (for example `my_flow/release`). Before, only the bare deployment name was returned, so a pattern like `my-flow*/release` also deployed `release` from other flows. `test_pattern_with_flow_keeps_flow_qualifier` covers this.

This PR does not change the error message for a pattern that matches nothing.

</details>

title: Make the delete-block message assertions actually run
body:
Both tests in `TestDeleteBlock` put the message check inside the `pytest.raises` block, after the `load` call that raises:

```python
with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exception:
    await new_block.load(new_block_name)
    assert (
        f"Unable to find block document named {new_block_name}"
        in exception.value
    )
```

Two things keep that from working. The line sits after the call that raises, so it never executes, and `exception.value` is only populated once the `with` block exits. It also compares against the exception object rather than `str(exception.value)`, which would raise `TypeError` had it ever run.

Moving the check after the block and comparing against `str()` makes it verify the message:

```
# with the fix
2 passed

# with the expected text replaced by something the error cannot contain
2 failed
```

So the assertions now have teeth, where before they were never evaluated. `ruff check` reports the same 43 pre-existing findings on this file before and after, and `ruff format` is clean.

Three more of the same shape sit in `src/integrations/prefect-snowflake/tests/test_credentials.py` (lines 226, 241, 258), where the assertion wraps the raising call. Those are a separate package so I left them out of this PR; happy to send them separately.

title: docs: document exit_with_error markup default in CLI AGENTS.md
body:
This PR updates the `exit_with_error` contract in `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`. #23763 changed `exit_with_error` so it does not render Rich markup by default. `console.print` and `exit_with_success` still render markup. Exception text from modules outside the CLI also goes through `exit_with_error`.

This is a docs-only change. It changes one line in one existing AGENTS.md file (net +0 lines).

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: Add to the existing "Always use `exit_with_error`" sentence: "Unlike `console.print` and `exit_with_success`, it disables Rich markup by default because messages often carry user input, server errors, or `str(exc)` from non-CLI modules (deploy, provisioners) — keep markup out of exception messages; pass `markup=True` only for trusted styling and `rich.markup.escape` interpolated values."
Non-obvious evidence: The default is not the same as the defaults of `console.print` and `exit_with_success` in the same file. The AGENTS.md also tells agents to "use `rich` for all output", so agents can think that markup in an error message will render. Code outside the CLI (`deploy/_core.py`, `infrastructure/provisioners/*.py`) raises exceptions that CLI commands show with `exit_with_error(str(exc))` or `exit_with_error(exc)`. #23763 had to remove Rich markup from those messages. The `exit_with_error` docstring does not tell about this contract between files.
Cross-cutting scope: All of the approximately 440 `exit_with_error` calls in `src/prefect/cli/`. Also all non-CLI code whose exception messages the CLI shows (deploy, provisioners, client errors).
Why not code comment/docstring: The docstring tells about the `markup` parameter. It cannot tell authors of exceptions in other modules that the CLI shows their messages as literal text. The AGENTS.md bullet already tells agents to use `exit_with_error`, so it is the correct location for this pitfall.
Durability: The safe default is a lasting design decision. It is the same as the existing `print_verbatim` guidance, and it will apply to each new CLI error path.
Counter-evidence checked: `exit_with_error`/`exit_with_success` docstrings in `src/prefect/cli/_utilities.py`, `tests/cli/test_utilities.py`, the existing `print_verbatim` bullet in `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`, `tests/AGENTS.md`. None of them tells about the non-CLI exception message contract or the different defaults.

title: Disable Rich markup by default in `exit_with_error`
body:
closes #23759

This PR sets `markup=False` as the default in `exit_with_error`. Error messages often contain user input or server error text. Before this change, a closing tag such as `[/x]` caused a `MarkupError` traceback, and the real error was lost.

```
$ prefect config unset "foo[/x]"
Unknown setting name 'foo[/x]'.
```

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

I checked all `exit_with_error` callers for messages that use markup. These callers now pass `markup=True` and escape the values they interpolate:

- `deploy/_actions.py`: Dockerfile `COPY` hint (static text only).
- `deploy/_commands.py`: unknown recipe message. Escapes `recipe`.
- `config.py`: `config set` validation errors. Escapes the setting name and the pydantic error message.

Some exception messages contained markup and reach `exit_with_error(str(exc))` or `exit_with_error(f"...{exc}")`. I removed the markup from them, because otherwise the tags would show as literal text:

- `deploy/_core.py`: `ValueError` with an unclosed `[yellow]` tag.
- `infrastructure/provisioners/coiled.py` and `modal.py`: credential `RuntimeError`s used `[blue]...[/]`. `prefect work-pool create --provision-infra` prints these. They now use backticks.

Callers can still pass `markup=True` because `setdefault` keeps explicit kwargs.

Tests:
- `tests/cli/test_utilities.py`: `exit_with_error` prints markup literally by default and renders markup when `markup=True`.
- `tests/cli/test_config.py`: `config unset "foo[/x]"` prints the expected error.

Out of scope: other `console.print` calls with interpolated user input can fail the same way. For example, `prefect config set PREFECT_API_URL="a[/x]"` fails on the `Set ... to ...` confirmation line.
</details>

title: Fix IndexError in `prefect block type inspect`/`ls` on empty description
body:
closes #23758

This PR fixes an `IndexError` in `prefect block type inspect` and `prefect block type ls` when a block type has an empty description (`""`).

<details>

The old guard checked only `description is not None`. `"".splitlines()` returns an empty list, so `[0]` raised `IndexError`. Both guards now use a truth test (`if block_type.description`). This shows an empty description for `""`, the same as for `None`.

Tests: added `test_inspecting_a_block_type_with_empty_description` and `test_listing_block_types_with_empty_description` in `tests/cli/test_block.py`. They register a block type with `description=""` and run the CLI commands. Both tests fail without the fix and pass with it.

</details>

title: Tidy up GitHub Actions workflows
body:
this PR tidies up the GitHub Actions workflows so Renovate can keep every action current, and makes a few workflow defaults explicit.

- Pins every action to a commit SHA with a version comment. `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` in `renovate.json` pins actions added later.
- Replaces the archived `8398a7/action-slack` with `slackapi/slack-github-action` v4.0.0 in the failure notification. The Slack message has the same fields.
- Sets `persist-credentials` on every checkout. It is `false` except in the two jobs that push a branch.
- Passes event fields, dispatch inputs, ref names, and a secret to `run:` scripts through `env:`. The SQLite builder workflow also checks the format of its inputs.
- Runs the flaky-test Devin workflow only for failures on this repository's `main` branch, not on a fork's `main` branch.
- Sets explicit token permissions on the linked-issue label workflow.

Each commit holds one of these changes. Only workflow files and `renovate.json` change, so there are no new tests.

## Rollout caveats

- `no-op: each pinned SHA is the commit its tag or branch pointed to on 2026-11-04, so every action runs the same code as before`
- `watch: the next message from Notify on Failure. No message means Slack rejected the new payload`
- `watch: the next @claude mention on a pull request. A git error before Claude starts means claude.yml needs persist-credentials: true`
- `watch: the label workflow runs from main, so this PR does not exercise it. "Resource not accessible by integration" after merge means it needs another permission`
- `rollback: a revert is enough`

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

Each pin was resolved with `git ls-remote` and checked against the GitHub API. `claude.yml` gets `persist-credentials: false` because `claude-code-action` fetches the pull request head before it sets up its own token, and on a public repository that fetch works without a token. The edited `run:` scripts were run locally with bash, and their outputs match the old scripts for normal inputs.

</details>

title: Drop two asserts that cannot run inside pytest.raises blocks
body:
Two assertions sit after the call their `pytest.raises` block expects to raise, so neither executes. `pytest.raises` already fails when nothing is raised, so they add nothing.

- `test_removed_in_v3` asserts `False` with a message after `import_from(module)`.
- `test_load_fails_validation_raises_exception` asserts `isinstance(person, Person)` after a `Person.load` that is expected to fail validation. The assignment it read goes with it, so no name is left unused.

Verified locally rather than by inspection. Replacing each line with `raise RuntimeError(...)`, which `pytest.raises(PrefectImportError)` and `pytest.raises(pydantic.ValidationError)` would not swallow, leaves both files passing, so the lines are unreachable:

```
# with a RuntimeError in place of each line
23 passed

# after removing them
76 passed   (tests/_internal/compatibility/test_migration.py + tests/input/test_run_input.py)
```

`ruff check` on both files reports the same 16 pre-existing findings before and after, so this adds none.

No user-facing behaviour changes; this only removes lines that never ran.

title: Skip locked rows when sweeping held events
body:
closes #23754

This PR makes `sweep_held_events` skip held events that another transaction has locked, instead of waiting on them. A later sweep deletes them.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Every triggers replica runs the sweep, and `hold_event` deletes held events too. A sweep that waits on a locked row while holding others can deadlock with them. The sweep now selects its rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, as the db vacuum does. SQLite ignores `FOR UPDATE`.

The new test locks a held event in another transaction and checks that the sweep finishes, leaves that event, and deletes it on the next run. Without the fix, the sweep waits on the lock and the test times out. It runs on PostgreSQL only.

</details>

title: Detect ACI container start from the container group instead of only the ARM deployment poller
body:
closes #23755

this PR makes the ACI worker detect a started container from the container group itself. Before, the worker used only the ARM deployment poller, so it deleted container groups that were already running.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `_wait_for_task_container_start` now reads the container group on each `task_watch_poll_interval` while the ARM deployment is in progress. The wait stops when the group is `Succeeded` or its container is `Running`/`Terminated`, even if the ARM deployment has not completed. Before the change, the timeout fired while the container was already running. The worker then deleted the group and reported the flow run as `Crashed`.
- The worker reads the group before it does the timeout check. Thus the timeout occurs only if the container had not started at the last read, and the `finally` block in `run()` does not delete a running container group.
- `_provisioning_succeeded` also accepts a group whose container is `Running` or `Terminated`. Thus `run()` gives that group to `_watch_task_and_get_exit_code` and does not raise `Container creation failed`.
- `begin_create_or_update` now gets `polling_interval=configuration.task_watch_poll_interval`. The ARM poller now uses the same interval as the worker, not the default 30 s interval of the SDK.
- A `ResourceNotFoundError` during the wait means that ARM has not created the group yet. Other `HttpResponseError`s are logged as warnings. In both cases the wait continues. `_get_container_group` already retries 5xx errors.
- Tests: the container is detected before the deployment completes (container `Running` with group `Creating`, and group `Succeeded` before the deployment), a status read error during the wait, the deployment `polling_interval`, `_provisioning_succeeded` cases, and a timeout test in which the container stays in `Waiting`. Two existing tests now use realistic container group mocks.

Not reproduced against a live Azure account. Verified with unit tests.

</details>

title: docs: document bind-parameter batching and keyed-task arg loss in server docs
body:
this PR adds two pieces of durable guidance to `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`, prompted by #23130 (only write deployments that a poll actually changes):

- a Key Contract saying that statements built from a variable number of rows/IDs must batch under `get_max_query_parameters()` (minus the statement's other binds), because Prefect's SQLite bind budget (999) is only exceeded at scale
- one sentence added to the existing Docket keyed-task guidance: since keyed `add()`/`replace()` can drop a call's arguments, per-request state that must not be lost (e.g. queue poll heartbeats) has to be written synchronously before scheduling

title: docs: document flow hook parity and bootstrap version skew in AGENTS.md
body:
this PR documents the flow state hook parity contract in `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`: the flow engines and `HookRunner` share `resolve_flow_hook_arguments`, and `runner/_workspace_runtime_bootstrap.py` keeps a copy that must change with it. It also adds a note to `src/prefect/runner/AGENTS.md` that the bootstrap runs under the flow's selected (possibly older) Prefect runtime, so it must not depend on newer internals.

Follows #23715.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: src/prefect/AGENTS.md

Change the shared function and the copy together."
Non-obvious evidence: The only pointer to the copy is an inline comment inside the bootstrap. Someone editing `resolve_flow_hook_arguments` or the engine's hook call sites gets no hint that it exists.

title: Keep inherited sync client open for tasks submitted via `ThreadPoolTaskRunner`
body:
closes #23748

This PR makes `ThreadPoolTaskRunner.submit` keep the sync client from the submitting context open until the submitted task is done.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

A sync task in an async flow creates its own `SyncClientContext`. Tasks that it submits run with a copy of the context, so they use the same sync client. When the parent task returns, it closes that client. If a submitted task is still running (for example, a downstream task that waits on an upstream future), its next API call fails with `RuntimeError: Cannot send a request, as the client has been closed.`

In a sync flow, the flow owns the client, so the problem does not occur.

The fix:
- After `submit` gives the task to the executor, if a `SyncClientContext` is active and its client is open, enter the client again. This increments the client's context stack.
- Add a done callback to the executor future that exits the client. The client closes only when the last holder exits.

Tests:
- `test_submitted_task_keeps_submitting_context_sync_client_open`: a submitted task uses the client after the submitting `SyncClientContext` exits. The client closes after the task is done.
- `test_tasks_submitted_from_sync_task_in_async_flow_outlive_parent`: the scenario from the issue, with a `threading.Event` in place of `time.sleep` so the test is deterministic.

Both tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. The reproduction from the issue now returns `4` for the sync flow and the async flow.

</details>

title: Generate automatic Dockerfile in `DockerImage` build context
body:
closes #23745

This PR makes `DockerImage` generate the automatic Dockerfile in the selected build context. Before this change, `DockerImage(context=..., dockerfile="auto")` sent the selected context to the builder but wrote the temporary Dockerfile in the current working directory.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `_build_with_docker_py` and `_build_with_buildx` now pass the resolved context (`Path(...)`, so `str` contexts also work) to `generate_default_dockerfile`. When there is no `context` kwarg, the context is still `Path.cwd()`, so the default behavior does not change.
- `generate_default_dockerfile` now resolves the context. A relative context such as `"."` therefore gives the real directory name in `/opt/prefect/<name>/`, not an empty name.
- The generated Dockerfile now uses the `requirements.txt` and directory name of the selected context. The Dockerfile is removed after the build, also when the build fails.
- A `Dockerfile` in the current working directory no longer causes a "Dockerfile already exists" error when a different context is selected.
- The "Dockerfile already exists" error message now shows the context path instead of "the current directory".

Tests: new `TestDockerImageAutoDockerfileContext` in `tests/docker/test_docker_image.py`. These tests use the real `generate_default_dockerfile` and the real filesystem, and mock only `build_image` / `buildx_build_image`. They cover both backends, `Path`, `str` and relative contexts, cleanup after a failed build, an unrelated `Dockerfile` in the cwd, and the default (cwd) context. Six of these tests fail on `main` and pass with this change.
</details>

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [x] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
