title: Upgrade cyclopts to 5.3.2 and keep CLI exit codes and command names
body:
This PR upgrades cyclopts in the lock from 4.22.2 to 5.3.2. cyclopts 5 requires rich-rst 2.x, which no longer depends on docutils, so docutils leaves the lock and the published Docker images. The `cyclopts>=4.8.0` floor is unchanged. The CLI test suite passes on both 4.22.2 and 5.3.2.

Two cyclopts 5 changes would alter CLI behavior, so the CLI now handles them itself:

- cyclopts 5 exits with code 2 on usage errors: an unknown command or option, a missing argument, or a value that fails conversion. The root app sets `exit_on_error=False`, and `_run_cli` exits with 1 when cyclopts raises a `CycloptsError`. The `prefect` entry point and `CycloptsCliRunner` both call `_run_cli`.
- cyclopts 5 requires exact command names. cyclopts 4 matched names with `-` and `_` removed and case ignored, so `prefect work_pool ls` ran `work-pool ls`. `_normalize_command_names` does that matching before dispatch.

Differences from cyclopts 4 that remain:

- `--help` after an unknown command exits with 1 and an error. cyclopts 4 printed the parent command's help and exited with 0.
- Help pages show a value type after each option that takes a value, such as `--type -t STR`.

### Checklist

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
  - If no issue exists and your change is not a small fix, please [create an issue](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/new/choose) first.
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.
  - The docs do not document CLI exit codes or command-name matching.
- [ ] If this pull request removes docs files, it includes redirect settings in `mint.json`.
- [ ] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings.

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

The upgrade started from a report of a CVE in a cyclopts dependency. OSV and the GitHub advisory database list no advisories against the cyclopts dependency tree at the locked versions, so this PR does not claim a specific fix.

The first version of this PR accepted cyclopts 5's defaults and raised the floor to 5.0.0. It now keeps the behavior of Prefect 3.6 through 3.9. Prefect 3.5 and earlier ran on Typer, which exited with 2 on usage errors and rejected names like `work_pool`.

To find the remaining differences, I ran 1,013 invocations that fail during argument parsing across all 334 command paths, on `main` with cyclopts 4.22.2 and on this branch, and compared exit codes and output. The two differences above are the only regressions. Under cyclopts 4, `--help` after a misspelled name such as `workpool` crashed with a `KeyError`. On this branch it prints the help page.

</details>

title: Replace stuck readiness tasks when a poll would mark something ready
body:
closes #23643

This PR makes a poll that would move a work queue or deployment to `READY` replace any pending readiness task with the same key, instead of being deduplicated against it.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Polling endpoints schedule keyed `mark_work_queues_ready` / `mark_deployments_ready` tasks (keys added in #20210). After a Redis restart, the API's background worker can fail `execution.claim()` on a stale pooled connection. The message stays pending and its key stays known. Every later `docket.add(..., key=...)` is then deduplicated until docket's `redelivery_timeout` (5 minutes by default) passes, so the queue stays `NOT_READY` while the worker keeps polling.

Changes:
- New `schedule_readiness_update` helper in `prefect/server/api/workers.py`. It uses `docket.replace(...)` when the poll is `becoming_ready` and `docket.add(...)` otherwise. Steady-state polls (everything already `READY`) are still deduplicated exactly as before.
- Queue and deployment readiness are decided separately:
  - Queue tasks replace when any polled queue is `NOT_READY`.
  - Deployment tasks replace when any polled queue is `NOT_READY`, or when `models.deployments.has_not_ready_deployments` finds a `NOT_READY` deployment. That query is a `LIMIT 1` lookup. It catches a new deployment in a queue that's already `READY`.
- `POST /work_pools/{name}/get_scheduled_flow_runs` with `work_queue_names` scopes its keys to the sorted selected queue IDs. Polls for different queue subsets no longer replace each other's payloads. Unfiltered polls keep the pool-wide key.
- `record_work_queue_polls` returns the queues it actually changed to `READY`. `mark_work_queues_ready` emits `prefect.work-queue.ready` only for those queues, so a replaced task that overlaps an execution already in progress can't emit a duplicate event. `mark_deployments_ready` already worked this way. The implementation doesn't use `RETURNING`, because Prefect supports SQLite versions older than 3.35.

Tests:
- `TestReadinessRecoversFromStuckTask` in `tests/server/api/test_docket_task_keys.py` covers:
  - work pool, work queue and deployment polls, each with a stale task seeded under its key
  - a `NOT_READY` deployment in a `READY` queue
  - disjoint filtered work-pool polls
- `TestMarkWorkQueuesReady` in `tests/server/models/test_work_queues.py` checks that repeated calls emit one ready event.
- The new tests fail without the corresponding change. The docket tests also pass against a real Redis (`PREFECT_SERVER_DOCKET_URL=redis://...`).

Linear: [OSS-8373](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/OSS-8373/work-queues-stay-not-ready-for-5-minutes-after-redis-recovers-even)
</details>

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed

title: Link to the docs at www.prefect.io/docs
body:
The docs moved from docs.prefect.io to www.prefect.io/docs, and docs.prefect.io now redirects there. This switches the links in the repo to the new address, so CLI and SDK messages, the UI, READMEs, package metadata and docs content skip the redirect and point search engines at the canonical URLs.

title: docs: Set canonical URLs to www.prefect.io
body:
The docs now live at www.prefect.io/docs, proxied from Mintlify, and docs.prefect.io redirects there. Mintlify still builds canonical tags from its own domain (`prefect-bd373955.mintlify.dev/docs/...`), so search engines are told the Mintlify URL is the real one. This sets the canonical base to `https://www.prefect.io`. Mintlify adds the `/docs` base path and the page path to it, so pages should get canonicals like `https://www.prefect.io/docs/v3/get-started`.

title: Keep recent runs visible in V2 deployment activity charts
body:
closes #23638

This PR fixes the V2 deployment "Activity" charts so that future scheduled runs do not hide recent runs.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The deployments list (`ActivityCell`) and the flow page deployments tab (`MiniDeploymentActivity`) get flow runs with `sort: "START_TIME_DESC"` and no time filter. The server sorts by `coalesce(start_time, expected_start_time)`, so future scheduled runs come first. When a deployment has many scheduled runs, they use all of the `limit`, and the chart (past week → now) shows no recent runs.

The change:
- Adds `flow_runs.start_time` `{ after_: now - 1 week, before_: now }` to both queries. On the server, this filter applies to `coalesce(start_time, expected_start_time)`, which is the same key as the sort. Runs that started in the window are included, also if they started late. Late or pending runs that did not start yet are included by their expected start time. Future scheduled runs are not included. This is like the V1 `MiniDeploymentHistory` / `DeploymentStatsFilter` window.
- Uses `useNow({ interval: 60_000 })` so the window moves forward each minute. The chart dates and the query use the same `now`. `keepPreviousData` prevents an empty chart when the window changes.
- Adds tests in `data-table.test.tsx` and `flow-deployments-tab.test.tsx` that check the request window. Both tests fail without the fix.

The feedback also asks for a view that shows the next N and the most recent N runs around "now". This PR does not add that view. It makes the V2 chart match V1, which is the behavior the user switched back to. Upcoming runs are still on the deployment page ("Next Run" and the "Upcoming" tab).
</details>

### Checklist

- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed. (UI bug fix, no docs change)

title: Recover cron occurrences shifted through DST gaps
body:
closes #23631

This PR retains still-upcoming cron occurrences shifted out of a spring-forward gap. A Berlin `30 2 * * *` schedule queried from `2027-03-28T03:00+02:00` now returns that day's shifted `03:30+02:00` occurrence instead of skipping to March 29.

Layer 2 of the cron DST stack, based on #23634. It looks back only across the current forward transition, merges shifted and ordinary occurrences in UTC order, and reuses the first layer's start/end filtering and deduplication.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and validation</summary>

Eight regression cases fail without this layer. Coverage includes Berlin and New York start/end bounds and microsecond cutoffs, Lord Howe's half-hour jump, and Apia's skipped day. The existing Python-version-dependent gap resolution is also covered; Python 3.11–3.12 Pendulum behavior is preserved.

Full schedule suite:

- Python 3.12: 137 passed, 46 skipped, 2 existing xfails.
- Python 3.13 and 3.14 with Whenever 0.11: 183 passed, 2 existing xfails each.
- Python 3.13 with Whenever 0.10.5: 183 passed, 2 existing xfails.
- Repository commit/push hooks pass, including generated OpenAPI verification.

Extracted from draft #23424. No interval scheduling, SDK contract, dependency, or public schema changes are included.
</details>

title: Preserve cron start bounds in repeated DST hours
body:
Related to #23631.

This PR prevents Python 3.13+ cron queries inside a repeated DST hour from returning timestamps before `start`. It preserves the requested fold and microsecond cutoff, selects the earliest viable occurrence, and compares bounds on the UTC timeline.

Layer 1 of the cron DST stack, based on `main`. Spring-gap recovery is #23636. Extracted from draft #23424; interval scheduling and Python 3.11–3.12 Pendulum behavior are outside this change.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and validation</summary>

For `30 2 * * *` in `Europe/Berlin`, a start at `2026-10-25T02:15+01:00` previously returned `02:30+02:00`, before the requested instant. It now returns `02:30+01:00`. Queries made before the transition still select only the first occurrence.

Five of the seven second-fold regression cases fail on main. Coverage includes New York hourly/minute schedules, Berlin daily schedules, microsecond cutoffs, bounded queries, and duplicate prevention.

Full schedule suite:

- Python 3.12: 136 passed, 30 skipped, 2 existing xfails.
- Python 3.13 and 3.14: 166 passed, 2 existing xfails each.
- Repository commit/push hooks pass, including generated OpenAPI verification.

The existing cron contract already promises dates on or after `start`; no public schema or configuration change is needed.
</details>

title: Fall back to placeholder for any `jsonable_encoder` error in `Flow.serialize_parameters`
body:
closes #23629

This PR changes `Flow.serialize_parameters` to catch all `Exception` subclasses from `jsonable_encoder`, not only `TypeError`, `ValueError` and `RecursionError`. When the encoder fails, the parameter gets the `"<Type>"` placeholder, as before.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`jsonable_encoder` calls `dataclasses.asdict`, which deep-copies field values. If a field value raises a different error from `__reduce__` (for example, `NotImplementedError`), the error escapes and the flow run fails before it starts. The list of exception types cannot be complete, because the encoder can call arbitrary user code. Parameter serialization is only for the API record, so a failure here must not stop the run.

`BaseException` subclasses such as `KeyboardInterrupt` are not caught.

Added `test_serialize_parameters_falls_back_on_arbitrary_encoder_errors` to `tests/test_flows.py` with the reproduction from the issue. Related: #22245.

</details>

title: Restore advisory Cloud API compatibility checks
body:
closes #23623

This PR restores Cloud API compatibility checks as non-blocking warnings so maintainers can catch API changes that need to reach Cloud before merging. New or changed failures produce one updated PR comment explaining who needs to act.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Compares the base and proposed changes against one deployed Cloud schema snapshot using the same shared suite. Existing failures are excluded, unavailable checks are reported separately, and the comment is updated when new failures resolve. The check runs on every PR update so removing an API change also clears its warning.

PR code runs with read-only permissions. A separate default-branch workflow handles comments, validates PR association, ignores stale runs, and treats report contents as untrusted data. The comment workflow becomes active after this PR reaches `main`.

Adds an opt-in compatibility schema format that restores the `/api` prefix and excludes OSS webserver routes, while preserving the schema used for UI type generation. Updates the local compatibility command to use it.

The corrected `main` baseline was 961 passes and four existing failures. Repeated runs produced zero new failures; a regression probe detected both a new endpoint and a new enum value in an already-failing test. The 20 Python tests, seven Node tests, workflow lint, and pre-commit hooks passed. GitHub execution and comment posting have not yet been exercised.

No user documentation is needed for this CI-only change. The original check was paused in #14773.

</details>

title: Return 422 instead of 503/500 for invalid values in request bodies
body:
closes #23615

This PR makes the server return 422 for invalid values in request bodies. Before, some of these values gave 503 (which the client retries) or 500.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `is_invalid_data_exception` (in `api/server.py`) finds database errors with SQLSTATE class 22 ("data exception"). Examples: a NUL character or `NaN` in a PostgreSQL JSON value. `is_client_retryable_exception` does not mark these errors as retryable, and `custom_internal_exception_handler` returns 422 for them. Other `DBAPIError`s continue to return 503.
- `PrefectAPIRoute` rejects JSON bodies that contain unpaired surrogates (for example `"\ud800"`) with a 422 that has the location of the bad string. These strings cannot be encoded as UTF-8, so the server can not store them or return them. This applies to SQLite and PostgreSQL. A fast byte check makes sure that bodies without surrogate escapes are not parsed a second time. Valid surrogate pairs (for example emoji) are accepted.
- `validation_exception_handler` replaces `NaN`/`Infinity` and unpaired surrogates in the response with strings. Before, rendering the 422 body raised an error and the server returned 500.

Results of the issue's reproduction script, after the change:

| request | PostgreSQL | SQLite |
| --- | --- | --- |
| flow run parameters: NUL | 422 | 201 (SQLite stores it, as before) |
| flow run parameters: lone surrogate | 422 | 422 |
| artifact data: `NaN` | 422 | 201 (as before) |
| retries: `NaN` | 422 | 422 |
| variable value: lone surrogate | 422 | 422 |

Note: orchestration rules call `is_client_retryable_exception`. A data exception in state validation now gives an `ABORT` response instead of a 503.

</details>

title: Fix 500 from flow run resume when run input has an integer beyond 64 bits
body:
closes #23616

This PR makes `POST /flow_runs/{id}/resume` accept `run_input` that contains an integer outside the 64-bit range. The run resumes, the server stores the exact value, and the SDK loads it back without losing precision.

<details>

`resume_flow_run` serializes the validated `run_input` with `orjson.dumps` before it stores it. `orjson` raises `TypeError: Integer exceeds 64-bit range` for such integers. The endpoint returned 500, the transaction rolled back, and the run stayed `PAUSED`.

The fix uses `pydantic_core.to_json(run_input, inf_nan_mode="null")` for this value. `pydantic_core` is already a dependency (`pyproject.toml` and `client/pyproject.toml`). It writes big integers exactly. `inf_nan_mode="null"` keeps the `orjson` behavior for `NaN`/`Infinity` (they become `null`), so the stored value is always valid JSON. The output is compact JSON, the same as before.

The SDK read path now keeps these integers too. `aread_flow_run_input`, `read_flow_run_input` (`prefect/input/actions.py`) and `FlowRunInput.decoded_value` parse with `json.loads` instead of `orjson.loads`. `orjson.loads` turned integers beyond 64 bits into `float`, so the typed `RunInput.load` raised `ValidationError`.

Tests:
- `test_resume_flow_run_waiting_for_input_with_integer_beyond_64_bit_range` (`tests/server/orchestration/api/test_flow_runs.py`) resumes with `2**64 + 1` and checks the stored value.
- `test_load_after_resume_preserves_integer_beyond_64_bit_range` (`tests/input/test_run_input.py`) pauses a run, resumes it through the client with `2**64 + 1`, then loads it with `RunInput.load` and the sync `read_flow_run_input`.
- `test_load_from_flow_run_input_preserves_integer_beyond_64_bit_range` covers `decoded_value`.

All three fail on `main`. I also ran the reproduction script from the issue against a local server:

```
run_input x=1: resume -> 201; state after: RUNNING; stored: {"x":1}
run_input x=18446744073709551616: resume -> 201; state after: RUNNING; stored: {"x":18446744073709551616}
```

Not changed: the SDK write helpers (`create_flow_run_input` / `send_input`) still serialize with `orjson`, so sending an integer beyond 64 bits from the SDK still fails on the client side.

Related: #15031, #23429.

</details>

body:
This PR corrects one existing pitfall in `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`. The pitfall told agents to add `state_details` preservation transforms to `CoreFlowPolicy` only. Forced state changes (`force=True`) use `MinimalFlowPolicy`, so a transform in `CoreFlowPolicy` only does not protect forced transitions. #23304 fixed this bug for `deployment_concurrency_lease_id`. The edit now tells agents to register the transform in both policies. The net line change is 0.

<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: In the "Pydantic v2 treats null JSON fields as explicitly set" pitfall, change "add a `FlowRunUniversalTransform` to `CoreFlowPolicy`" to "add a `FlowRunUniversalTransform` to both `CoreFlowPolicy` and `MinimalFlowPolicy` (used for `force=True`, otherwise forced transitions drop the field)".
Non-obvious evidence: `models/flow_runs.py` selects `MinimalFlowPolicy` for forced transitions, and `orchestration/dependencies.py` selects `CoreFlowPolicy` for usual transitions. A docstring on one transform does not help a person who adds a new transform. The existing AGENTS.md pitfall is the location that agents read for this pattern.
Durability: This stays correct while `force=True` uses a separate minimal policy. It applies to all future `state_details` fields.

title: Fix flaky `TestFlowRunLogs` tests by filtering logs by flow run
body:
This PR fixes the flaky `tests/test_flows.py::TestFlowRunLogs::test_user_logs_are_sent_to_orion` test that failed on `main` ([run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40430114883), commit 4a1a1cc06a0cdaf5a353026323c32495de07b7fe).

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

`TestFlowRunLogs` tests that are not marked `clear_db` share the database with tests that ran before them on the same xdist worker. `_wait_for_logs` read all logs without a filter. When earlier tests had left 3 or more logs in the database, `_wait_for_logs(expected_num_logs=3)` returned at once, before the `APILogWorker` flushed this test's logs. The CI failure shows this: the logs read back were `{'... [truncated]', 'hello'}`, which come from `tests/test_logging.py`, not from this test.

The fix:
- `_wait_for_logs` now accepts `flow_run_ids` and filters `read_logs` with `LogFilterFlowRunId`. This matches the helper in `tests/test_tasks.py`.
- `test_user_logs_are_sent_to_orion` and `test_repeated_flow_calls_send_logs_to_orion` (the two tests without `clear_db`) pass their flow run IDs and assert on the filtered logs.

**Reproduction:** on the original code, `uv run pytest tests/test_logging.py "tests/test_flows.py::TestFlowRunLogs" -p no:randomly` fails both tests every time. With this change, the same command passes. `TestFlowRunLogs` also passes 20 times in a row with `pytest-repeat` and `-n4`.

title: Fix flaky `TestProcessPoolTaskRunner::test_submit_remains_non_blocking`
body:
This PR swaps the wall-clock check in `test_submit_remains_non_blocking` for a deterministic gate.

Failed on main: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40422419881 (commit 5656c7799c131b1081c60866f35879893a4c494a) with `assert 0.5182864665985107 < 0.5`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Root cause:** The test timed two `submit()` calls and required the total to be under 0.5s, which was also how long the task slept. That total includes overhead that grows with load, like logging and `serialize_context()`. Since #23376, `serialize_context()` runs on every submit. On a loaded CI runner the total reached 0.518s, so the test failed even though `submit()` never blocked on `wait_for`.

**Fix:** The task now waits for a file under `tmp_path`, and the flow creates that file only after both `submit()` calls return. If `submit()` blocked on `future_a` (the regression this test guards against, from #19172), the flow would deadlock and pytest-timeout would fail the test. If `submit()` doesn't block, the test passes however slow the runner is.

**Verification:**
- 20 out of 20 local runs passed.
- I also checked that the new test catches a regression. I temporarily added `resolution_future.result()` to `ProcessPoolTaskRunner.submit()` to make it block, and the test hung instead of passing. I reverted that change afterwards.
- `ruff format` passes on the changed file.

</details>

title: Read automation buckets in a single query to avoid refresh race
body:
closes #23603

This PR changes `read_bucket_by_trigger_id` to read the bucket with one SELECT that uses `populate_existing=True`. It removes the `session.refresh(bucket)` call that came after the SELECT.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Before this change, the function ran two statements: a SELECT by `(automation_id, trigger_id, bucketing_key)`, then `session.refresh(bucket)`, which runs a second SELECT by primary key. On Postgres (READ COMMITTED), a different transaction can delete the bucket and commit between the two statements. Possible sources are a second reactive consumer, proactive evaluation, or the closed-bucket sweep. When this occurs, the refresh finds no row and raises `InvalidRequestError: Could not refresh instance '<AutomationBucket ...>'`. The broker then retries the message.

The refresh was necessary because the bucket upserts are Core statements. Without the refresh, an `AutomationBucket` that is already in the session identity map keeps stale attributes. `populate_existing=True` replaces those attributes from the single SELECT, so the result is equally fresh and there is no window between two statements. If the row is deleted before the SELECT, the function returns `None`, and the callers (`reactive_evaluation`, `hold_expect_event`) already handle `None`.

Tests in `tests/events/server/triggers/test_regressions.py`:

Defaults for omitted `Query`, `Header`, `Cookie`, and `Form` parameters and model fields are no longer treated as user input. Defaults are not validated unless `validate_default=True` is enabled. If you rely on validators running for omitted values, enable default validation with `Field(validate_default=True)` for model fields or, for example, `Query(validate_default=True)` for individual parameters. `Body(validate_default=True)` is now honored too.

For parameter models, applying a default no longer marks a field as explicitly set, so `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` excludes it. Default factories run once, and validation errors no longer include injected defaults in `input`.

Omitted boolean form fields still become `False` and count as explicitly set.

Omitted `bool` and `bool | None` form fields are now interpreted as `False`, matching unchecked HTML checkboxes. title: Scope prefect-azure setuptools cap to AzureML extras
body:
Unblocks https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23583 (setuptools 80.10.2 → 84.1.0).

### Summary

`prefect-azure` declared an unconditional `setuptools` runtime cap (`<81` on PyPI, `<82` in source) so that `pkg_resources` stayed importable for `azureml-core`, which imports it at runtime on older supported versions (see #13672, #20617). Because AzureML is an optional extra, ordinary `prefect-azure` installs were inheriting that cap — and with setuptools 84.1 published, resolvers downgrade `prefect-azure` all the way to 0.4.8 to satisfy it.

This PR moves the cap to `setuptools<81` on the extras that actually install AzureML:

- `ml_datastore` extra: `azureml-core` + `setuptools<81`
- `all_extras` extra: same
- `dev` dependency group (which installs `azureml-core`): `setuptools<81`

Base runtime dependencies no longer mention setuptools. Build-system requirements and all other dependency minimums are unchanged.

### Verification (Python 3.12)

- Built wheel metadata: `Requires-Dist: setuptools<81` appears only under `extra == "ml-datastore"` and `extra == "all-extras"` markers — asserted by a new regression test.
- Resolution: `uv pip install 'prefect-azure[ml-datastore]' 'setuptools==84.1'` correctly fails as unsatisfiable; `ml-datastore` alone selects setuptools 80.10.2; base + `setuptools==84.1` resolves cleanly.
- Import smoke: `prefect_azure` and all non-ML modules (`credentials`, `blob_storage`, `cosmos_db`, `container_instance`, `workers.container_instance`, `repository`, `plugins`) import with setuptools 84.1 installed and `pkg_resources` absent. These are smoke tests only — they verify imports, not live Azure calls.
- Full `prefect-azure` suite (192 tests, with `azure-storage-blob`, `azure-cosmos`, and `azureml-core` installed via the dev group): all pass.
- The root `prefect[azure]` extra (`prefect-azure>=0.4.0`, no extras) will not select ML extras or a setuptools cap once a release with this change is published.

### Regression coverage

New `tests/test_packaging.py` asserts:

- base `dependencies` contain no setuptools requirement;
- `ml_datastore` / `all_extras` / the dev group carry `setuptools<81` alongside `azureml-core`;
- the built wheel's `Requires-Dist` metadata scopes setuptools to the ML extras only;
- base modules import with `pkg_resources` blocked.

### Limitations

- **A corrected `prefect-azure` release must be published before #23583 can land.** `uv.lock` resolves `prefect-azure` from PyPI (currently 0.4.13, which still carries the unconditional cap), so the dependabot PR can only be relocked against setuptools 84.1 after a release containing this fix is out. This PR intentionally does not touch `uv.lock`.
- `prefect_azure.deployments.steps` imports `azure.storage.blob` unconditionally, so it still requires the `blob_storage` extra — unchanged by this PR.
- Credential-dependent tests (live Blob/Cosmos/ACI/AML calls) were not run; coverage here is unit tests plus import smoke tests.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull re

--- src/integrations/prefect-azure/tests/test_packaging.py (+153/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,153 @@
+"""Regression tests for prefect-azure packaging metadata.
+
+`prefect-azure` used to declare an unconditional `setuptools<81` runtime
+dependency so that `pkg_resources` remained importable for `azureml-core`
+(AzureML imports `pkg_resources` at runtime on older supported versions).
+AzureML is optional, so the cap belongs on the ML extras — an unconditional
+cap forces resolvers to downgrade `prefect-azure` (or hold back
+`setuptools`) for users who never install AzureML. See
+https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23583.
+"""
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tomllib
+import zipfile
+from email.parser import Parser
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+PACKAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+PYPROJECT_TOML = PACKAGE_DIR / "pyproject.toml"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def pyproject():
+    with PYPROJECT_TOML.open("rb") as f:
+        return tomllib.load(f)
+
+
+def _deps_starting_with(deps, name):
+    return [d for d in deps if d.split(";")[0].strip().lower().startswith(name)]
+
+
+def test_base_dependencies_do_not_require_setuptools(pyproject):
+    """Ordinary installs must not inherit AzureML's setuptools cap."""
+    base_deps = pyproject["project"]["dependencies"]
+    assert _deps_starting_with(base_deps, "setuptools") == []
+
+
+def test_ml_extras_carry_the_setuptools_cap(pyproject):
+    """extras that pull in azureml-core must still pin setuptools<81 so
+    pkg_resources is available for older supported AzureML versions."""
+    extras = pyproject["project"]["optional-dependencies"]
+    for extra in ("ml_datastore", "all_extras"):
+        deps = extras[extra]
+        assert any(dep.startswith("azureml-core") for dep in deps), (
+            f"{extra} should install azureml-core"
+        )
+        assert _deps_starting_with(deps, "setuptools") == ["setuptools<81"], (
+            f"{extra} must cap setuptools<81 for pkg_resources"
+        )
+
+
+def test_dev_dependency_group_pins_setuptools(pyproject):
+    """The dev group installs azureml-core, so it needs pkg_resources too."""
+    dev_deps = pyproject["dependency-groups"]["dev"]
+    assert any(dep.startswith("azureml-core") for dep in dev_deps)
+    assert _deps_starting_with(dev_deps, "setuptools") == ["setuptools<81"]
+
+
+def test_built_wheel_scopes_setuptools_to_ml_extras(tmp_path, pyproject):
+    """Build the wheel and assert the setuptools requirement only appears in
+    the ml_datastore/all_extras extras' Requires-Dist metadata."""
+    expected_extras = set(pyproject["project"]["optional-dependencies"])
+
+    subprocess.run(
+        ["uv", "build", "--wheel", "--out-dir", str(tmp_path)],
+        cwd=PACKAGE_DIR,
+        check=True,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+    )
+    wheels = list(tmp_path.glob("*.whl"))
+    assert len(wheels) == 1, f"expected one wheel, got {wheels}"
+
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(wheels[0]) as zf:
+        metadata_name = next(n for n in zf.namelist() if n.endswith("METADATA"))
+        metadata = Parser().parsestr(zf.read(metadata_name).decode())
+
+    requires = metadata.get_all("Requires-Dist") or []
+    setuptools_reqs = [r for r in requires if r.lower().startswith("setuptools")]
+    # non-setuptools requirements must not be conditioned on ML extras
+    other_extra_reqs = [
+        r
+        for r in requires
+        if not r.lower().startswith("setuptools")
+        and ('extra == "ml-datastore"' in r or 'extra == "all-extras"' in r)
+    ]
+
+    assert setuptools_reqs, "wheel should still require setuptools for ML extras"
+    for req in setuptools_reqs:
+        assert "setuptools<81" in req.replace(" ", "")
+        assert "extra ==" in req
+        # wheel metadata normalizes extra names per PEP 685 ('-' not '_')
+        marker_extra = req.split('extra == "')[1].rstrip('"').replace("-", "_")
+        assert marker_extra in {"ml_datastore", "all_extras"}
+
+    marked_extras = {
+        req.split('extra == "')[1].rstrip('"').replace("-", "_")
+        for req in setuptools_reqs
+    }
+    assert marked_extras == {"ml_datastore", "all_extras"}
+    # sanity: azureml is only ever required by those same extras, and no
+    # unrelated extra (blob_storage/cosmos_db) carries a setuptools requirement
+    assert expected_extras >= marked_extras
+    assert not any(r.lower().startswith("setuptools") for r in other_extra_reqs)
+
+
+BASE_MODULES = [
+    "prefect_azure",
+    "prefect_azure.credentials",
+    "prefect_azure.blob_storage",
+    "prefect_azure.cosmos_db",
+    "prefect_azure.container_instance",
+    "prefect_azure.workers.container_instance",
+    "prefect_azure.repository",
+    "prefect_azure.plugins",
+]
+
+
+def test_base_modules_import_without_pkg_resources():
+    """Smoke test: importing the base package and its non-ML modules must not
+    touch `pkg_resources` (which only exists under setuptools<81).
+
+    `prefect_azure.ml_datastore` is intentionally excluded: it imports
+    `azureml-core`, which is exactly the code path that still needs
+    `pkg_resources`. `prefect_azure.deployments.steps` is also excluded:
+    it requires the `blob_storage` extra.
+    """
+    blocker = """
+import sys
+
+class _BlockPkgResources:
+    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
+        if name == "pkg_resources" or name.startswith("pkg_resources."):
+            raise ImportError("pkg_resources is not available (setuptools>=81)")
+        return None
+
+sys.meta_path.insert(0, _BlockPkgResources())
+sys.modules.pop("pkg_resources", None)
+"""
+    imports = "\n".join(f"import {mod}" for mod in BASE_MODULES)
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        [sys.executable, "-c", blocker + imports],
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+    assert result.returncode == 0, (
+        "base prefect_azure modules must import without pkg_resources:\n"
+        f"{result.stderr}"
+    )

title: docs: clarify whenever guard exception in src/prefect AGENTS.md
body:
This PR fixes two problems in the `whenever` import-guard sentence that #23577 added to `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`. Both problems come from [Codex review comments](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23577#discussion_r4369517952) on #23577.

- The exception said "only server code that the client build strips". But `client/build_client.sh` also strips `cli/`, `testing/`, and `deployments/{recipes,templates}`. Code in those paths can also import `whenever` unconditionally. The text now says "only code that the client build strips".
- The pointer `client/AGENTS.md` can resolve to `src/prefect/client/AGENTS.md`, which documents the HTTP client. The text now says "the repo-root `client/AGENTS.md`".

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: Change "only server code that the client build strips may import it unconditionally (see `client/AGENTS.md`)" to "only code that the client build strips may import it unconditionally (see the repo-root `client/AGENTS.md`)".
Non-obvious evidence: `client/build_client.sh` removes `cli/`, `testing/`, `deployments/recipes/`, and `deployments/templates` in addition to the server internals. Two AGENTS.md files have the path `client/AGENTS.md` relative to different roots.
Cross-cutting scope: All code under `src/prefect/` that the `prefect-client` build strips, and the cross-reference to the package-build guide.

title: Bump fast-uri from 3.1.7 to 3.1.9 in /ui-v2
body:
Bumps [fast-uri](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri) from 3.1.7 to 3.1.9.
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

title: Fix flaky events E2E tests: filter by exact resource IDs
body:
This PR fixes the flaky `Events List Page` E2E tests "Events timeline shows events from multiple resource types" and "Filter by event type". These tests failed on main in [run 40144138487](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40144138487) (shard 2/3).

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

The two tests filter the events page by resource to keep their events on the first page (limit 50, DESC order). The filter had the exact flow-run ID, but it also had the broad prefixes `"prefect.deployment."` and `"prefect.work-pool."`. The UI sends these values as `any_resource.id_prefix`, so the filter matches every deployment and work-pool event that other tests in the shard emit. The test events have an `occurred` time 2 minutes in the past. More than 50 newer deployment events push them off the first page. The CI failure screenshots show this: the page shows "3 resources selected" and lists only `Deployment Created` / `Flow Run Scheduled` events from other specs.

The fix gives the deployment and work-pool test events fixed UUID resource IDs and uses these exact IDs in the resource filter. Other tests' events can no longer match the filter.

**Local verification**
- Reproduced the failure on `main`: I emitted 100 `prefect.deployment.created` noise events (occurred 70s ago, which is inside the UI query window and newer than the test events), then ran the tests. "Events timeline shows events from multiple resource types" failed the same way as in CI.
- With this fix and the same noise before each run: the two target tests passed 20/20 times, and the full `events.spec.ts` passed 5/5 times (15/15 tests each run).
- `npx biome check e2e/` is clean.

</details>

title: docs: add whenever import guard rule to src/prefect AGENTS.md
body:
This PR is a follow-up to #23570. It adds the `whenever` import-guard rule to `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`. Agents that edit files in `src/prefect/` load that file. They do not load `client/AGENTS.md`, so the rule from #23570 did not apply to the files that it protects (from a [Codex review comment](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23570#discussion_r4368974637)). The packaging details stay in `client/AGENTS.md`.

The change adds one sentence to the existing `whenever` compat-helper bullet. The net line change is zero.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "`prefect-client` depends on `whenever` only on Python 3.13+, so modules it ships must keep `whenever` imports behind `sys.version_info >= (3, 13)`; only server code that the client build strips may import it unconditionally (see `client/AGENTS.md`)."
Non-obvious evidence: Since #23205, the root `pyproject.toml` lists `whenever` with no marker, and `server/schemas/schedules.py` imports it unconditionally. Dev installs always include `whenever`, so repo tests do not find an unguarded import in client-side code. Only the Python 3.11 `prefect-client` smoke tests can find it, and only for code paths that they import.
Cross-cutting scope: All modules under `src/prefect/` that go into `prefect-client`.
Why not code comment/docstring: The mistake is a new import in any module. No single module comment is the right place. The existing `whenever` rule in `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` is where agents look for this guidance.
Durability: It stays true while the client marker `python_version>='3.13'` differs from the root dependency.
Counter-evidence checked: `client/AGENTS.md` (has the rule from #23570, but it is outside the ancestor scope of `src/prefect/`), the existing `whenever` bullet in `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` (says "on Python 3.13+" but does not give the reason), `types/_datetime.py` (has the guards but does not explain them), `tests/client/test_prefect_client_build.py`.

title: docs: document tolerant reads of unknown automation values
body:
This PR adds one bullet to the Key Contracts section of `src/prefect/events/AGENTS.md`. The bullet tells agents that client automation schemas must read action types and metric names that this version does not know. It also tells agents that code which reads automations must handle these unknown variants.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/events/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "**Automation schemas must read values this version doesn't know.** Cloud can add action types and metric names before a client release knows about them, so unknown actions parse as `UnknownAction` and unknown metric names stay `str` in `MetricTriggerQuery.name`. Code that reads automations must handle these variants (e.g. no `.value` on a metric name without an `isinstance` check), and `prefect transfer` skips automations that use them instead of copying them."

Why not code comment/docstring: The rule applies to consumers in other packages (for example `cli/transfer/`) and to schema fields that do not exist yet. A docstring on one model does not reach these places.

title: docs: document whenever dependency split in client AGENTS.md
body:
This PR adds one contract to `client/AGENTS.md`. After #23205, `prefect` needs `whenever` on all Python versions. `prefect-client` still needs it only on Python 3.13+. Code that goes into `prefect-client` must keep its `whenever` imports behind a version guard.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `client/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "`whenever` is required by `prefect` on all Pythons but by `prefect-client` only on 3.13+. Server-only code (e.g. `server/schemas/schedules.py`) may import it unconditionally; code shipped in `prefect-client` must keep it behind `sys.version_info >= (3, 13)` like `types/_datetime.py`. Repo tests won't catch a violation because dev installs always include `whenever`. Marker-only differences like this must be allowlisted explicitly in `tests/client/test_prefect_client_build.py`."
Non-obvious evidence: The root `pyproject.toml` now lists `whenever` with no marker. A developer who looks at it, or at the unconditional `import whenever` in `server/schemas/schedules.py`, can think it is safe to import `whenever` anywhere. But `client/pyproject.toml` keeps `python_version>='3.13'`. The full test suite always has `whenever` installed, so it does not find this mistake. Only the Python 3.11 `prefect-client` smoke tests in CI can find it, and only for code paths that they import.
Cross-cutting scope: All modules in `src/prefect/` that go into `prefect-client` (everything except stripped server/CLI code). It also applies to the dependency-mirroring check in `tests/client/test_prefect_client_build.py`.
Why not code comment/docstring: The contract connects the root `pyproject.toml`, `client/pyproject.toml`, `build_client.sh` strip rules, and any client-side module. No single file is the right place for it. `client/AGENTS.md` already owns the "mirror dependencies" contract that this refines.
Durability: It stays true while the marker split exists. The split continues until `prefect-client` drops support for Python < 3.13, or the client starts to need `whenever` on all versions.

title: docs: document SQLAlchemy minor-version contract in server AGENTS.md
body:
this PR adds one Key Contracts bullet to `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`: server code must run on every SQLAlchemy minor allowed by `pyproject.toml` (currently 2.0 and 2.1), even though CI only tests the version locked in `uv.lock`.

Follow-up to #23201, where SQLAlchemy 2.1 broke deployment scheduling on fresh installs while CI (locked to 2.0.45) stayed green.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "**Server code must run on every SQLAlchemy minor allowed by `pyproject.toml` (currently 2.0 and 2.1)** — CI only tests the version locked in `uv.lock`, and tests turn `SADeprecationWarning` into errors, so newer-minor breakage surfaces only on fresh installs. Avoid APIs deprecated in the newest minor (e.g. `Result.t`, `orm.noload`, PostgreSQL `Select.distinct(expr)`); feature-detect where versions diverge (see `distinct_on` in `database/query_components.py`). Check with `uv run --with 'sqlalchemy[asyncio]==<newest>' pytest tests/server`."
Non-obvious evidence: `pyproject.toml` allows `sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0,<3.0.0` but `uv.lock` pins 2.0.45 and no CI workflow tests a newer SQLAlchemy, so an agent validating locally/CI never sees 2.1 failures. `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]` only ignores `SAWarning`, not `SADeprecationWarning`, which is easy to miss.
Cross-cutting scope: All server ORM/query code (`models/`, `database/`, `api/`, `schemas/filters.py`) on both SQLite and PostgreSQL — #23201 touched five unrelated modules for the same root cause.
Why not code comment/docstring: The constraint spans every query site; the single inline comment next to `distinct_on` only explains that one call site, not the general contract or the CI gap.
Durability: Holds as long as the dependency range spans more than the locked minor, which is the normal state between lockfile bumps; the "currently 2.0 and 2.1" parenthetical is the only part that ages.
Counter-evidence checked: Existing `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md` (only mentions SQLAlchemy as the model layer), root `AGENTS.md` (lists SQLAlchemy 2.0 in the tech stack, no compatibility guidance), `tests/AGENTS.md`, `pyproject.toml` filterwarnings, `.github/workflows/` (no SQLAlchemy version matrix), and the inline comments added in #23201.

body:
This PR adds one bullet to the "API Integration" section of `ui-v2/AGENTS.md`. The bullet tells agents not to use `useSuspenseQuery` for queries whose key changes as the user types in a search or filter input. A new key suspends the tree again. This remounts the input, and the input loses focus. The bullet tells agents to use `useQuery` with `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` for these queries. It also tells agents to get filtered counts from the paginated response.

Before this change, the section said "Use `useSuspenseQuery` over `useQuery`" and gave only one exception. Agents who follow that rule cause this bug again. The bug occurred three times: #19827 (events feed), #22497 (deployments), and #23338 (flows).

title: Ignore Python 3.15 multi-threaded fork warning in forked child service test
body:
This PR fixes the `test_forked_child_exits_cleanly_with_running_service` failure on `main` for Python 3.15 ([failed run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40108528899)). #23464 added this test.

<details>

**Root cause**

The test starts a `MockService`, which starts a thread. Then the test calls `fork()`. Python 3.15 emits a `DeprecationWarning` ("This process ... is multi-threaded, use of fork() may lead to deadlocks in the child") when a multi-threaded process calls `fork()`. The pytest config sets `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]`, so the warning becomes an error. On Python 3.15 the test fails every time. It is not a random failure.

**Fix**

Add a `pytest.mark.filterwarnings` mark to ignore this warning for this test only. The test must fork while the service thread runs, so the warning is expected. This is the same mark that `test_manager_has_lock_information_when_deserialized_in_new_process_with_fork` in `tests/test_locking.py` uses (added in #23400).

**Verification**

- Python 3.15.1: the failure reproduces before the fix. After the fix, the test passes 20 of 20 runs, and `tests/_internal/concurrency/test_services.py` passes (48 tests).
- Default Python: `tests/_internal/concurrency/test_services.py` passes.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed file.

</details>

title: docs: document SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE contract in server AGENTS.md
body:
This PR documents the SQLite read-then-write transaction contract in `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`. Passing `with_for_update=True` starts SQLite transactions with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, avoiding a stale deferred-read snapshot when another connection commits before the write. PostgreSQL ignores this session flag; query-level locking must be explicit there.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification and conflict resolution</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: Use `with_for_update=True` for SQLite transactions that read before writing, with explicit PostgreSQL query locking where required.
Non-obvious evidence: The session option changes SQLite transaction start behavior but does not add PostgreSQL row locks.
Cross-cutting scope: Server transaction callers across models, services and event processing.
Why not code comment/docstring: The configuration implementation already explains it, but callers across the server need this editing contract.
Durability: Applies to SQLite snapshot upgrades and the existing database session API.
Counter-evidence checked: SQLite and PostgreSQL `begin_transaction` implementations in `server/database/configurations.py`.

Merged main to resolve adjacent additions in this file. Retained both the original SQLite guidance and main's SQLAlchemy compatibility guidance unchanged; the PR difference from that main remains exactly the original one-line addition.

Validation: a disposable two-connection SQLite WAL reproduction confirmed deferred read followed by another connection's commit fails on write with `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT`; an immediate read/write succeeds. Verified the resolved file equals main plus the original rule. Commit hooks passed. This is documentation-only; no server runtime code changed and the full database suite was not rerun.

</details>

title: docs: document CLI logging-config leak pitfall in tests AGENTS.md
body:
this PR adds a flaky-test pitfall to `tests/AGENTS.md`: CLI tests that run without test mode call `setup_logging()` from the CLI entrypoint (`src/prefect/cli/_app.py`), which resets process-wide `prefect` logger levels and breaks DEBUG-log assertions in unrelated later tests on the same xdist worker. The fix is an autouse teardown fixture that calls `setup_logging(incremental=False)`.

<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: tests/AGENTS.md
Proposed text: One paragraph in "Flaky Tests": CLI tests that turn off test mode leak logging config through the CLI entrypoint's `setup_logging()` call. Restore it with an autouse fixture that calls `setup_logging(incremental=False)` on teardown.
Non-obvious evidence: The failure shows up far from its cause. #23297 fixed a flaky `TestWorkerLogging` test whose root cause was in `tests/cli/test_config.py`. The trigger is a `test_mode` guard in `src/prefect/cli/_app.py`, which you would not find while debugging a worker test.

title: Allow the provisioned ECS execution role to create CloudWatch log groups
body:
closes #20237

This PR lets the execution role created by `prefect work-pool create --type ecs:push --provision-infra` create CloudWatch log groups, and adds that permission to roles created by earlier versions when provisioning is run again.

`AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy` allows `logs:CreateLogStream` and `logs:PutLogEvents` but not `logs:CreateLogGroup`. The ECS worker sets `awslogs-create-group: "true"` when `configure_cloudwatch_logs` is enabled, so tasks failed to start with the `AccessDeniedException` in the issue.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `ExecutionRoleResource` now puts an inline role policy, `PrefectEcsTaskExecutionRoleLogsPolicy`, that allows only `logs:CreateLogGroup`. The other two log actions already come from the AWS managed policy, so they are not repeated.
- Whether the role needs the policy is checked separately from whether the role exists (`get_role_policy`). This covers the upgrade path @desertaxle raised on #21805: an existing role without the policy now shows up in the planned actions and the task count, and gets the policy on the next run. A role that already has it is left alone.
- An inline policy keeps the change scoped to the role and makes the re-run idempotent (`put_role_policy` overwrites by name), so no extra customer-managed policy has to be looked up across pages of `list_policies`.
- `Resource` is `*` because the log group name can be overridden through `cloudwatch_logs_options`; the default is `prefect`.
- The docs list of IAM permissions needed to run the provisioner gains `iam:GetRolePolicy` and `iam:PutRolePolicy`.

Tests in `tests/infrastructure/provisioners/test_ecs.py` (moto):

- a new role gets `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy` plus the logs policy, with the exact statement asserted
- an existing role without the logs policy (new `existing_execution_role_without_logs_policy` fixture) requires provisioning, lists one planned action, counts one task, and gets the policy on `provision()`
- `existing_execution_role` now represents a fully provisioned role, so the "nothing to do" cases still assert no work
- task counts and planned actions for `AuthenticationResource` updated for the extra step

`uv run pytest tests/infrastructure/provisioners/test_ecs.py`: 85 passed. Without the source change, 10 of the 19 `TestExecutionRoleResource` and `TestAuthenticationResource` tests fail. `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

Reproduced with moto before the change: the provisioned role's policies allow `logs:CreateLogStream` and `logs:PutLogEvents` only, and a second provisioning run does not change that. After the change, both runs end with `logs:CreateLogGroup` allowed.

</details>

title: Fix flaky `StateFilter` discovery cap search test
body:
This PR fixes the flaky `searches beyond the discovery cap and keeps deleted selected names` test in `state-filter.test.tsx`. It failed on `main` in [UI v2 Checks run 40103970615](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40103970615) (commit 213a369488c4983e8c4e7256b6eb4b62ac5540d4) with `Unable to find role="menuitem" and name "Baseline, NOT Met"`.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

`useStateOptions` debounces the search query by 300ms before it sends the `/observed-states?query=Base` request. The test types "Base" and then calls `findByRole`, which waits 1000ms by default. The 300ms debounce, the MSW response, and the re-render all had to finish inside that 1000ms. Instrumented local runs showed that the time from the end of typing to the request was 300–510ms under load. On a busy CI runner, the full sequence can go above 1000ms.

The fix uses `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })` in this test, with `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers })`. The test then calls `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300)` after it types. This advances the debounce on purpose, so the debounce does not use the `findByRole` wait time. `afterEach` restores real timers. This is the same pattern as `rich-date-range-selector.test.tsx`.

Verification:
- Before the fix, the test failed 1 of 3 times when run alone on its own.
- After the fix, it passed 24 of 24 runs (3 rounds of 8 parallel runs on 8 cores). The full file passes.
- `npm run lint` and `npm run check` pass.

</details>

title: Fix flaky `TestRemoteFileSystem` tree-project tests
body:
This PR fixes the flaky test `tests/test_filesystems.py::TestRemoteFileSystem::test_put_directory_put_file_count` (failed on `main` in [run 40024246163](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40024246163) with `assert 5 == 6`).

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

**Root cause:** The test reads `tests/test-projects/tree-project` directly. This directory is shared. Tests in `tests/utilities/test_importtools.py` import modules from `tree-project`. These imports write `__pycache__` entries into the directory. Under xdist, the two test files run at the same time on different workers (both ran in group 14 of the failed run).

`filter_files` walks the tree two times: one walk for `ignored_files`, one walk for `all_files`. If a `__pycache__/*.pyc` file appears between the two walks, the file is not in `ignored_files` but it is in `all_files`. Thus it is counted as included. `put_directory` does its own walks. The two counts in the test then can be different.

**Fix:** Add a `tree_project` fixture that copies `tree-project` (without `__pycache__`) into `tmp_path`. `test_put_directory_put_file_count` and `test_put_directory_tree` now use this private copy, so other workers cannot change the directory during the test.

**Verification:**
- Reproduced locally with a background script that creates and removes `tree-project/imports/__pycache__/*.pyc` in a loop: the original test failed with the same count mismatch.
- With the fix and the same background script: 25/25 runs passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_filesystems.py tests/utilities/test_importtools.py -n auto --maxprocesses 6`: 125 passed, 1 skipped.

title: docs: document Rich markup/emoji pitfall for CLI JSON output
body:
This PR adds one rule to `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`: print JSON and other verbatim user data with `markup=False, emoji=False`.

Rich `console.print` reads `[...]` as markup and `:name:` as emoji aliases. This silently changes JSON payloads, or raises `MarkupError` on a stray closing tag. #23530 fixed this for `prefect variable`, but many other `--output json` paths in `src/prefect/cli/` still call `_cli.console.print(json_output, soft_wrap=True)` without these flags. The rule tells future agents about the hazard before they add or change JSON output.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "**Print JSON and other verbatim user data with `markup=False, emoji=False`.** `console.print` otherwise parses `[...]` as Rich markup and `:name:` as emoji aliases, silently rewriting payloads (or raising `MarkupError` on stray closing tags). `print_json` and `Pretty` are not affected."
Non-obvious evidence: The shared console (`_app.py`) sets `highlight=False` but keeps Rich's markup and emoji parsing on. Corruption only occurs when user data contains brackets or `:alias:` text, so normal tests do not find it. Before #23530 no CLI code passed `markup=False`. Verified locally: `console.print('{"a": "[bold]x[/bold] :smile:"}')` outputs `{"a": "x 😄"}`, and `'[/red]'` raises `MarkupError`. `print_json(data=...)` and `Pretty(...)` keep the text unchanged.
Cross-cutting scope: All CLI command groups that emit JSON or echo user values through `_cli.console.print` (for example `deployment`, `flow_run`, `task_run`, `work_queue`, `artifact`, `concurrency_limit`, `global_concurrency_limit`, `profile`, `config`, `cloud`). This is not specific to `variable.py`.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule applies to each new output call in every command module. No single function owns it, so a comment in one place does not reach agents who edit other modules. The CLI AGENTS.md already holds the JSON-output contract next to this rule.
Durability: Rich defaults will not change, and new `--output json` commands are added often. The rule stays useful after #23530 is old.
Counter-evidence checked: `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md` (the JSON bullet covers mixing stray prints only), root `AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`, and `tests/AGENTS.md` (no mention of markup/emoji). `_app.py` console setup (no `markup=False`). `variable.py` has no explaining comment. `tests/cli/test_variable.py` covers only the variable commands.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Files changed in triggering push (6b8f5e6581..96b160acb0)</summary>

- `src/prefect/cli/variable.py`
- `tests/cli/test_variable.py`

</details>

### Checklist

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
  - No issue. This is a documentation-only AGENTS.md update after #23530.
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes func

@@ -6,6 +6,7 @@ Prefect command-line interface, powered by **cyclopts**.
 
 - **Use `rich` for all output.** Console output via `rich.console`, tables via `rich.table`, progress bars via `rich.progress`. Always use `exit_with_error` for error exits.
 - **Support JSON output whenever possible.** Commands should have a `--json` flag or equivalent for machine-readable output. Any diagnostic or informational `print()` calls must be suppressed when JSON output is active — mixing human-readable text with the JSON payload breaks machine consumers.

 - **Page through "all records" reads.** Client `read_*` list calls without `limit` return at most `PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT` (200) rows (server `LimitBody`), so `--all`/bulk commands must loop on `offset`. When deleting while paging, re-read from offset 0 each pass — advancing `offset` skips rows that shifted into earlier pages.
 - **Excluded from `prefect-client`** — the entire `cli/` directory is stripped during the client package build.

title: Bump lodash-es and mermaid in /ui-v2
body:
Bumps [lodash-es](https://github.com/lodash/lodash) to 4.18.1 and updates ancestor dependency [mermaid](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `lodash-es` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash-es's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

title: docs: document flow archival and restoration policies
body:
Refs [CLOUD-4655](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/CLOUD-4655/document-flow-archival).

This PR documents flow archival in Prefect Cloud so customers can retire flows without deleting run history and restore them when needed. It adds a guide for manual and bulk archival, the two workspace policies, API filtering, and older-client compatibility; updates the flows and automations concepts; and documents the three archival events and the archived-flow label on flow-run events.

The guide describes the current UI: the All and Favorites tabs with a menu for the Unarchived, All, and Archived views, **Pause and archive** for flows with schedules that are on, the warning for deployments that automations run, and the run block for archived flows while the Archived flow restoration policy is off.

<details>
<summary>Behavior and validation</summary>

The documentation follows the current nebula and nebula-ui implementation and the Prefect voice guide. Both policies are documented as off by default. The guide explains deployment schedule requirements, retention-limited inactivity windows, the dormant flow eligibility rules, gradual archival, and restoration when matching run events arrive.

The guide says archiving deletes a flow's scheduled runs that haven't started. That behavior is in a Prefect Cloud change that hasn't shipped yet, so this PR waits for it.

Validation:
- `mint broken-links` passed.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed.
- JSON examples, navigation entries, new internal links, and Mintlify-generated anchors checked.

Keep this PR in draft until the feature rollout is ready for customer-facing documentation.
</details>

title: Document OIDC identity tokens for Modal push work pools
body:
This PR adds one paragraph and an example to the Modal tab of the serverless push work pool guide (`docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployment_infra/serverless.mdx`).

<details>

The paragraph explains the new **Include OIDC Identity Token** work pool toggle. When it is on, Modal injects `MODAL_IDENTITY_TOKEN` into each sandbox. The paragraph links to [Modal's OIDC integration guide](https://modal.com/docs/guide/oidc-integration) for the AWS trust setup. It shows the `AWS_ROLE_ARN` + `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` pattern: write the token to a file, then let boto3 assume the role and re-assume it when the credentials expire. Runs that last longer than the role's maximum session duration continue to work.

The example uses `{/* pmd-metadata: notest */}` because it needs Modal and AWS credentials.

The Prefect Cloud change that adds the toggle is tracked in the internal ticket CLOUD-5439.

</details>

     This allows Prefect Cloud to securely interact with your Modal account.
+
+    To let flow runs authenticate with AWS without static keys, enable **Include OIDC Identity Token**. Modal then
+    injects a signed identity token into each sandbox as the `MODAL_IDENTITY_TOKEN` environment variable; see
+    Modal's [OIDC integration guide](https://modal.com/docs/guide/oidc-integration) to configure AWS to trust it and
+    create the IAM role to assume. Set `AWS_ROLE_ARN` to that role in the work pool's environment variables, then
+    write the token to a file and point `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` at it before creating any boto3 clients.
+    boto3 then assumes the role from the token file and re-assumes it whenever the temporary credentials expire,
+    so runs that last longer than the role's maximum session duration keep working. Each re-assumption reuses the
+    same token, because Modal sets `MODAL_IDENTITY_TOKEN` once when the sandbox starts. Further credential
+    refreshes require an unexpired identity token; its `exp` claim gives the expiration time:
+
+    {/* pmd-metadata: notest */}

+    from pathlib import Path
+
+    import boto3
+    from prefect import flow
+
+
+    @flow
+    def list_reports():
+        token_file = Path("/tmp/modal-identity-token")
+        token_file.write_text(os.environ["MODAL_IDENTITY_TOKEN"])
+        os.environ["AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE"] = str(token_file)
+
+        s3 = boto3.client("s3")
+        print(s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket="my-reports-bucket").get("KeyCount"))

v3.2.12

Patch-release GraphQL-core v3.2.12, based on GraphQL.js v16.14.2.

This patch-release supports Python 3.7 to 3.14.

This is a security release. It fixes two denial-of-service vulnerabilities in the validator and the parser. Upgrading is recommended for all users.

Security fixes:

  • CVE-2026-75507 (GHSA-vj8h-fx38-h3vc, High) — the OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged validation rule could be driven into quadratic and worse running time by a small, highly compressible query using repeated inline fragments, occupying a worker for minutes of CPU during validation, before any resolver runs. Validation now enforces a per-document comparison budget and aborts with a GraphQLError once it is exhausted.
  • CVE-2026-75508 (GHSA-r77w-qph3-7vf8, High) — comment tokens were allocated and retained but not counted toward the parser's max_tokens limit, so a comment-padded document could bypass the limit while allocating one token object per comment. max_tokens now counts every token the parser consumes, including skipped comments.

Please note the two behaviour changes this implies:

  • A pathological query that previously validated — slowly — now produces a validation error. Realistic queries stay far below the limit, which defaults to 250,000 field comparisons and can be adjusted by assigning to graphql.validation.rules.overlapping_fields_can_be_merged.MAX_FIELD_COMPARISONS.
  • Comments now count toward max_tokens, so a comment-heavy document that was previously accepted may now be rejected. If you parse documents with substantial comments and set max_tokens, you may need to raise the limit. The token_count of a parsed document now includes comments as well.

Both limits complement, but do not replace, a request body-size limit applied to the decompressed request body in your web framework.

Other changes:

  • Updated development dependencies and CI tooling.

The security issues were reported by @​BZHunt, who also reviewed the fixes before release. In memory of ZaX, who was the driving force behind this discovery. The first one was also independently found and diagnosed by @​bcmyguest.

Release notes

Sourced from virtualenv's releases.

21.14.9

Bugfixes - 21.14.9

  • Parse VIRTUALENV_PERIODIC_UPDATE_INSECURE as a boolean, so 0, false, no and off keep certificate verification enabled. (#3398)

  • Reject destinations whose resolved path contains the platform's PATH separator, including separators inherited from the working directory or a directory symlink. (#3399)

  • Preserve an existing pyvenv.cfg when a prompt or configuration value cannot be encoded as UTF-8, instead of leaving the file empty after a failed environment creation. The file now ends its lines with LF on every platform.

    Debug logs show each configuration line as a Python string literal, so control characters are visible. (#3400)

  • Skip writing a .venv redirect when the environment name contains a line boundary. The environment is still created, and any existing redirect remains unchanged. (#3401)

  • Preserve non-ASCII values in activate_this.py when applications read the script with a legacy text encoding before executing it. (#3402)

  • Reject malformed seed versions and requirements ending in archive suffixes before starting pip, with an error identifying the invalid value instead of a misleading download or local-file error. (#3403)

  • Allow a literal percent sign as a csh prompt and preserve carets in tcsh prompt display instead of interpreting them as control-character notation.

    Separate csh history and prompt escapes from preceding non-ASCII text in legacy locales. (#3404)

  • Report an error when an existing pyvenv.cfg is not a regular file, instead of trying to read or write directories, pipes, or devices as configuration files. (#3405)

  • Preserve percent-containing paths during batch reactivation and show dollar signs literally in command prompts. Skip batch scripts for paths containing line boundaries, and remove stale batch scripts for unsupported paths even when only other activators are selected. (

title: docs: document whenever 0.11 compat rules in prefect AGENTS.md
body:
This PR updates the `whenever` compat bullet in `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` for whenever 0.11 (now allowed by #23164).

The bullet now says:
- Compat flags use feature detection, not version checks: `_WHENEVER_NEW_API` (>= 0.10.0) and `_SYSTEM_TZ` (>= 0.11).
- Do not call `.assume_system_tz()` / `.to_system_tz()` directly. They are deprecated in 0.11, and the deprecation warning fails tests because pytest uses `filterwarnings = error`. Use `in_local_tz()`.
- Do not import `DateTimeDelta` directly. It is removed in 0.11. Use the `Interval` alias.

The edit changes one line in place (net 0 lines).

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: Replace "abstract over API differences between whenever 0.7.x–0.9.x and ≥ 0.10.0. The `_WHENEVER_NEW_API` flag ... guards version-specific code." with a statement that the helpers cover supported whenever releases through feature-detection flags (`_WHENEVER_NEW_API`, `_SYSTEM_TZ`). Add `.assume_system_tz()`/`.to_system_tz()` (use `in_local_tz()`) and direct `DateTimeDelta` imports (use `Interval`) to the existing list of forbidden direct whenever calls.
Non-obvious evidence: The only note about the 0.11 change is one inline comment in `types/_datetime.py`. Code outside that module cannot see it. I confirmed on whenever 0.11.0 that `assume_system_tz()` and `to_system_tz()` emit `WheneverDeprecationWarning`. `pyproject.toml` sets `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]`, so a new direct call fails tests on Python 3.13+ only. `whenever.DateTimeDelta` does not exist in 0.11.0.
Cross-cutting scope: All Python 3.13+ datetime code in `src/prefect/` (client and server). For example, `server/schemas/schedules.py` needed a matching `DateTimeDelta` fix in the same push.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule is about code written outside `types/_datetime.py`. Contributors read the AGENTS.md bullet before they write new datetime code. They do not read a comment inside the helper module first.
Durability: The repo supports a range of whenever versions (`>=0.10.5,<0.12.0`), so the feature-detection pattern and these forbidden calls stay relevant until the lower bound moves past 0.11.
Counter-evidence checked: The existing `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` whenever bullet (it was stale: it named only 0.7–0.10 differences). `tests/fixtures/AGENTS.md` (only pendulum/`frozen_time` guidance). The inline comments and `in_local_tz()` in `types/_datetime.py`. The `schedules.py` fallback. No other AGENTS.md mentions whenever 0.11, `SYSTEM_TZ`, or `DateTimeDelta`.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Files changed in the triggering push (0d5d47a..e516d51, #23164)</summary>

- `client/pyproject.toml`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `scripts/proxy-test/requirements.txt`
- `src/integrations/prefect-dask/pyproject.toml`
- `src/prefect/server/schemas/schedules.py`
- `src/prefect/types/_datetime.py`
- `uv.lock`
</details>

Avoid no-argument `datetime.datetime.now()` because it returns a tz-naive datetime that raises `TypeError` when compared to the tz-aware datetimes produced by `now()`. Explicitly timezone-aware stdlib calls such as `datetime.now(ZoneInfo("UTC"))` are allowed when needed to preserve timezone information. Never call `ZonedDateTime.from_py_datetime()`, `PlainDateTime.from_py_datetime()`, or `.py_datetime()` directly — use the helpers instead. The task engine emits `prefect.task_run.*` events (delivered via WebSockets) but advances state locally through `set_state` calls with polling/backoff — do not assume the two engines work the same way.

The task engine, by contrast, manages state transitions locally via `set_state` and emits `prefect.task_run.*` events — it does not propose states to the server.

Any `wait_for` futures must be waited on in the parent process and converted to `State` objects before submission. The subprocess task engine handles `State` objects via `resolve_to_final_result`, which raises `UpstreamTaskError` for non-completed upstreams.

title: Lock current prefect-redis and prefect-kubernetes for the Docker image
body:
closes #23536

This PR updates `uv.lock` to prefect-redis 0.3.0 and prefect-kubernetes 0.8.0, which the Docker image installs since #23225. It also fixes the reason the lock fell behind.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

### Root cause

Dependency bots clone without tags (see the existing comment in `pyproject.toml`). In those clones versioningit uses `default-tag`, so the local `prefect` resolves as `3.6.24+...`. Newer integration releases need a newer `prefect`:

| Package | Last release `uv lock` can pick at 3.6.24 | First release it can't pick | Floor of that release |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| prefect-redis | 0.2.11 | 0.2.12 | `prefect>=3.7.4` |
| prefect-kubernetes | 0.7.x | 0.7.13 | `prefect>=3.8.4` |

So every lock update from those clones kept, or moved the lock back to, these old releases. Reproduced in a `git clone --depth 1 --no-tags` checkout: `uv lock --upgrade-package prefect-kubernetes --upgrade-package prefect-redis` moved the lock *down* to 0.7.7 / 0.2.11 (resolver output: `prefect-kubernetes >0.7.13 depends on prefect >=3.8.4`).

### Changes

- `pyproject.toml`: raise versioningit `default-version` / `default-tag` from 3.6.24 to 3.9.0. That is at or above the highest in-repo integration floor, which is now `prefect>=3.8.4`.
- `uv.lock`: `uv lock --upgrade-package prefect-redis --upgrade-package prefect-kubernetes`. Only these two entries change.
- `tests/_internal/test_integrations.py`: new test that both fallback versions satisfy the `prefect` requirement of every `src/integrations/*/pyproject.toml`. It fails on `main` (`3.6.24+nogit` does not satisfy `prefect>=3.8.4` from prefect-aws). So the next time an integration raises its floor, the test will flag that the fallback needs raising too.

### Verification

- In the tagless clone with this branch: `uv lock --check` passes, and re-running the upgrade keeps 0.8.0 / 0.3.0. Before this change it downgraded them.
- Installed `.[redis,kubernetes,client,otel]` with `--constraint` from `uv export --frozen --no-dev --all-extras --no-emit-project --no-hashes`, the same command the Dockerfile runs. Result: prefect-redis 0.3.0 and prefect-kubernetes 0.8.0, and `import prefect_redis.cleanup_queue` works.
- Did not run a full `docker build` locally. The existing `uv sync --check` step in `run-docker-tests` checks that the image matches the lock.

### Not changed

Other integrations are also behind their latest releases in the lock, for example prefect-aws 0.7.7 vs 0.7.12 and prefect-gcp 0.6.17 vs 0.6.22. The published image flavors don't install them, so this PR leaves them alone. Now that the fallback is fixed, a normal lock refresh can update them.

</details>

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
