title: Retry flows that return a failed state when `retries` is configured
body:
closes #23534

This PR makes flow-level `retries` work when a flow *returns* a state (or futures/states) that resolve to `Failed`, instead of raising.

<details>

Before, `RetryFailedFlows` on the server turned the proposed `Failed` into `AwaitingRetry` and set `retry_type="in_process"`. `handle_exception` and `handle_timeout` catch this case and go back to `Running`. `handle_success` (sync and async) did not, so the engine loop exited. The run was left in `AwaitingRetry`, and workers skip `in_process` runs, so nothing ever picked it up.

`handle_success` now does the same check in both engines, but only when the proposed terminal state was failed (`terminal_state.is_failed() and state.is_scheduled()`). In that case it logs, resets `_return_value` to `NotSet`, sets `Running`, and returns early, which skips the success telemetry and the result linking. Resetting `_return_value` matters: `run_context` re-raises exceptions whenever `_return_value` is set, so without the reset, an exception on the retry attempt would skip `handle_exception`. When a flow explicitly returns `Scheduled()` or `AwaitingRetry()`, that state is kept and the body is not re-run.

Tests in `TestFlowRetries` cover:
- sync and async flows that return `Failed` every time (body runs twice, ends `Failed`)
- sync and async flows that return `Failed` first and then succeed
- a flow that returns `Failed` first and then raises
- a flow that returns a submitted task future whose task fails on the first attempt
- sync and async flows that return `Scheduled`/`AwaitingRetry`, with `retries=0` and `retries=1` (state is kept, body runs once)

Reproduced with the script from the issue: before, `body runs=1 SCHEDULED/AwaitingRetry retry_type='in_process'`; after, `body runs=2 FAILED/Failed retry_type=None`.

</details>

title: Read `.env` once per process when loading settings
body:
closes #23532

This PR makes `import prefect` open `./.env` one time instead of 216 times (FIFO) or 324 times (regular file). This stops the startup stall when `.env` is a 1Password Environments mount (a FIFO).

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The issue says all reads come from `FilteredDotEnvSettingsSource`. Measurement shows three sources of reads per settings class load (54 classes, 2 loads each during import):

| Caller | Opens (before) |
|---|---|
| pydantic-settings default `DotEnvSettingsSource` (built in `BaseSettings._settings_init_sources`, then discarded by `PrefectBaseSettings.settings_customise_sources`) | 108 |
| `FilteredDotEnvSettingsSource` | 108 |
| `_get_profiles_path` (regular files only) | 108 |

Changes:

- `src/prefect/settings/sources.py`: add `_read_dotenv_file`. It caches the raw `.env` contents in the existing `_file_cache` TTL cache (the same cache as `_read_toml_file`, cleared with `_file_cache.clear()`). Each call parses the cached contents with `dotenv.dotenv_values(stream=...)`, so `${VAR}` interpolation uses the current environment.
  - Regular files: the cache key includes inode, size and `st_mtime_ns`, so a changed `.env` is read again.
  - FIFOs: the cache key does not include `stat` data, so the file is read again after the TTL (60 s).
  - `_dotenv_file_lock` serializes loads, so concurrent cache misses open the file once.
  - `FilteredDotEnvSettingsSource._read_env_file` and `_get_profiles_path` use this function.
- `src/prefect/settings/base.py`: `build_settings_config` now sets `env_file` to `_DEFAULT_ENV_FILE`, an empty `_DefaultEnvFile` tuple. The default pydantic-settings dotenv source therefore has no file to read, and `PrefectBaseSettings.settings_customise_sources` passes `.env` to `FilteredDotEnvSettingsSource` in its place. Any other `env_file` value set by a subclass (a path, or `None` to not load a dotenv file) is passed through unchanged, as before.

Result with `repros/23532.py` (the issue's script):

```
before: .env opened 216 times during `import prefect`   (FIFO)
        .env opened 324 times during `import prefect`   (regular file)
after:  .env opened 1 times during `import prefect`     (FIFO and regular file)
```

Also checked with pydantic-settings 2.9.1 (lowest supported), 2.14.2 (locked) and 2.16.1.

Tests (in `TestSettingsSources`):
- `test_dotenv_file_read_once_across_settings_sources`
- `test_dotenv_file_changes_are_reloaded`
- `test_dotenv_fifo_read_once_across_settings_sources` (a thread serves the FIFO; skipped on pydantic-settings < 2.14, which does not read FIFOs)
- `test_dotenv_file_read_once_by_concurrent_settings_loads`
- `test_dotenv_file_interpolation_uses_current_environment`
- `test_env_file_can_be_overridden` (custom path, and the `env_file=None` opt-out)

`tests/test_settings.py`, `tests/cli/test_config.py` and `tests/cli/test_profile.py` pass.

</details>

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"

+def _read_dotenv_file(path: Path, encoding: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str | None]:
+    """Read a dotenv file, sharing its contents across all settings sources.
+
+    Each settings class builds its own dotenv source, so without a cache `.env`
+    is opened once per settings class every time settings are loaded. Regular
+    files are re-read when they change. FIFOs (e.g. 1Password Environments
+    mounts) are slow to open and their `stat` may not reflect content
+    changes, so they are re-read once the cache TTL expires.

+    Only the file contents are cached. Values are parsed on each call, so
+    `${VAR}` interpolation uses the current environment. Loads are serialized
+    so that concurrent cache misses open the file only once.
+    """
+    path_stat = path.stat()
+    if stat.S_ISFIFO(path_stat.st_mode):
+        version = "fifo"
+    else:
+        version = f"{path_stat.st_ino}:{path_stat.st_size}:{path_stat.st_mtime_ns}"
+    cache_key = f"dotenv_file:{path.absolute()}:{encoding}:{version}"

+            with _file_cache_lock:

+    def test_dotenv_fifo_read_once_across_settings_sources(
+        self,
+        monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+        tmp_path: Path,
+        dotenv_opens: list[str],

+        """Regression test for https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23532
+
+        1Password Environments mounts `.env` as a FIFO, where every open is
+        served by 1Password, so it must only be read once.
+        """
+        monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
+        os.mkfifo(".env")
+        stop = threading.Event()
+
+        def serve() -> None:
+            while not stop.is_set():
+                fd = os.open(".env", os.O_WRONLY)
+                try:
+                    os.write(fd, b"PREFECT_API_URL=http://from-fifo:4200/api\n")
+                except BrokenPipeError:
+                    pass
+                finally:
+                    os.close(fd)
+
+        server = threading.Thread(target=serve, daemon=True)
+        server.start()
+        try:
+            assert Settings().api.url == "http://from-fifo:4200/api"
+            assert Settings().api.url == "http://from-fifo:4200/api"
+        finally:
+            stop.set()
+            # unblock the server if it is waiting for a reader
+            fd = os.open(".env", os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NONBLOCK)

title: Cache `get_timezones()`
body:
Cache `get_timezones()` so schedule validation stops rescanning tzdata.

`get_timezones()` calls `zoneinfo.available_timezones()`, which walks the tzdata files on disk (~2.5 ms) on every call. It runs whenever a schedule with a `timezone` is validated, which includes every schedule the server reads from the database. Validation is synchronous, so these scans block the event loop in the scheduler service and in worker deployment reads.

The function returns an immutable tuple, so this PR adds `@cache`.

### Impact

```python
import time
from prefect.client.schemas.schedules import CronSchedule

N = 1000
start = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(N):
    CronSchedule(cron="*/5 * * * *", timezone="America/New_York")
print(f"{(time.perf_counter() - start) / N * 1000:.3f} ms per validation")
```

| | Per validation | Scheduler pass, 500 deployments |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 2.56 ms | 7.0 s (3.9 s in `get_timezones`) |
| After | 0.04 ms | 2.7 s |

**Tradeoff:** tzdata is read once per process, so a tzdata update made while a process is running won't be picked up until it restarts. This matches prefect.types.TimeZone, which already builds its list once at import.

### Tests

Added `test_get_timezones_scans_tzdata_once`: validating two schedules calls `available_timezones()` exactly once.

I used Claude to help write the regression test and this description. I reproduced the issue, ran the benchmarks and the tests locally, and reviewed the change myself.

title: Preserve literal markup and emoji aliases in variable CLI JSON output
body:
closes #23529

This PR stops Rich from changing variable values in machine-readable output. `prefect variable get`, `prefect variable inspect --output json`, and `prefect variable ls --output json` now print serialized JSON with `markup=False` and `emoji=False`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- Before this change, Rich parsed the JSON text as markup. A value such as `[red]literal[/red]` became `literal`, and `:smile:` became an emoji. A value such as `literal [/unexpected]` caused `rich.errors.MarkupError`.
- `variable get` now also uses `soft_wrap=True`, so long values do not get line breaks at the terminal width when `PREFECT_CLI_WRAP_LINES` is enabled. The two `--output json` paths already used it.
- Human-readable output (the `ls` table and the `inspect` pretty view) and the global console do not change.
- New parametrized tests check that the decoded JSON is equal to the stored value for markup, emoji aliases, an unmatched closing tag, a 1000-character string, and a nested object. The tests run with `PREFECT_CLI_WRAP_LINES=True` and give the variable literal markup/emoji tags, which `inspect` and `ls` JSON must also keep. All 15 new cases fail on `main` and pass with this change.

Other CLI commands use the same `console.print(json_output, soft_wrap=True)` pattern. This PR does not change them, to keep the scope to the reported issue.

</details>

title: Bump stale integration pins in uv.lock and keep them current on release
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23524
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23536

this PR:
- bumps every `prefect-*` pin in `uv.lock` that was behind PyPI — kubernetes 0.7.6→0.8.0, redis 0.2.11→0.3.0, aws 0.7.7→0.7.12, azure 0.4.8→0.4.13, bitbucket 0.3.6→0.3.7, docker 0.7.1→0.7.4, email 0.4.2→0.4.3, gcp 0.6.17→0.6.22, github 0.4.2→0.4.4, gitlab 0.3.4→0.3.5, ray 0.5.0→0.6.0, shell 0.3.6→0.3.7, slack 0.3.1→0.4.0, snowflake 0.28.8→0.28.9
- adds a workflow that keeps `uv.lock` integration pins current going forward, via a release-tag-triggered bump plus a weekly sweep

<details>

Since the Dockerfile installs extras via `uv pip install --constraint /dist/constraints.txt` (generated from `uv export --frozen --all-extras`), the images ship whatever version of each integration `uv.lock` pins — and every integration pin constrains every image flavor. The lock held stale pins since 3.6.24: kubernetes 0.7.6 (3.8.1 images shipped 0.7.11, missing the observer fix from #22965 released in 0.7.13) and redis 0.2.11 (3.8.7 images shipped 0.2.15, missing `prefect_redis.cleanup_queue` added in 0.2.12), so upgrading images downgraded bundled integrations.

Bumps generated with `uv lock --upgrade-package <pkg>` for each stale pin. Verified `uv export --frozen --no-dev --all-extras` now constrains `prefect-kubernetes==0.8.0` and `prefect-redis==0.3.0`. The only non-integration lock change is setuptools 83.0.0→80.10.2, required by prefect-azure 0.4.13's `setuptools<81` constraint.

The new workflow (`.github/workflows/update-uv-lock-integrations.yaml`) keeps pins current two ways:
- **Tag push** — fires on the same `prefect-<name>-<semver>` tag pushes as `integration-package-release.yaml`, runs `uv lock --upgrade-package <released package>` on main, and opens a PR. No-ops for tags whose package isn't in the lock, when the pin is already current, or when a bump branch exists.
- **Weekly sweep** (Mondays 15:00 UTC, also `workflow_dispatch`) — upgrades every `prefect-*` pin behind PyPI and opens one PR, as a backstop for releases cut before the tag-triggered path existed or any bump PR that was missed.

</details>

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
  - Lockfile bumps verified via the constraint export output locally; the workflow only triggers on tag pushes and a weekly schedule.

title: Fix `KubernetesJobRun.wait_for_completion` raising on interim K8s 1.31+ Job conditions
body:
closes #23525

This PR makes `KubernetesJobRun.await_for_completion` treat only `Complete=True` (success) and `Failed=True` (failure) as terminal. Before this, any `True` condition other than `Complete` counted as a failure. On Kubernetes 1.31+ a Job can first show `SuccessCriteriaMet` or `FailureTarget` before its terminal condition is set, and in that window the method raised `RuntimeError: Job '...' failed due to []`, even for jobs that went on to succeed.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The loop now works out which condition types are `True` once per poll. It reuses that set for the existing `job_is_terminal` log-capture check and for the completion branch.
- When no terminal condition is present, the loop sleeps for `interval_seconds` and counts that time toward `timeout_seconds`. This also covers jobs with `active=0` and no conditions, where the old loop polled again immediately with no sleep.
- Added tests for `SuccessCriteriaMet` followed by `Complete`, which now succeeds, and `FailureTarget` followed by `Failed`, which now raises with the real reason. Both tests fail without this change.

</details>

Returning `Failed` state caches the exception and later calls skip execution.

Check this example:

```python
from uuid import uuid4

from prefect import task
from prefect.cache_policies import INPUTS
from prefect.states import Failed

attempts = 0

@task(cache_policy=INPUTS)
def charge_customer(order_id: str):
    global attempts
    attempts += 1

    if attempts == 1:
        return Failed(data=ValueError("Payment API temporarily unavailable"))

    return {"order_id": order_id, "status": "paid"}

order_id = str(uuid4())

first = charge_customer(order_id, return_state=True)
print(first.name, first.type.value, attempts)
# Failed FAILED 1

second = charge_customer(order_id, return_state=True)
print(second.name, second.type.value, attempts)
# Cached COMPLETED 1

print(repr(second.result()))  # Returns normally; does not raise.
# ValueError('Payment API temporarily unavailable')
```

Fixed by excluding peristed failures from sync and async tasks.

title: fix(cli/automation): delete every automation with prefect automation delete --all
body:
closes #23504

### Summary

This PR fixes `prefect automation delete --all` so that it pages through all automations rather than reading only the first page returned by `client.read_automations()` (which defaults to `PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, 200 rows). It mirrors the fix applied to `prefect deployment delete --all` in #23440.

### Root Cause & Changes

- **Accurate total count for confirmation**: Pages `client.read_automations(offset=total)` until an empty page is returned, summing page lengths to report the true count before prompting the user.
- **Safe repeated deletion**: Repeatedly reads and deletes from the start of the list until no automations remain. Reading from offset 0 ensures the result set continuously shrinks without being affected by sorting instability across page boundaries.
- **Verification**: Added `test_deleting_all_automations_across_pages` in `tests/events/client/cli/test_automations.py` to verify multi-page pagination and deletion count.

title: Refresh pip and Conda CA trust in Prefect 2 images
body:
This PR refreshes pip's separate CA bundle and Conda's base environment in Prefect 2 images, then blocks image builds that still trust an affected eMudhra root in the OS, certifi, or pip store. It builds on #23512 and adds an explicit `certifi>=2026.10.19` dependency floor.

**Depends on #23512.** This branch includes its two commits; merge that PR first so this diff shows only the supplemental hardening.

<details>
<summary>Python compatibility and validation</summary>

Python 3.10+ uses patched pip >=26.2.2. title: Refresh and verify Docker image CA trust stores
body:
This PR refreshes the OS, pip, and Conda trust stores in Prefect and prefect-client images, then fails the image build if any of those stores or certifi still trusts an affected eMudhra root. #23483 updated certifi and uv; pip's vendored bundle and Conda's base environment need separate handling.

<summary>Validation and coverage</summary>

- Seven offline tests pass on Python 3.11, including direct and cross-signed incident chains, each compromised trust store, and OpenSSL's lazily loaded CA directory.
- Targeted Linux container smoke checks pass for the updated OS/certifi/pip stores on Python 3.8 and for the Conda base bootstrap. These exercise the installation steps without building the Prefect application locally.
- Pre-commit checks pass.
- The dedicated trust-test CI matrix passes on Python 3.11–3.15. Final image checks run after optional extra packages are installed and cover both the active environment and Conda base.

Fixtures are public certificates from the [incident disclosure](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/); verification uses a fixed time to avoid certificate expiration masking trust.

Merging this PR does not refresh already published image tags. Rebuild and publish the intended tags with fresh layers, then verify the resulting image digests. Historical Python 3.10 images need the separate backport; the current release matrix starts at Python 3.11.

No API or usage documentation changes are needed: this updates image trust data and adds publication checks.

title: Skip unset Pydantic private attributes when rebuilding models in `visit_collection`
body:
closes #23514

This PR fixes task input resolution for Pydantic models that have a private attribute without a value (for example `_cache: dict = PrivateAttr()`).

When `visit_collection` changes a public field, it rebuilds the model with `model_construct` and then copies the private attributes. Before this change, it called `getattr` for each name in `__private_attributes__`. An unset private attribute has no value, so `getattr` raised `AttributeError`, and `resolve_inputs` / `resolve_inputs_sync` raised a `PrefectException`.

Now it copies only the values in `__pydantic_private__`. Pydantic stores private attribute values there, and unset attributes are not in it. Private attributes that have values are copied as before and are not traversed.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- `tests/utilities/test_collections.py`: rebuild of mutable and frozen models with no private attributes set, only the implicit `_y` set, and only the explicit `_z` set. Set values are kept; unset attributes stay unset.
- `tests/test_task_engine.py`: sync and async tasks that receive a model with a quoted field and an unset `PrivateAttr()`. These cover `resolve_inputs_sync` and `resolve_inputs`.

All new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. No docs change is necessary because this is a bug fix with no change to the public API.
</details>

title: Read metric triggers on metrics this version doesn't know
body:
Reading an automation with a metric trigger on a metric this client doesn't know now keeps the metric name as a string instead of raising a `ValidationError`.

## The problem

`MetricTriggerQuery.name` is the closed enum `PrefectMetric`: `lateness`, `duration` and `successes`. Prefect Cloud also supports metric triggers on `volume`, `sla_violations` and `sla_violations_by_severity`. Any automation that uses one fails to parse:

```python
Automation.model_validate({..., "trigger": {"type": "metric", "metric": {"name": "volume", ...}}})
# pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Automation
# trigger.metric.metric.name
#   Input should be 'lateness', 'duration' or 'successes' [type=enum, input_value='volume', input_type=str]
```

`read_automations()` parses the whole response at once, so **one such automation breaks the call for the whole workspace**. `prefect automation ls`, `prefect transfer` and `Automation.read()` all fail. This is the trigger-side version of #23426, which did the same for unknown action types. 3.9.0 includes that fix and still fails here.

## The change

- **`MetricTriggerQuery.name` is `Union[PrefectMetric, str]`, validated left to right.** Known names still parse as `PrefectMetric` members, so code that compares against `PrefectMetric` keeps working. An unknown name stays a string.
- **Round trips are lossless.** `Automation.update()` rebuilds an `AutomationCore` from `model_dump()`, and the string survives that, so updating the automation (for example, enabling it) sends the name back unchanged.
- **`describe_for_cli()`** shows an unknown name as is, for example `Metric: volume < 1.0 for 1 day, 0:00:00`.
- **`prefect transfer` skips automations with an unknown metric name**, including one inside a compound or sequence trigger. It reports `TransferSkipped("Uses metrics this version of Prefect does not recognize: ...")` in the results table, as it does for unknown action types. This version can't check whether the destination supports the metric.

### Why a left-to-right union rather than a discriminator

#23426 used a discriminator so that a known action type with invalid fields would still fail validation. A metric name is a bare string with no fields of its own, so there's no invalid known case for a fallback to hide. `union_mode="left_to_right"` keeps known names as enum members. Pydantic's default smart mode would turn them into plain strings.

## Behavior changes to note

- The static type of `MetricTriggerQuery.name` is now `Union[PrefectMetric, str]`. Code that reads `name.value` must handle a string. `isinstance` checks and comparisons with `PrefectMetric` members are unaffected.
- The client no longer catches a misspelled metric name such as `MetricTriggerQuery(name="latness", ...)` before it's sent. The server rejects it on create.
- Clients without this change still fail on these automations. Only clients that include this change benefit.

## Tests

- `tests/events/client/test_automations_schema.py`, `

title: Drop the eMudhra-compromised CA roots from 2.x images
body:
The published 2.x images still trust two CA roots named in the eMudhra intermediate CA compromise advisory: emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and Comodo AAA Services. Outbound TLS from these images, including client calls to the Prefect API, accepts a certificate for any hostname that the compromised intermediates signed.

Debian has shipped `ca-certificates` updates that remove both roots (`20250419+deb13u1` on trixie, `20250419~deb12u2` on bookworm). The 2.x images do not receive them. The `python:3.8`/`3.9`/`3.10-slim` bases are no longer rebuilt upstream, and the 2.x final stage never runs `apt-get upgrade`. This PR adds that upgrade to the final stage. The 3.x Dockerfile on `main` already does this, and the current 3.x images on Python 3.11+ trust neither root.

certifi needs no change. The eager `pip install --upgrade` already resolves certifi 2026.10.19 on every build, and that release drops both roots.

### Example

Built locally from this branch and from `origin/2.x` on the same day, default flavor unless noted:

| Image | `ca-certificates` | Trusted root links in `/etc/ssl/certs` |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/2.x`, Python 3.10 | `20250419` | 2 |
| this branch, Python 3.10 | `20250419+deb13u1` | 0 |
| this branch, Python 3.8 (bookworm) | `20250419~deb12u2` | 0 |
| this branch, Python 3.10, `-conda` | `20250419+deb13u1` | 0 |

The published `2-latest` image (pushed 2026-09-02) has 2 links and certifi 2026.07.22, which still includes emSign ECC Root CA - G3. In the `-conda` flavor, Python reads conda's own bundle, and conda's `ca-certificates` 2026.10.20 also has neither root. `prefect version` passes in each build.

Not covered: the `git>=1:2.47.3` line in the same `RUN` is unquoted, so the shell reads `>=1:2.47.3` as a redirect and apt installs the distro's git. The bookworm-based Python 3.8 image ships git 2.39.5. That fix belongs in a separate PR.

### Checklist

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
	- No issue exists. This is a small fix.
- [ ] If this pull request adds new functionality, it includes unit tests that cover the changes
	- No new functionality.
- [ ] This pull request includes a label categorizing the change e.g. `maintenance`, `fix`, `feature`, `enhancement`, `docs`.

## Rollout caveats

- `rollout: merging to 2.x publishes nothing.` The image workflow builds on pushes to `main` only, and its recovery dispatch rebuilds an existing tag's own Dockerfile. The fix reaches `prefecthq/prefect` only through a new 2.x release (2.20.27).
- `rollout: older patch tags stay unpatched.` Images such as `2.20.25-python3.10` are never rebuilt. Users pinned to one need to move to the new patch release.
- `watch: build time per matrix cell.` The upgrade adds a package-upgrade step to all 15 cells, including QEMU arm64 builds.

<summary>Session context</summary>

This came out of customer questions about the eMudhra advisory. We checked the published OSS images: the 3.x images on Python

title: Fix background worker shutdown hang when worker cancellation is lost
body:
This PR makes `background_worker` shutdown rely on exiting the docket `Worker` context, not just on `worker_task.cancel()`. It fixes the flaky `test_client_runs_migrations_for_two_different_ephemeral_apps[True]` failure on main ([run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39633388366), Python 3.11 only), where the app lifespan shutdown hung until `asgi_lifespan` gave up after 30s.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

On Python 3.11, `asyncio.wait_for` drops a cancellation if the inner future finishes in the same loop iteration. Python 3.12 rewrote `wait_for` and doesn't have this problem. docket's worker calls `wait_for` (through `_wait_for_event`) while it waits for its cancellation listener to start. If an app's lifespan opens and closes right away, as in this test, `worker_task.cancel()` can arrive in that window and get dropped. The worker then keeps running forever, and the old `await worker_task` inside the `Worker` context never returns.

The fix:
- `background_worker` still cancels the task.
- It now waits for the task only after leaving `async with Worker(docket)`. `Worker.__aexit__` sets the worker's stop event and waits for the run loop to finish, so shutdown completes even when the cancellation was dropped.
- If the task never started, cancelling it still keeps it from running.

This also affects real servers running on Python 3.11, not just the tests.

Regression test: `tests/server/api/test_background_workers.py` wraps `Worker.run_forever` so it ignores cancellation, which simulates the dropped cancel. With the old code the test hangs; with this change it passes (20/20 runs on both 3.11 and 3.12). On 3.11, 20 repeat runs of the originally failing test also pass, and the related server and client test modules pass.
</details>

+from docket import Docket, Worker

title: Move the remaining Node 20 pins to Node 22
body:
Three Node pins in this repo are still on Node 20. Node 20 is end-of-life, so the October 2026 Node security releases have no fix for it. Advisory: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases

This PR moves all three pins to 22.23.4, the patched release on the 22.x line:

- `Dockerfile` `NODE_VERSION` default: 20.20.2 to 22.23.4. The published images and the Python tests do not use this default, because they pass `.nvmrc` as a build arg. Local image builds use it.
- `time-docker-build.yaml` base-branch build: 20.19.0 to 22.23.4.
- `.github/docker/old-sqlite.Dockerfile` `NODE_VERSION` default: 20.20.2 to 22.23.4. The SQLite compatibility jobs build this image and do not override the value.

I moved to 22 and not 24 because 22 is the smallest step off Node 20. The V1 UI builds with `npm ci` and `npm run build` on Node 22.23.4.

Related to #23508, which moves the `.nvmrc` files to 24.22.1 and `NODE_V2_VERSION` to 22.23.4.

title: Update Node to the October 2026 security releases
body:
Node.js published security releases on 2026-10-21. They fix three TLS certificate hostname checks, a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, and other issues. The fixed versions are 24.22.1 and 22.23.4. Advisory: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases

This PR moves the Node pins to patched releases:

- `.nvmrc`, `ui/.nvmrc`, and `ui-v2/.nvmrc`: 24.20.0 to 24.22.1. CI and the published images build the V1 UI with the root `.nvmrc`.
- `Dockerfile` `NODE_V2_VERSION`: 22.23.2 to 22.23.4. No workflow overrides this value, so the published images build the V2 UI with it. Node is only in the build stage, not in the final image.
- `.github/docker/old-sqlite.Dockerfile` `NODE_V2_VERSION`: 22.23.2 to 22.23.4. The SQLite compatibility jobs build this image and do not override the value.

title: Publish duration lower bounds only where validation enforces them
body:
Related to #23400

This PR stops `DurationOrSecondsTimeDelta` from publishing `minimum: 0`. Each field whose validation enforces a lower bound now publishes that bound itself.

**The problem.** #23400 gave `DurationOrSecondsTimeDelta` a JSON Schema with `minimum: 0` on its number branch, in both validation and serialization mode. `CompositeTrigger.within` uses the alias but has no lower bound, so server and client `CompoundTrigger(..., within=-5)` both validate. The server's OpenAPI schema still says `minimum: 0` for that field. A client that validates responses against it would reject an automation the API returned.

**The fix.**
- The alias publishes no bound.
- `EventTrigger.within` publishes `minimum: 0` through `json_schema_extra` in both automations modules. Pydantic leaves a timedelta field's `ge` out of the JSON Schema, so `ge=timedelta(seconds=0)` publishes nothing by itself.
- `NonNegativeTimeDelta` adds its own `WithJsonSchema` pair with the bound. It replaces the alias's pair in both modes, so the three `schedule_after` fields keep publishing `minimum: 0`.
- The client `MetricTriggerQuery.range` and `firing_for` publish `minimum: 300`, which matches `enforce_minimum_range`. Before this PR they published `minimum: 0`.
- `CompositeTrigger.within` stays unbounded in validation. The server reads stored automations back through these models, so adding `ge` would fail reads of any stored automation with a negative `within`.

`docs/v3/api-ref/rest-api/server/schema.json` is regenerated, and its diff contains only these bounds. `ui-v2/src/api/prefect.ts` regenerates with no change, because openapi-typescript does not emit numeric bounds.

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

Pydantic 2.10.1, 2.11.5, 2.12.5, 2.13.0, and 2.14.1 all leave a timedelta `ge` out of the schema, and in all of them the outer `WithJsonSchema` pair wins in both modes. On pydantic 2.10.x, `WithJsonSchema` returns its dict without copying it. A field's `default` or `json_schema_extra` is then written into the dict that every field using the alias shares, so another field's `minimum` can appear on `CompositeTrigger.within` depending on generation order. Main publishes it there on every version, and 2.10 already leaks field defaults the same way. Pydantic 2.11 copies the dict, and CI does not test 2.10. Raising the floor to 2.11.5 is left for a separate change.

The `CompositeTrigger.within` and alias tests fail on main. The bound tests pass on main, because main publishes the bound everywhere. They fail when the `json_schema_extra` lines and the `NonNegativeTimeDelta` pair are removed.

</details>

title: Remove direct dependency on ruamel.yaml.clib
body:
this PR removes Prefect's direct dependency on `ruamel.yaml.clib`, which has no cp315 wheels and breaks the `prefect-client` Python 3.15 Docker build, and pins `ruamel.yaml` to exclude 0.19.0 (the one release that requires `ruamel.yaml.clibz`).

<details>

The 3.9.0 release run of the "Docker images" workflow failed on "Build and publish to DockerHub (prefecthq/prefect-client, 3.15)": https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39529569042/job/118992111168

`ruamel.yaml.clib` 0.2.15 has no cp315 wheels, so `uv pip install` tried to build it from source and failed because `client/Dockerfile` has no C compiler (`error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'gcc'`). Upstream has moved to `ruamel.yaml.clibz` and is not expected to publish 3.15 wheels for `clib`.

The direct `clib` dependency was added in #20068 when `ruamel.yaml` 0.19.0 required `ruamel.yaml.clibz` (which needs Zig to compile). Since 0.19.1, both extensions are optional extras, so a plain `ruamel.yaml` install is pure Python. Prefect's only use is `YAML()` with the default round-trip loader in `src/prefect/deployments/base.py`, which doesn't use the C extension.

Changes:
- `pyproject.toml` and `client/pyproject.toml`: removed `"ruamel.yaml.clib>=0.2.8; platform_python_implementation == 'CPython'"` and changed the pin to `"ruamel.yaml>=0.17.0,!=0.19.0"`.
- Regenerated `uv.lock` with `uv lock`.

Verified locally:
- `docker build --build-arg PYTHON_VERSION=3.15 -f client/Dockerfile` succeeds; the image contains `ruamel-yaml 0.19.1` and no `ruamel.yaml.clib`/`clibz`.
- `docker build --build-arg PYTHON_VERSION=3.11 -f client/Dockerfile` still succeeds.
- `uv run pytest tests/deployment/ tests/cli/test_deploy.py -n4`: 386 passed, 1 skipped.

</details>

body:
This PR documents how internal SDK calls should use `_pendulum_call` to avoid emitting user-facing Pendulum deprecation warnings on Python 3.11/3.12. The guidance lives in `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`, where it applies to callers throughout the SDK.

<details>
<summary>Scope, justification and validation</summary>

Resolved the conflict with main by retaining the current Whenever compatibility and optional-import guidance unchanged, alongside the original Pendulum rule.

Path: `src/prefect/AGENTS.md`

Non-obvious evidence: Internal calls can emit warnings intended for user calls; the pytest warning filter can hide mistakes.
Cross-cutting scope: SDK callers of Pendulum-backed datetime methods.
Why not code comment/docstring: The helper docstring explains implementation, but an ancestor instruction reaches callers across the SDK.
Durability: Applies while the SDK wraps Pendulum methods with user-facing deprecations.
Counter-evidence checked: `_pendulum_call`, `pyproject.toml` warning filters and datetime warning regression tests.

Documentation only; no runtime code changes. Focused Python 3.12 reproductions passed for parameter default unwrapping, multi-pass dict/list/inline preservation, and internal Pendulum warning bypass.  - **Event and log WebSocket subscribers are parallel implementations.** `events/clients.py::PrefectEventSubscriber` and `logging/clients.py::PrefectLogsSubscriber` duplicate the same reconnect/backoff/dedup logic, including the `reconnect_on_clean_close` option (used by `events/subscribers.py::FlowRunSubscriber` so a clean disconnect doesn't hide a terminal event). Mirror any reconnection-behavior change across both.
 - **Flow run observers own their stream recovery.** `_internal/observers.py` observers create subscribers with `reconnection_attempts=0` and delegate polling fallback, reconnect backoff, and setup deadlines to `_internal/_observation_delivery.py::ObservationDelivery`. Version-specific code is guarded by feature-detection flags (`_WHENEVER_NEW_API` for ≥ 0.10.0, `_SYSTEM_TZ` for ≥ 0.11), not version checks. Never call `DateTime.now()` or `pendulum.now()` directly — use `now()` from `types/_datetime.py` instead. Avoid no-argument `datetime.datetime.now()` because it returns a tz-naive datetime that raises `TypeError` when compared to the tz-aware datetimes produced by `now()`. Explicitly timezone-aware stdlib calls such as `datetime.now(ZoneInfo("UTC"))` are allowed when needed to preserve timezone information. Never call `ZonedDateTime.from_py_datetime()`, `PlainDateTime.from_py_datetime()`, or `.py_datetime()` directly — use the helpers instead. +- **Call Pendulum-only members via `types/_datetime.py::_pendulum_call` on Python 3.11/3.12.** Prefect's `DateTime`/`Date`/`Duration` wrap Pendulum-only members (and some shared stdlib methods like `replace`) with user-facing deprecation warnings; `_pendulum_call` bypasses them so users only see warnings for their own calls. `pyproject.toml` ignores these warnings in pytest, so direct calls from Prefect code pass tests silently unless covered by the guards in `tests/test_datetime.py`.
 - **Flow and task engines advance state differently.** The flow engine makes blocking API calls to the server to propose and advance states. The task engine emits `prefect.task_run.*` events (delivered via WebSockets) but advances state locally through `set_state` calls with polling/backoff — do not assume the two engines work the same way.
 - **Flow state transitions go through the server.** The flow engine proposes states to the server, which accepts or rejects them via orchestration rules. title: Guard internal call sites against Pendulum deprecation warnings
body:
this PR adds a regression test that fails if Prefect's own code calls deprecated Pendulum-only members directly, instead of going through `_pendulum_call`. It also documents that rule in the `_pendulum_call` and `_datetime_deprecations` docstrings.

This is a follow-up to #23328. It replaces #23489, which tried to capture the same rule in AGENTS.md; a maintainer asked for it to live in code instead.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `pyproject.toml` ignores `Pendulum datetime member` warnings globally, so a new direct call like `dt.in_tz(...)` passes CI while still warning end users on Python 3.11–3.12.
- The existing `test_prefect_helpers_do_not_emit_pendulum_warnings` only covers helpers in `types/_datetime.py`.
- The new test `test_prefect_call_sites_do_not_emit_pendulum_warnings` turns that warning into an error and runs call sites outside that module:
  - `IntervalSchedule.get_dates`, both the sub-day and the daily-interval branches
  - `CronSchedule.get_dates`
  - `runtime.flow_run._parse_datetime_UTC`
  - `generate_deprecation_message`
- I checked that the test catches a regression: replacing `_pendulum_call(start, "naive")` with `start.naive()` in `CronSchedule` makes it fail with `Pendulum datetime member 'naive'`.
- `tests/test_datetime.py` passes locally on Python 3.12 (275 passed). The new test is skipped on 3.13+.

</details>

title: Remove deprecated Runner execution paths
body:
Related to #21252

**The problem.** `Runner.execute_flow_run`, `Runner.execute_bundle` and `Runner.reschedule_current_flow_runs` were deprecated in 3.6.24 (#21252), and the deprecation message promised removal after Sep 2026. Their private code was a second execution path next to `FlowRunExecutor`, with its own process map, kill logic, crash handling and cancellation branch.

**The change.** This PR removes the three methods and the private code that only they used. `Runner._cancel_run` now only delegates to `CancellationManager` for runs that `ProcessManager` tracks.

`ProcessWorker._submit_adhoc_run` was the last internal caller. It now opens a `FlowRunExecutorContext` with `BundleExecutionStarter` and `propose_submitting=False`, the same way `ProcessWorker.run` does. The worker no longer creates a `Runner`.

The runner webserver's `/run_count` read the removed process map. That map was empty for served runs, so the endpoint always returned 0. It now reads `ProcessManager.flow_run_count()`, which takes the map's length without iterating it, because the endpoint runs on the webserver thread.

## Breaking change

Code that ignored the deprecation warnings and still calls these methods now fails with `AttributeError`:

- `Runner.execute_flow_run`: use `FlowRunExecutorContext` with a `ProcessStarter`, such as `WorkspaceResolvingEngineCommandStarter`.
- `Runner.execute_bundle`: use `execute_bundle()` from `prefect.bundles.execute`.
- `Runner.reschedule_current_flow_runs`: no replacement. `prefect flow-run execute` handles SIGTERM rescheduling.

`prefect.runner.runner.ProcessMapEntry` described entries in the removed process map. It still imports, but it now emits a `PrefectDeprecationWarning`.

## Rollout caveats

- `no-op: served runs and direct ProcessWorker runs already used FlowRunExecutor. Only ad hoc ProcessWorker bundle runs change path.`

title: Substitute `apply_values` placeholders in a single pass
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23491

this PR makes `apply_values` resolve every placeholder in a string and then substitute them into the original template in one `PLACEHOLDER_CAPTURE_REGEX.sub` pass. Previously each placeholder was applied with sequential `str.replace` calls over a `set`, so a value that contained placeholder syntax could be substituted again, and the result depended on `PYTHONHASHSEED`.

<details>

```python
apply_values("prefix {{ first }} / {{ second }}", {"first": "{{ second }}", "second": "resolved"})
# before: "prefix {{ second }} / resolved" or "prefix resolved / resolved" depending on hash seed
# after:  "prefix {{ second }} / resolved" always
```

Unchanged: whole-string typed replacement, `skip_prefixes`, block/variable placeholders left for later resolution, `remove_notset`/`warn_on_notset` handling (still one warning per unique placeholder), and the explicit multi-pass pipeline in deployment steps.

Tests added for standard and env-var values containing placeholder syntax; verified they fail on main under `PYTHONHASHSEED=1` and pass on this branch under seeds 0–3. No docs change needed — this matches documented behavior.

</details>

title: Percent-encode path values in `url_for`
body:
closes #23492

this PR percent-encodes the values `url_for` interpolates into URL path templates (`obj_id` and additional format kwargs like `work_pool_name`), so names containing `#`, `?`, or `/` stay a single path segment instead of becoming a fragment/query.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

```python
pool = WorkPool(name="gpu#west?blue", type="process")
url_for(pool, default_base_url="https://prefect.example.com")
# before: https://prefect.example.com/work-pools/work-pool/gpu#west?blue
# after:  https://prefect.example.com/work-pools/work-pool/gpu%23west%3Fblue
```

- Encoding uses `urllib.parse.quote(..., safe="")` via a private `_quote_path_segment` helper.
- UUIDs and other IDs made of unreserved characters are unchanged; event `occurred` dates are formatted as before.
- Added tests for UI/API work pool URLs and the worker UI URL's `work_pool_name` segment.

title: Add custom state discovery and filters
body:
closes #21566

This PR adds separate state type and state name filters to UI v2 so custom states such as `Failed(name="NewObjects")` can be discovered and selected.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- Adds `GET /observed-states` with a Cloud-compatible schema, prefix search, and first/last transition timestamps from retained flow and task run histories. Exact spelling and case are preserved; deleting runs removes their observations.
- Applies type and name filters to run lists, flow details, deployment runs and upcoming runs, and automation state selection. Alternatives within each filter use OR; type and name use AND.
- Preserves existing name-based URLs and saved filters, keeps selected names available outside the 200-result discovery limit, and searches the server for additional names.
- Adds SQLite covering indexes on `(type, name, timestamp)`. SQLite builds these indexes while holding its write lock; the PostgreSQL companion migration is a no-op.

Focused API and migration tests passed on SQLite and PostgreSQL (36 checks total). The 249 focused UI tests, production build, targeted lint, and browser checks also passed.

Endpoint docstrings and the generated API schema describe discovery semantics; migration notes document index-build costs. The UI filters require no additional configuration.

</details>

+"""Discover states from retained flow and task run transitions."""
+
+import sqlalchemy as sa
+from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
+
+from prefect.server.database import PrefectDBInterface, db_injector
+from prefect.server.schemas.observed_states import ObservedState, ObservedStateSort
+
+
+@db_injector
+async def read_observed_states(
+    db: PrefectDBInterface,
+    session: AsyncSession,
+    query: str | None = None,
+    order_by: ObservedStateSort = ObservedStateSort.LAST_SEEN_DESC,
+    limit: int = 200,
+) -> list[ObservedState]:
+    """Combine exact state pairs and timestamp bounds from retained run histories."""
+    # Group each history before combining them: the union only contains distinct
+    # pairs, rather than every retained transition. SQLite uses covering indexes.
+    histories = sa.union_all(
+        *(
+            sa.select(
+                state.type.label("state_type"),
+                state.name.label("state_name"),
+                sa.func.min(state.timestamp).label("first_seen"),
+                sa.func.max(state.timestamp).label("last_seen"),
+            ).group_by(state.type, state.name)
+            for state in (db.FlowRunState, db.TaskRunState)
+        )
+    ).subquery()
+    observed = (
+        sa.select(
+            sa.cast(histories.c.state_type, sa.String).label("state_type"),
+            histories.c.state_name,
+            sa.func.min(histories.c.first_seen).label("first_seen"),
+            sa.func.max(histories.c.last_seen).label("last_seen"),
+        )
+        .group_by(histories.c.state_type, histories.c.state_name)
+        # Prevent prefix predicates from being pushed into the full history scans.
+        # OFFSET works on supported SQLite versions that predate MATERIALIZED CTEs.
+        .offset(0)
+        .subquery()
+    )
+    statement = sa.select(observed)
+    if query and (prefix := query.strip()):
+        statement = statement.where(
+            sa.or_(
+                observed.c.state_type.istartswith(prefix, autoescape=True),
+                observed.c.state_name.istartswith(prefix, autoescape=True),
+            )
+        )
+    ordering = [observed.c.state_type.asc(), observed.c.state_name.asc()]
+    if order_by == ObservedStateSort.LAST_SEEN_DESC:
+        ordering.insert(0, observed.c.last_seen.desc())
+    result = await session.execute(statement.order_by(*ordering).limit(limit))
+    return [ObservedState.model_validate(row) for row in result.mappings()]

title: Update certifi and uv for eMudhra CA compromise
body:
This PR requires `certifi>=2026.10.19` and updates `uv` to `0.13.4` to remove trust paths affected by the [eMudhra intermediate CA compromise](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/).

<details>
<summary>Details and checks</summary>

- Applies the `certifi` requirement to both `prefect` and `prefect-client`.
- Updates the `uv` dependency floors, Docker pins, pre-commit hook, and proxy-test pin. Only `certifi` and `uv` versions change in the lockfile.
- Refreshes six lines of generated deployment settings types required by the OpenAPI pre-push hook, in a separate commit.
- Passes 31 focused TLS/WebSocket/subscription tests, 8 interval-schedule UI tests, and the UI production build.
- Checks the lockfile and Docker dependency export. The installed `certifi` rejects all 12 published compromised chains offline, and `uv` rejects both published test hosts with certificate errors.

No application logic changes or additional API documentation are needed for these dependency updates. Existing tests and explicit certificate checks cover the affected behavior.

</details>

Note: Published images and existing installations still need rebuilding or updating and restarting to receive the fixes. System CA stores and Node updates require separate follow-up.

title: Cap fastapi below 0.151
body:
Caps FastAPI below 0.151 in `pyproject.toml` and `client/pyproject.toml`, and locks it to 0.150.0.

FastAPI 0.151.0 ([fastapi/fastapi#16536](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/16536)) validates an explicit JSON `null` against a body parameter instead of using the parameter's default. The client sends `null` for unset `sort`, `limit` and filters, so on 0.151 and later about 144 body parameters across 55 server endpoints return 422: most `/filter`, `/count`, `/paginate` and `/history` routes, which break `read_flow_runs`, `prefect deploy`, worker heartbeats and artifact and log reads. A fresh install currently resolves FastAPI 0.155, so it hits this. The cap comes off once the server treats `null` as the default again; that work is tracked separately.

Two smaller changes between 0.141 and 0.150 also needed fixes:

- 0.145 removed `FastAPI.extra`, which browser `prefect cloud login` used to pass state between the login server and the CLI. It now uses the app's `state`.
- 0.148 stopped validating omitted query defaults, so the flow-run graph's `since` default reached the handler as a string. The default is now the datetime itself.

The existing cloud-login and flow-run-graph tests fail on 0.150 without these fixes and pass with them. The server, client, runner, worker and CLI suites pass on 0.150.0 (4,233 passed).

title: Wait for the events client to confirm events before asserting in checkpoint tests
body:
`test_background_checkpoint_reconnects_after_connection_loss[PrefectCloudEventsClient]` failed on CI with `assert 1 == 0`: the client still held one unconfirmed event. The test kills the connection after the event arrives, then sleeps a fixed 0.5s and asserts the background checkpoint has reconnected, resent the event, and confirmed it. In the failing run, asyncio logged `Executing <Task ... PrefectEventsClient._checkpoint_loop() running at clients.py:502 ...> took 0.809 seconds`: an event-loop stall on the busy runner outlasted the sleep, so the assertion ran before the reconnect finished. The client behaved correctly.

This replaces the fixed sleeps with a helper that polls until the client holds no unconfirmed events, for up to 5 seconds, and then lets the existing assertion report the result. Two sibling tests used the same sleep-then-assert pattern (`test_background_checkpoint_clears_unconfirmed_events`, `test_background_checkpoint_retries_reconnect_until_server_available`) and get the same change. No assertion changes.

Verification: forcing a 0.6s stall inside `_reconnect` reproduces the CI failure 40 of 40 runs before this change and passes 120 of 120 after (with the two sibling tests, at 0.6s and 1.5s stalls). With the client's reconnect disabled, the test still fails after the 5s wait. `tests/events/client/` passes (430).

title: Use min_length and max_length on request bodies so the server imports on FastAPI 0.155
body:
FastAPI 0.155.0 (released 2026-10-20) removed the deprecated catch-all `**extra` from `Path`, `Query`, `Header`, `Cookie`, `Body`, `Form` and `File`, so an unknown keyword now raises `TypeError`. Six request parameters in the server API passed keywords FastAPI never had, so on a fresh install that resolves FastAPI 0.155, `prefect.server.api` fails to import:

```
TypeError: Body() got an unexpected keyword argument 'min_items'
```

This switches them to the keywords FastAPI does have:

- `min_items=1` to `min_length=1` on `names` for `POST /v2/concurrency_limits/increment`, `/increment-with-lease` and `/decrement`
- `max_items=200` to `max_length=200` on the id lists for `POST /ui/flow_runs/count-task-runs`, `/ui/flows/count-deployments` and `/ui/flows/next-runs`

On FastAPI before 0.155 the old keywords were never validated. They were copied into the OpenAPI schema as non-standard `min_items`/`max_items` keys and nothing else, so the new keywords start enforcing limits that were only documented:

- An empty `names` now returns 422 on the three concurrency slot endpoints. Before, it returned 200; on `increment-with-lease` it created a lease that held no limits. The SDK's `concurrency()` and `rate_limit()` return early on empty names (since #14789), so they never send one, but a direct `client.increment_concurrency_slots([])` or `client.release_concurrency_slots([])` now raises.
- More than 200 ids now returns 422 on the three UI routes. The UIs send at most one page of ids (the server caps pages at `PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, 200 by default) or batch them at 200.

`tests/server/api/test_fastapi_param_keywords.py` checks every FastAPI request-parameter call in `src/prefect/` against the function's real signature. CI runs the locked FastAPI 0.141.1, which accepts unknown keywords without a warning, so without it the next one would pass CI and fail installs. The regenerated `docs/v3/api-ref/rest-api/server/schema.json` changes only these six fields, now standard `minItems`/`maxItems`.

There is no linked issue: this fixes an import failure on the current FastAPI release.

### Checklist

--- tests/server/api/test_fastapi_param_keywords.py (+103/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+"""
+Calls in `src/prefect/` to FastAPI's request parameter functions (`Path`,
+`Query`, `Header`, `Cookie`, `Body`, `Form`, `File`, `Security`, `Depends`)
+pass only keywords those functions name in their signatures, and never unpack
+`**kwargs` into them.
+
+FastAPI before 0.155 accepted unknown keywords, copied them into the OpenAPI
+schema, and did not validate them, so `Body(max_items=200)` accepted a list of
+any length. FastAPI 0.155 raises `TypeError` on an unknown keyword, so one such
+call makes `prefect.server.api` fail to import.
+"""
+
+import ast
+import importlib
+import inspect
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import prefect
+
+SRC_DIR = Path(prefect.__file__).parent
+
+PARAM_FUNCTION_NAMES = frozenset(
+    {"Path", "Query", "Header", "Cookie", "Body", "Form", "File", "Security", "Depends"}
+)
+PARAM_FUNCTION_MODULES = frozenset(
+    {"fastapi", "fastapi.params", "fastapi.param_functions"}
+)
+
+# `src/prefect/` makes about 470 such calls. A scan that finds far fewer has
+# stopped resolving imports and would pass without checking anything.
+MINIMUM_EXPECTED_CALLS = 280
+
+
+def _named_keywords(module: str, name: str) -> frozenset[str]:
+    signature = inspect.signature(getattr(importlib.import_module(module), name))
+    return frozenset(
+        parameter.name
+        for parameter in signature.parameters.values()
+        if parameter.kind is not inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD
+    )
+
+
+def _param_function_calls(tree: ast.Module) -> list[tuple[ast.Call, str, str]]:
+    imported_functions: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
+    fastapi_module_names: set[str] = set()
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module in PARAM_FUNCTION_MODULES:
+            for alias in node.names:
+                if alias.name in PARAM_FUNCTION_NAMES:
+                    imported_functions[alias.asname or alias.name] = (
+                        node.module,
+                        alias.name,
+                    )
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            for alias in node.names:
+                if alias.name == "fastapi":
+                    fastapi_module_names.add(alias.asname or alias.name)
+
+    calls: list[tuple[ast.Call, str, str]] = []
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
+            continue
+        if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id in imported_functions:
+            calls.append((node, *imported_functions[node.func.id]))
+        elif (
+            isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute)
+            and isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Name)
+            and node.func.value.id in fastapi_module_names
+            and node.func.attr in PARAM_FUNCTION_NAMES
+        ):
+            calls.append((node, "fastapi", node.func.attr))
+    return calls
+
+
+def test_fastapi_param_function_calls_use_only_named_keywords():
+    call_count = 0
+    violations: list[str] = []
+    for py_file in sorted(SRC_DIR.rglob("*.py")):
+        location = py_file.relative_to(SRC_DIR.parent)
+        for call, module, name in _param_function_calls(ast.parse(py_file.read_text())):
+            call_count += 1
+            named_keywords = _named_keywords(module, name)
+            for keyword in call.keywords:
+                if keyword.arg is None:
+                    violations.append(
+                        f"{location}:{call.lineno}: {module}.{name}(**...) "
+                        "unpacks keywords that cannot be checked"
+                    )
+                elif keyword.arg not in named_keywords:
+                    violations.append(
+                        f"{location}:{call.lineno}: {module}.{name}() has no "
+                        f"parameter named {keyword.arg!r}"
+                    )
+
+    assert call_count >= MINIMUM_EXPECTED_CALLS, (
+        f"found only {call_count} FastAPI parameter function calls in "
+        f"{SRC_DIR}; the scan no longer resolves imports"
+    )
+    assert not violations, (
+        "FastAPI parameter functions called with keywords they do not name "
+        "(for example, use max_length= rather than max_items=):\n"
+        + "\n".join(violations)
+    )

title: docs: document patched test-clock timezone pitfall in fixtures AGENTS.md
body:
This PR adds a short pitfall to `tests/fixtures/AGENTS.md`, following #23465. It notes that hand-rolled patches of `prefect.types._datetime.now` must pass tz-converted values through `create_datetime_instance`, because on Python ≤3.12 pendulum drops a plain `ZoneInfo` on `timedelta` arithmetic.

Docs-only change: one existing bullet expanded, 0 net lines.

<details>
<summary>Justification</summary>

Path: tests/fixtures/AGENTS.md
Proposed text: Extend the `time.py` bullet: "Hand-rolled patches of `prefect.types._datetime.now` must pass tz-converted values through `create_datetime_instance`: on Python ≤3.12, pendulum drops a plain `ZoneInfo` on `timedelta` arithmetic"
Non-obvious evidence: Checked on Python 3.12: `now("UTC").astimezone(ZoneInfo("UTC")) - timedelta(minutes=1)` has `tzinfo=None`, while a stdlib `datetime` with `ZoneInfo` keeps it. The bug only appears on ≤3.12 (pendulum path), not on 3.13+ (whenever path), so a test can pass locally and fail in one CI matrix leg. #23465 fixed exactly this in the shared fixtures.
Cross-cutting scope: Any test across the suite that patches `prefect.types._datetime.now`. There are 9 hand-rolled patches outside `fixtures/time.py` (events triggers/ordering, CLI deployment run, docker registry, events subscriber), plus 19 files using the fixtures.
Why not code comment/docstring: The explanation exists only as a comment on the private `_in_timezone` helper in `tests/fixtures/time.py`. Authors writing their own patch in other test files would never see it. The fixtures AGENTS.md is where agents look to choose a time-control approach.
Durability: Applies for as long as Python 3.11/3.12 are supported (the pendulum branch of `prefect.types._datetime`), and to every future time-sensitive test, not only the triggering PR.
Counter-evidence checked: `tests/fixtures/time.py` (comment on private helper only), `tests/test_datetime.py::TestPatchedClock` (regression test, does not guide hand-rolled patches), `src/prefect/types/_datetime.py` (no note), `tests/AGENTS.md` and root `AGENTS.md` (only generic "mock time-sensitive operations" guidance), existing `tests/fixtures/AGENTS.md` (only listed fixture names).
</details>

<summary>Files changed in triggering push (817bc93b6e..abf878fc9f)</summary>

- tests/events/server/triggers/test_early_expect_events.py
- tests/fixtures/time.py
- tests/test_datetime.py

title: Aggregate nested collections of states when determining the final state
body:
**Update (2026-10-28):** per @desertaxle's review, nested aggregation is now opt-in behind the new `experiments.aggregate_nested_states` setting (`PREFECT_EXPERIMENTS_AGGREGATE_NESTED_STATES`, default `false`), following the default-off pattern of `runner.crash_on_cancellation_failure`. With the setting disabled, flows and tasks keep the historical behavior (`[[Failed(...)]]` completes as plain data). With it enabled, nested collections aggregate as originally proposed.

Persisted aggregates stay readable: `get_state_exception`/`aget_state_exception` understand nested collections regardless of the setting, so a run aggregated while the setting was on still reports its failure when read back after the setting is turned off (covered by round-trip tests, in-memory and via persisted result metadata). This also means a manually constructed `Failed` state holding nested states now yields its inner exception instead of a `TypeError`.

Docs now state the collection boundaries (mixed data, empty containers, reference cycles, 1000-level depth cap) and a migration note (opt in via the setting; keep intentional state-as-data returns by leaving the setting off or wrapping the return value in `quote()`).

closes #23137

This PR makes final state determination aggregate states nested inside returned collections, so a flow that returns the results of several `.map()` calls (a list of lists of futures) ends `FAILED` when one of the mapped tasks failed, instead of silently ending `COMPLETED`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`return_value_to_state` received the return value after futures were resolved to states, so a flow returning `[task_a.map(...), task_b.map(...)]` arrived as a list of lists of states. `is_state_iterable` only inspects the direct elements of a collection, so the nested states were treated as plain data and the aggregate rule never ran.

Changes:

- Add `experiments.aggregate_nested_states` (`PREFECT_EXPERIMENTS_AGGREGATE_NESTED_STATES`, default `false`), defined in `src/prefect/settings/models/experiments.py`, following the default-off pattern of `runner.crash_on_cancellation_failure`. When disabled, nested collections are treated as plain data (historical behavior); when enabled, they aggregate.
- Add `_flatten_nested_states` in `prefect.states`, which recursively collects states from nested `list`/`set`/`tuple` containers. Values that mix states with other data, contain only empty collections, or reference themselves are still treated as plain data, matching the previous behavior for non-state values.
- Add `_get_states_to_aggregate` in `prefect.states`, and use it in `return_value_to_state` and its sync counterpart `return_value_to_state_sync`, so nested states feed the same `StateGroup` aggregate (counts and messages now include the nested states) when the setting is enabled. The returned value itself is stored unchanged as the result data.

title: Cut CPU spent delivering events and API logs
body:
closes #23472

This PR cuts the CPU a flow run spends sending events and API logs to the API: 66% less for logs and 45% less for events, with lower peak memory under log load.

Queue services now take an item directly when one is already queued, and wait on the queue thread only when the queue is empty. A service working through a backlog yields to the global event loop every 256 items. `APILogWorker.send` serializes each log with orjson and queues only the bytes, and `_handle_batch` posts them joined to `/logs/`.

| Workload, median of 3 runs | CPU before → after | Peak RSS growth before → after |
|---|---|---|
| 20,000 run-logger lines | 1.43 s → 0.49 s | +16.2 MB → +12.2 MB |
| 5,000 `emit_event` calls in one flow | 0.78 s → 0.43 s | +7.9 MB → +7.9 MB |

Every log and event reached the server in every run. I measured against a local `prefect server start` on SQLite, on macOS with Python 3.14.

Behavior changes for review:

- `APILogWorker` is now `BatchedQueueService[bytes]`. `send()` still accepts dicts. A subclass that overrides `_handle_batch` or `_get_size` now receives bytes.
- `__payload_size__` values are smaller, because orjson writes compact UTF-8. httpx 0.28 already sent compact UTF-8, so request bodies are unchanged. Truncation still keeps each log within `PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_MAX_LOG_SIZE`.
- A message with a lone surrogate now fails in `prepare()`, and only that log is dropped. Before, httpx failed to encode the request and dropped the whole batch.
- When `PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_BATCH_SIZE` is less than twice `PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_MAX_LOG_SIZE`, batches now hold fewer logs, so each request stays within the batch size. The defaults (4,000,000 and 1,000,000, or 25,000 on Prefect Cloud) are not affected.

title: fix(server): begin SQLite write transaction before reading automation buckets
body:
closes #23470

This PR makes `reactive_evaluation` start its transaction with the write lock on SQLite, so concurrent events no longer fail with `database is locked` when they update an automation bucket.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Some trigger paths read bucket state before they write it. For example, an `expect` event for a trigger with `after` calls `read_bucket` and then `increment_bucket`. On SQLite, the transaction starts as `BEGIN DEFERRED`. If another connection commits between the read and the write, SQLite cannot upgrade the transaction and fails immediately with `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` ("database is locked"). The busy timeout does not apply to this error.

Changes:
- `automations_session` now accepts `with_for_update` and passes it to `db.session_context`.
- `reactive_evaluation` uses `automations_session(begin_transaction=True, with_for_update=True)`. On SQLite this emits `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so the transaction waits for the write lock (with the busy timeout) before it reads. On Postgres, `with_for_update` has no effect on the transaction begin, so behavior does not change.

This is the same approach as #23052 (`mark_deployments_ready`).

The new test `test_concurrent_bucket_updates_count_each_event_once` opens a bucket with an `after` event, then evaluates 25 `expect` events concurrently. It checks that the bucket count is exactly 25 (no lost or double-counted events). Without the fix, the test fails on SQLite with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked`.
</details>

title: fix task returning another task's cached results

If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://docs.prefect.io/contribute/index

<!-- Whether or not AI tools helped draft this PR, you are responsible for understanding the change, keeping it scoped, validating it locally, and explaining the approach. -->
<!-- Maintainers may close PRs that appear low-effort, likely AI-generated, and substantially far from the expected implementation. -->

Found this case during when the agent wrote a similar code like the one below. 
Different tasks can then get the same cache key, causing one task to return another’s saved result.
Fixed by hashing the complete code object.

```python
from prefect import flow, task

# These might come from a database or YAML configuration.
customer_rules = {
    "standard_customer": 1,
    "enterprise_customer": 100,
}


def create_pricing_task(customer, fee):
    namespace = {}
    exec(
        f"def calculate_total(amount):\n"
        f"    return amount + {fee}\n",
        namespace,
    )
    return task(name=f"price-{customer}", persist_result=True)(
        namespace["calculate_total"]
    )


standard_price = create_pricing_task(
    "standard_customer", customer_rules["standard_customer"]
)
enterprise_price = create_pricing_task(
    "enterprise_customer", customer_rules["enterprise_customer"]
)


@flow
def generate_invoices():
    standard = standard_price(10, return_state=True)
    enterprise = enterprise_price(10, return_state=True)

    print(f"Standard invoice:   ${standard.result()} ({standard.name})")
    print(f"Enterprise invoice: ${enterprise.result()} ({enterprise.name})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    generate_invoices()
```

Expected:

```text
Standard invoice:   $11 (Completed)
Enterprise invoice: $110 (Completed)
```

With the bug:

```text
Standard invoice:   $11 (Completed)
Enterprise invoice: $11 (Cached)
```

title: docs: document held expect events for proactive triggers with after
body:
This PR updates the docs for a change in #23445. Devin made this update. Devin analyzed the diff from the triggering push (`71d1906204..189bf69608`).

Before #23445, the docs told the user this: an `expect` event that arrives before the `after` event does not count, and for a Proactive trigger this can cause a spurious firing. This statement is now incorrect. A Proactive trigger with `after` now holds each `expect`-only event. When a later `after` event opens a window, that window counts the held events that occurred inside it. Thus, the arrival order does not cause a spurious firing.

Changes:
- `docs/v3/concepts/event-triggers.mdx` ("Event ordering and `after`"): The missed-firing risk is now for Reactive triggers only. A new paragraph tells how Proactive triggers with `after` count held `expect` events.
- `docs/v3/how-to-guides/workflows/state-change-hooks.mdx`: The race now causes only missed firings on Reactive triggers. The text no longer says "missed or spurious firings".

The `follows` guidance does not change. It is still correct for both postures.

No missing-coverage recommendations. The other changes in the push are internal (the `automation_held_event` table and its migrations, and the DB interface). Also, the `within` validator change only makes more timedelta input forms (for example, ISO 8601 durations) pass the Proactive minimum check. The docs do not have incorrect information about this.

title: Keep the patched test clock timezone-aware on Python 3.12
body:
Follows #23445.

On Python 3.11 and 3.12, `prefect.types._datetime.DateTime` is pendulum's. The `frozen_time` and `advance_time` fixtures returned `now(tz)` as a pendulum datetime with a plain `ZoneInfo` tzinfo, and pendulum drops that tzinfo on arithmetic. So `now("UTC") - delta` came back naive, and code that compared it with an aware time raised `TypeError`. `get_lost_followers` in the in-memory causal ordering does exactly that, which failed a test in #23445 on 3.12 only.

Both fixtures now convert through `create_datetime_instance`, the same path the real `now(tz)` uses, so the patched clock returns the same kind of object. A new test in `tests/fixtures/test_time.py` checks both fixtures. The lost-follower test in #23445 goes back to using `advance_time`.

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

Found while fixing CI on #23445. That PR worked around it by patching `now` inside the one test. This PR fixes the fixtures instead, so other tests that subtract from the patched clock on 3.11 and 3.12 get aware times too.

</details>

title: Fix forked child processes exiting with code 1 because of QueueService at-exit drain
body:
closes #23463

This PR makes `_QueueServiceBase._drain` return immediately when `_done_event` is `None`. This is the state after `reset_for_fork`, or when the service did not start in this process.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`start()` registers `_at_exit` with `threading._register_atexit`. In a forked child, `reset_for_fork` sets `_done_event = None`, but the at-exit callback stays registered. When the child exits, `threading._shutdown()` calls `_at_exit` → `drain(at_exit=True)` → `_drain`, and `assert self._done_event is not None` fails. `multiprocessing` then sets the child exit code to 1. This makes PyTorch `DataLoader` workers fail inside flow runs.

Now `_drain` returns a completed future (`False`) in this state. This is the same result as for a service that is already done.

Tests:
- `test_drain_after_reset_for_fork_does_not_error`: drain after `reset_for_fork` does not raise.
- `test_forked_child_exits_cleanly_with_running_service`: a forked child exits with code 0 while a service runs in the parent. This test fails without the fix.
- `test_multiprocessing_after_test_harness` used `os._exit(0)` in its worker to avoid this bug. The worker now returns normally. This test also fails without the fix.

Repro script from the issue: child exit code goes from 1 to 0.
</details>

title: Apply both `any_` and `not_any_` in flow run state filters
body:
Closes #23458

This PR makes a flow run state filter apply when its type or name part sets both `any_` and `not_any_`. Before, the state criteria were dropped and every flow run matched: with a Completed run and a Failed run, `any_=["COMPLETED", "FAILED"]` with `not_any_=["FAILED"]` returned both.

<details>
<summary>Cause, test and range</summary>

`FlowRunFilterState._get_filter_list` kept the `as_sql_filter()` result of its type and name parts only if it was a `BinaryExpression` ([filters.py](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/1c866f04d6268a56a02bdbc1f8aa4b1788c39f89/src/prefect/server/schemas/filters.py#L429-L436)). Both fields set give an `and_` of two comparisons, not a `BinaryExpression`, so the part was skipped. The fix skips a part only when it sets nothing (`sa.true()`), so each part stays one group: with `operator="or_"`, spreading its two comparisons into the outer `or_` would match every flow run. `TaskRunFilterState` has the same check, but its parts only have `any_`, so it is not affected.

Test: `test_read_flow_runs_filters_by_states_any_and_not_any` reads three flow runs with a type filter and a name filter that each set both fields, then with both parts under `or_`. `pytest tests/server/models/test_flow_runs.py -k states_any_and_not_any -n 0`: 1 failed before the fix, 1 passed after.

</details>

title: Filter Kubernetes observer LIST/WATCH server-side and page initial lists
body:
closes #22208

This PR makes the Kubernetes worker observer ask the API server only for Prefect-labeled pods and jobs, and splits the initial LIST into pages of 500. Before this change, kopf listed and watched every pod and job in scope and filtered them client-side.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `configure` (the kopf startup handler) now sets `settings.watching.label_selectors` for `("v1", "pods")` and `("batch", "v1", "jobs")`, and sets `settings.watching.chunk_size = 500`. These settings were added in [kopf 1.45](https://github.com/nolar/kopf/releases/tag/1.45.0) ([nolar/kopf#1311](https://github.com/nolar/kopf/pull/1311)). kopf applies them to the initial LIST and to the WATCH that follows, for both namespaced and cluster-wide URLs. Namespace and CRD discovery are not filtered.
- The selector comes from the existing filter definition. `_pod_label_filters`/`_pod_label_selector` are renamed to `_observed_label_filters`/`_observed_label_selector`. The pod handler, the job crash handler (which used to build its own copy of the mapping), pod lifecycle reconciliation, and the server-side selector all use them now. The default is presence of `prefect.io/flow-run-id`. `additional_label_filters` are merged in afterward with the same precedence as before, and an empty value renders as `key=` (equality), not presence.
- With a server-side selector, Kubernetes reports a job whose labels stop matching (for example, an `additional_label_filters` value changed or the `prefect.io/flow-run-id` label removed) as `DELETED` with its old body, even though the job still exists. Before treating a `DELETED` event as a deletion, `_mark_flow_run_as_crashed` now reads the job by namespace and name with `_job_still_exists`:
  - A 404, or a job with a different UID (a replacement), confirms the deletion. The handler then re-reads the flow run, re-applies the terminal, cancelling, paused and scheduled checks, and continues into the existing replacement-job wait. That wait now excludes the deleted job by UID rather than by name, so a replacement that reuses the name keeps the run alive.
  - The same UID means the job only left the selector, so the handler skips without proposing `Crashed`.
  - kopf runs `@kopf.on.event` handlers once, with no retry. So transient lookup failures (408, 429, any 5xx except 501, timeouts, connection errors) are retried in place with capped exponential backoff and jitter (1s up to 60s). Each request has a 30s timeout, so a hung request becomes a retry. Retries continue until the lookup gives a definite answer or kopf cancels the handler. Each attempt opens and closes its own API client.
  - Permanent errors (for example 401/403/422/501) log a warning and leave the flow run alone. A failed lookup never counts as proof that the job is gone.
  - The label-filtered job LIST isn't used to decide whether a job was deleted, because it can't see a job whose flow run label was removed.
- No field selectors, and `initial_streaming` keeps its d

title: Read every global concurrency limit in `prefect transfer`
body:
Closes #23455

This PR makes `prefect transfer` collect all global concurrency limits from the source profile. Before, it collected only the first 10: with 12 limits, `collect_resources` returned 10 and the other 2 were not collected.

<details>
<summary>Cause, test and range</summary>

`collect_resources` called `read_global_concurrency_limits()` once ([_transfer_utils.py](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/1c866f04d6268a56a02bdbc1f8aa4b1788c39f89/src/prefect/cli/_transfer_utils.py#L31)), and the client reads 10 limits per call by default ([client.py](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/1c866f04d6268a56a02bdbc1f8aa4b1788c39f89/src/prefect/client/orchestration/_concurrency_limits/client.py#L929-L931)). The fix reads pages with `offset` until a call returns no limits. The other reads in `collect_resources` return at most 200 rows each and are not changed here.

Test: `test_collect_resources_reads_every_global_concurrency_limit` creates 12 limits on the test server and expects all 12. `pytest tests/cli/test_transfer.py -k test_collect_resources_reads_every`: 1 failed before the fix (3 runs), 1 passed after (3 runs). `tests/cli/test_transfer.py` in full: 19 passed.

</details>
