title: Resolve numeric string dict keys in `get_from_dict`
body:
closes #23452

This PR changes `get_from_dict` so that a string path segment finds a string dictionary key with the same value. Before this change, `get_from_dict` changed each segment to an `int` before the lookup. Thus `{"years": {"2026": 42}}` with the path `years.2026` returned the default value, and `apply_values` removed the templated field.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

For each segment, the lookup now depends on the container type:

- **Mapping:** use the exact key if it is in the mapping. If it is not, change the key to an `int` only when the string is a canonical integer (`"1"`, `"-1"`). Strings such as `"01"` stay as strings, because `str(int("01")) != "01"`.
- **Other containers (lists, tuples):** no change. The segment is changed to an `int` when possible, so `a.1`, `a[1]`, `a[-1]`, and `a.-1` work as before.

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `get_from_dict({"years": {"2026": 42}}, "years.2026")` | `None` | `42` |
| `apply_values({"year": "{{ years.2026 }}"}, {"years": {"2026": 42}})` | `{}` | `{"year": 42}` |
| `get_from_dict({"items": {"01": "first"}}, "items.01")` | `None` | `"first"` |
| `get_from_dict({"a": {1: "int", "1": "str"}}, "a.1")` | `"int"` | `"str"` |
| `get_from_dict({"a": {1: "int"}}, "a.1")` | `"int"` | `"int"` |

One small change in behavior: `get_from_dict({"a": {1: "x"}}, "a.01")` now returns the default value, not `"x"`. The issue asks for this, because `"01"` identifies a string key.

`set_in_dict` already uses string segments as they are, so `set_in_dict` and `get_from_dict` now agree on paths with numeric string keys.

Tests: new parametrized cases in `tests/utilities/test_collections.py::TestGetFromDict` and a new `apply_values` test in `tests/utilities/test_templating.py`. `uv run pytest tests/utilities/test_collections.py tests/utilities/test_templating.py` passes (203 tests).

Docs: the `get_from_dict` docstring describes the new lookup order. No other documentation update is necessary.
</details>

title: Fix flaky `date_diff_seconds` from-now tests
body:
This PR fixes the flaky test `TestDateFunctions::test_date_diff_seconds_from_now_column` and the related `_literal` test in `tests/server/utilities/test_database.py`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Failure on main ([run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39274620070), postgres:14): `assert 17.940248 == 17 ± 0.2`.

**Root cause:** The tests set `value = now() - 17s` from the Python clock. Then they asserted that the database `now() - value` is 17s ± 0.2s. This is true only when less than 0.2s passes between the Python `now()` and the database "now". The `_column` test also does an insert and a commit between the two. On Postgres, `now()` is the start time of the next transaction. A CI runner under load can easily add approximately 1s.

**Fix:** Select the database `now()` in the same statement as `date_diff_seconds(...)`. Then assert that the result is equal to `(db_now - value).total_seconds()` (abs=0.01, which covers SQLite millisecond clock resolution and `julianday` rounding). Both values use the same database "now", so the delay between Python and the database does not change the result. The test still makes sure that the one-argument form of `date_diff_seconds` measures from the database "now".

Verification: 20 runs each on SQLite and on Postgres 14 passed. The full module passes with `-n4` on Postgres.
</details>

title: Fix flaky worker channel tests racing a 1s wall-clock deadline
body:
This PR fixes a flaky test: `TestWorkerChannelClient::test_unhealthy_channel_reconnects_with_rest_fallback_active`. It failed on `main` in [this Unit tests run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/39274770756) with a `TimeoutError` from `anyio.fail_after(1)`.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

The test polled `channel.state.terminal` in a loop with `anyio.sleep(0)` inside `anyio.fail_after(1)`. In CI, asyncio logged that the `WorkPoolWorkerChannel._run` task took 1.128 seconds for one step. That delay was enough to go past the 1-second deadline before the channel reached the terminal state.

`WorkPoolWorkerChannel._run` returns by itself after `WorkerChannelTerminalError`. Because of this, the test now lets the `anyio` task group wait for the run loop to finish, and it does not use a wall-clock deadline. If the test hangs, `pytest-timeout` still stops it.

`test_stop_before_run_scope_cancels_started_channel` had the same `fail_after(1)` polling pattern. `channel.stop()` cancels the run scope, so the task group exits after the session closes. The test now checks `exited` after the task group exits.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- To reproduce the failure, I added a temporary `await anyio.sleep(1.5)` to `FakeWorkerChannelConnect.__aexit__`. The original test failed with the same `TimeoutError`. The fixed test passed.
- Both tests passed 30 times each with `--flake-finder --flake-runs=30 -n4`.
- `tests/workers/test_base_worker.py` passes with `-n auto`. The one exception is `TestSubmit::test_basic`, which also fails locally on `main` without this change. It passes in CI.
- pre-commit (ruff check and ruff format) passes.

</details>

title: docs: document pagination contract for bulk reads in CLI AGENTS.md
body:
This PR adds one contract to `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`. Bulk and `--all` CLI commands must page through client `read_*` calls. Delete loops must read again from offset 0 on each pass.

#23440 fixed `prefect deployment delete --all`. Before the fix, it deleted only the first 200 deployments. `prefect automation delete --all` still calls `client.read_automations()` one time without paging, so the same failure can occur there.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: "**Page through "all records" reads.** Client `read_*` list calls without `limit` return at most `PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT` (200) rows (server `LimitBody`), so `--all`/bulk commands must loop on `offset`. When deleting while paging, re-read from offset 0 each pass — advancing `offset` skips rows that shifted into earlier pages."
Non-obvious evidence: An unbounded call such as `client.read_deployments()` looks like it returns all rows. The server applies the cap through the shared `LimitBody` dependency, and the cap is documented only in individual client method docstrings. The same bug existed in `deployment delete --all` (fixed in #23440) and is still present in `automation delete --all`. `deployment schedule pause/resume --all` already pages correctly. So the CLI has an inconsistent pattern that recurs.
Cross-cutting scope: All CLI commands that act on all records or on many records (deployments, automations, schedules, and future `--all` commands), across many command-group files.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule applies to the callers in many CLI files, not to one function. A comment at one call site does not help an agent who writes a new bulk command in a different file.
Durability: The server default limit and the offset-shift behavior during deletion are stable API properties. They do not depend on the triggering PR.
Counter-evidence checked: `src/prefect/cli/AGENTS.md`, `src/prefect/client/AGENTS.md`, root `AGENTS.md` (none mention pagination limits), the `read_deployments`/`read_automations` docstrings, `LimitBody` in `src/prefect/server/api/dependencies.py`, the new inline comment in `deployment.py` (it explains only that call site), and `automation.py`/`deployment.py` bulk paths.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Files changed in the triggering push</summary>

Range `3047941030d088d558fb72cfcbcd8a7b59372042..e79a711b745707a47e350ee0f2154915541e6ed6`:

title: Fix overlapping action branches in the automation JSON schema
body:
This PR fixes the JSON schema that the client automation models generate for actions. It is a follow-up to #23426.

After #23426, `actions`, `actions_on_trigger`, and `actions_on_resolve` generate a `oneOf` with a branch for the known action types and a branch for `UnknownAction`. The `UnknownAction` schema accepted any string `type`, because the Python validator that rejects known types is not in the schema. Thus a valid known action, such as `{"type": "do-nothing"}`, matched both branches, and JSON schema validation failed. Runtime Pydantic parsing was not affected.

The `UnknownAction.type` schema now has `not: {enum: [...]}` with the known action types, from the existing `_KNOWN_ACTION_TYPES`. Runtime routing (the callable discriminator and tags), the runtime validator, and the preservation of extra fields do not change.

<details>
<summary>Example</summary>

```python
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
from prefect.events.schemas.automations import AutomationCore

payload = {
    "name": "example",
    "trigger": {"type": "event", "posture": "Reactive"},
    "actions": [{"type": "do-nothing"}],
}
AutomationCore.model_validate(payload)  # passed before and after
Draft202012Validator(AutomationCore.model_json_schema()).validate(payload)
# before: fails, the action matches more than one oneOf branch
# after: passes
```

A known type with invalid fields, such as `{"type": "change-flow-run-state", "state": 123}`, now fails both runtime and JSON schema validation. It cannot use the `UnknownAction` branch to pass the schema.

</details>

title: Count expect events that race or precede a proactive trigger's window
body:
A proactive trigger with `after` could fire on a window that an `expect` event
had satisfied, so the zombie flow detection automation in #21932 crashed flow
runs that completed. Two gaps let this happen. The same-event reset in
`evaluate` opened the next window empty, and `ensure_bucket` overwrote
`last_event`, so a terminal state that raced the final heartbeat was lost.
Also, the server can evaluate one key's events in any order, and an
`expect`-only event evaluated before its window opened found no bucket and was
dropped. Now every `expect`-only event of a proactive trigger with `after` is
held in a new `automation_held_event` table, whether or not a bucket exists,
and each window that opens or rolls counts the held events that occurred
inside it. An event that finds an open bucket is also counted in it, as
before. No bucket counts an event twice: a window counts held events only
when it is created, and a held event evaluated again is skipped.
`ensure_bucket` also no longer overwrites `last_event`.

Closes #21932

### Where held events go

Held events go in a new `automation_held_event` table, one row per event, keyed
by automation, trigger, bucketing key, and event id. This follows
`automation_bucket` and `automation_event_follower`: plain rows that work the
same on Postgres and SQLite, and that every server replica shares.

- Opening a bucket counts the held rows for its key that occurred inside its
  window, from `start` up to but not including `end`.
- Holding an event deletes rows for the same key that occurred more than
  `PRECEDING_EVENT_LOOKBACK` (15 minutes) before it, and keeps only the newest
  100, or the trigger's threshold if that is higher.
- The periodic triggers task deletes rows held longer than twice the lookback,
  in its own step so a failure elsewhere in the periodic work does not skip it.
  The extra lookback covers an `after` event that causal ordering held for the
  full lookback before evaluating it.
  Deleting an automation cascades to its rows.
- The held-event count is a subquery inside the bucket upsert, so it adds no
  round trip.
- On Postgres, the transaction that evaluates an event for a proactive trigger
  with `after`, and proactive evaluation when it opens a bucket, take an
  advisory lock on the trigger and bucketing key. Holding
  an event and opening a bucket each read what the other writes, so without the
  lock two replicas could each miss the other's uncommitted write. SQLite
  allows one writer at a time and takes no lock, like the composite trigger
  lock.

Only proactive triggers with `after` hold events, count them, or take the
lock.

### Behavior change

An `expect` event with the same `occurred` as the `after` event now counts
whichever of the two is evaluated first. Before, it counted only when the
`after` event was evaluated first.

This includes the `ensure_bucket` change proposed in #21936, and replaces its
one-event carry-forward with the held events.

title: Allow `Task.with_options(tags=[])` to clear existing tags
body:
closes #23443

this PR makes `Task.with_options` treat an explicitly passed empty tags collection (`[]`, `set()`, `()`) as "no tags" instead of falling back to the original task's tags, matching the docstring ("If given, existing tags are ignored, not merged").

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The fallback used `tags or copy(self.tags)`, so any falsy value fell through to the existing tags. It now checks `tags is not None`, so omitting `tags` still keeps the original tags and passing a non-empty collection still replaces them.

```python
@task(tags=["original"])
def example(): ...

example.with_options(tags=[]).tags  # before: {"original"}, after: set()
```

Added a parametrized test in `TestTaskWithOptions` covering `[]`, `set()` and `()`. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.
</details>

title: Copy hook lists in `with_options` for tasks and flows
body:
Closes #23441

This PR makes `Task.with_options`, `Flow.with_options` and `MaterializingTask.with_options` copy the hook lists they take from the original. Before, a hook added to the copy (for example with `@copy.on_failure`) was also added to the original, and the other way round.

<details>
<summary>Cause, tests and range</summary>

The constructors keep a non-empty list as is, and `with_options` passed the original's list in: [tasks.py](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/87b5243845e733ed938b21cf7b9aeda6d6a4e194/src/prefect/tasks.py#L845-L847), [flows.py](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/87b5243845e733ed938b21cf7b9aeda6d6a4e194/src/prefect/flows.py#L581-L585), [`MaterializingTask`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/87b5243845e733ed938b21cf7b9aeda6d6a4e194/src/prefect/tasks.py#L2260-L2263). `Task.with_options` has copied `on_rollback` and `on_commit` since #23186. The same lines are in 3.0.0 and 3.8.8.

Tests: `test_hooks_are_copied_from_original_task` (3 hooks), `test_hooks_are_copied_from_original_flow` (5) and `test_with_options_hooks_are_copied_from_original_task` for `@materialize` (5). `pytest tests/test_tasks.py tests/test_flows.py tests/assets/test_materializing_tasks.py -k hooks_are_copied`: 13 failed before the fix, 13 passed after. `tests/test_tasks.py` and `tests/test_flows.py` in full: 746 passed with the fix (738 on the base commit, plus the 8 new tests).

</details>

title: Delete every deployment with `prefect deployment delete --all`
body:
closes #23438

this PR makes `prefect deployment delete --all` delete every deployment instead of only the first page returned by `read_deployments()` (`PREFECT_SERVER_API_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, 200 by default), and report/confirm the real count.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The confirmation count comes from paging `read_deployments(offset=...)` until an empty page. Summing page sizes gives the exact total even if row order varies between requests.
- Deletion repeatedly reads the first page and deletes it until nothing is left. Offset paging while collecting IDs isn't safe here: the default `NAME_ASC` sort has no tiebreaker, and deployment names are only unique per flow. When same-named deployments straddle a page boundary, one can be returned twice and another skipped (the issue raised on #23439). Reading from offset 0 each time doesn't depend on order, and every successful delete shrinks the result set, so the loop terminates.
- The reported `Deleted N deployments.` is the number actually deleted.

Tests: `small_unstable_pages` serves deployments two per page and rotates the full ordering on every request. Five deployments named `daily` on different flows are created. Both new tests fail on `main` and also fail with the offset-collection approach from #23439, which deletes the same ID twice and gets a 404. They pass with this change. I also checked against a local server: with the ticket's 201 deployments plus 3 tied-name ones, the command printed `Deleted 204 deployments.` and none were left.

Alternative to #23439.
</details>

closes #23887

This PR preserves RDATE and EXDATE instants when an rruleset uses dates in another timezone. It also keeps both occurrences of a repeated DST hour distinct in the client and server schedules.

<details>

No documentation change is needed because this restores the existing schedule contract.

title: Return run input from async `pause_flow_run` when pause is rejected
body:
closes #23434

This PR makes `apause_flow_run` return the loaded run input when the orchestrator rejects the pause (the `state.is_running()` branch). Before this change, the function loaded the input but did not return it. Thus a second `pause_flow_run(wait_for_input=..., key=K)` with the same key returned `None` in async flows.

<details>

- `src/prefect/flow_runs.py`: change `await wait_for_input.aload(run_input_keyset)` to `return await wait_for_input.aload(run_input_keyset)`. This matches the sync `pause_flow_run` and the other branches of `apause_flow_run`.
- `tests/test_flow_engine.py`: add `TestPauseFlowRun.test_repeated_pause_with_same_key_returns_input`. The test pauses an async flow two times with the same key and `wait_for_input`, and asserts that both calls return the input. The test fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- The bug came from the `@sync_compatible` to `@async_dispatch` migration (#20178).

Local checks: `uv run pytest tests/test_flow_engine.py -k "TestPauseFlowRun or TestSuspendFlowRun"` (42 passed, 1 xfailed). Pre-commit passes.

title: Preserve JSON Schema references in flow parameters
body:
closes #15763

This PR preserves non-block `$ref` values in flow parameters. A schema containing `#/$defs/Item` currently fails with `ParameterTypeError` before the flow runs, including when the schema is nested inside a Pydantic model. Local paths, relative references, URLs and non-UUID URNs now pass through as parameter data.

UUID objects, all strings accepted by the UUID parser, and dictionaries containing `block_document_id` or `block_document_slug` still reach `Block.load_from_ref`. This preserves direct UUID-URN block references and errors for malformed explicit block IDs. UUID-parseable schema references retain their existing block interpretation; this change does not introduce a separate schema discriminator. The `validate_parameters` docstring records that boundary.

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

- The direct `urn:uuid:` and `uuid:` block regressions pass on the merge base (`87b5243`), fail on the previous PR head (`f4fdb44`), and pass with this revision.
- The original five schema regressions fail on unchanged upstream with block-resolution errors.
- `uv run pytest tests/blocks/test_block_reference.py tests/test_flows.py -q -n 4`: 402 passed, 11 existing skips, 2 expected failures.
- `uv run pytest tests/typesafety/test_flows.yml -q`: 6 passed.
- `uv run pre-commit run --files src/prefect/flows.py tests/blocks/test_block_reference.py`: all applicable hooks passed.

title: Fix ECS container resource expectations for Moto 5.2.4
body:
This PR fixes the baseline AWS integration CI failure in `test_default` by expecting string CPU and memory values in running-container responses. Moto 5.2.4 now serializes these fields according to the AWS ECS API; the test still expected integers.

Related: #23407, whose S3 changes are independent of this failure.

<details>
<summary>Contract and validation</summary>

[AWS Container](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/API_Container.html) defines `cpu` and `memory` as strings. [Moto #10307](https://github.com/getmoto/moto/pull/10307) corrected JSON serialization in 5.2.4. A controlled comparison with boto3/botocore 1.43.106 confirmed integer values with Moto 5.2.3 and string values with 5.2.4.

The change updates the two running-container expectations and requires `moto[cloudformation]>=5.2.4` in the AWS development dependencies so every allowed Moto version supports these expectations. Container-definition expectations remain integers, and production behavior is unchanged. The integration-local lockfile is explicitly ignored; the generated lock passes `uv lock --check`. The tracked root lock uses the released AWS package and needs no update. No documentation update is needed for this test-only correction.

- Unmodified main `e29ee8a5`: reproduced the exact assertion failure with Moto 5.2.4.
- Main with this correction: all 123 ECS worker tests passed.
- Complete AWS suite on this branch: 702 passed, 1 skipped, 2 xfailed.
- All applicable repository pre-commit and pre-push hooks passed.

Local validation uses Python 3.12 and mocked AWS services.

</details>

title: Fix 500 from flow run list endpoints when a parameter exceeds 64 bits
body:
closes #15031

This PR makes `POST /flow_runs/filter` and `POST /flow_runs/paginate` return normally when a flow run has an integer parameter outside the 64-bit range.

<details>

Both handlers build the response with `orjson.dumps`, which raises `TypeError: Integer exceeds 64-bit range` for integers that don't fit in 64 bits. Flow run creation accepts such parameters (they're arbitrary user data), so one run like `parameters={"x": 2**64 + 1}` makes the list endpoints return 500, which also breaks the UI's flow run views, until that run is deleted.

I added a small private helper in `server/api/flow_runs.py`, `_json_response`, that tries orjson first and falls back to `pydantic_core.to_json` on `TypeError`. `pydantic_core` is already a dependency and serializes big integers exactly. The normal path is unchanged, so no performance difference. I did not touch the other orjson call sites in that file (`resume_flow_run` input handling), since they weren't part of the report.

Tests: two new tests in `tests/server/orchestration/api/test_flow_runs.py` (`TestReadFlowRuns` and `TestPaginateFlowRuns`) create a run with `2**64 + 1` as a parameter and check the endpoint returns 200 with the exact value. Both fail on main with the orjson `TypeError` and pass with the change. The whole file passes locally (173 passed). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (0.15.19, the pre-commit pin) and codespell are clean.

</details>

title: fix(callables): align positional-only arg defaults in source-parsed signatures
body:
## Problem

`_generate_signature_from_source` (`src/prefect/utilities/callables/__init__.py`) reconstructs a function's signature from its AST — used by `parameter_schema_from_entrypoint` to build a deployment's parameter schema without importing the module.

It aligned `ast.arguments.defaults` against only `func_def.args.args`:

```python
defaults = [None] * (len(func_def.args.args) - len(func_def.args.defaults)) + func_def.args.defaults
for param, default in zip(parameters, defaults):
```

But in the AST, `args.defaults` applies to the trailing positional parameters spanning **both** `posonlyargs` and `args`. When a function mixes a required positional-only parameter with later defaulted parameters, `len(args) - len(defaults)` can go negative (collapsing the padding to `[]`), and the `zip` starts at the positional-only params — so defaults land on the wrong parameters. For `def f(a, b=5, /, c=10)` this assigned `a=5, b=10, c=<none>`, producing an invalid signature:

```
ValueError: non-default argument follows default argument
```

So an entrypoint whose function has positional-only args with mixed defaults fails schema generation.

## Fix

Align the defaults against the combined positional count and zip only over the positional parameters:

```python
num_positional = len(func_def.args.posonlyargs) + len(func_def.args.args)
defaults = [None] * (num_positional - len(func_def.args.defaults)) + func_def.args.defaults
for param, default in zip(parameters[:num_positional], defaults):
```

Keyword-only defaults (`args.kw_defaults`) are handled separately earlier and are untouched.

## Test

Adds `TestEntrypointToSchema::test_function_with_positional_only_args_and_mixed_defaults` to `tests/utilities/test_callables.py`. Reverting the alignment change makes it fail with the `ValueError` above, confirming the test is load-bearing. Verified `def f(a, b=5, /, c=10)`, `def f(x, /, y=2)`, and `def f(a, b, /, c=1, *, d=2)` all reconstruct to signatures matching `inspect.signature`.

+    # Handle default values for positional args e.g. def func(a=1, b="hello", c=3.14)

+    # both positional-only and positional-or-keyword args, so align against both.

title: fix(collections): return empty list from extract_instances when no match
body:
## Problem

`extract_instances` (`src/prefect/utilities/collections.py`) documents, for a single `type` argument, that it returns "a list of instances of that type". But it ended with:

```python
return ret[type_]
```

`ret` only gets a key via `setdefault` when a matching object is found, so when **no** object matches the requested type the dict is empty and the subscript raises `KeyError` instead of returning an empty list. This also hits the default `types=object` path on an empty iterable, and the single-element-tuple case.

```python
>>> from prefect.utilities.collections import extract_instances
>>> extract_instances([1, 2, 3], str)
KeyError: <class 'str'>
>>> extract_instances([])
KeyError: <class 'object'>
```

## Fix

Return the documented empty list when nothing matches:

```python
return ret.get(type_, [])
```

Matching behavior is unchanged (`extract_instances([1, "a", 2], int) == [1, 2]`), and the tuple-of-types mapping path is untouched.

## Test

Adds `TestExtractInstances` to `tests/utilities/test_collections.py` covering the single-type match, the no-match/empty cases that previously raised, the single-element-tuple case, and the tuple-mapping path. Reverting the one-line fix makes the three no-match cases fail with `KeyError`, confirming the test is load-bearing.

title: Read automations with action types this version doesn't know
body:
Reading an automation that uses an action type this client doesn't know about now returns an `UnknownAction` instead of raising a `ValidationError`.

## The problem

The client's `ActionTypes` union is closed. Prefect Cloud supports several action types that are not in it:

- `send-email-notification`
- `pause-schedule-for-flow-run`
- `resume-schedule`
- `sla-violation`
- `run-execution-plan`

Any automation that uses one of these fails to parse:

```python
Automation.model_validate({..., "actions": [{"type": "send-email-notification", ...}]})
# pydantic_core.ValidationError: 21 validation errors for Automation
```

`read_automations()` and `read_resource_related_automations()` parse the whole response with `Automation.model_validate_list`. **One such automation breaks the call for the whole workspace**, not only for itself. On Cloud, these fail as soon as a workspace has an automation that uses one of these actions:

- `prefect automation ls` (and `prefect transfer`, which reads every automation)
- `prefect automation inspect`, `enable`, `disable`, and `delete` for that automation
- `Automation.read()` / `Automation.aread()`

Adding each Cloud type to the union, as was done for `DeclareIncident`, doesn't solve this. Cloud can add a type at any time, and every client released before that type keeps failing. The client needs to tolerate action types it doesn't know.

## The change

- **`UnknownAction`** (`prefect.events.actions`, also exported from `prefect.events`) is an `Action` with `type: str` and `extra="allow"`. It keeps every field of the original action.
  - `describe_for_cli()` works as for any other action. For example, `send-email-notification` shows as "Send email notification".
  - It rejects known types, so it can't hide a known action.
- **`ActionTypesOrUnknown`** wraps `ActionTypes` with a callable discriminator, following the pattern `TriggerTypes` already uses. An action with a `type` that isn't in `ActionTypes` goes to `UnknownAction`. Every other action, including one with no `type`, validates against `ActionTypes` as before.
- `AutomationCore.actions`, `actions_on_trigger`, and `actions_on_resolve` use `ActionTypesOrUnknown`.
- **Round trips are lossless.** `Automation.update()` rebuilds an `AutomationCore` from `model_dump()`. The unknown action's extra fields survive that, so updating an automation (for example, enabling it) sends its unknown actions back unchanged rather than dropping or corrupting them.
- **`prefect transfer` skips automations with unknown actions.** It reports `TransferSkipped("Uses action types this version of Prefect does not recognize: ...")`.

title: Fix flaky `test_results_with_timeout` racing a 10ms SIGALRM
body:
This PR changes the timeout in `TestPrefectFutureList::test_results_with_timeout` from `0.01` to `10` seconds.

The test checks that `PrefectFutureList.result(timeout=...)` raises the `TimeoutError` of a failed future. The test does not need the timeout to expire.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and evidence</summary>

Failure: [Unit tests run 38947238913](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/38947238913), job "Canonical Tests: group 18/18 - python:3.12, postgres:14". The xdist worker `gw3` stopped ("node down: Not properly terminated") while it ran this test. The log has no traceback. The setup of the test took 9.13s, so the runner had a high load.

The test runs in the main thread with `@pytest.mark.timeout(method="thread")`. Thus `as_completed` → `timeout_context` → `cancel_sync_after` uses an `AlarmCancelScope`. This scope arms a 10ms `SIGALRM`. The failed future raises from `future.result()` in the body of the `for` loop in `PrefectFutureList.result`. Then the `as_completed` generator closes while the alarm is still armed. On a slow runner, the alarm can fire while the generator closes. Then `CancelledError` comes out of `gen.close()` and the `AlarmCancelScope` exit occurs later, at garbage collection.

I reproduced this race with 16 CPU-burn processes and a loop of the test body (`repros/`, not committed):
- `timeout=0.01`: `Exception ignored in: <generator object as_completed ...> ... CancelledError` from `_sigalarm_to_error`.
- `timeout=10`: 0 occurrences in 10,000 iterations.

I did not reproduce the worker crash itself. The alarm race is the only nondeterministic part of the test, and it explains a failure only under load.

Other tests (`test_wait_with_timeout`, `test_result_timeout_covers_slow_result_retrieval`) continue to test timeouts that expire.

</details>

Verification:
- `test_results_with_timeout` with `--flake-finder --flake-runs=200 -n 4`: 200 passed.
- `tests/test_futures.py -n auto --maxprocesses 6 --dist worksteal`: passed.
- `ruff format` passes. `ruff check` on the file only reports errors that were there before this change.

title: Recover cancellation and suspension observers from websocket outages
body:
closes #23420

this PR makes `FlowRunCancellingObserver` and `FlowRunSuspendingObserver` recover from temporary websocket outages. They poll while the events stream is down, retry it with jittered backoff, and stop polling once a reconnect succeeds and current server state has been reconciled. Previously they stayed in polling mode until shutdown.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- New private `_internal/_observation_delivery.py::ObservationDelivery` is the single owner of the polling/stream handoff, retry timing, and owned task lifetime. Observers give it three operations: consume an event, check current state, and report unavailability. It has no knowledge of observer types, tracked IDs, cancellation claims, or suspension watches.
  - Setup failure, abnormal stream failure, and clean consumer completion all start polling (via the existing `critical_service_loop`) and schedule a reconnect.
  - Each reconnect attempt is bounded by a 10s deadline that covers open/ping/auth/filter. Idle streaming has no deadline.
  - After setup succeeds, events (retained replay plus live) are consumed while `check_current_state` reconciles. Polling is cancelled and awaited only after reconciliation succeeds, so quiet streams recover without needing an event.
  - Reconnect delays are jittered and capped at 5 minutes. The backoff only resets after a connection has stayed up for a while, so connections that close right after the handshake keep backing off.
  - Polling exhaustion with no working stream reports failure right away, even if a reconnect is pending. A poll that fails while a reconnect is completing does not report failure if the handoff succeeds. Deliberate cancellation during handoff or shutdown is normal cleanup. Once shutdown completes, no reconnect or callback can fire.
  - Logging: fallback at warning, restoration at info, individual reconnect failures at debug.
- Observers create subscribers with `reconnection_attempts=0`, so every stream failure reaches the recovery owner. Defaults for other subscribers are unchanged.
- Cancellation: event, polling, and reconciliation paths now share one synchronous per-registration dispatch claim, taken before `on_cancelling` is called (notification dedup, not exactly-once execution). Responses for a removed or re-added registration are ignored, and re-adding a run starts a fresh registration lifetime.
- Suspension: the existing `_SuspensionWatch` objects and checkpoints are kept across reconnects, so replay after resume still confirms through the existing superseded-transition logic. Polling responses only notify the watch they were read for.
- `PrefectEventSubscriber` and `PrefectLogsSubscriber` (the paired implementations) now close a socket left open by a failed or cancelled `__aenter__`. `AsyncExitStack` never exits a context whose entry failed.
- Limits: the stream has no subscription acknowledgement, so the handoff is not atomic; it relies on bounded replay plus reconciliation. A suspension/resume that

title: Make `*args`/`**kwargs` optional collections in flow parameter schemas
body:
closes #23416

this PR makes `*args: T` an optional array of `T` and `**kwargs: T` an optional object with `T` values in generated flow parameter schemas, so deployments with `enforce_parameter_schema` accept runs that omit them or pass valid values for them.

Related to #23417, which makes the same schema change. This PR also fixes the run-time binding and entrypoint gaps that the schema change exposes (see below).

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `process_v2_params` / `process_v1_params`: wrap variadic types in `list[...]` / `dict[str, ...]` and default them to `[]` / `{}`. The explicit schema default also keeps `preprocess_schema` from making them nullable, so `{"kwargs": null}` is rejected rather than failing at execution.
- `parameters_to_args_kwargs`: for `def f(x=1, *args)`, `{"args": [2]}` (now admitted by the schema) was bound as `f(args=[2])`, because `BoundArguments.args` stops at the first missing positional parameter. When `*args` is a non-string, non-mapping iterable, it's converted to a tuple. If that tuple is empty it's dropped; otherwise the omitted defaulted positional parameters before it are filled with their defaults (unwrapping `pydantic.Field` defaults) so the values bind positionally. Other values (`None`, `0`, `False`, strings, dicts) are left untouched, so `Flow.validate_parameters` still rejects them.
- `_generate_signature_from_source` (used by `prefect deploy`): annotations on `*args`/`**kwargs` were discarded, so entrypoint schemas were untyped. They're now evaluated via a small `_evaluate_annotation` helper, which also replaces the three existing copies of that logic.

Example, `def my_flow(x: int = 1, *names: str, **options: int)` with an enforced schema:
- `{}` → previously 409 (`'names' is a required property`), now runs with `(1, (), {})`
- `{"x": 5, "names": ["a", "b"], "options": {"retries": 3}}` → previously 409 (`is not of type 'integer'`), now `(5, ('a', 'b'), {'retries': 3})`

Tests cover:
- the schema for v2, v1 and entrypoint signatures
- the binder, including non-list iterables and invalid values that are passed through
- rejection of invalid `*args` values in `Flow.validate_parameters`
- an end-to-end `run_deployment` + `run_flow` with `enforce_parameter_schema=True`, including rejection of `null` variadics
</details>

title: Add opt-in clearing for empty deployment schedules
body:
closes #23097

this PR adds `PREFECT_DEPLOYMENTS_CLEAR_SCHEDULES_ON_EMPTY` (default `false`) so users can opt in to clearing schedules with `schedules: []` while retaining the current documented behavior by default, following [the maintainer's proposed migration](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23412#issuecomment-6269749384).

With the default setting, an explicit empty list on redeployment preserves schedules and emits a visible `FutureWarning`. The warning explains how to opt in or preserve schedules explicitly, and states the deprecation window: at least six months or three minor releases, whichever is longer. Clearing will become the default in a later release, which will remove the setting and warning.

Both `RunnerDeployment.apply(schedules=[])` and `aapply(schedules=[])` honor the setting. The CLI continues to distinguish explicit `[]` from omitted schedules, `null`, and a declined schedule prompt; those preservation cases work in either mode. New deployments do not emit the warning.

<details>
<summary>Implementation and compatibility</summary>

- When opted in, empty-list updates clear schedules with or without slugs. The existing deployment update API clears schedules without slugs. For deployments whose schedules all have slugs, the client deletes them explicitly after a successful deployment update, using the same API as `prefect deployment schedule clear`.
- Explicit deletions are separate requests, so they are not atomic with the deployment update. Already-removed schedules are tolerated; other deletion failures propagate, and clearing can be retried.
- Default empty-list preservation explicitly excludes schedules from the update payload, even when the deployment object already contains empty or populated schedules or was used for an earlier opt-in clear. The object's schedule value is left unchanged.
- The server's schedule reconciliation behavior is unchanged.
- Added the setting to the deployment settings model and test registry, and regenerated settings types, JSON schema, and reference documentation. Updated the YAML guide with the default behavior and opt-in command.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

The preset-object regression matrix produced **8 failures and 16 passes before the follow-up fix**, then **24 passes afterward** within the broader suite. It covers sync and async calls, both setting values, slugged and unslugged schedules, pre-set empty/populated lists, and reuse after an earlier opt-in clear. Preservation retains the server's schedules and the object's schedule value while still updating deployment metadata.

The existing compatibility tests cover both SDK paths and CLI redeployment, both setting values, slugged and unslugged schedules, omitted/null/empty inputs, populated SDK updates, and declined CLI prompts.

Additional tests cover multiple and mixed schedules, repeated clearing, empty/new deployments, the default setting, and preserving schedules when the API rejects a deploymen

title: fix: Replace dead Sanity logo URLs in bundled collection metadata
body:
this PR replaces the remaining Sanity-hosted logo URLs (now 404) in the bundled collection metadata, completing the migration from #23231 and #23235. It's the 3.x equivalent of the 2.x change in #23353.
Details #23235 updated `_logo_url` on block classes but intentionally left the bundled collection metadata unchanged. On startup, `_register_collection_blocks` registers block types from `collection_blocks_data.json` and overwrites the stored metadata, so integration block types such as `s3-bucket` and `aws-credentials` keep showing a missing icon in the UI, even after upgrading Prefect or the integration. - `src/prefect/server/collection_blocks_data.json`: 40 `logo_url`s replaced. 29 use the repo-hosted assets from `assets/block-logos/mapping.json`. dbt, GitLab and Databricks have no repo-hosted asset, so their 11 entries use the URL their integration's `_logo_url` has on `main`. - `src/prefect/server/api/collections_data/views/aggregate-worker-metadata.json`: 8 `logo_url`s replaced via the same mapping (offline fallback when the registry fetch fails). Validation: - Every `logo_url` in both files returns HTTP 200 - `uv run pytest tests/server/orchestration/api/test_collections.py tests/server/models/test_block_registration.py`: 15 passed - A fresh local server registers `s3-bucket` with the new `aws.png` URL - `pre-commit` passed on both files

title: fix timeout=0 raising Timeout error in PrefectFutureList.result
body:
<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://docs.prefect.io/contribute/index
-->

<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
<!-- Whether or not AI tools helped draft this PR, you are responsible for understanding the change, keeping it scoped, validating it locally, and explaining the approach. -->
<!-- Maintainers may close PRs that appear low-effort, likely AI-generated, and substantially far from the expected implementation. -->

`futures.result(timeout=0)` gives `TimeoutError`. It was happening because of the deadline check in `PrefectFutureList.result`.
This check treats a zero timeout as fail after first result instead.

The following example shows the problem:
```py
from prefect import flow, task
from prefect.futures import wait


@task
def add_one(x: int) -> int:
    return x + 1


@flow
def demo():
    futures = add_one.map([0, 1])
    wait(futures)  # every task is now complete

    print([f.result(timeout=0) for f in futures])  # [1, 2]
    print(futures.result(timeout=0))  # expected [1, 2], raises TimeoutError
```

title: Preserve S3 bucket prefixes for paths with leading slashes
body:
closes #15267

This PR keeps `S3Bucket.bucket_folder` when a read or write path starts with `/`. For example, writing `/reports/file.txt` with `bucket_folder="/appname"` now stores `/appname/reports/file.txt`.

It preserves the configured folder's leading slash, already-prefixed keys, and behavior without a configured folder. This follows the earlier work in #15287 and #22842, both closed without merging.

<details>
<summary>Implementation and verification</summary>

`pathlib` treats a leading-slash path as absolute and discards the left side of the join. `_resolve_path` now removes leading slashes from incoming child paths before joining them to a configured folder. For relative folders, the already-prefixed check uses the normalized input. It also recognizes exact folder keys when the configured folder ends in `/`. The synchronous and asynchronous read/write docstrings describe the leading-slash behavior.

Regression tests check actual S3 keys, read-back using the original and returned paths, and object downloads using their documented relative-path contract. The 48-case matrix covers both credential fixtures, sync/async calls, leading and trailing slashes, already-prefixed inputs, empty paths, a `/` folder, and prefix segment boundaries.

- Unchanged S3 baseline: 166 passed, 2 xfailed.
- Original 20 regression cases against unchanged code: 16 failed, 4 passed. All failures were at the expected key assertion.
- Review follow-up: 16 cases failed on the first patch; all 48 cases pass with the follow-up.
- Complete final S3 suite: 214 passed, 2 xfailed.
- All applicable pre-commit and pre-push hooks passed. GitHub's pre-commit, type checks, and CodeQL checks also passed on `00817b6`.
- Final [AWS CI](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/38508462387) on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13: each has 749 passed, 1 skipped, 2 xfailed, 1 failed. The only failure is the existing ECS `test_default` assertion. It also reproduces locally with both changed files restored to upstream `302beb37`: expected numeric `cpu` and `memory` values are strings in the mocked response with moto 5.2.4 and boto3 1.43.106. This corresponds to Moto's [serializer change](https://github.com/getmoto/moto/pull/10307). All S3 tests passed.

Local tests used Python 3.12.11 on macOS and moto's AWS mocks. No live AWS or Windows verification was performed.

</details>

title: Fix `visit_collection` returning another object's cached result after id reuse
body:
closes #23403

`visit_collection` caches results in `_seen` by `id()` (added in #18434 for shared references). When the visitor returns a new collection and that collection is then copied because its items changed, nothing keeps the new collection alive. Python frees it, the next new collection is often created at the same address, and `visit_collection` returns the earlier cached result for it.

A real case is `Block.save()` for a block with a field like `list[Credential]` where `Credential` has a `SecretStr`. `handle_secret_render` returns a new `model_dump()` dict per model, and most entries end up stored as copies of the first ones (see the issue).

The fix stores the visited object next to its result in `_seen` (`(expr, result)`), so its id cannot be reused while the traversal runs. Lookups read the result part. Nothing else changes, and `_seen` is private to `visit_collection`.

Tests:
- `tests/utilities/test_collections.py`: a visitor that returns a new list per item, whose items are then replaced. Fails on `main`, passes with the fix.
- `tests/blocks/test_core.py`: dumping a block with a list of 20 models holding secrets, with `include_secrets`. Fails on `main`, passes with the fix.
- `tests/utilities`, `tests/blocks`, `tests/test_futures.py`, `tests/test_task_engine.py`, `tests/test_flows.py`, `tests/test_tasks.py` (`-n 4`): 2,374 passed with the fix. The only failures are 6 tests in `tests/blocks/test_redis.py` that need a Redis server; they fail the same way without the fix.
- Saving and loading a block with 20 credentials against a local test server: 18 wrong entries before, 0 after.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue. (small fix)
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed. (bug fix, no docs change)
- [ ] If this pull request removes docs files, it includes redirect settings in `mint.json`. (not applicable)
- [ ] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings. (not applicable)

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to help find, fix and test this. I reviewed the change and can explain every line.

--- src/prefect/utilities/collections.py (+6/-4)
@@ -432,11 +432,13 @@ def visit_expression(expr: Any) -> Any:
         return result if return_data else None
     elif obj_id in _seen:
         # Return the cached transformed result
-        return _seen[obj_id] if return_data else None
+        return _seen[obj_id][1] if return_data else None
 
     # Mark this object as being processed to handle circular references
-    # We'll update with the actual result later
-    _seen[obj_id] = expr
+    # We'll update with the actual result later. The object is stored next to
+    # its result so it stays alive and its id cannot be reused by a different
+    # object during this traversal.
+    _seen[obj_id] = (expr, expr)
 
     # Then visit every item in the expression if it is a collection
 
@@ -547,7 +549,7 @@ def visit_expression(expr: Any) -> Any:
 
     # Update the cache with the final transformed result
     if return_data:
-        _seen[obj_id] = result
+        _seen[obj_id] = (expr, result)
 
     if return_data:
         return result

         assert result["level1"]["unique"] is result["level1"]["level2"]["also_unique"]
 
+    def test_visit_collection_new_collections_from_visitor_are_not_mixed_up(self):
+        """Collections created by the visitor must not share cached results, even
+        if one is freed and a later one is allocated at the same address."""
+
+        class Ref:
+            def __init__(self, value: int):
+                self.value = value
+
+        def _visitor(x):
+            if isinstance(x, Ref):
+                # a new list on every call, whose items are transformed below
+                return [x.value, "placeholder"]
+            if x == "placeholder":
+                return "replaced"
+            return x

+            [Ref(i) for i in range(100)], _visitor, return_data=True
+        )

---

### CairoSVG: Quadratic-time DoS parsing a crafted SVG <path>
[CVE-2026-107378](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-107378) / [GHSA-c3jg-qh8m-j3h2](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-c3jg-qh8m-j3h2)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

Rendering an untrusted SVG whose `<path d="...">` contains many segments is O(n²) CPU. A single `<path>` under 1 MiB burns tens of seconds. Two independent O(n²) sites in `cairosvg/path.py`:

1. **Tokenizer** — the path-data parser consumes the `d` string with a `while string:` loop that repeatedly slices/re-scans the *remaining* string (each step is O(len remaining)), giving O(n²) over the whole attribute.
2. **draw_markers** — marker handling drains `node.vertices` with `while node.vertices: ... node.vertices.pop(0)`; `list.pop(0)` is O(n), so draining n vertices is O(n²).

Both are hit on a normal render path (`svg2png`/`svg2pdf`), attacker controls only the SVG document.

##### PoC (installed cairosvg 2.9.0)

```python
import cairosvg
d = "M0 0 " + "L1 1 " * 100000
svg = f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="10" height="10"><path d="{d}"/></svg>'
cairosvg.svg2png(bytestring=svg.encode())   # ~4.4 s for a 488 KB doc
```

| path segments | SVG size | time |
|---|---|---|
| 50,000 | 244 KB | 1.14 s |
| 100,000 | 488 KB | 4.36 s |
| 200,000 | ~960 KB | ~18 s |

Doubling segments ≈ 4× time ⇒ quadratic. Sub-MiB input ⇒ ~18 s CPU; any service rendering user-supplied SVG (thumbnails, avatars, PDF export) is a DoS target.

##### Reachability

Public API `svg2png` / `svg2pdf` / `svg2ps` on an untrusted SVG string.

##### Suggested fix

Tokenize with a single forward scan / index (or `re.finditer`) instead of re-slicing the remainder; drain `vertices` with an index or `collections.deque.popleft` instead of `list.pop(0)`. Optionally cap path-segment count.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 8.7 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

title: Add Python 3.15 support
body:
Adds support for Python 3.15, released October 9, 2026.

### Changes
- `pyproject.toml` / `client/pyproject.toml`: extend `requires-python` to `<3.16` and add the `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.15` classifier
- `.github/workflows/python-tests.yaml`: add `"3.15"` to the test matrix
- `.github/workflows/docker-images.yaml`: add `"3.15"` to both image matrices (stable `python:3.15` images are on Docker Hub)
- `uv.lock` refreshed for the wider range. Packages bumped to versions that publish cp315 wheels or fixed 3.15 incompatibilities: `beartype` 0.22.9 → 0.23.1 (`typing.no_type_check_decorator` removed), `rpds-py` 0.30.0 → 2026.9.1, `libcst` 1.8.6 → 1.9.0, `grpcio` 1.76.0 → 1.84.0, `pydantic` 2.13.4 → 2.14.1 (`pydantic-core` 2.46.4 → 2.50.1), `asyncpg` 0.31.0 → 0.32.0, `orjson` 3.11.9 → 3.13.0, `whenever` → 0.10.5, `greenlet`, `cffi`, `librt`, `markupsafe`, `regex`, `typing-inspection`
- `numpy` resolves per Python version: `<2.5` on Python <3.15 (locks 2.4.1; 2.5's PEP 695 `type` stubs break mypy with `python_version = "3.11"`), `>=2.5.4` on 3.15 for its cp315 wheels
- `whenever` bumped to `>=0.10.5`, which publishes cp315 wheels

#### Code changes needed for 3.15 / new dep versions
- `src/prefect/types/_datetime.py` + `src/prefect/server/schemas/schedules.py`: use `ZonedDateTime.add()`, which works in both whenever's compiled and pure-Python implementations (`ZonedDateTime + ItemizedDelta` is unsupported in the pure-Python fallback used when no wheel is available).
- Deployment parameters follow Pydantic's native serialization. With Pydantic 2.14+, datetimes, dates, and times serialize as ISO strings with timezone offsets preserved; timedeltas remain numeric seconds. Parameters annotated `str | datetime` retain the serialized string after validation; use `datetime` when datetime coercion is required.
- `src/prefect/types/__init__.py` + automation schemas: pydantic 2.14 also stopped applying `ser_json_timedelta` to generated JSON schemas (pydantic/pydantic#13711), so `timedelta` fields declare `{"format": "duration"}` while dumps emit float seconds. Added `DurationOrSecondsTimeDelta` (`anyOf[number, duration]` — matching what validation accepts and serialization emits) and applied it to trigger `within`/`range`/`firing_for` fields and `NonNegativeTimeDelta` (`schedule_after`).
- `src/prefect/utilities/pydantic.py`: pyright fix — `TypeForm` annotations lack `__name__`.
- `tests/test_locking.py`: ignore the new Python 3.15 `DeprecationWarning` for `fork()` in a multi-threaded process; the test deliberately exercises the fork start method.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

Full dev environment syncs and installs cleanly on CPython 3.15.0 locally:

- `pytest tests/test_flows.py tests/test_tasks.py` — 733 passed
- `pytest tests/_internal tests/engine tests/test_flow_engine.py tests/test_task_engine.py` — 1017 passed
- `pytest tests/runner/test_runner.py` — 241 passed
- `pytest tests/events` — 1205 passed
- CI: all `python:3.15` lanes pas

title: Reset pause keys when a blocking pause is rescheduled
body:
closes #23398

This PR makes `HandleResumingPausedFlows` clear the pause metadata when a run moves from a blocking pause (`pause_reschedule=False`) to a `SCHEDULED` state, such as `AwaitingRetry` after SIGTERM. It also makes `HandlePausingFlows` drop stale run input for a pause key that is accepted again.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Problem.** A flow pauses with `pause_flow_run()` and the pod gets SIGTERM. The supervisor (`prefect flow-run execute` with the reschedule SIGTERM behavior, or `Runner`) then proposes `AwaitingRetry` directly from `Paused`. The new attempt runs the flow from the start, and the client pause counter starts again at `"1"`. The server still has `{"1", "2"}` in `empirical_policy.pause_keys`. Thus `HandlePausingFlows` rejects each pause with "This pause has already fired." and returns `RUNNING`. The flow continues without human approval.

**Fix.** A blocking pause always resumes in-process with `Running()`. Thus, `PAUSED -> SCHEDULED` from a blocking pause always starts a new attempt. In that case, `after_transition` now sets `pause_keys = set()`, `resuming = False` and `retry_type = "reschedule"`. This is the same reset that `RetryFailedFlows` and `HandleFlowTerminalStateTransitions` do, with the same `api-version >= 0.8.4` gate. Like those paths, it clears the whole set, so a suspension approved earlier fires again on the new attempt. That costs an extra approval but can't skip one.

All other exits from `PAUSED` do not change. Reschedule-style pauses (`suspend_flow_run`, `pause_reschedule=True`) resume with `Scheduled(name="Resuming")`. They keep their keys, because they rerun the flow from the start and use the keys to skip pauses that already fired.

Because `resuming` is now `False` on the new attempt, `IncrementFlowRunCount` also increments `run_count` for the retried attempt. Before this change, it did not.

**Replayed input pauses.** When a `wait_for_input` pause fires again, the schema/description/response records from the earlier attempt are still stored under the same `run_input_keyset`. Saving the schema then fails with a 409. When `HandlePausingFlows` accepts a pause, it now deletes the input stored under that keyset. Any such records must come from an earlier attempt, because the key had not yet fired on this one.

**Tests.**
- `TestResumingFlows`: a blocking pause to `AwaitingRetry` clears the keys. A reschedule-style pause to `Scheduled("Resuming")` keeps them.
- `TestPausingFlows::test_clears_stale_run_input_for_accepted_pause`
- `TestSetFlowRunState::test_pauses_fire_again_after_blocking_pause_is_rescheduled`: an API-level test of the full sequence from the issue. It fails on `main` with "This pause has already fired."
- `TestSetFlowRunState::test_input_pauses_can_be_replayed_after_blocking_pause_is_rescheduled`: pause for input, resume, reschedule, then replay. Without the input cleanup, saving the schema again returns 409.

title: fix silently skipped task retries in `retry_condition_fn`

<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://docs.prefect.io/contribute/index
-->

<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
<!-- Whether or not AI tools helped draft this PR, you are responsible for understanding the change, keeping it scoped, validating it locally, and explaining the approach. -->
<!-- Maintainers may close PRs that appear low-effort, likely AI-generated, and substantially far from the expected implementation. -->

When writing a prefect flow with a retry policy using `class` method, it fails. Docs say the `retry_condition_fn` has to be a callable but it only works with plain functions. This PR fixes it.

```py
from prefect import flow, task


class APIError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status_code):
        self.status_code = status_code
        super().__init__(f"API returned HTTP {status_code}")


class APIRetryPolicy:
    """Reusable retry rules for tasks calling our API."""

    def __init__(self, retryable_status_codes):
        self.retryable_status_codes = set(retryable_status_codes)

    def should_retry(self, task, task_run, state):
        print("Retry policy was called")

        try:
            state.result()
        except APIError as exc:
            # Retry temporary failures, but not errors like 401 or 403.
            return exc.status_code in self.retryable_status_codes
        except Exception:
            return False

        return False


policy = APIRetryPolicy(
    retryable_status_codes={429, 500, 502, 503, 504}
)


@flow
def demonstrate_retry_bug():
    attempts = 0

    @task(
        retries=2,
        retry_delay_seconds=0,
        retry_condition_fn=policy.should_retry,
        cache_policy=None,
        persist_result=False,
    )
    def fetch_customer():
        nonlocal attempts
        attempts += 1
        print(f"API request #{attempts}")

        # Simulate a temporary outage on the first request.
        if attempts == 1:
            raise APIError(503)

        return {"customer_id": 123, "name": "Alice"}

    state = fetch_customer(return_state=True)
    print(f"{attempts} attempt(s), final state={state.name}")

    if state.is_completed():
        print(f"Customer: {state.result()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demonstrate_retry_bug()


# Actual output

# API request #1
# 1 attempt(s), final state=Failed

#  Expected output

#  API request #1
#  Retry policy was called
#  API request #2
#  2 attempt(s), final state=Completed
#  Customer: {'customer_id': 123, 'name': 'Alice'}
```

title: fix(client): preserve pytz timezone names in `RRuleSchedule.from_rrule()`
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23394

This PR makes `_iana_timezone_name` read the `zone` attribute. pytz timezones keep their IANA name in `zone`. Before this change, the function checked only `key`, `name`, and `_filename`. Thus `RRuleSchedule.from_rrule()` stored `UTC` for every rrule that had a pytz-zoned `dtstart`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The `is_valid_timezone` guard stays. If `zone` is not a valid IANA name (for example `pytz.FixedOffset`, where `zone` is `None`), the function continues to fall back to `UTC`.
- Tests: a `pytz` case is added to the two parametrized `from_rrule` tests. New tests cover `tz.localize(...)` dtstarts for a single rrule and for an rruleset. They also cover `_iana_timezone_name` with a named pytz zone, `pytz.utc`, and `pytz.FixedOffset`.
- The server-side `RRuleSchedule.from_rrule` has a similar `name`/`key` lookup. This PR does not change it, because only tests call it.
- [#23295](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/23295) changes the `_filename` branch of the same function. If both PRs merge, a small rebase can be necessary.

</details>

title: Exit non-zero from `flow-run execute` when a crash cannot be reported
body:
closes #23392

This PR makes `prefect flow-run execute` exit non-zero when the flow run process crashes and the runner can't record a final state for the run. It exits with the process status code, or `1` if there's no non-zero code to pass through.

Before this change, `execute` ignored the result of `FlowRunExecutor.submit()` and exited 0. When the `Crashed` proposal failed (for example, the API returned 500 or was unreachable), the run stayed `Running`. Infrastructure-level crash detection (such as the prefect-aws ECS observer) didn't act because the container exit code was 0.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `FlowRunExecutionResult` has a new field, `crash_unreported`. `FlowRunExecutor.submit()` sets it to `True` when the process exits non-zero (or fails after it has exited), no engine receipt exists, and `propose_crashed` does not return a final state.
- If the starter raises after the process has started and exited (for example, an output stream failure in `run_process`, which drains the pipes and waits before re-raising), `submit()` now gets the handle with `ProcessManager.get` and handles it like a normal exit. Before, this path returned `None`, so `execute` exited 0, and the handle was never removed from the process manager. If the process is still alive (`returncode is None`), `submit()` takes the existing "could not start" path and leaves the handle registered, so `ProcessManager` can still stop the process.
- `execute` keeps the result. After the executor context exits, if `crash_unreported` is `True`, it exits non-zero. A negative (signal) status code becomes `128 + signum` (for example, `-9` becomes `137`).
- If the runner reports `Crashed` successfully, `execute` still exits 0. This keeps the current behavior for infrastructure that retries on non-zero exit (for example, Kubernetes jobs with `backoffLimit > 0`), so a run that is already `Crashed` is not retried.
- The SIGTERM reschedule/relinquish exits do not change.
- To keep exits outside the executor context (a `SystemExit` in an anyio task group gets wrapped), the no-signal-handler path now uses `if/else` instead of an early `return`. Most of the CLI diff is this re-indent; view it with whitespace hidden.

Tests:
- `tests/runner/test__flow_run_executor.py` covers `crash_unreported` for:
  - an accepted `Crashed` state
  - a failed proposal (`None`)
  - a non-final returned state
  - a zero exit
  - an engine receipt
  - a starter that fails after the process exits (exit `1` and `0`)
  - a starter that fails while the process is still alive
  - a starter that fails before handoff
- `tests/cli/test_flow_run.py` has end-to-end tests with a flow that calls `os._exit(1)`:
  - With the API available, the run is `Crashed` and `execute` exits 0.
  - With `propose_state` failing in the runner, `execute` exits 1 and the run is not final.
  - With the output stream also failing, `execute` still exits 1. This test fails on the first commit of this PR.
- Unit tests in `tests/cli/te

title: Fix `prefect deploy` dropping list items templated from step outputs
body:
This PR keeps unresolved list items in `apply_values` when `remove_notset=False`, so `prefect deploy` no longer drops list entries that reference build/push step outputs.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`prefect deploy` applies environment variables to the deployment config early, with `apply_values(deploy_config, os.environ, remove_notset=False)`, so that placeholders for step outputs survive until the build steps have run. For dict values this works: an unresolved value is kept as-is. For list items it does not: the list branch of `apply_values` always dropped items that resolved to `NotSet`, regardless of `remove_notset`. A list entry that is only a step output placeholder was removed before its step ran.

Reproduction, `prefect.yaml`:

```yaml
build:
- prefect.deployments.steps.run_shell_script:
    id: get-commit-hash
    script: echo abc123
    stream_output: false
deployments:
- name: demo
  entrypoint: flow.py:hello
  work_pool:
    name: demo-pool
  tags:
  - "{{ get-commit-hash.stdout }}"
  - prod
  description: "commit {{ get-commit-hash.stdout }}"
```

`prefect deploy --all` then `prefect deployment inspect hello/demo`:

- before: `'description': 'commit abc123'`, `'tags': ['prod']`
- after: `'description': 'commit abc123'`, `'tags': ['abc123', 'prod']`

The fix keeps the original list item when `remove_notset` is False, matching the existing dict behavior. The default (`remove_notset=True`) is unchanged, so worker job-variable templating and step input templating behave as before. Placeholders that still cannot be resolved after the steps run are removed (with a warning) by the later `apply_values(..., warn_on_notset=True)` call, the same as for dict values.

</details>

title: Fix JSON flow results with `data` or `result` keys reading back wrong
body:
closes #23372

This PR changes `ResultRecord.coerce_old_format` so that it only converts the exact legacy `PersistedResultBlob` shape. The keys must be a subset of `serializer`, `data`, `prefect_version`, and `expiration`. The `data` value must be a string and the `serializer` value must be an object.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Flow result stores write the raw serialized value, with no record envelope. When Prefect reads the result from metadata, `ResultRecord.deserialize` first tries to validate the raw bytes as a record. Before this change, `coerce_old_format` changed every object with a `data` key into a record, and it added an empty `metadata` to every object. Thus a JSON flow result such as `{"data": [1, 2, 3], "total": 3}` or `{"result": 5, "status": "ok"}` validated as a record. Prefect then returned the inner value with pickle metadata, or failed with a base64 error.

Now, objects that do not have the legacy shape do not get coerced. Raw results without `metadata` fail validation, and `deserialize` uses the `backup_serializer` as before. Full records from `serialize()` and legacy `PersistedResultBlob` payloads are still read correctly.

The store cannot tell if a stored value is raw or an envelope: `_from_metadata` reads flow results (raw) and task results (envelope) with the same store settings. Thus a strict shape check is used. A raw value with exactly the legacy keys and types is still read as a legacy blob.

Tests:
- `test_deserialize_raw_result_with_record_like_keys` and `test_flow_json_result_with_record_like_keys` cover the issue payloads and objects with `data` and `serializer` keys. They fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- `test_deserialize_legacy_persisted_result_blob` makes sure that the legacy blob format is still readable.

The repro script in the issue now returns the same value from the API as the in-process value for all payloads.
</details>

title: Serialize context on every `ProcessPoolTaskRunner.submit()`
body:
closes #23371

This PR makes `ProcessPoolTaskRunner.submit()` serialize the caller's context on every submit. Before, the runner kept the context from the first submit and used it for all later submits. Thus `tags()` and `temporary_settings()` around a later submit had no effect in the subprocess. Also, tags from the first submit went to all later tasks, and `tag:` concurrency slots came from those incorrect tags.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `serialize_context()` now runs on each submit. This is the same behavior as `ThreadPoolTaskRunner`, which calls `copy_context()` on each submit.
- The env dict from #20972 is still cached. It is now keyed on the active `Settings` object (`_cached_env_settings`). Thus the runner makes the env again when the settings change (for example, inside `temporary_settings`).
- `_run_task_in_subprocess` now restores the worker's `os.environ` after each task. Before, a reused worker kept the env vars from an earlier task. Thus a setting from a `temporary_settings()` block stayed active for later tasks after the block ended.
- `_cached_context` is removed. `cancel_all()` clears `_cached_env` and `_cached_env_settings`.
- Tests: the `test_cached_context_*` tests asserted the incorrect reuse. They are replaced by env-cache tests and by regression tests for these cases: tags on a later submit, no leak of tags from an earlier submit, and default → `temporary_settings` → default on one worker. The regression tests fail on `main` and pass with this change.

Repro from the issue, with this change:
```
Thread: ([], ['late'])
Process: ([], ['late'])
```
</details>

title: Check out pinned `commit_sha` when a git checkout already exists
body:
closes #23370

This PR fixes `GitRepository.is_current_commit`. Before this change, it ran `git rev-parse <commit_sha>` and compared the output to `commit_sha`. For a full 40-character SHA, `rev-parse` returns its input, so the check was always `True`. HEAD was never read. Because of this, `pull_code()` returned early when the destination already had a checkout, and runs kept the code of the previous commit.

Now the method compares `git rev-parse HEAD` with `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`. Short SHAs now also resolve correctly.

With the check fixed, the "switch an existing checkout to a new pin" path runs, and this PR fixes three gaps in it:
- **Shallow checkouts**: `git fetch origin --unshallow` became `git fetch origin --unshallow <sha>`. Before, a commit that was only reachable from another branch could not be checked out.
- **Commit already local**: no fetch runs when the commit is already present (`_has_commit`). A pin that is cached locally still works when the remote is unreachable, and the checkout is not deleted and recloned.
- **Submodules**: with `include_submodules=True`, `git submodule update --init --recursive` now runs after checking out a pinned commit. Both the existing-checkout path and the fresh-clone path go through `_checkout_commit`, which calls the new `_update_submodules` helper. Before, a fresh pinned clone (`--no-checkout`) left submodules empty, and switching pins left submodules at the old revisions. The update also runs when `HEAD` already matches the pin, so a pull that failed partway through gets retried. If the update fails, it raises a sanitized `RuntimeError`, the same way `_clone_repo` does. Credentials are removed from stderr, and the chained exception is dropped when credentials are present.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- The existing mocked tests did not cover the comparison. The new `TestGitRepositoryCommitSha` tests use real `git` with a local upstream over `file://`, so they need no network:
  - Pull commit A, then commit B, into the same destination. HEAD and file contents must be B.
  - Shallow branch checkout, then pin a commit that only exists on another branch.
  - Pin A, then B, then make the upstream unreachable and pin A again.
  - Parent repo with a submodule: pin two parent commits that reference different submodule commits.
  - Parent repo with a submodule whose upstream is unreachable on the first pull. A second pull at the same pin, with the upstream restored, fills in the submodule.
  - `is_current_commit()` for the full SHA of HEAD, a short SHA of HEAD, a different commit, and a SHA that does not exist.
- `test_submodule_update_errors_obscure_access_token` makes a submodule update fail with a token in the URL, and checks that the token is absent from the error, the traceback, and the output.
- All of the behavior tests above fail before this change and pass with it.
- No docs change: this restores the documented behavior of `commit_sha`.

</details>

### Checklist

- [x]

title: Unwrap `FieldInfo` defaults for unmapped parameters in `task.map()`
body:
closes #23368

This PR fixes `task.map()` so that a parameter declared with `Field(default=...)` gets its default value instead of the `FieldInfo` object.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

#23228 unwrapped `FieldInfo` defaults in `get_call_parameters`, which direct calls and `.submit()` use. `.map()` does not apply defaults through `get_call_parameters`. It fills unmapped parameters from `get_parameter_defaults`, which returned `param.default` unchanged. Both map paths use this helper: `TaskRunner.map` and `expand_mapping_parameters` (the `deferred=True` path).

Changes:
- Add the private helper `_resolve_field_info_default` in `prefect.utilities.callables`. `get_call_parameters` and `get_parameter_defaults` both use it. The unwrap behavior in `get_call_parameters` does not change.
- Add tests for `get_parameter_defaults`, `expand_mapping_parameters`, and `TestTaskMap` (sync and async tasks). The new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change.

Out of scope: `Field(default_factory=...)` still resolves to `PydanticUndefined` on direct calls, and on `.map()` too after this change (before, `.map()` passed the `FieldInfo`). Pydantic 2.10 has no public API to detect factories that take validated data, so a fix for that needs its own change.

</details>

title: prefect-dbt: track microbatch models as a single task run
body:
dbt emits a `NodeStart`/`NodeFinished` pair for a microbatch model and one pair for each batch. All pairs have the model's `unique_id`, and the batch pairs are nested in the model pair. `PrefectDbtRunner` created a task run for each `NodeStart`. `NodeTaskTracker` then replaced the node's completion event, so the earlier task runs stayed in `Running`.

This PR changes `PrefectDbtRunner._create_unified_callback`:

- It counts the open `NodeStart` events for each node (`_open_node_starts`). Only the first `NodeStart` creates a task run. Only the `NodeFinished` that closes the last open start sets the node status and runs the `post_model` hooks. The callback queue gives `NodeStart` a higher priority than `NodeFinished`, so the count cannot go to zero too early.
- `_reset_callback_processor` clears the counter.
- dbt>=1.9 gives a microbatch model with failed batches the status `partial success`. dbt marks dependents of this status as errors, but the runner set the task run to `Completed`. This PR adds `NodeStatus.PartialSuccess` to `FAILURE_STATUSES` when it is available, so the task run fails and dependents are skipped.

Tests:
- Unit test with a nested start/finish sequence: one `_call_task` call, the task completes only at the outermost finish, and the hook runs one time.
- `execute_dbt_node` test parametrized with `partial success`.
- DuckDB integration test with a real microbatch model (3 batches), for a success run and a run where one batch fails. Before the fix, the success run made 4 task runs for the model.

title: Add Run action to the React flows list menu and flow page
body:
Users who open **Flows** to start work currently have no run control there — Quick run / Custom run only live on deployment pages. This adds a **Run** item to each React Flows-list row's overflow menu (first, above Copy ID) (shown only when the flow has deployments) and a **Run** button in the flow detail page header (next to the overflow menu). Both open a dialog that lets you pick one of the flow's deployments and run it with the existing deployment-run behavior.

Related to #15512. Prior discussion of the same request (Prefect 2.x, closed): #9806.

**Behavior**
- Flows list: the row menu shows **Run** only once the flow's deployment count has loaded and is above zero. The menu reuses the `buildDeploymentsCountByFlowQuery` query the Deployments column already makes, so there's no extra request. If deployments disappear after the menu opens, the dialog says the flow has no deployments and links to the deployments docs.
- Flow detail page: the header **Run** button is always visible. It's disabled, with a tooltip and an accessible description, while the deployment count loads ("Checking for deployments"), if the count request fails ("Could not check deployments. Refresh to retry."), or if the flow has no deployments ("Create a deployment to run this flow from the UI."). The count comes from `buildDeploymentsCountByFlowQuery`.
- `FlowRunDialog` (exported alongside `FlowRunAction`) opens a `Run {flow.name}` dialog with a searchable deployment picker. The picker only lists this flow's deployments and is paginated, so every deployment can be reached. If the flow has exactly one deployment it's preselected. With several, you have to pick one. The dialog doesn't remember a choice between openings, and opening it or selecting a deployment never creates a run.
- Once a deployment is selected, the dialog shows the existing `RunFlowButton` (Quick run / Custom run). A successful Quick run, with or without the required-parameters dialog, closes the dialog, leaves you on the current page, and shows the existing "View run" toast. A failed run keeps the dialog open with the existing error toast. Custom run goes to the existing `/deployments/deployment/$id/run` page.

**Shared run-control changes**
- `RunFlowButton`, `useQuickRun`, and `QuickRunParametersDialog` take an optional `onRunCreated` callback, called only after a run is created successfully. Existing callers are unchanged.
- Repeat submissions are blocked while a run is being created, and in `QuickRunParametersDialog` also while parameter validation is in flight. This also fixes an existing bug: `RunFlowButton`'s trigger never actually became disabled while pending, because Radix's `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild` overrode `Button`'s `loading`-derived `disabled`. `useDeploymentCreateFlowRun` now has a `mutationKey`, which the dialog uses to lock the picker during submission.
- `useDebounceCallback` now clears its pending timeout on unmount. Before, a debounced schema revalidation could still send `/ui/sch
