title: Fix 2.x CI: replace dead Sanity logo URLs and repoint bullseye apt sources to archive.debian.org
body:
## Problem

Unrelated breakages fail every PR into `2.x` and none of them come from a PR's own changes:

1. **Block logo URLs return 404.** `tests/blocks/test_block_standards.py::TestAllBlocksAdhereToStandards::test_has_a_valid_image` downloads each block's `_logo_url`, and all `https://cdn.sanity.io/images/3ugk85nk/...` URLs now return HTTP 404 — 26 failing blocks on every Python test job.
2. **Docker builds fail.** The `ui-builder` stage is `FROM node:16.15-bullseye-slim`. Debian 11 (bullseye) LTS ended, and while the `bullseye-security` index on security.debian.org still lists packages, the files themselves 404, so `apt-get install chromium` exits 100. This breaks the `docker, python:3.10` / `docker, python:3.11` test jobs and the 2.x Docker image release workflow, which uses the same Dockerfile.
3. **Integration test suites fail on dependency drift.** The `integration-package-tests` matrix installs the latest released `prefect` 2.x and latest upstream dependencies, and several suites are red on `2.x` for environment reasons unrelated to the code under test (details under "Integration fixes" below).

This blocks #23350 (AnyIO compatibility for 2.x), which is waiting on a green 2.x CI run.

## Fix

### Original two breakages

- **Logo URLs:** applied the same old→new mapping as `main`'s fix in #23235 (`5b6d85e793`), pointing each URL at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/420d0d6a78bb6df1fc18bcf188fdad43c1d22ea9/assets/block-logos/<name>.png`. Nine Sanity URLs exist only on `2.x` and had no pair in that commit; for those I used the image those blocks use on `main` (Contentful `images.ctfassets.net` URLs for dbt, GitLab, Databricks, and the JSON/String/DateTime system blocks) or the closest asset in `assets/block-logos` (`googlecloud.png` for GCS, `sqlalchemy.png` for `DatabaseCredentials`, `prefect-logo-mark-gradient.png` for `prefect-agent`). Every replacement URL was verified to return HTTP 200; there were no URLs that could not be mapped. `grep -rn cdn.sanity.io src` now returns nothing.
- **Dockerfile:** repointed the `ui-builder` stage's apt sources to `archive.debian.org` (with `Acquire::Check-Valid-Until "false"`) before `apt-get update`. Smallest change that keeps the build identical — same `node:16.15-bullseye-slim` base and same `chromium` install, which is still required for arm64 builds per the existing comment.

### Integration fixes

- **Dependency resolution:** `uv pip install -e .[dev]` in `integration-package-tests.yaml` was resolving `prefect==2.20.10`, which allows `pydantic<3` and unpinned `anyio`/`sqlalchemy`. With pydantic 2.14, `generate_parameter_schema` (which passes a v1-style `Config` class to `create_model` in that release) raises `TypeError: 'type' object is not iterable` (all `prefect-sqlalchemy` failures on 3.9/3.10), and anyio ≥ 4.14 adds an abstract `create_task` to `TaskGroup`, which breaks `GatherTaskGroup` (all `prefect-gcp`/`prefect-aws` failures). The workflow now installs `prefect>=2.20.26

title: Fix `GitRepository.pull_code()` re-cloning a shallow clone on every new commit
body:
closes #16241

this PR updates an existing shallow clone with `git fetch origin <branch> --depth 1` + `git reset --hard FETCH_HEAD` instead of `git pull origin <branch> --depth 1`, so a new remote commit is applied in place instead of failing and falling back to `rmtree` + re-clone.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `GitRepository` clones with `--depth 1`. Once the remote branch has a new commit, the shallow clone shares no history with it, so `git pull --depth 1` fails on every update (`Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches` on recent git, `refusing to merge unrelated histories` on older git). `_pull_code_locked` then deletes the checkout and clones it again, logging `Failed to pull latest changes` at ERROR level after every push, as reported in the issue.
- The re-clone deletes a directory that may be in use: `.serve()` runs flow runs from `storage.destination`, and process-worker deployments whose pull steps share a directory behave the same way.
- With `include_submodules=True`, `git submodule update --init --recursive` runs after the reset, replacing `git pull --recurse-submodules`.
- The `rmtree` + re-clone fallback is kept for real fetch or reset failures. The checkout is managed by Prefect, so discarding local changes with `reset --hard` matches what the re-clone already did.
- Repro and context: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/16241#issuecomment-6066064428

Tests:
- new `TestGitRepositoryUpdatesShallowClone` uses real git repositories and checks that a new commit, a merge commit and a force push are applied in place (an untracked file in the checkout survives the update); it fails on `main` and passes with this change
- updated the mocked command expectations in `test_clone_existing_repo_sparse`, `test_include_submodules_property` and `test_failed_clone_does_not_rmtree_while_locked`
- passing locally: `tests/runner/test_storage.py`, `tests/deployment/test_steps.py -k git` and `tests/runner -k "pull or git or storage"`

</details>

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
  - The approach is proposed on the issue and not confirmed yet; happy to adjust it.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.
  - No docs change: `git_clone` and `GitRepository` keep the same interface; the update stops re-cloning and stops logging a spurious error.
- [x] If this pull request removes docs files, it includes redirect settings in `mint.json`. (n/a)
- [x] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings. (n/a)

title: Allow patched AnyIO releases on 2.x
body:
The `anyio >= 4.4.0, < 4.14` pin in `requirements-client.txt` blocks AnyIO 4.14.2. That release fixes GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6 (critical), GHSA-3w57-8xmc-8v26 (high), and GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp (moderate). #22862 added the pin because AnyIO 4.14 broke `gather()` and runner shutdown.

This PR fixes those breakages and replaces the pin:

- On Python 3.10 and newer, require `anyio >= 4.14.2, < 5.0`, so installs get the patched release.
- On Python 3.8 and 3.9, allow `anyio >= 4.4.0, < 5.0`. AnyIO 4.13 and newer require Python 3.10, so these users stay on AnyIO 4.5.2 (3.8) or 4.12.1 (3.9) and do not get the fix.
- `GatherTaskGroup` implements `create_task` and `cancel_scope`. AnyIO 4.14 made `create_task` abstract on `anyio.abc.TaskGroup`, so `gather()` raised `TypeError`. This backports #22309.
- `Runner.__aexit__` exits the runs task group even when pausing schedules raises. AnyIO 4.14 runs each task in its own cancel scope, so the skipped exit raised `RuntimeError` when a cancelled runner shut down.
- `anyio.abc.BlockingPortal` and `anyio.abc.CancelScope` are deprecated aliases in AnyIO 4.15, and the test config turns the warning into an error. They are replaced with `anyio.from_thread.BlockingPortal` and `anyio.CancelScope`.
- `test_service_sends_many_notifications_and_clears_queue` now runs with events disabled. With events on, the in-app triggers service writes to the same SQLite database, and the notification service fails with "database is locked". The flake also happens on AnyIO 4.13 (10 of 240 stress runs), and this PR's CI hit it twice.

### Checklist

- [x] If this pull request adds new functionality, it includes unit tests that cover the changes
- [x] This pull request includes a label categorizing the change e.g. `maintenance`, `fix`, `feature`, `enhancement`, `docs`.

## Rollout caveats

- `watch: dependency resolution errors on Python 3.10+. A project that also pins anyio below 4.14.2 cannot install this release.`

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

With AnyIO 4.15.1 on Python 3.12 and SQLite, the full suite had 27 failures, and none came from AnyIO. 26 block logo URLs return HTTP 404, and one test needs `pip` in the virtual environment. The new runner test fails without the runner fix on both AnyIO 4.13 and 4.15.1. The new `GatherTaskGroup` tests skip on AnyIO versions without `create_task`.

</details>

title: fix(ui-v2): render run graph artifact icons instead of black boxes
body:
Related to #23347 (the black artifact icons in the run graph). Related to #15512.

This PR fixes the artifact icons in the flow run graph, which render as solid black squares.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

### Cause
The icon SVGs in `ui-v2/src/graphs/textures/icons` only declare a `viewBox`. WebGL can't upload an SVG image without intrinsic dimensions as a texture: `texImage2D` fails with `INVALID_VALUE`, and Chrome logs "bad image data". Pixi then draws the empty texture as an opaque black square. This happens in both code paths in `textures/icon.ts`: URL loading in dev, and inlined data URIs in production builds. The original `@prefecthq/graphs` package used the same SVGs without problems, because Pixi v7's `Texture.from(svg, { resolution: DEFAULT_TEXT_RESOLUTION })` rasterized them itself. The Pixi v8 port loads them as plain images.

### Change
Each icon now declares `width`/`height` of `DEFAULT_TEXT_RESOLUTION` (4) times its `viewBox`: `width="80" height="80" viewBox="0 0 20 20"`.
- **Why the size matters:** the image is rasterized at its intrinsic size, and the graph zooms in up to 2×. With 20 px, the icons rendered but looked blurry next to the text when zoomed in, which is rendered at the same 4× resolution.
- **On-screen size is unchanged:** it's still set by `artifactIconSize` on the sprite.

### Alternatives considered
- **Rasterizing the SVG to a canvas in `textures/icon.ts`**, to restore v1's resolution option. That's more code in the texture loader. Declaring the size in the files fixes both loading paths without touching the loader.

### Tests
- **New `icons.test.ts`:** checks that every icon's `width`/`height` equals its `viewBox` size times `DEFAULT_TEXT_RESOLUTION`. It fails on the previous SVGs.
- **README:** the icons README documents the requirement.
- **Checked by hand** in the flow run graph:
  - The icons render instead of black squares.
  - They stay sharp at maximum zoom on a 2× display.
  - In a minimal WebGL test, uploading each previous SVG as a texture fails with `GL_INVALID_VALUE` and the updated one succeeds.

</details>

 1. In prefect, icons are assigned `currentColor` as the default fill. Here they need to set to `white` so that they can be colorized by the `tint` property of a sprite.

title: fix(runner): schedule `astop` on SIGTERM instead of dropping the coroutine
body:
`Runner.handle_sigterm` called `self.stop()` and then `sys.exit(0)`. `stop` uses `@async_dispatch(astop)`. The signal handler runs on the main thread while the runner's loop is running, so `stop()` returned an `astop()` coroutine that nobody awaited. Served flow runs were not cancelled. The `SystemExit` then left the parent process to wait on non-daemon `process.join` worker threads until the flow finished.

This PR changes `handle_sigterm` to:
- Schedule `astop()` on the runner's loop with `execute_in_background`. `astop` cancels in-flight runs and the polling loops, and `start()` then returns through `__aexit__` (pause deployments, drain runs).
- Set `stopping = True`, so a second SIGTERM during shutdown exits immediately with `sys.exit(0)`.
- Keep `sys.exit(0)` when the runner is not started.

`execute_in_background` uses `run_coroutine_threadsafe`, which wakes the loop's selector. A plain `create_task` from a signal handler can wait until the next selector event.

It also changes `Runner.__aenter__`, so restarting a runner works:
- `stopping` is reset to `False`. Before, after any `astop`, a restarted runner skipped every poll and treated the next SIGTERM as repeated.
- `_loop` is set to the running loop on every start, not only the first. A runner restarted under a new `asyncio.run` kept the closed loop, and `execute_in_background` targeted it.

Checked with the reproduction from the issue (async `flow.serve()`, SIGTERM to the parent during a 30s task):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| parent exit after SIGTERM | ~26.5s | 3.2s |
| final flow run state | `COMPLETED` | `CANCELLED` |
| `astop` never awaited warning | yes | no |
| flow `except`/`finally` cleanup | no | yes |

Not addressed here:
- The child still logs `Finished in state Running()` and an `unhandled exception during asyncio.run() shutdown` traceback when it is killed. That comes from the child engine on the cancellation path, not from this handler.
- A run still in `_submit_run` (proposing Pending or pulling storage) when SIGTERM arrives is not in `cancel_all`'s snapshot, so shutdown can still wait for it. All `astop` callers have this race, and it predates this PR. Fixing it belongs in the poller/executor; see the review thread.

Tests in `TestHandleSigterm` (`tests/runner/test_runner.py`):
- exits when the runner isn't started
- `astop` is scheduled and `start()` returns
- a restarted runner handles SIGTERM, on the same loop and on a new `asyncio.run` loop
- a repeated SIGTERM exits
- end to end: a served `tired_flow` run ends `Cancelled`

closes #23345

title: Skip duplicate worker submissions of runs that already hold a limit slot
body:
A worker with `--limit` stops polling when a poll returns a flow run that the worker is already executing.

`_submit_run` removes the flow run id from `_submitting_flow_run_ids` when the infrastructure starts. But the limiter token stays held until the run exits. If a later poll returns the same run, `acquire_on_behalf_of_nowait` raises `RuntimeError: this borrower is already holding one of this CapacityLimiter's tokens`. `_submit_scheduled_flow_runs` only catches `anyio.WouldBlock`, so `critical_service_loop` treats the error as fatal.

This change catches the "already holding" `RuntimeError` in `BaseWorker._submit_scheduled_flow_runs`, logs a warning, and continues to the next run in the batch. Other `RuntimeError`s are re-raised. This is the same behavior as `LimitManager.acquire_for_flow_run` / `Runner._acquire_limit_slot`, and it is the acquire-side counterpart of the double-release fix in #19188.

The regression test `test_worker_skips_duplicate_submission_of_run_holding_limit_slot` fails on `main` with the reported `RuntimeError`. With this change, it passes: the duplicate run is skipped, a new run in the same poll is still submitted, and the token count is correct.

title: fix(ui-v2): open a run's artifacts directly from the Artifacts tab and run graph
body:
closes #23347. Related to #15512.

This PR lets you open the artifacts a flow run produced directly from the flow run page again:
- **Artifacts tab:** cards on the flow run and task run Artifacts tabs link to the artifact itself instead of the key's list of versions.
- **Graph:** clicking a single artifact in the flow run graph opens it in the artifact drawer.

The black artifact icons in the graph, also described in #23347, are fixed separately in #23348.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

### Artifacts tab links
`ArtifactCard` sent every artifact with a key to `/artifacts/key/<key>`. That's right on the global Artifacts page, where each card is an `ArtifactCollection` (all versions of a key). It's wrong on a run's Artifacts tab, where each card is one `Artifact` produced by that run. The card now links to the key page only for collections; an individual artifact links to `/artifacts/artifact/<id>`.

### Graph click
The graph emits an `artifact` selection for a single artifact and an `artifacts` selection for a group of overlapping ones. `FlowRunGraph` only handled `artifacts`, so clicking a single artifact did nothing. A single-artifact selection now opens the existing `FlowRunGraphArtifactDrawer`. Closing the drawer clears the selection.

### Drawer changes
- **Rendering:** the drawer now shows the artifact's content with the same views as the artifact detail page (markdown, table, image, progress), instead of raw JSON. Those views moved out of `ArtifactDetailPage` into a shared `ArtifactDataView`.
- **Unexpected data falls back to raw data instead of crashing.** The API accepts any JSON as `data`, so `ArtifactDataView` only uses a type's view when the data has the shape that view expects. Table rows are accepted as a JSON string (what the SDK sends) or as an array. Anything else shows the raw data: malformed JSON, column-oriented tables, or non-string markdown. On the artifact detail page, those cases previously crashed the page.
- **Error boundary:** the flow run graph isn't inside an error boundary, so a failed artifact fetch (e.g. a deleted artifact) replaced the whole flow run page with the route error screen. The drawer content now has its own error boundary and shows "This artifact could not be loaded."
- **Open artifact link:** added, opening the artifact page in a new tab so the flow run page stays open.
- **Width:** the drawer is wider (`sm:max-w-xl`), so tables and markdown fit.

### Alternatives considered
- **Navigating straight to the artifact page on graph click** instead of opening the drawer. The drawer keeps you on the flow run page, and it already existed for the artifact-group popover.
- **Changing `DetailTable` to accept arrays.** Normalizing the data in `ArtifactDataView` keeps `DetailTable`'s contract unchanged.

### Tests
- **Tab-level:** on both the flow run and the task run Artifacts tabs, a keyed artifact links to that artifact. These tests fail on `main`.
- **`artifact-card.test.tsx`:** an individual keyed artif

title: fix(ui-v2): keep flows search input focused while filtering
body:
closes #23337

This PR fixes the Flows page (`/flows`) search in the V2 UI, where each debounced keystroke re-suspended the route — flashing the page loader, remounting the search input, and dropping focus so subsequent keystrokes were lost. It also fixes the search input disappearing entirely when a filter matched zero flows.

### Root cause

- The filtered flow count was fetched with `useSuspenseQuery` keyed on the `name`/`tags` search params. Every URL update produced a new uncached query key, which suspended the whole route (`wrapInSuspense` → `PrefectLoading`) and unmounted the `SearchInput`.
- When the filtered count hit zero, `FlowsPage` rendered `FlowsFilteredEmptyState` *instead of* `FlowsTable`, unmounting the toolbar inputs.

### Changes

- `ui-v2/src/routes/flows/index.tsx`: drop the filtered count suspense query and read `count` from the `/flows/paginate` response, which already returns it — one less request, same value. The paginate query already uses `useQuery` + `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`, so search-param changes no longer suspend the route. Also removed the now-unused filtered-count loader prefetch.
- `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flows-page.tsx`: only `totalCount === 0` (no flows at all) renders the onboarding empty state; the table — including toolbar — stays mounted otherwise.
- `ui-v2/src/components/flows/data-table.tsx`: render the "No flows match your filters" state in place of the table body, gated on `count === 0 && !isPending && !isPlaceholderData`, matching the Deployments page pattern from #22497.
- `ui-v2/src/components/flows/data-table.test.tsx`: new tests covering the filtered empty state, gating on pending/placeholder states, search, and pagination.

### Verification

Reproduced the bug on `main` with a real server + dev UI, then re-ran the same script on this branch: typing `alpha` and `zzz` character-by-character (>200ms debounce interval per keystroke) now keeps `focused: true` and `hiddenOrUnmounted: false` for every keystroke, and the input stays mounted on a zero-match search.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes #23337"

title: docs: document Mintlify anchor slug rules in docs AGENTS.md
body:
Adds a short note to the Links section of `docs/AGENTS.md`: in-page anchors have to match Mintlify's heading slugs, which differ from GitHub-style slugs. Mintlify drops backticks, turns dots and spaces into hyphens, and keeps underscores. The note also points out that `just links` (which is what CI runs) skips anchors unless you pass `--check-anchors`.

#23331 fixed broken anchors in 17 pages, and every one of them followed GitHub-style slugs (`#prefectautomationcreated`, `#connection-url`). CI didn't flag any of them because the anchor check isn't on by default.

Verified: `npx mint@latest broken-links --check-anchors` passes on the pages #23331 fixed.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: docs/AGENTS.md
Proposed text: One paragraph under "Links". In-page anchors must match Mintlify heading slugs: backticks are dropped, dots and spaces become hyphens, underscores are kept (e.g. `prefect.automation.created` → `#prefect-automation-created`, `connection_url` → `#connection_url`). `just links` and CI skip anchors by default, so verify them with `npx mint@latest broken-links --check-anchors --files <path>`.
Non-obvious evidence: The slug rules belong to Mintlify and aren't written down anywhere in the repo. GitHub-style slugs, which strip dots and turn underscores into hyphens, are the intuitive default, and they produced broken anchors across 17 pages (#23331). `docs/justfile`'s `links` recipe runs `mint broken-links` without `--check-anchors`, so CI (`.github/workflows/docs-broken-links.yaml`) never catches this.
Cross-cutting scope: Every in-page or cross-page `#anchor` link anywhere in `docs/`: events reference, settings reference, Python API reference, integrations, how-to guides.
Why not code comment/docstring: This is about writing MDX content and isn't tied to any code. `docs/AGENTS.md` already holds the docs link conventions.
Durability: Holds as long as the docs are on Mintlify and CI doesn't check anchors by default. People will keep adding anchor links.
Counter-evidence checked: `docs/AGENTS.md` (Links and Local development sections), the root `AGENTS.md`, the `.claude/skills/write-docs/` skill (no mention of anchors or slugs), `docs/justfile`, `.github/workflows/docs-broken-links.yaml`, and `mint broken-links --help`.
</details>

title: Fix prefect.yaml creation when optional contents is omitted
body:
closes #23333

This PR fixes `create_default_prefect_yaml(path, name="demo")` raising a `TypeError` when its optional `contents` argument is omitted or explicitly `None`.

The function documents that omitted contents use the bundled defaults, but it currently assigns into `None`. Normalize only `None` to a fresh dictionary before adding metadata. Explicit dictionaries and the early return for an existing file keep their current behavior. The follow-up also resolves an omitted project name to `path.resolve().name`, preserving explicitly supplied names.

<details>
<summary>Tests and validation</summary>

Six focused cases cover omitted contents, explicit None, an empty dictionary, both optional arguments omitted, custom build/push/pull/deployment values, and preservation of an existing file.

The original five-case suite produced **2 failed, 3 passed** before the contents fix and **5 passed** afterward.

Revalidated commit `7ef74185bfa0eb0e9311f562fd5ce0b5c9bc2df9` on October 8: **all 6 focused tests passed**. Removing only the name fallback makes the added regression fail (**1 failed, 5 passed**); restoring the exact committed source returns **6 passed**.

Local validation used the exact upstream source module and bundled template with real Prefect 3.8.8 dependencies on Python 3.12/Linux. A small importlib harness loaded that source module before running the new pytest file. This was a focused source-module run, not the full upstream test environment or its root conftest fixtures.

Ruff 0.15.19 lint and formatting, codespell 2.4.1, Python compilation, and diff whitespace checks passed. In the partial source snapshot, Ruff was given an explicit `prefect` first-party import mapping. The full pre-commit hook suite and full Prefect tests were not run locally.

For the latest commit, upstream CI has passed all 18 canonical test groups, pre-commit checks, Type Checks, typesafety, and CodeQL. Other broader jobs were still running when checked; this is not a claim that the entire CI run has completed. [Upstream test workflow](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/37725341153) · [Pre-commit and type-check workflow](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/37725341152).

No documentation change is needed: this restores the existing documented optional-contents behavior. The ordinary `initialize_project()` path already passes a dictionary.

</details>

### Checklist
- [x] Related issue linked.
- [x] Behavior-focused regression tests included.
- [x] Documentation impact explained.
- Complex-change maintainer approval: not applicable to this small default-argument fix.

@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+import yaml
+
+import prefect
+from prefect.deployments.base import create_default_prefect_yaml
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kwargs", [{}, {"contents": None}, {"contents": {}}])
+def test_create_default_prefect_yaml_uses_defaults(
+    tmp_path: Path, kwargs: dict[str, Any]
+):
+    assert create_default_prefect_yaml(str(tmp_path), name="demo", **kwargs)
+
+    contents = yaml.safe_load((tmp_path / "prefect.yaml").read_text())
+    assert contents["name"] == "demo"
+    assert contents["prefect-version"] == prefect.__version__
+    assert contents["build"] is None
+    assert contents["push"] is None
+    assert contents["pull"] is None
+    assert len(contents["deployments"]) == 1
+    assert contents["deployments"][0]["entrypoint"] is None
+
+
+def test_create_default_prefect_yaml_uses_directory_name_by_default(
+    tmp_path: Path,
+):
+    assert create_default_prefect_yaml(str(tmp_path))
+
+    contents = yaml.safe_load((tmp_path / "prefect.yaml").read_text())
+    assert contents["name"] == tmp_path.name
+
+
+def test_create_default_prefect_yaml_preserves_overrides(tmp_path: Path):
+    overrides = {
+        "build": [{"example.build": {"image": "demo"}}],
+        "push": [],
+        "pull": [
+            {"prefect.deployments.steps.set_working_directory": {"directory": "."}}
+        ],
+        "deployments": [{"name": "daily", "entrypoint": "flow.py:main"}],
+    }
+    assert create_default_prefect_yaml(str(tmp_path), name="demo", contents=overrides)
+
+    contents = yaml.safe_load((tmp_path / "prefect.yaml").read_text())
+    for key in ("build", "push", "pull", "deployments"):
+        assert contents[key] == overrides[key]
+
+
+def test_create_default_prefect_yaml_does_not_overwrite_existing_file(tmp_path: Path):
+    prefect_file = tmp_path / "prefect.yaml"
+    original = "# Keep this configuration\nname: existing\n"
+    prefect_file.write_text(original)
+
+    assert not create_default_prefect_yaml(str(tmp_path), name="demo")
+    assert prefect_file.read_text() == original

title: Show a not-found error from `prefect flow-run inspect` for missing runs
body:
`prefect flow-run inspect <id>` for a flow run that doesn't exist printed a traceback and "An exception occurred." instead of the "not found" message the command is meant to show. `client.read_flow_run` already turns a 404 into `ObjectNotFound`, so the `except httpx.HTTPStatusError` branch in `inspect` never matched. This catches `ObjectNotFound`, the same way `flow-run delete`, `cancel` and `logs` do.

Added `test_inspect_flow_run_not_found` to `tests/cli/test_flow_run.py`. It fails on `main` (the `ObjectNotFound` escapes) and passes here. `pytest tests/cli/test_flow_run.py` passes, and ruff (the pre-commit version) is clean.

title: Deprecate Pendulum datetime behavior on Python 3.11–3.12
body:
<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
This PR deprecates Pendulum-specific datetime behavior on Python 3.11–3.12 while preserving current datetime behavior and dependencies.

It is the bottom layer of the staged split of the original pendulum-removal work (preserved in full on `devin/preserve-pendulum-removal-full`), and can merge independently.

<details>
<summary>What changes</summary>

**Python 3.11–3.12:** `prefect.types.DateTime`, `Date`, and `Duration` remain genuine Pendulum types. Pendulum-only methods such as `.in_tz()`, `.add()`, `.diff()`, and `.start_of()` emit a `DeprecationWarning` when called.

Shared methods with Pendulum-specific defaults or accepted arguments warn on every call:

- `DateTime.now`, `fromtimestamp`, `today`, `utcnow`, `strptime`, `combine`, and `replace`.
- `Date.replace` and derived time values' `replace` methods.

Compatible calls such as `.replace(year=2025)` intentionally warn too. The warning policy applies to whole methods and does not inspect argument combinations. Imports, formatting, extraction, arithmetic, attribute access, and `.astimezone()` stay silent. Prefect's module helpers return warning-enabled values while keeping internal operations quiet. Python warning filters control suppression and repetition.

The temporary deprecation module owns the method list and wrappers. Regression tests audit the shared-method classification and cover `None` components, compatible calls, warning filters, task keys, serialization, and internal operations.

**Python 3.13–3.14:** unchanged — standard-library behavior as today.

The deprecation window is at least **six months AND three minor releases** after the release announcing it, whichever is longer; a later minor release will return standard-library datetime types without Pendulum-specific members.

Also included: `generate_deprecation_message` now accepts tz-aware `start_date` values (previously raised `ValueError`), plus a narrowly scoped pytest warning filter for the new message. Scheduling algorithms, interval contracts, dependencies, UI, and generated schemas are unchanged; the remaining migration work lives in the stacked PRs.
</details>

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"

title: Keep the runner healthcheck healthy while the API is in maintenance
body:
closes #23326

This PR keeps the `Runner` / `serve()` webserver healthcheck healthy while the Prefect API is in maintenance. It is the runner follow-up to #23230, which did the same for workers.

### The problem

`/health` on the runner webserver reports unhealthy once the last poll is older than `PREFECT_RUNNER_SERVER_MISSED_POLLS_TOLERANCE × PREFECT_RUNNER_POLL_FREQUENCY`, which is 20s by default. During a Prefect Cloud maintenance window the API answers `503` with `Prefect-Maintenance: true` and a `Retry-After`, and the client waits that out before retrying the poll. A served flow behind a liveness probe is therefore reported dead about 20s into any maintenance window and restarted. Restarting a runner also stops the flow runs it is executing.

There is a second, smaller bug in the same check: `runner.last_polled` is `None` until the first poll completes, and the check subtracts it unconditionally, so `/health` answers `500 Internal Server Error` from webserver start until the first poll. Normally that is a short gap, but when the first poll is waiting out maintenance it lasts for the whole window.

### The approach

- **One shared rule.** `polling_window_start(last_polled)` in `prefect._internal.server_maintenance` returns the later of the last poll and the end of the latest maintenance back-off. The worker's `_is_within_polling_window` now uses it, and so does the runner's `perform_health_check`, so the two can't drift apart. Each keeps its own threshold (worker: 30 × query interval; runner: missed polls × poll frequency).
- **Before the first poll,** the runner's check measures from when the health check was created (when the webserver starts), with the same window and the same maintenance extension, instead of raising.

As with the worker, only responses carrying `Prefect-Maintenance: true` extend the window. The open-source server never sends it; ordinary `503`s, `Retry-After` on rate limits and timeouts do not extend it, and a test covers that.

<details>
<summary>Details: tests, checks, docs, and a known gap</summary>

**Tests** (`tests/runner/test_runner.py::TestHealthCheckDuringServerMaintenance`) drive the real client through `ScheduledRunPoller._get_and_submit_flow_runs()` against `respx` responses, with time advanced by `mock_anyio_sleep`:

- `test_runner_waiting_out_maintenance_reports_healthy`: a poll waiting out three 200s maintenance back-offs stays healthy at 200s, 400s and 600s after the last poll.
- `test_runner_gets_the_polling_window_after_maintenance_ends`: after the last back-off the API answers a plain `503`; the runner is healthy 19s after the back-off ended and unhealthy at 21s.
- `test_ordinary_retries_do_not_extend_the_polling_window`: the same timings with plain `503` + `Retry-After` go unhealthy at the first retry.
- `test_healthcheck_uses_the_polling_window_before_the_first_poll`: with no poll yet, healthy for the window from creation, extended by a maintenance back-off, unhealthy after that, and healthy again on

title: Drop Python 3.10 support
body:
<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
This PR drops support for Python 3.10, which is end of life, and raises the minimum supported version to Python 3.11. It follows the same approach as #19273 (the Python 3.9 removal).

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Version floors**
- `requires-python` bumped to `>=3.11,<3.15` in `pyproject.toml`, `client/pyproject.toml`, and all `src/integrations/*/pyproject.toml` (including `prefect-kubernetes/integration_tests`).
- `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10` classifiers removed everywhere.
- The pytest/pytest-asyncio `<3.11` dependency split is removed now that pytest 9 is safe on all supported versions.
- mypy `python_version` and pre-commit `uv -p` pins updated to 3.11.

**CI / tooling**
- `"3.10"` removed from all test and docker-image matrices; single-version jobs pinned to `3.10` now use `3.11`.
- `Dockerfile` and `client/Dockerfile` `PYTHON_VERSION`/`BUILD_PYTHON_VERSION` defaults bumped to 3.11; `.github/docker/old-sqlite.Dockerfile` bumped to `python:3.11-slim` (with matching `renovate.json` description).
- `scripts/generate_integration_package_tests_matrix.py`, `scripts/build-all-dev-images`, and `justfile` generator pins updated.

**Dead compatibility code removed**
- `src/prefect/_internal/_logging.py`: dropped the `<3.11` `getLevelNamesMapping` shim.
- `src/prefect/logging/loggers.py`: dropped the `<3.11` `LoggerAdapter` branch in `print_as_log`.

title: Bump multidict from 6.7.0 to 6.9.1
body:
Bumps [multidict](https://github.com/aio-libs/multidict) from 6.7.0 to 6.9.1.
Release notes

Sourced from multidict's releases.

6.9.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed the C extension reading freed memory on free-threaded builds when a list handed to :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.update, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.extend, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.merge or the :py:class:~multidict.MultiDict and :py:class:~multidict.CIMultiDict constructors, a [key, value] item inside any iterable handed to them, or a list tested with in against :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.items, is changed by another thread; a call that catches the list shrinking under it now raises :py:exc:RuntimeError -- by :user:rodrigobnogueira.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1437.

  • Fixed a data race on the free-threaded build where a retired hash table's reader count used relaxed atomics, letting a lock-free get()/getone()/ __getitem__() read race a concurrent free of that table. The reader-exit decrement and the drain's free check now use release/acquire ordering instead -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1481.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where two threads calling update(), merge(), or __setitem__() on the same key at the same time could lose the key entirely instead of just racing on which value wins. A decref of the replaced value could transiently suspend the writer's critical section, letting a second writer for the same key observe the first writer's in-progress entry as absent and, once both settled, mistake it for a stale duplicate and delete it. Every such decref is now deferred until the writer has released its critical section, so the window can no longer open. setdefault() had an unrelated instance of the same blind spot (it could insert a duplicate rather than recognizing an in-flight key), fixed alongside it -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1483.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where getall() and the items()/ keys()/values() equality path could raise KeyError or report a present, never-deleted key as missing. A concurrent update()/extend()/ __setitem__() call can have its critical section transiently

title: Bump mako from 1.3.12 to 1.4.2
body:
Bumps [mako](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/mako) from 1.3.12 to 1.4.2.
Release notes

Sourced from mako's releases.

1.4.2

Released: Tue Sep 22 2026

bug

  • [bug] [tests] Adjusted the test suite to accommodate for a change in Pygments 2.21.0 where the HtmlFormatter now renders " and ' characters literally rather than as HTML entities, which caused failures in tests that assert against the rendered output of html_error_template().

    References: #440

  • [bug] [template] Fixed issue in TemplateLookup where a URI beginning with a drive designator (e.g. C:/../../secret.txt) could bypass the directory traversal check on Windows, allowing reads of arbitrary files outside of the template directory. The check in Template normalized the URI using os.path, which on Windows is ntpath; as ntpath splits the drive designator off and treats the remainder as rooted, the .. segments were absorbed before the check could inspect them. Normalization is now performed with posixpath, which is the same module used by TemplateLookup.get_template() to resolve the URI to a file.

    References: #441

1.4.1

Released: Wed Aug 5 2026

bug

  • [bug] [installation] Fixed issue in the 1.4.0 packaging where the repository's internal tools/ directory was detected by setuptools package discovery and installed as a top-level tools package into site-packages, shadowing unrelated tools packages belonging to other applications. Package discovery is now limited to the mako package explicitly.

title: docs: document buffered-consumer flush invariant in server AGENTS.md
body:
Adds one pitfall to `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`: `TaskRunRecorder` and `EventPersister` use the same buffered-consumer pattern (a queue plus a `flush_periodically` task that is never awaited). Their failure handling has to stay in sync. Shutdown is told apart from a `CancelledError` raised by the database driver using a `stopping` flag.

This is the second fix for the same class of bug, where periodic flushing quietly dies. #22441 fixed it for the recorder only, and #23308 fixed it for both services.

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: `src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md`
Proposed text: New "Orchestration Pitfalls" bullet. It says that `TaskRunRecorder` and `EventPersister` share a buffered-consumer shape. Any exception that escapes the never-awaited `flush_periodically` loop silently stops flushing. DB drivers can raise `CancelledError` during outages, so the loop should exit on cancellation only after shutdown sets `stopping`. Retry, drop, and cancellation fixes should be mirrored in both services.
Non-obvious evidence: Each file's inline comments explain only its own loop. Nothing in either file says a sibling implementation exists that needs the same fix. #22441 fixed the recorder only, and #23308 later had to apply the same class of fix to the persister. It also isn't obvious that a `CancelledError` can come from the database driver rather than from shutdown.
Cross-cutting scope: Covers two services in different packages (`services/` and `events/services/`) that share a contract, plus the general rule about un-awaited background flush loops.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule is about keeping two separate files in step. A comment in one file can't steer someone editing the other one. Server AGENTS.md is the least common ancestor of both.
Durability: Applies as long as both services buffer and flush in the background. It doesn't depend on details of the triggering PR.
Counter-evidence checked: The inline comments in both `flush_periodically` implementations, the existing `record_bulk_task_run_events` and `_segment_task_runs_for_upsert` bullets (they cover lock ordering, not flush liveness), the perpetual-services contract (that one is about Docket, a different mechanism), and `src/prefect/AGENTS.md` (no mention). There is no AGENTS.md under `server/services/` or `server/events/`.
</details>

title: docs: document worker healthcheck maintenance contract in AGENTS.md
body:
Adds one Pitfalls bullet to `src/prefect/workers/AGENTS.md` after #23230. Client requests answered with `Prefect-Maintenance: true` retry with no limit, so any API call can block for a whole maintenance window. That means worker health has to be served before the first API call, and the wait must not count as a missed poll (`_is_within_polling_window()` handles this).

<details>
<summary>AGENTS.md justification</summary>

Path: src/prefect/workers/AGENTS.md
Proposed text: "Requests answered with `Prefect-Maintenance: true` retry indefinitely, so any API call can block for an entire Cloud maintenance window. Worker health must be served before the first API call and must not count that wait as a missed poll (`_is_within_polling_window()` handles this)."
Non-obvious evidence: The unlimited-retry behavior is in `client/base.py`, and the rule it forces on workers is spread across `_internal/server_maintenance.py`, `workers/base.py`, `workers/server.py`, and `cli/worker.py`. Nothing in `workers/` says API calls can block without limit.
Cross-cutting scope: Worker liveness/health for all worker types and both start paths (CLI and `BaseWorker.start`), combined with the HTTP client's maintenance retry behavior.
Why not code comment/docstring: The rule matters to anyone adding an API call or a health signal anywhere in the worker startup path, not to one function.
Durability: The maintenance retry semantics and the health-before-API ordering are architectural. They will still apply after #23230 is old.

On Windows, the interactive `prefect deploy` flow picker shows each flow location with backslashes (for example `flows\hello.py`). The selected entrypoint also uses backslashes, and this value can be saved to `prefect.yaml`.

title: Keep event persister periodic flush alive when the database raises `CancelledError`
body:
During a database outage, the database driver can raise `asyncio.CancelledError` from a write. In `EventPersister`, this caused two problems:

1. `flush()` caught only `Exception`. The batch was already taken from the queue, so the events were lost.
2. `flush_periodically()` treated every `CancelledError` as a shutdown and returned. Periodic flushing then stopped for the life of the service. Events were written only when the queue reached `batch_size`.

This PR makes these changes in `create_handler` (`event_persister.py`):

- `flush()` catches `CancelledError`. It applies the same failure handling as for other errors (it puts the batch back on the queue and counts toward `max_flush_retries`), and then raises the error again. The shared logic moves to `handle_failed_flush()`. If the queue becomes full while the batch is put back, it logs how many events it drops. It does not raise `QueueFull`.
- `flush_periodically()` returns only when the handler is shutting down. A `stopping` flag is set before `periodic_flush.cancel()`. Any other `CancelledError` is logged as a warning, and the loop continues. It also catches and logs `Exception`, as `TaskRunRecorder` already does.
- When the handler exits, it cancels the periodic task and then waits for it to finish before the final flush. So a batch that was in progress is put back on the queue and the final flush writes it.

`TaskRunRecorder.consumer` has the same problem, so it gets the same fix. A `CancelledError` from `flush()` goes through the same `persist_attempts` retry and drop rules, and then it is raised again. The periodic flush uses the same `stopping` flag and waits for the periodic task at shutdown.

title: Fix `filter_files` aborting on a directory symlink cycle
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23305

## The problem

`filter_files()` is how every deployment-upload path decides which project files to ship — `prefect.filesystems`, the `pull`/`push` steps in `prefect-aws`/`prefect-azure`/`prefect-gcp`, and `prefect init`'s flow discovery. If a project contains a directory symlink that points back at one of its own ancestors, the walk reaches the same real directory twice, `pathspec` raises `pathspec.util.RecursionError`, and `filter_files` returns nothing at all. The user does not get a partial upload or a warning; the call raises out of whatever was trying to deploy.

Reproduced on `main` (`69b2c7f`) with the reporter's case, with `pathspec` 1.1.1:

```
pathspec.util.RecursionError: ('/tmp/tmp9tyun0m5', '', 'src/project-root')
```

The symlink does not have to be deliberate. A `project-root` convenience link, a `current -> .` in a deploy directory, or a container mount arranged that way is enough.

## The change

`filter_files` now retries the walk once with `follow_links=False` when `pathspec` reports a cycle. Symlinks are then listed as entries but not descended into — which is what `git` itself does with a directory symlink, and this function's docstring already says it implements the `.gitignore` specification.

The three traversal calls moved into a `_walk_tree` helper so the retry cannot accidentally mix modes: `all_files - ignored_files` is only meaningful if both sets came from the same walk.

```python
try:
    all_files, ignored_files = _walk_tree(root, spec, include_dirs)
except pathspec.util.RecursionError as exc:
    logger.warning(...)
    all_files, ignored_files = _walk_tree(root, spec, include_dirs, follow_links=False)
```

### Why a retry rather than `follow_links=False` outright

Passing `follow_links=False` unconditionally is a smaller diff, and I decided against it. A project that symlinks a shared directory in — a common layout — would silently stop shipping that directory's files. Trading a loud crash for a quiet incomplete upload is the wrong direction, and it would change behaviour for every user rather than only for the ones currently broken.

With the retry, the only trees whose behaviour changes are the ones that raise today. A tree with a non-cyclic symlink still follows it exactly as before. The test below pins that, and it is the test that fails if someone later simplifies this to an unconditional `follow_links=False`.

The tradeoff I am accepting: a cycle anywhere in the tree turns off link-following for the whole of that walk, so a legitimate symlink elsewhere in the same project would stop being followed too. `pathspec` offers no way to skip just the cycle, and this is strictly better than returning nothing — but it is the reason the retry logs a warning naming both paths and the real directory they share, rather than recovering silently.

If you would rather take the simpler unconditional form and accept the behaviour change, say so and I will cut it dow

title: Preserve deployment concurrency lease ID on forced flow run state changes
body:
closes #23296

this PR adds `PreserveDeploymentConcurrencyLeaseId` to `MinimalFlowPolicy`, so forced flow run state changes (like cancelling from the UI) keep the deployment concurrency lease ID and a cancelled run's slot is released once instead of twice

`formal/tla/deployment-concurrency` is still valid: the model doesn't distinguish forced from non-forced transitions, and this change doesn't alter any modeled action. It only makes forced transitions keep the lease ID the way non-forced ones already do, so terminal release takes the lease-revoking path instead of the no-lease fallback that `CounterexampleFallbackRelease` shows is unsafe

Thanks @samhallam-2025 for the clear report and root cause. You mentioned opening a PR yourself; if you'd rather send yours, I'm happy to close this one

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Cancelling a run from the UI sends `set_state` with `force=true`, which goes through `MinimalFlowPolicy`. That policy didn't include `PreserveDeploymentConcurrencyLeaseId` (`CoreFlowPolicy` has it), so the forced Running -> Cancelling state dropped `deployment_concurrency_lease_id`.

When the run then reached Cancelled, `ReleaseFlowConcurrencySlots` hit its no-lease fallback: it decremented the slot but never revoked the lease. Once that orphaned lease expired, the repossessor decremented the slot again, freeing a slot that another RUNNING run still held, so the deployment could go over its concurrency limit.

The fix adds `PreserveDeploymentConcurrencyLeaseId` first in `MinimalFlowPolicy`, the same position it has in `CoreFlowPolicy`. The lease ID is now carried through every forced flow run transition, not only cancels, so the release path finds and revokes the lease.

Before / After, using a deployment with `concurrency_limit=1`: run A goes Pending -> Running, is cancelled with `force=true`, then run B takes the slot and keeps renewing its lease. Then the repossessor handles A's expired lease.

Before (main):
```
A UI cancel (Cancelling, force=true) ('ACCEPT', 'CANCELLING', None) active_slots = 1
A Cancelled ('ACCEPT', 'CANCELLED', None) active_slots = 0
leases still present for A's slot after release: 1
after repossessor ran: B state = RUNNING active_slots = 0 (limit is 1; B is still RUNNING and holds a slot, so expect 1)
```

After (this branch):
```
A UI cancel (Cancelling, force=true) ('ACCEPT', 'CANCELLING', '297ce4c9-...') active_slots = 1
A Cancelled ('ACCEPT', 'CANCELLED', '297ce4c9-...') active_slots = 0
leases still present for A's slot after release: 0
after repossessor ran: B state = RUNNING active_slots = 1 (limit is 1; B is still RUNNING and holds a slot, so expect 1)
```

Added `TestSetFlowRunState::TestConcurrencyLeaseInteraction::test_lease_handling_force_cancelled` next to the existing `test_lease_handling_cancelled`. It fails on main (the Cancelling state has no lease ID) and passes with the change. `tests/server/orchestration`, `tests/server/models/test_flow_runs.py` and `tests/server/services/test_

title: prevent incorrect cached task results by preserving DataFrame column order
body:
<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://docs.prefect.io/contribute/index
-->

<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
<!-- Whether or not AI tools helped draft this PR, you are responsible for understanding the change, keeping it scoped, validating it locally, and explaining the approach. -->
<!-- Maintainers may close PRs that appear low-effort, likely AI-generated, and substantially far from the expected implementation. -->

DataFrame columns are sorted before computing INPUTS cache keys and reordered columns produce the same key.
A following example like this one works incorrectly:

```py
import pandas as pd

from prefect import task
from prefect.cache_policies import INPUTS


@task(cache_policy=INPUTS, persist_result=True)
def first_column(df: pd.DataFrame) -> list:
    print("Executing task")
    return df.iloc[:, 0].tolist()


df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [10, 20]})
reordered = df[["b", "a"]]

first = first_column(df, return_state=True)
second = first_column(reordered, return_state=True)

print(first.name, first.result())    # Completed [1, 2]
print(second.name, second.result())  # Cached [1, 2] — incorrect
print("Expected:", reordered.iloc[:, 0].tolist())  # [10, 20]
```

This PR fixes it.

title: Fix flaky `TestWorkerLogging` test caused by logging leak from `prefect config` CLI tests
body:
This PR fixes the flaky test `tests/test_logging.py::TestWorkerLogging::test_worker_logger_sends_log_to_api_worker_when_connected_to_cloud`. It failed on `main` in [this run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/37362289766) (`Canonical Tests: group 4/18 - python:3.12, postgres:14`) with `assert len(log_statement) == 1` (actual `0`).

### Root cause

Some tests in `tests/cli/test_config.py` (for example `test_view_prefers_canonical_dot_env_value_over_alias`) remove all `PREFECT_*` environment variables and invoke the CLI with `use_profile(..., include_current_context=False)`. Thus test mode is off, and the CLI callback calls `setup_logging()` with default settings. This changes the process-wide `prefect` logger level from `DEBUG` to `INFO`. The test does not restore it.

The worker test sends its message with `worker._logger.debug(...)`. When the same xdist worker runs the worker test after the CLI test, the logger drops the DEBUG record before `WorkerAPILogHandler` gets it. Thus `APILogWorker.send` is never called. The failure occurs only when pytest-split/xdist puts the two tests on the same worker in this order.

I found the leak with a plugin that recorded logger state changes between tests for the full group-4 test set. The only change came from the test above (`prefect` logger level `10 -> 20`).

### Fix

Add an autouse `restore_logging_setup` fixture to `tests/cli/test_config.py`. The fixture calls `setup_logging(incremental=False)` after each test. `tests/cli/cloud/test_cloud.py` already uses this same fixture for the same reason.

### Verification

- Before the fix, the test always failed when it ran after `test_view_prefers_canonical_dot_env_value_over_alias` (`-p no:randomly`).
- After the fix, that pair passed 20 times in sequence (`--count=20 --repeat-scope=session`, 40 passed).
- The flaky test passed alone with `--count=20`.
- `tests/cli/test_config.py` and `tests/test_logging.py` passed with xdist (`197 passed, 1 skipped`).
- `ruff format --check` passes. The `ruff check` findings in `tests/cli/test_config.py` were already on `main`, and this change adds no new findings.

title: fix: preserve IANA timezone when dateutil resolves via tzdata (Windows)
body:
closes #23294

`_iana_timezone_name` identifies a `dateutil` tzfile by scanning its `_filename` for a `/zoneinfo/` path component. On Windows there is no system zoneinfo directory; `dateutil` resolves zones through the `tzdata` package and `_filename` is the bare IANA name (`America/New_York`), so the marker lookup missed and `RRuleSchedule.from_rrule` fell back to `"UTC"` — schedules created from dateutil rrules ran at the wrong wall-clock time with no DST handling.

### Changes

`src/prefect/client/schemas/schedules.py`: when the `/zoneinfo/` marker is absent, accept the normalized `_filename` itself if it is a valid IANA timezone name. Purely additive fallback; POSIX behavior is unchanged (the marker path still wins when present).

### Validation

On Windows 11 / Python 3.13 with `tzdata` installed:

- `tests/client/schemas/test_schedules.py`: 2 failed ([dateutil] params) → **35 passed**
- `tests/server/schemas/test_schedules.py`: **110 passed, 2 xfailed** (regression check)

Docs: no user-facing surface change beyond the bug fix itself.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes #23294"
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed. (covered by the existing `TestRRuleScheduleFromRRule` parametrization over `dateutil`/`ZoneInfo`, which now passes on Windows)
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.

title: Add opt-in POSIX paths to filter_files while preserving the native default
body:
this PR adds opt-in POSIX output to `filter_files` while preserving its platform-native default for existing callers and released integrations.

`filter_files(..., as_posix=True)` returns forward-slash-separated paths. Matching and ancestor-directory expansion continue to use native paths; normalization happens only at the return boundary. Core local and remote filesystem callers opt in and compare `Path.as_posix()` values.

The AWS, Azure, and GCP compatibility changes have moved to the independent #23321. Neither PR changes the default path format, so the core release can ship without requiring users to upgrade those integration packages first.

Related to #23290 (OSS-8291). This takes a compatibility-preserving approach instead of changing the public default.

<details>
<summary>Contract coverage</summary>

Tests cover default/native and opt-in POSIX paths, directory inclusion, negated patterns and ancestor directories, literal backslashes in POSIX filenames, and nested included/ignored files through synchronous and asynchronous local copies and remote uploads. The Windows workflow now triggers for these paths and runs the filesystem contract tests.

Local checks on macOS: 105 focused tests passed; one optional SMB test was skipped. Repository hooks passed. Windows checks are pending CI.

title: Migrate AGENTS.md/docs update workflows from Claude Code SDK to Devin
body:
<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
Migrates the `agents-md-update.yml` and `docs-update.yml` workflows from the Claude Code SDK (`npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code`) to Devin.

On push to `main`, each workflow still computes the push range and changed-file list to decide whether to run, then fires a Devin session via `POST /v3/organizations/{org}/sessions` (the same pattern as `devin-fix-flaky-tests.yaml`). The Devin session does the edits, review, and PR creation itself:

- **AGENTS.md**: the prompt carries over the same selection criteria, guardrails (max 2 files / 10 net lines / 80-line new files), justification structure, and a default-to-reject self-review that replaces the second-pass Claude judge and the shell quality gate. Devin opens a draft PR with the `agents-md` label.
- **Docs**: same document-changes/write-docs skill references, edit-mode instruction, missing-coverage reporting, and `docs: ` PR title conventions. Devin opens the PR.

Workflow permissions drop from `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write` to `contents: read`, since the workflow no longer pushes branches or opens PRs — Devin does that. The `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` secret is no longer used; `DEVIN_API_KEY` and `DEVIN_ORG_ID` (already used by `devin-fix-flaky-tests.yaml`) are required.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [apprise](https://redirect.github.com/caronc/apprise) | `>=1.13.0,<2.0.0` → `>=2.0.0,<2.1.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/pypi/apprise/2.0.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/pypi/apprise/1.13.0/2.0.0?slim=true) |
| [apprise](https://redirect.github.com/caronc/apprise) | `>=1.13.0, <2.0.0` → `>=2.0.0, <2.1.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/pypi/apprise/2.0.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/pypi/apprise/1.13.0/2.0.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>caronc/apprise (apprise)</summary>

### [`v2.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/caronc/apprise/releases/tag/v2.0.0): Apprise v2.0.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/caronc/apprise/compare/v1.13.1...v2.0.0)

##### What's Changed

:tada: **Welcome to Apprise v2.0.0!** :tada:

This is the first official release of Apprise v2. It's a big one. Much of how Apprise works under the hood was rebuilt, and many features people have asked for over the years are finally here:

- template variables to keep secrets out of your config files
- tag priorities and escalation
- smarter retries
- timeouts
- a detailed `AppriseResult` object returned from every `notify()` call
- ...and much more

**Note:** :warning: **This is a breaking release for anyone using Apprise v1.x.** If you are a developer embedding Apprise in your own project, please read the **Breaking Changes** section below before upgrading. If you are not ready to move yet, pin your `pyproject.toml` or `requirements.txt` to `apprise >=1.0.0, <2.0.0`. The v1 codebase lives on in the [`apprise-v1-release`](https://redirect.github.com/caronc/apprise/tree/apprise-v1-release) branch. I will keep patching it for security issues and bugs where practical for a year or two, but v2.x is the way forward.

##### :warning: Breaking Changes

- **`notify()` now returns an `AppriseResult` object instead of `True`/`False`/`None`**
  - `bool(result)` still gives you `True`/`False`, so most existing `if apobj.notify(...):` checks keep working. `None` can't come back from `bool()`, so a "nothing matched" result now reads as `False`.
  - The object also holds the logs for each individual service called, plus a status for each one, so your application can report exactly what worked and what didn't.
  - The status values line up with the CLI exit codes:
    - `SUCCESS` (0) - every service was notified successfully (the old `True`)
    - `FAILURE` (1) - the notification failed (the old `False`)
    - `NOMATCH` (3) - nothing matched the tags given, or no services were loaded (the old `None`)
    - `PARTIAL` (4) - some services succeeded but at least one failed (v1 returned `False` here)
    - `TIMEOUT` (5) - a service

title: Pass the configured botname to NotifyMattermost
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23282
`MattermostWebhook` exposes a `botname` field, but `block_initialization` never passes it to `NotifyMattermost`. The name is accepted by pydantic, persisted on the block document, then dropped at send time no exception, no warning, no log line.

```
$ grep -rn "botname" src/ --include='*.py'
src/prefect/blocks/notifications.py:709:    botname: Optional[str] = Field(     # Mattermost, declared
src/prefect/blocks/notifications.py:811:    botname: Optional[str] = Field(     # Discord, declared
src/prefect/blocks/notifications.py:863:                botname=self.botname,   # Discord, passed
```

In webhook mode the default, and the only mode this block can reach since it does not expose `mode` apprise builds the sender name as `payload["username"] = self.user if self.user else self.app_id` (`apprise/plugins/mattermost.py:646`). With `self.user` unset, every message is signed with the asset name instead of the configured one.

## How it regressed

#19780 set `user=self.botname` on this exact call. `block_initialization` was later rewritten to add the plugin instance directly instead of going through `.url()`, because apprise >= 1.9.9 stopped putting channels in the URL and renamed `channels` to `targets`. That rewrite kept seven of the eight fields and left `user=self.botname` behind. The comment above the call (`notifications.py:747-749`) documents the `.url()` and `targets` changes only.

## Why `user=` and not `botname=`

`NotifyMattermost.__init__` takes no `botname` keyword. apprise declares it as an alias of `user` (`mattermost.py:225-227`) and relays `**kwargs` to `URLBase`, which reads `user`. Passing `botname=` lands in `**kwargs` and is ignored the original bug #19780 fixed.

## Verification

The added test, plus the existing `test_notify_with_multiple_channels` as a witness, run against the patched source and against the source with the one line removed:

```
line removed:  1 failed, 1 passed
               AssertionError: assert None == 'Prefect Bot'
line present:  2 passed
```

Driving the plugin directly with `requests.post` patched, no network and no server:

```
before:  plugin.user = None          payload['username'] = 'Apprise'
after:   plugin.user = 'Deploy Bot'  payload['username'] = 'Deploy Bot'
```

`targets` and `port` are unchanged in both.

The full `TestMattermostWebhook` class could not be run here: every test in it, including the five that predate this change, errors on `RuntimeError: Timed out while attempting to connect to hosted test Prefect API` (`src/prefect/testing/fixtures.py:135`). That is my environment, not this change, which is why the checks above were run outside the session fixture.

Measured with `apprise==1.13.1` (the pin is `apprise>=1.13.0,<2.0.0`).

## Noted while reproducing, out of scope

The fallback prints `Apprise`, not `Prefect Notifications`. `Apprise.add()` given an already constructed plugin inst

title: fix(client): parse HTTP-date and invalid `Retry-After` headers instead of crashing
body:
closes #23276

This PR changes how `PrefectHttpxAsyncClient` and `PrefectHttpxSyncClient` read the `Retry-After` header. Before, the retry loops cast the header with `float()`. An RFC 9110 HTTP-date (for example, from a proxy or gateway) or any other non-numeric value raised `ValueError` out of the retry loop, so the request failed and did not retry.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- New helper `_parse_retry_after()` in `src/prefect/client/base.py`:
  - delay-seconds: same as before (negative values clamp to `0`).
  - HTTP-date: wait until that time; a date in the past gives `0`.
  - unusable values (text, bad dates, `inf`/`nan`, out-of-range timezone offsets): return `None`, so the loop uses its existing `2**try_count` backoff.
- Jitter selection now uses a `retry_after_from_header` flag, not header presence. An invalid header now gets the same symmetric jitter as a missing header. Also, a retryable exception that comes after a `Retry-After` response no longer uses the bounded jitter from the old response.
- Both async and sync loops have the same change.

Tests in `tests/client/test_base_client.py`:
- async client: future HTTP-date is waited out, past HTTP-date retries immediately, invalid values fall back to `2, 4` backoff.
- sync client: numeric, past HTTP-date, and invalid values.

9 of the 10 new tests fail on `main` with `ValueError`; all pass with this change. Full `tests/client/test_base_client.py` passes locally.

Related: #23277 also targets this issue. This PR also covers the two review findings there (jitter branch selection and `OverflowError`).

</details>

title: Allow sorting task runs by duration
body:
closes #23229

this PR adds "Longest to shortest" and "Shortest to longest" options to the task runs sort dropdown, backed by new `DURATION_DESC` / `DURATION_ASC` values on `TaskRunSort`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- Sorting happens on the server since the task runs list is paginated, so the order holds across pages
- Sorts by `estimated_run_time`, the same duration shown on each task run card, so runs that are still running sort by how long they've been running instead of 0
- Ties (e.g. task runs that haven't started yet) are broken by `expected_start_time`, then `id`, so pagination is stable
- The name matches Prefect Cloud's existing `DURATION_DESC` flow run sort
- Also applies to the Task Runs tab on the Runs page, which shares the same dropdown
- No docs changes: no docs page covers the task run sort options
- The second commit is the `ui-v2/src/api/prefect.ts` regeneration from the pre-push OpenAPI sync hook; besides the new sort values it picks up schema changes already on `main` that hadn't been synced
- Tested locally with a sample flow of 29 task runs (mixed durations, a retry, a failure, a cache hit) on SQLite; Postgres is covered by CI

Written with help from Claude Code; I reviewed and tested the changes locally.

</details>

title: Align flow runs timeline ticks to local time boundaries
body:
<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://docs.prefect.io/contribute/index
-->

`generateNiceTimeTicks` placed ticks on multiples of the interval since the Unix epoch. For day and week steps that is UTC midnight, which isn't a day boundary anywhere east or west of UTC. The tick formatter only shows a date at local midnight, so every tick on a multi-day range fell through to the hour label.

The 30-day preset also picked the weekly step (3 days ideal, next interval up was 7), so it only got 4 or 5 ticks.

Output of the old and new tick helpers with `TZ=Europe/Paris` (UTC+2, same as the reporter), ranges ending 2026-09-24 16:10 UTC.

```
old 24h 8   8 PM | 11 PM | 2 AM | 5 AM | 8 AM | 11 AM | 2 PM | 5 PM
old 7d  7   2 AM | 2 AM | 2 AM | 2 AM | 2 AM | 2 AM | 2 AM
old 30d 5   2 AM | 2 AM | 2 AM | 2 AM | 2 AM
new 24h 8   9 PM | 24 Thu | 3 AM | 6 AM | 9 AM | 12 PM | 3 PM | 6 PM
new 7d  7   18 Fri | 19 Sat | 20 Sun | 21 Mon | 22 Tue | 23 Wed | 24 Thu
new 30d 10  26 Wed | 29 Sat | September | 4 Fri | 7 Mon | 10 Thu | 13 Sun | 16 Wed | 19 Sat | 22 Tue
```

What changed in `scatter-plot-utils.ts`.

- Steps of an hour or more are now generated in local time. Day steps start at local midnight, the month step at the 1st, and hour steps land on local hours divisible by the step. That also fixes half-hour offsets like India, where 3-hour ticks used to sit at :30.
- 2-day and 3-day steps are added, so 30 days gets about 10 ticks.
- Sub-hour steps are unchanged.
- DST is handled. A day that starts at 01:00 (America/Santiago on 2026-09-06) doesn't shift later day ticks, and the hour that repeats when clocks fall back gets both ticks. For that second occurrence the formatter now reads `getMinutes()` and friends directly instead of rounding with setters, which had labelled it `.000`.

I kept the existing formatter, so labels follow its current style ("24 Thu") rather than the `YYYY-MM-DD` the issue suggested. Happy to change that if you'd prefer it.

Tests: two existing alignment tests checked `tick % DAY_MS === 0`, which only means local midnight in UTC, so they now check local hours and minutes instead. There are three new tests, for local midnight on 30 days, 3-hour local alignment on 24 hours, and the 30-day tick count. CI runs vitest in UTC, where local and UTC midnight are the same, so there the old code fails two of the new tests and both on tick count. I ran the file under `TZ=UTC`, `Europe/Warsaw`, `Asia/Kolkata`, `America/New_York`, `America/Santiago`, `Pacific/Auckland` and `Australia/Lord_Howe`. All tick tests pass in each. The old code fails the new alignment tests in Warsaw and Kolkata.

The `createXAxisTickFormatter` tests already fail outside UTC on `main` because their inputs are UTC timestamps. I left them alone.

`npx vitest run src/components/flow-runs` gives 322 passed under `TZ=UTC`. `biome check`, `eslint` on the two files and `tsc --no

title: Preserve init=False dataclass fields in visit_collection
body:
closes #23269

This PR fixes `visit_collection` for dataclasses that have `field(init=False)` fields. When anything inside such a dataclass changes, for example a future in a task parameter being resolved, it called `dataclasses.replace()` with every field, which raises `ValueError` for `init=False` fields. The task then fails with "Failed to resolve inputs in parameter ...".

Only `init=True` fields go to `replace()` now. The visited values of `init=False` fields are set on the new instance afterwards with `object.__setattr__`, so frozen dataclasses work and a value set after construction isn't reset to its default.

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

New tests: `test_visit_collection_transforms_dataclass_with_non_init_field` (regular and frozen) in `tests/utilities/test_collections.py`, and `test_resolve_futures_transforms_future_in_dataclass_with_non_init_field` in `tests/test_futures.py`. All 3 fail on `main` with the `ValueError` and pass with this change.

- `uv run pytest tests/utilities/test_collections.py tests/test_futures.py -n4`: 185 passed
- `uv run pytest tests/test_task_engine.py -n8`: 202 passed, 2 xfailed
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: passed
- The repro script from the issue prints `result: 3` with this change
</details>

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed. (Bug fix only, no docs change needed.)
- [ ] If this pull request removes docs files, it includes redirect settings in `mint.json`.
- [ ] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings.

     - When `return_data` is `False`, no copies are created, and only side effects from
       `visit_fn` are applied. This mode is faster and should be used when no transformation
       of the collection is required, because it never has to copy any data.
+    - When a dataclass is copied, fields declared with `init=False` keep their
+      visited values. They are not recomputed by `__init__` or `__post_init__`
+      from the new field values; this is intentional.
 
     Supported types:
     - List (including iterators)
@@ -519,8 +522,14 @@ def visit_expression(expr: Any) -> Any:
             )

-                    expr, **{f.name: v for f, v in zip(expr_fields, values)}

                 )
+                # `replace` rejects `init=False` fields and resets them, so set
+                # their visited values directly; this also works on frozen dataclasses
+                for f, v in zip(expr_fields, values):

title: fix(ui-v2 e2e): wait for Runs page URL sync instead of re-navigating
body:
Fixes the flaky `UI v2 E2E Tests` failure on main ([run 36903337590](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/36903337590), Shard 3/3): `displays flow runs with state, name, and timestamps` and `filters by state with URL persistence` in `e2e/runs/runs-flow-runs.spec.ts`.

### Root cause
When the Runs page mounts, it changes its URL two times with `replace` navigations: first the default filter (`range=past-7-days`, tab/sort defaults), then the page limits (`limit`, `task-runs-limit`). Each change re-suspends the route, so the run list stays hidden behind `PrefectLoading` until the last change is complete. The CI trace shows the run link in the DOM but hidden, with the loading spinner visible.

The tests used this pattern:

```ts
await expect(async () => {
  await page.goto(url);
  await expect(runName).toBeVisible({ timeout: 2000 });
}).toPass({ timeout: 15000 });
```

On a slow CI runner, the mount cycle takes more than 2 s. The `page.goto` in each retry starts the cycle again, so no attempt can complete. The data was created before navigation, thus the re-navigation does not help.

### Fix
Add a `gotoRunsPage` helper: navigate one time, wait for the final URL change (`task-runs-limit=` is always added on mount), then assert visibility with one 15 s wait (the same total budget as before). All assertions stay the same.

### Verification
- A/B with 6x CPU throttling (CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`) on the two CI-failing tests, 3 repeats each: original failed 3/3 with the same `Timeout: 2000ms` hidden-element error; fixed passed 6/6.
- Full `runs-flow-runs.spec.ts` with `--repeat-each=20 --workers=1` and 6 CPU-busy background processes: 220/220 passed.
- `biome check` clean.

title: fix(tests): wait for LISTEN registration in automation notification test
body:
This PR fixes the flaky test `test_automation_listener_receives_notifications_and_processes_them`. The test failed on main in https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/36903337533 (Server Tests, python 3.13, postgres 14) with `assert 2 == 3`. The `created` call was missing.

**Root cause**

The test starts `listen_for_automation_changes()` and then sleeps 0.1s before it creates the automation. Postgres does not deliver a NOTIFY to a session that has not run LISTEN yet. In the CI log, the listener task blocked for 0.814s before its asyncpg connection was ready. The log shows this order:

```
18:02:31.563 Sent Postgres NOTIFY ... event: created
18:02:31.570 Listening on Postgres channel: prefect_automation_changes
```

So the `created` NOTIFY was sent before `add_listener` was registered, and Postgres dropped it. `retry_asserts` cannot fix this, because the notification is lost.

**Fix**

The test now wraps `asyncpg.Connection.add_listener`. The wrapper sets an `asyncio.Event` after the listener is registered on `AUTOMATION_CHANGES_CHANNEL`. The test waits for that event instead of `asyncio.sleep(0.1)`. The change is only in the test file.

**Verification**

- I added a temporary `await asyncio.sleep(1)` after `asyncpg.connect` in `get_pg_notify_connection` to simulate the CI delay. With that delay, the old test failed every time. The new test passed 5 out of 5 runs.
- I removed the delay. The module then passed 10 out of 10 runs against postgres:14, and `tests/events/server/models/` passed with `-n 4`.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.

title: Fix failed state losing metadata during retry
body:
<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://docs.prefect.io/contribute/index
-->

<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
<!-- Whether or not AI tools helped draft this PR, you are responsible for understanding the change, keeping it scoped, validating it locally, and explaining the approach. -->
<!-- Maintainers may close PRs that appear low-effort, likely AI-generated, and substantially far from the expected implementation. -->

Found this error when agent wrote code using prefect.states and retry conditions. Here is a minimal example of the code.

```py
from prefect import flow, task
from prefect.runtime import task_run
from prefect.states import Failed


def retry_if_rate_limited(task, task_run, state):
    print(f"Retry rule received: {state.name!r}") # state.name is "Failed" instead of "RateLimited"
    return state.name == "RateLimited"


@task(retries=1, retry_condition_fn=retry_if_rate_limited)
def call_api():
    attempt = task_run.run_count
    print(f"API attempt: {attempt}")

    if attempt == 1:
        return Failed(name="RateLimited", message="Try again")

    return "API request succeeded"


@flow
def generate_image():
    state = call_api(return_state=True)
    print(f"Final task state: {state.name}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    generate_image()
```

This happens because engine puts both an Exception and failed state in the same generic `Failed` state. Fixed by passing existing states directly to the retry rule.
