title: Share orchestration clients across automation actions
body:
this PR reuses one orchestration client and one events API client for the lifetime of the automation actions consumer, instead of building new clients for every triggered action. It replaces #22302, which was closed as stale. This version is rebased on current `main` and includes the narrower scope requested in [that PR's review](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/22302#pullrequestreview-4506957880): the clients are owned by the actions consumer rather than shared globally. Every triggered automation action constructed a fresh `OrchestrationClient` or `PrefectServerEventsAPIClient`. Each one builds a new httpx `ASGITransport`, calls `create_app()`, and re-runs `Settings.hash_key()` and `setup_logging()`. When background services run separately from the API server, flamegraphs of a trigger-heavy server show this costing about 7% CPU per action.
Details - `actions.consumer()` opens one `OrchestrationClient` and one `PrefectServerEventsAPIClient` when it starts and closes them when it shuts down. The message handler exposes them through contextvars while each action runs. - `ExternalDataAction.orchestration_client()` and `events_api_client()` reuse the consumer's clients when they are available, and fall back to a short-lived client otherwise (for example, when an action is invoked directly). Existing `async with await self.orchestration_client(...)` call sites are unchanged. - The `Prefect-Automation-ID` and `Prefect-Automation-Name` headers are applied per request by an httpx request hook that reads a contextvar (`scoped_headers()`), so concurrent actions sharing a client never see each other's headers. Flamegraphs before and after the change:

Changed



    

  • JWKSetCache now stores the parsed PyJWKSet rather than the raw JWKS

title: Bump urllib3 from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0
body:
Bumps [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3) from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0.
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cook

title: Don't reschedule a flow run the server already finished on SIGTERM
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23243

With `PREFECT_FLOW_RUN_EXECUTE_SIGTERM_BEHAVIOR=reschedule`, `prefect flow-run execute` proposed `AwaitingRetry` without checking the run's current server state. The server accepts terminal → `Scheduled` for deployment runs, so a run the server had already set to `Cancelled` started again when the pod received SIGTERM. The `Cancelled` can come from a cancellation timeout, or from an ordinary cancel if the supervisor's `FlowRunCancellingObserver` commits it before the SIGTERM handler runs.

Now `_terminate_on_signal` reads the run's state before it proposes `AwaitingRetry`, and reports whether the proposal took effect:

```python
already_final = await _final_state_blocking_reschedule(ctx.client, id)
# -> state if state.is_final() and not state.is_crashed(), else None
#    (a failed read logs a warning and returns None)
if already_final is None:
    rescheduled = (
        await propose_state(ctx.client, AwaitingRetry(), flow_run_id=id)
    ).is_scheduled()
...
exit_with_success(
    "Flow run successfully rescheduled." if rescheduled else "Flow run was not rescheduled."
)
```

- `Cancelled`, `Completed`, and `Failed` keep their state. The engine is still killed, and the process exits 0 because the infrastructure must not retry a finished run.
- `Crashed` and non-final states are still rescheduled. The Kubernetes observer can set an evicted run to `Crashed` before the reschedule arrives.
- If the state read fails, the process still proposes `AwaitingRetry`, as it did before this PR.
- The success message now depends on whether the proposal took effect. Before, a rejected proposal also printed "successfully rescheduled". For example, `EnforceCancellingToCancelledTransition` rejects the proposal while the run is `Cancelling`, and the run stays `Cancelling`. An abort or a failed proposal also printed the success message.

Limitation: the read and the proposal are two separate calls, because the API has no compare-and-set on state. This covers the reported order, where `Cancelled` arrives before the SIGTERM. Closing the race fully needs a server-side rule that rejects the transition. That changes orchestration for every client, so it is not in this PR.

Verification:
- Parametrized `test_reschedule_leaves_final_states_other_than_crashed` covers `Cancelled`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Cancelling`, and `Crashed`, and checks both the resulting state and the exit message. The `Cancelled`, `Completed`, and `Failed` cases fail on `main`.
- `test_reschedule_proceeds_when_state_read_fails`.
- I ran the reproduction script from the issue against a local server: `Cancelled` stayed `Cancelled`, and `Crashed` moved to `AwaitingRetry`.

The Kubernetes guide's row for `reschedule` now says that finished runs keep their state.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed appro

title: Page through all runs in cancellation cleanup and pause expiration monitors
body:
closes #23239

this PR pages through all matching runs in the cancellation cleanup and pause expiration monitors, so children of cancelled runs and expired pauses are handled no matter how many matching runs the server has.

<details>

`monitor_cancelled_flow_runs`, `monitor_subflow_runs` and `monitor_expired_pauses` queried a fixed batch of 200 with no cursor. Their rows keep matching after processing (cancelled runs stay cancelled, healthy subflows keep running, unexpired pauses stay paused), so each loop re-read the same rows. Each monitor now pages by `id > high_water_mark`, the pagination the cancellation monitors had before #19715.

Because each pass now covers every matching run instead of at most 200, the enqueued tasks are also keyed per run (`cancel-child-task-runs:<id>`, `cancel-subflow-run:<id>`, `fail-expired-pause:<id>`), following the server `AGENTS.md` rule for monitor loops. A repeated pass is a no-op while that run's task is still queued or running.

Each new test runs a monitor twice over more than 200 matching runs and asserts every due run is scheduled exactly once. They fail on `main` (runs missing) and with pagination alone (duplicates). Verified on SQLite and PostgreSQL.

Possible follow-ups, not changed here: narrow `monitor_subflow_runs` to subflows whose parent was cancelled, and `monitor_cancelled_flow_runs` to runs that still have non-terminal task runs, so each pass scans less.

</details>

title: Reload collections when a worker type is missing after install
body:
Closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/17504

`prefect worker start` offers to install a missing worker integration, installs it, then reports "Unable to start worker" anyway. Running the command a second time works.

The cause is the cache in `load_prefect_collections()`. The first call, made before the install, stores the loaded `prefect.collections` entry points in a module global. After `_install_package`, `_load_worker_class` calls it again, gets the cached result without the new package, and `lookup_type` raises `KeyError`.

## Change

- `load_prefect_collections(reload=False)` gains a `reload` keyword. With `reload=True` it invalidates import caches, reads the entry points again, loads only the ones not already loaded, and merges them into the cache. Collections already imported are not imported twice.
- `_load_worker_class` tries the lookup with the cached collections first. Only on a miss does it reload once and look up again, so the common path is unchanged.

I kept the reload opt-in rather than dropping the cache, because `load_prefect_collections()` runs at import time and on every worker lookup.

## Testing

- New tests in `tests/test_plugins.py`: reload picks up an entry point added after the first load and loads only that one, and `_load_worker_class` reloads once on a miss, returns `None` after a second miss, and does not reload on a hit.
- `pytest tests/test_plugins.py` passes.
- A standalone script that loads collections, then writes a module plus a `dist-info` with a `prefect.collections` entry point onto `sys.path` (what `pip install` leaves behind), then calls `_load_worker_class` for the new type: before this change the type is not found; after it, the worker class loads.
- I could not run `tests/cli/test_worker.py -k install_policy` locally. Those tests import `readchar._posix_read`, which needs `termios`, and I was on Windows.

## How this was made

Written with Claude (`claude-sonnet-5-5`). A second Claude instance reviewed the change. The checks listed under Testing were run before opening this PR.

+    loaded.name = "collection1"
+    broken = Mock()
+    broken.name = "collection2"
+    mock_entry_points.return_value = EntryPoints([loaded, broken])
+    mock_safe_load.side_effect = [
+        {"collection1": "module1", "collection2": ImportError("missing")},
+        {"collection2": "module2"},
+    ]
+
+    load_prefect_collections()
+    result = load_prefect_collections(reload=True)
+
+    assert result == {"collection1": "module1", "collection2": "module2"}
+    assert [ep.name for ep in mock_safe_load.call_args_list[1].args[0]] == [
+        "collection2"
+    ]
+
+
+async def test_install_package_reloads_collections_after_install():
+    from prefect.cli import _worker_utils
+
+    calls = []
+    with (
+        patch(
+            "prefect._internal.installation.ainstall_packages",
+            side_effect=lambda *args, **kwargs: calls.append("install"),
+        ),
+        patch.object(
+            _worker_utils,
+            "load_prefect_collections",
+            side_effect=lambda **kwargs: calls.append(("load", kwargs)),
+        ),
+    ):
+        await _worker_utils._install_package(Mock(), "prefect-kubernetes")
+
+    assert calls == ["install", ("load", {"reload": True})]
+
+
+async def test_worker_installed_after_first_load_is_found(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    from prefect.cli import _worker_utils
+    from prefect.utilities.dispatch import get_registry_for_type
+    from prefect.workers.base import BaseWorker
+
+    worker_type = "test-late-installed-worker"
+    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))
+    monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, "late_installed_worker", raising=False)
+
+    assert _worker_utils._load_worker_class(worker_type) is None
+
+    async def install(*args, **kwargs):
+        # What pip leaves on disk: a module and a dist-info with the entry point.
+        (tmp_path / "late_installed_worker.py").write_text(
+            "from prefect.workers.base import BaseWorker\n"
+            "\n"
+            "class LateInstalledWorker(BaseWorker):\n"
+            f"    type = {worker_type!r}\n"
+        )
+        dist_info = tmp_path / "late_installed_worker-0.1.dist-info"
+        dist_info.mkdir()
+        (dist_info / "METADATA").write_text(
+            "Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: late-installed-worker\nVersion: 0.1\n"
+        )
+        (dist_info / "entry_points.txt").write_text(
+            "[prefect.collections]\nlate_installed_worker = late_installed_worker\n"
+        )
+
+    try:
+        with patch("prefect._internal.installation.ainstall_packages", install):
+            await _worker_utils._install_package(Mock(), "late-installed-worker")
+
+        worker_class = _worker_utils._load_worker_class(worker_type)
+        assert worker_class is not None
+        assert worker_class.__name__ == "LateInstalledWorker"
+    finally:
+        get_registry_for_type(BaseWorker).pop(worker_type, None)
+        sys.modules.pop("late_installed_worker", None)

title: assets: add repository-hosted block and worker logos
body:
### Overview

Add a complete, square PNG asset set for the 26 distinct Sanity-hosted block and worker logo images currently referenced by `src/prefect/` and `src/integrations/`.

- Adds 25 reusable 256×256 RGBA assets, a deterministic Pillow validation script, mapping data, and a review contact sheet.
- Uses 17 recovered Sanity originals supplied after the initial asset pass.
- Uses color artwork throughout: version-pinned Simple Icons 11.0.0 sources under CC0 1.0 where recovered originals were monochrome, plus color repository-authored generic artwork where needed.
- Leaves Contentful URLs and registered metadata unchanged; the follow-up URL replacement must wait for this PR's full merge commit SHA.

![Logo contact sheet](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..QZL8Pxfbi-eMovU4syN7A-pPjbV-pjR07QH5GApDqxU)

- `uv run --with pillow python assets/block-logos/validate.py`
- `uv run ruff check assets/block-logos/validate.py`
- `uv run ruff format --check assets/block-logos/validate.py`

+"""Validate the repository-hosted block and worker logo assets."""
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from PIL import Image
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).parent
+MAPPING = ROOT / "mapping.json"
+
+
+def reject_duplicate_keys(pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> dict[str, str]:
+    mapping: dict[str, str] = {}
+    for key, value in pairs:
+        assert key not in mapping, key
+        mapping[key] = value
+    return mapping
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    mapping: dict[str, str] = json.loads(
+        MAPPING.read_text(), object_pairs_hook=reject_duplicate_keys
+    )
+    assert mapping
+    for filename in mapping.values():
+        path = ROOT / filename
+        assert path.is_file(), path
+        with Image.open(path) as image:
+            width, height = image.size
+            assert (width, height) == (256, 256), path
+            assert image.format == "PNG", path
+            assert image.mode == "RGBA", path
+            image.verify()
+    assert len(mapping) == len(set(mapping))
+    print(
+        f"validated {len(set(mapping.values()))} assets for {len(mapping)} Sanity URLs"
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

title: Keep the worker healthcheck healthy while the API is in maintenance
body:
This PR keeps a worker started with `--with-healthcheck` healthy while the Prefect API is in maintenance, and gives it the normal polling window to recover after the maintenance ends.

### The problem

During a Prefect Cloud maintenance window the API answers `503` with `Prefect-Maintenance: true` and a `Retry-After`. The client waits out the `Retry-After` and retries indefinitely. A worker behind a liveness probe is restarted again and again for the whole window, for two reasons:

1. **The poll waits longer than the health window allows.** `is_worker_still_polling` reports unhealthy once the last poll is older than `PREFECT_WORKER_QUERY_SECONDS × 30` (300s by default). A poll waiting out a long maintenance goes past that, so a worker that is only doing what the API asked is reported dead.
2. **After a restart, nothing answers the probe.** The health server only started after `setup()`. `setup()` awaits the first sync with the API, and that sync is also waiting out the maintenance. The probe gets "connection refused" and restarts the worker again, until the window ends.

Restarting cannot end the maintenance sooner, and a restarted worker has to wait again before it can poll.

### The approach

- **Record when each maintenance back-off ends.** When `_send_with_retry` (async and sync) is about to sleep on a `Prefect-Maintenance: true` response, it records `now + retry_seconds` in a private, process-wide record (`prefect._internal.server_maintenance`), keeping the latest end if requests back off concurrently.
- **Count the health window from the later of the last poll and that time.** `is_worker_still_polling` measures staleness from `max(last poll, end of the last maintenance back-off)` against the existing 30× threshold. There is no special case: the worker is healthy while it waits, and after the lift it gets the full window to poll again, even if the first post-lift retries hit ordinary 502/503s or timeouts.
- **Start the health server before any API request.** `prefect worker start --with-healthcheck` starts one health server before the pool/queue checks and worker-type discovery, which also wait out maintenance. It keeps that server through `worker.start(with_healthcheck=False)` and stops it when the command exits. Until the worker exists, the private `_WorkerStartupHealthcheck` callback measures from `max(startup time, end of the last maintenance back-off)` with the same 30× window. After the worker exists, it delegates to `worker.is_worker_still_polling()`. A direct `BaseWorker.start(with_healthcheck=True)` starts the same private `_run_healthcheck_server(is_healthy)` helper before `async with self`. The public `build_healthcheck_server()` keeps its signature. `Runner.start` in `src/prefect/runner/runner.py` already starts its webserver before `async with self`, so this brings the worker in line with the runner.

The record lives in `_internal` rather than `client/base.py` so the Runner can read it later without importing the client, and it

--- src/prefect/_internal/server_maintenance.py (+46/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+"""
+Process-wide record of requests waiting out Prefect API maintenance.
+
+When the API answers with a `Prefect-Maintenance: true` header, the HTTP clients
+retry indefinitely, sleeping for the `Retry-After` they were given. Health checks
+read this record so that a process deliberately waiting is not reported as stuck.
+"""
+
+import datetime
+import threading
+
+import prefect.types._datetime
+
+_backoff_ends_at: datetime.datetime | None = None
+_backoff_lock = threading.Lock()
+
+
+def record_maintenance_backoff(retry_seconds: float) -> None:
+    """
+    Record that a request is sleeping for `retry_seconds` before retrying a
+    maintenance response.
+    """
+    global _backoff_ends_at
+    ends_at = prefect.types._datetime.now("UTC") + datetime.timedelta(
+        seconds=retry_seconds
+    )
+    with _backoff_lock:
+        # Concurrent requests each back off; the latest end wins.
+        if _backoff_ends_at is None or ends_at > _backoff_ends_at:
+            _backoff_ends_at = ends_at
+
+
+def maintenance_backoff_ends_at() -> datetime.datetime | None:
+    """
+    When the latest maintenance back-off in this process ends, or `None` if no
+    request has backed off for maintenance.
+    """
+    with _backoff_lock:
+        return _backoff_ends_at
+
+
+def reset_maintenance_backoff() -> None:
+    """Forget any recorded maintenance back-off (for tests)."""
+    global _backoff_ends_at
+    with _backoff_lock:
+        _backoff_ends_at = None

closes #23227

This PR fixes Quick Run failing when flow parameters use `pydantic.Field(default=...)`.

`get_call_parameters` calls `bound_signature.apply_defaults()` to fill in missing parameters. When a default is `Field(default=..., ...)`, Python's `inspect` machinery inserts the `FieldInfo` object rather than the actual value. On Quick Run the UI sends no parameters, so all defaults come from this path — causing Pydantic validation to reject them with a type error. Custom Run was unaffected because the form always sends an explicit user value.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `src/prefect/utilities/callables/__init__.py`: after `apply_defaults()`, iterate the arguments and unwrap any `pydantic.fields.FieldInfo` values to their `.default`.
- Also removed a stale comment referencing Python 3.9, which is below Prefect's minimum supported version (3.10).
- `tests/utilities/test_callables.py`: add `test_field_defaults_are_unwrapped` to `TestGetCallParameters` covering `str`, `int`, and `list[str]` with empty and non-empty `Field` defaults.

</details>

-    # ordered dictionary to values during execution; this is the default behavior in
-    # Python 3.9 anyway.
-    return dict(bound_signature.arguments)
+    # ordered dictionary to values during execution.
+    arguments = dict(bound_signature.arguments)

+    # apply_defaults() fills in param.default directly from the signature, which is
+    # a FieldInfo object when the user writes `param: T = Field(default=..., ...)`.
+    # Unwrap those to their actual default values.
+    for key, value in arguments.items():
+        if isinstance(value, pydantic.fields.FieldInfo):
+            arguments[key] = value.default

title: Install locked dependency versions in the Docker image
body:
Install the locked dependency versions in the published Docker image instead of resolving fresh at build time.

### Problem

`Dockerfile` installs Prefect with a plain `uv pip install` of the built sdist, so every dependency is resolved against PyPI on build day under the loose constraints in `pyproject.toml`. CI, on the other hand, runs against `uv.lock` (`uv sync --locked`). The two can diverge silently.

That is how the 3.8.7 images shipped broken (#23199): `pyproject.toml` allows `sqlalchemy>=2.0,<3`, `uv.lock` pins 2.0.45, and SQLAlchemy 2.1.0 was released two days before the 3.8.7 build. The image resolved 2.1.1, the server's scheduler fails on every tick with `Can't evaluate bulk DML statement`, and no scheduled runs are created. Anyone who pulled `3-python3.x` after 2026-09-27 got a server that looks healthy but never schedules anything. CI was green because it never installed 2.1.

### Change

- In the `python-builder` stage, after building the sdist, run `uv export --frozen --no-dev --all-extras --no-emit-project --no-hashes` and write the result next to the sdist as `dist/constraints.txt`. The existing bind mount already carries `dist/` into the final stage.
- In the final stage, pass `--constraint /dist/constraints.txt` to the existing `uv pip install`.

Two lines of behavior. The install still comes from the sdist with whatever `PREFECT_EXTRAS` the flavor requests; the constraints only pin versions to what the lockfile says. `--all-extras` is used so the same file covers the `-kubernetes` flavor and any custom `PREFECT_EXTRAS`; constraints on packages that are not installed are ignored by the resolver. `EXTRA_PIP_PACKAGES` is deliberately left unconstrained so downstream users can still layer newer packages on top.

The lockfile is already resolved for all supported Python versions, so the same constraints file is valid for every `PYTHON_VERSION` lane.

A second commit adds a regression check to the existing `run-docker-tests` job: `uv sync --check` run inside the built image, against the checkout, with the image's system environment as the target. It exits non-zero and prints the differing packages if the installed set does not match `uv.lock`. No new files; three lines of workflow.

### Not changed

- `client/Dockerfile` builds a separate generated package without the server. It has the same unconstrained install pattern but was not the failure here, so it is left for a follow-up if maintainers want the same treatment.
- This does not replace #23200 (cap SQLAlchemy below 2.1) or #23201 (support 2.1). Those fix the actual incompatibility. This one closes the gap that let an untested resolution ship as an official image, which would otherwise recur the next time any dependency cuts a release between a lock update and an image build.

### Verification

- Clean `python:3.12-slim` container with uv 0.12.10 (the version pinned in the Dockerfile): installing `prefect[redis,client,otel]==3.8.7` unconstrained resolves `sqlalchemy==2.1.1`; t

title: Preserve cache policy configuration when excluding inputs
body:
closes #23223

this PR makes subtracting an input name from a configured cache policy keep its `key_storage`, `isolation_level` and `lock_manager`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`Inputs.__sub__` and `CompoundCachePolicy.__sub__` built brand-new policies (`Inputs(exclude=...)` / `CompoundCachePolicy(policies=...)`), so anything set via `.configure()` was dropped. For example `INPUTS.configure(isolation_level="SERIALIZABLE", lock_manager=MemoryLockManager()) - "client"` ran without locking, and `DEFAULT.configure(key_storage=...) - "y"` wrote cache records to the default location.

Both methods now use `dataclasses.replace(self, ...)`, so the existing configuration (and subclass type) is carried over. `replace` re-runs `CompoundCachePolicy.__post_init__`, so the Inputs de-duplication from #16773 is unchanged. `+` already preserved configuration; this aligns `-` with it. No docs change is needed: this restores the behavior the caching docs already describe.

Tests: added `test_subtraction_preserves_configuration` to `TestInputsPolicy` and `TestCompoundPolicy`; both fail on `main` and pass with this change. `tests/test_cache_policies.py` (47 passed) and `tests/test_tasks.py -k cache_policy` (27 passed) pass locally.

</details>

title: Fix `UnboundLocalError` in observer `_get_k8s_jobs` when the Kubernetes client can't be created
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23219

this PR makes `_get_k8s_jobs` in the prefect-kubernetes observer return `[]` as intended when `_get_kubernetes_client()` raises, instead of failing in the `finally` block.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`client` is now initialized to `None` before the `try`, and the `finally` only calls `client.close()` when a client was actually created. title: Fix automation edit crash for flow-run triggers with non-state events
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23217

Linear: [OSS-8272](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/OSS-8272/automation-edit-form-crashes-with-react-error-130-for-proactive)

this PR fixes the ui-v2 automation edit form crashing (React error #130) when opening the documented [zombie-flow detection](https://docs.prefect.io/v3/advanced/detect-zombie-flows) automation:

```
posture=Proactive, after={"prefect.flow-run.heartbeat"}, expect={"prefect.flow-run.*"}, for_each={"prefect.resource.id"}, within=90
```

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Root cause.** `isFlowRunStateTrigger` classified any trigger whose `after`/`expect` events merely *start with* `prefect.flow-run` as the `flow-run-state` template. `FlowRunStateTriggerFields` then stripped the prefix and cast the remainder to `StateName`, so `prefect.flow-run.heartbeat` became the "state" `heartbeat`. `StateMultiSelect` -> `StateBadge` looked up `STATE_NAME_TO_TYPE["heartbeat"]`, got `undefined`, and rendered an undefined icon component — React error #130.

**Fix.**
- `trigger-utils.ts`: new `isFlowRunStateEvent(event)` — true only for `prefect.flow-run.*` or `prefect.flow-run.<known STATE_NAME>`. `isFlowRunStateTrigger` uses it for both `after` and `expect`, so the heartbeat trigger now falls through to the `custom` template (and the details page describes it as a custom trigger instead of "stays in heartbeat").
- `flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx`: `fromStateNameEvents` filters to known state names as a defensive measure so an unknown event can never reach the state selector.
- `duration-input/index.tsx`: found while browser-testing the fix — the custom (and deployment-status) trigger forms pass `min={10}`, which filtered the *Seconds* unit out entirely, leaving the unit `Select` with a value not in its options and corrupting `within` (90 -> NaN/null, Save did nothing). `getAvailableUnits(min)` now always keeps the largest unit that fits within `min`, the initial unit is chosen from the available units (largest divisor), and non-numeric unit changes are ignored. `min={60}` behaviour (hide seconds) is unchanged.

Server-side behavior is untouched. Existing flow-run-state triggers (known states or wildcard) still use the specialized form.

**Tests.** Added cases to `trigger-utils.test.ts` (heartbeat `after`/`expect` -> `custom` template; wildcard still flow-run-state), `flow-run-state-trigger-fields.test.tsx` (renders selected states from `expect`; renders without crashing for non-state events) and `duration-input.test.tsx` (90s with `min=10` renders as 90 Seconds without firing `onChange`; 120s picks Minutes).

</details>

title: Resolve single-value block keys that start with "value"
body:
this PR fixes `{{ prefect.blocks.<type>.<name>.<key> }}` for blocks whose only field is `value` (e.g. a `Secret` holding a dict) when `<key>` starts with the letters `value`.

For these blocks, `resolve_block_document_references` resolves the keypath inside `value` by default. That way `{{ prefect.blocks.secret.creds.region }}` returns `value["region"]`. It skips that unwrapping when the keypath already names `value` (`...creds.value.region`). The check is `value_keypath[0].startswith("value")`, so it also matches keys like `values`, `value_type` or `valueFrom`. Those get looked up at the top level of the block data and fail:

```
ValueError: Invalid template: '{{ prefect.blocks.secret.creds.values }}'. Could not resolve the keypath in the block document data.
```

This affects every place these placeholders are resolved: `prefect.yaml` deployment steps, job variables, and work pool base job templates. The fix only skips the unwrapping when the first segment is exactly `value` or starts with `value.`/`value[`. Explicit `...value.<key>` paths keep working.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

I added `test_resolve_block_document_references_system_block_key_starting_with_value` to `tests/utilities/test_templating.py`. It saves a real `Secret(value={"values": [1, 2], "value_type": "int", "region": "us"})` and resolves `.values`, `.value_type`, `.region` and the explicit `.value.values`.

- On `main` (c24d832), the test fails with the `ValueError` above for `.values`.
- With the fix, the test passes.

```
uv run pytest tests/utilities/test_templating.py
# 74 passed
uv run pytest tests/runner/test_storage.py tests/cli/test_deploy.py tests/deployment/test_steps.py tests/workers/test_base_worker.py -n4
# 560 passed, 2 skipped
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (v0.15.19, as pinned in pre-commit) and `codespell` pass on the changed files.
</details>

title: Match `_` and `%` literally in log and event text search
body:
this PR makes log and event text search treat `_` and `%` in a search term as literal characters on the database path, so it matches the in-memory `includes()` path.

`LogFilterTextSearch` and `EventTextFilter` build their SQL with `sa.func.lower(field).contains(term.lower())`. SQLAlchemy's `contains()` doesn't escape by default, so a term becomes `LIKE '%' || term || '%'` with `_` and `%` still acting as wildcards:

- searching events for `flow_run` returns every `prefect.flow-run.*` event, because `_` matches the `-`
- searching logs for `run_failed` returns a log that says "Flow run failed", because `_` matches the space
- searching for `%` returns everything
- exclusions over-match the same way, so `-my_task` also hides lines that contain `my-task`

Snake_case names like `flow_run` and `my_task` are common in logs, and the same filter already matches literally when it runs in memory (`includes()`, used for streamed logs and events). So the results you get depend on which path runs the query. The fix passes `autoescape=True` to each `contains()` call: 3 in each filter, one each for include, exclude and required terms.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

I added `test_underscore_and_percent_are_matched_literally` to `tests/server/api/test_logs_text_search.py` and `tests/events/test_events_text_search.py`. Both files already run every case against the `memory` and `database` backends and expect the same results, and the new tests use the existing fixture data.

On `main` (c24d832), the `memory` variants pass and the `database` variants fail. The logs query for `run_failed` returns 1 log instead of none. The events query for `flow_run` returns 5 events instead of none.

With the fix:

```
uv run pytest tests/server/api/test_logs_text_search.py tests/events/test_events_text_search.py
# SQLite:          61 passed, 1 xfailed
# PostgreSQL 16:   62 passed
```

The red/green results are the same on SQLite and on PostgreSQL 16 (`PREFECT_SERVER_DATABASE_CONNECTION_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://...`). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (v0.15.19, as pinned in pre-commit) and `codespell` pass on the changed files.
</details>

title: Return `0.0` from `clamped_poisson_interval` for non-positive intervals
body:
Linear: [OSS-8271](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/OSS-8271)

this PR makes `clamped_poisson_interval(average_interval <= 0)` return `0.0` instead of raising `ZeroDivisionError` from `exponential_cdf` (`1 / average_interval`).

Concretely, `retry_async_fn(base_delay=0)` (or `max_delay=0`) previously died inside its own `except` block on the first failure — the caller saw a `ZeroDivisionError` after one attempt and the original exception was lost. It now retries immediately up to `max_attempts` and surfaces the original exception.

<details>
<summary>Why guard in `math.py` rather than in `exponential_backoff_with_jitter`</summary>

`clamped_poisson_interval` has several callers (`_internal/retries.py`, `client/base.py`, `task_engine.py`, `utilities/services.py`, `server/api/concurrency_limits_v2.py`, `server/orchestration/core_policy.py`); only `core_policy.py` guards `base_delay > 0` today. Putting the guard next to the division fixes every call site at once, and a zero average interval unambiguously means "no wait".

</details>

Tests: `tests/utilities/test_math.py` (helper returns `0.0` for `0`, `0.0`, `-1`) and `tests/_internal/test_retries.py` (`retry_async_fn` with zero `base_delay`/`max_delay` makes all attempts with `0.0` sleeps).

title: Keep daily IntervalSchedule wall-clock time across DST when start is after the change
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23204
Linear: [OSS-8270](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/OSS-8270)

Fixes `IntervalSchedule.get_dates` returning shifted local times when `start` is after a DST change from the anchor. The scheduler calls `get_dates(start=now)`, so a daily 9 AM New York deployment anchored in summer could be scheduled at 8 AM in winter. It also restores the anchored series for monthly `ItemizedDelta` schedules.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The previous anchor-to-start jump counted calendar days and months as fixed numbers of seconds. A direct multi-day jump can also lose the hour change caused by a nonexistent local time during spring-forward.

Exact-second intervals and UTC calendar days still jump directly. Local calendar-day and month-based intervals advance through each occurrence from the anchor when `start` is later. For a future daily anchor, earlier occurrences remain relative to that anchor until it is reached. These rules preserve the hour after a skipped local time, keep the future anchor in the series, and retain month-end clamping (January 31 → February 28 → March 28). Mixed day-and-hour intervals retain their existing estimate and sequential stepping.

Seeking through local calendar-day and month-based schedules now takes one step per occurrence between the anchor and `start`.

The schedule tests cover both reported DST directions, late starts, future anchors across skipped local times, and monthly cadence after DST and month-end clamping. `tests/server/schemas/test_schedules.py` passed on Python 3.12 (111 passed, 11 skipped, 2 xfailed) and Python 3.14 with `whenever` 0.10.3 (122 passed, 2 xfailed).

</details>

title: Allow clearing deployment `job_variables` with an empty dict
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23202

this PR makes an explicit `job_variables: {}` clear a deployment's stored overrides on both `POST /deployments/` (upsert) and `PATCH /deployments/{id}`, and makes the ui-v2 deployment form send `{}` when the job variables editor is blank.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`create_deployment` (insert values, on-conflict update fields) and `update_deployment` in `src/prefect/server/models/deployments.py` used `if job_variables:`, so `{}` was falsy and `infra_overrides` was left out of the write — stale overrides stuck around and flow runs never fell back to the work pool's base job template.

```diff
 job_variables = insert_values.pop("job_variables", None)
-if job_variables:
+if job_variables is not None:
     insert_values["infra_overrides"] = job_variables
```

(same change in the on-conflict branch and in `update_deployment`)

Omitted fields still behave as before: `DeploymentUpdate.job_variables` defaults to `None` and the update path dumps with `exclude_unset=True`, so a PATCH without `job_variables` keeps the stored value.

UI: `use-deployment-form.ts` mapped a blank editor to `undefined`, which the server treats as "not provided". It now sends `{}`.

**Behavior change worth noting for reviewers:** `DeploymentCreate.job_variables` defaults to `{}`, so an SDK `deployment.apply()` / `flow.deploy()` that re-applies an existing deployment *without* job variables now clears previously stored ones (consistent with the deploy call being the full definition of the deployment). `tests/runner/test_runner.py::test_apply_with_work_pool` asserted the old "sticky" behavior and was updated accordingly.

Tests:
- server model + API: upsert with `{}` clears; PATCH with `{}` clears; PATCH without `job_variables` retains
- ui-v2 `use-deployment-form.test.tsx`: blank editor sends `{}` on edit and duplicate

Linear: [OSS-8269](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/OSS-8269)
</details>

title: Make the server compatible with SQLAlchemy 2.1
body:
closes #23199

this PR makes the server work on SQLAlchemy 2.1 (released 2026-09-24 and allowed by `sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0,<3.0.0`) while staying compatible with the 2.0.x pinned in `uv.lock`. It is an alternative to the version cap in #23200: the cap remains reasonable as a stopgap, but nothing here requires it.

<details>
<summary>What broke on 2.1 and how it's fixed</summary>

- **Deployment scheduling** (`_insert_scheduled_flow_runs`): the bulk ORM insert passed dicts containing a `state` key. 2.1 resolves that key to the `FlowRun.state` hybrid property and raises `Can't evaluate bulk DML statement; please supply a bulk_dml decorated function`. The `state` key is now stripped from the rows (the state is inserted into `flow_run_state` in the following statement, as before).
- **`UUID` TypeDecorator**: `impl = TypeEngine` has no `operator_classes`, which 2.1 warns about on every use (and the test suite turns warnings into errors). `impl` is now `sa.Uuid()`; `load_dialect_impl` still selects `postgresql.UUID` / `CHAR(36)` so the on-disk representation is unchanged.
- **Log text search**: `sa.func.concat(...)` is no longer rewritten to `||` on SQLite (`no such function: concat`). Replaced with `db.Log.message + " " + db.Log.name`, which SQLAlchemy renders as `||` on both dialects; both columns are non-nullable so semantics are identical to `concat`.
- **Flow run graph (SQLite)**: `argument.c.value["id"].astext` now compiles to `CAST(JSON_EXTRACT(...) AS VARCHAR)`, which changed SQLite's plan enough that the `json_group_array` of parent ids came back unordered. The SQLite query now uses `json_extract(value, '$.id')` directly, restoring the SQL 2.0 produced.
- **Flow run graph (PostgreSQL)**: `Select.distinct(expr)` is deprecated in 2.1 in favour of the `postgresql.distinct_on` extension. The graph CTE uses `distinct_on` when available and falls back to `.distinct(expr)` on 2.0 (ec0cc72, by @desertaxle).
- **Deprecations that 2.1 emits at runtime** (`SADeprecationWarning`, errors in tests): `Result.t` -> iterate the `Result` directly (rows unpack the same way); `orm.noload(FlowRun.state)` in `get_scheduled_flow_runs_from_work_pool` -> `orm.selectinload(FlowRun._state)`. `noload` is deprecated because it returns `None` for the relationship; the worker response now carries the run's actual state at the cost of one `IN` query per poll. `TestGetScheduledRuns::test_get_all_runs_include_state` asserts this on both databases.
- **Tests**: `test_read_flow_runs_with_only_*_column*` now accept `StatementError` as well as `MissingGreenlet`, since 2.1 wraps the greenlet error when a lazy load is attempted outside the async context. Production behavior is unchanged.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- `uv run --with 'sqlalchemy[asyncio]==2.1.0' pytest tests/server` (SQLite): 5585 passed, 0 failed (was 62 failed / 8 errors on `main`).
- Graph tests pass on SQLite and PostgreSQL with 2.0.45 and 2.1.0.
- `uv run pytest tests/server tests/ev

title: fix(runner): stop truncating runner names that contain dots
body:
## Problem

`Runner.__init__` normalised every name through `Path(name).stem`, which treats
everything after the last `.` as a file extension. Measured on `main` @ `148e99781f`:

```
Runner name 'runner-v1.2.3'  -> runner-v1.2
Runner name 'etl.hello'      -> etl
Runner name 'thing.py'       -> thing
Runner name 'my-runner'      -> my-runner
```

`RunnerDeployment.validate_name` had exactly this bug and was fixed in #16553
(`.py` only), plus #19179 for `from_storage`, so the deployment side is already
correct today:

```
RunnerDeployment name 'v1.2.3'    -> v1.2.3
RunnerDeployment name 'etl.hello' -> etl.hello
RunnerDeployment name 'thing.py'  -> thing
```

`Runner` is the one remaining site, and it is not only cosmetic: `Runner.add_flow()`
defaults the deployment name to the runner name
(`name = self.name if name is None else name`, `runner.py`), so a truncated runner
name still leaks into the deployment name created through `Runner` / `flow.serve()`
— which is what this issue reports. The name also shows up in the runner's
`prefect.runner.*` event resources and `repr`.

## Approach

Mirror `RunnerDeployment.validate_name`: strip the suffix only when a filename was
actually passed (`name.endswith(".py")`), otherwise keep the name verbatim. This is
the "unify the name validation logic" direction @cicdw pointed at in the issue,
applied to the one place that still diverged; a shared helper for both classes is a
reasonable follow-up but would touch more surface than this fix needs.

Sibling call sites checked (`rg '\.stem'` over `src/prefect`): `flows.py:1126`
already guards with `Path(name).is_file()`, `_sdk/renderer.py` and `cli/sdk.py`
operate on real paths. `Runner.__init__` was the only unguarded one.

## Tests

`tests/runner/test_runner.py::TestRunner::test_runner_name_with_dots_is_not_truncated`
— asserts the runner name is preserved, that `.py` is still stripped, and that a
deployment created via `add_flow()` from a dotted runner name keeps the full name.

Sabotage run (restore `self.name = Path(name).stem` and rerun the new test):

```
>       assert Runner(name="etl.hello").name == "etl.hello"
E       AssertionError: assert 'etl' == 'etl.hello'
1 failed, 240 deselected in 5.32s
```

With the fix, plus the whole `Runner`/`RunnerDeployment` surface:

```
$ uv run pytest tests/runner/test_runner.py -k "TestRunner or TestRunnerDeployment" -n4
169 passed, 2 skipped in 47.22s
```

`ruff format --check` clean on both files. `ruff check` reports the same 134
pre-existing findings on the unmodified `upstream/main` copies of these two files as
on the patched ones (local ruff 0.16.2 vs the 0.15.19 pinned in
`.pre-commit-config.yaml`), i.e. the diff adds none.

## Deliberately out of scope

- No shared name-validation helper / refactor across `Runner` and
  `RunnerDeployment` — happy to do it if you'd prefer that shape.
- No change to the existing `/` and `%` rejection, or to the random
  `runner-<uuid>` default.
- No change to `RunnerDeployment`, whic

title: Fix nested schema `required` list leaking onto sibling properties in `process_properties`
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23189

this PR fixes `process_properties()` in `prefect.utilities.schema_tools.validation` so that a nested object's `required` list no longer rebinds the loop variable and leaks onto sibling properties declared after it. Whether `None` validated for a property previously depended on dict ordering (optional fields rejected / required fields silently accepted).

The recursive call now also forwards `allow_none_with_default`, matching how `preprocess_schema()` already calls it for the top level and `definitions`, so nested fields with defaults honor the option the server passes (`server/api/validation.py`).

```diff
         if "properties" in schema:
-            required_fields = schema.get("required", [])
-            process_properties(schema["properties"], required_fields)
+            process_properties(
+                schema["properties"],
+                schema.get("required", []),
+                allow_none_with_default,
+            )
```

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

Added `TestPreprocessSchemaNestedRequired` covering both property orderings for optional/required siblings and forwarding of `allow_none_with_default` to nested properties. All five reproduction cases from the issue are covered.

</details>

title: Fix reading results persisted to an unsaved local filesystem outside the default storage path
body:
closes #23187

this PR fixes `state.result()` failing with `Provided path ... is outside of the base path ...` when the result was persisted with `result_storage=Path("./custom-storage")` (or any unsaved `LocalFileSystem`) whose basepath differs from `PREFECT_RESULTS_LOCAL_STORAGE_PATH`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

When results are written through an unsaved `LocalFileSystem`, `create_result_record` records the fully resolved absolute path as `storage_key` and `storage_block_id=None`. On read, `ResultStore._from_metadata` had no block id to resolve, so it fell back to the default local storage and `LocalFileSystem._resolve_path` rejected the absolute key as outside its basepath.

`_from_metadata` now handles the no-block-id case:

```python
if metadata.storage_block_id is not None:
    storage_block = await aresolve_result_storage(metadata.storage_block_id)
elif Path(metadata.storage_key).is_absolute():
    storage_block = LocalFileSystem(basepath=str(Path(metadata.storage_key).parent))
else:
    storage_block = None  # default storage
```

Verified with the repro from the issue (fails on `main`, prints `The result was <uuid>` with this change). Added a regression test in `tests/results/test_result_record.py`.
</details>

title: fix: add url property to client-side ReceivedEvent
body:
## Summary

`ReceivedEvent.url` exists on the server-side class but not on the client-side one, so `client_event.url` raises `AttributeError` while `url_for(client_event)` works fine.

#19851 added the property to `src/prefect/server/events/schemas/events.py` and made `url_for` duck-type so it accepts both classes. The client-side twin in `src/prefect/events/schemas/events.py` never got it. There is already a passing test for `url_for` on the client-side event (`tests/utilities/test_urls.py:262`), so the helper path is covered and only the attribute is missing.

This adds the same property to the client-side class, mirroring the server-side one.

## Note on the import

`url_for` is imported at module level, as in the server-side version. `prefect.utilities.urls` only imports this module under `TYPE_CHECKING` or inside functions, so there is no cycle. It is also already loaded by the time `prefect.events.schemas.events` finishes importing (`prefect.utilities.urls` and `httpx` are in `sys.modules` on the commit before this change), so the import adds nothing to import time.

## Testing

```
pytest tests/utilities/test_urls.py                          82 passed
pytest tests/utilities/test_urls.py::test_received_event_url_property   1 passed
```

Reverting only `src/prefect/events/schemas/events.py` and keeping the test fails it with `AttributeError`; restoring makes it pass.

Regression runs:

```
pytest tests/events/client/test_events_schema.py tests/events/server/test_events_schema.py tests/events/jinja_filters
  50 passed

pytest tests/events/server/actions/
  202 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format` clean using the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (0.15.19). The dev group installs 0.16.2, whose wider defaults flag 30 pre-existing errors in this file on a clean tree plus `UP045` on the new line; I matched the surrounding style, which uses `Optional[...]` in both this class and its server-side twin.

## How I found it

While investigating #22957, where `{{ event.url }}` renders empty in a Cloud automation template. That issue is not fixed by this change and I am not claiming it is.

For what it is worth as triage, since #22957 has no comments: I enumerated what every branch of `url_for` renders as through the automation template environment. An unset `PREFECT_UI_URL` renders the literal string `None`, not empty. Empty is only reachable when the bound object has no `url` attribute at all and Jinja falls through to `ChainableUndefined`. I confirmed the OSS path binds the server-side class end to end, through the same JSON round-trip the action consumer does, and it renders the URL correctly.

So the missing client-side property is the only mechanism I could find that produces an empty render. Whether Cloud binds that class is not something I can see, so this is offered as the symmetry gap it plainly is, not as a fix for that report.

title: Log the real size when refusing to publish an oversized event
body:
`EventPublisher.publish_event` warns when an event exceeds `PREFECT_EVENTS_MAXIMUM_SIZE_BYTES`:

```python
logger.warning(
    "Refusing to publish event of size %s",
    extra={"event_id": ..., "event": ..., "length": len(encoded)},
)
```

`extra` is a keyword argument — it populates record attributes and does not feed the format string — so there is no argument for the `%s` and the line reads:

```
WARNING  prefect.server.events.messaging:messaging.py:53 Refusing to publish event of size %s
```

With `len(encoded)` passed positionally it reads:

```
WARNING  prefect.server.events.messaging:messaging.py:53 Refusing to publish event of size 30253
```

`extra["length"]` is unchanged, so structured consumers see the same field as before; this only fixes the human-readable message.

`test_maximum_event_message_size` already asserts the message prefix, which is why the placeholder went unnoticed. I added one line asserting the size is interpolated — it fails on `main` and passes here:

```
pytest tests/events/server/test_messaging.py
3 passed
```

Note this shape is invisible to lint: ruff's `PLE1206` only fires when at least one positional argument is passed, so a message with a placeholder and none is never flagged.

title: Fix flaky interval schedule anchor time test when the clock reads 14:35
body:
this PR fixes a time-of-day–dependent flake in `interval-schedule-form.test.tsx` ("is able to select a time of day for the anchor date"), seen on `main` in https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/35741208480.

Related to #15512

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

The new-schedule form defaults `anchor_date` to `new Date()`, so the controlled `<input type="time">` is pre-filled with the current `HH:mm`. The test hardcoded `fireEvent.change(..., { value: "14:35" })`. When CI happens to run the test at 14:35 UTC, the input already holds `"14:35"`; React's value tracker sees no change and never dispatches `onChange`, so `setTimeOfDay` (which zeroes seconds/ms) never runs and the saved anchor keeps the wall-clock seconds:

```
expected '2026-09-22T14:35:55.010Z' to match /T14:35:00\.000Z$/
```

Reproduced locally by firing the change with `format(new Date(), "HH:mm")` instead of a fixed string — the anchor date comes back with non-zero seconds every time.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Fix</summary>

Add a `pickTimeOfDay()` helper that chooses hour 14, or 15 if the current hour is 14, so the fired value can never equal the input's pre-filled value (same pattern the file already uses to avoid picking "today" in the calendar). The two tests that type a time now derive input/display/ISO expectations from it. No component change.

Verified: `npx vitest run .../interval-schedule-form.test.tsx` passes (ran at 14:3x UTC, exercising the alternate-hour branch); biome, eslint and tsc are clean on the file.

</details>

title: Add `log_prefix` to `ShellOperation` to allow suppressing the PID stream output prefix
body:
closes #13079

this PR adds a `log_prefix` field to `ShellOperation` so callers can drop (or customize) the `PID <pid> stream output:\n` prefix that is prepended to every streamed subprocess log record. The prefix + `os.linesep` currently forces every line of subprocess output onto two log lines, which breaks aligned output such as dbt progress tables. `stream_output=False` is not a workaround since it drops the output entirely.

```python
ShellOperation(commands=["dbt run"], log_prefix=None)              # raw output only
ShellOperation(commands=["dbt run"], log_prefix="[{pid}] {label} | ")  # custom template
```

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `log_prefix: Optional[str]` defaults to `"PID {pid} {label}:\n"`. `\n` is swapped for `os.linesep` at format time, so the emitted record is byte-identical to before (existing tests asserting the prefix pass unchanged) while the block schema default — and therefore the schema checksum — is the same on every platform.
- `{pid}` and `{label}` placeholders are supported; `label` is `stream output` for stdout and `stderr` for stderr, on both the sync and async capture paths.
- Both `_capture_output` (async) and `_capture_output_sync` go through a single `ShellProcess._format_output_log` helper.
- Tests cover default, `None`, and custom template (stdout + stderr) for both `run()` and `trigger()`.
- The ticket's original blocker (`PrefectLogAdapter.getChild` missing) is no longer relevant; a plain field is sufficient.

Linear: [OSS-8233](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/OSS-8233)
</details>

title: Never hand out a stopped `QueueService` instance from `instance()`
body:
this PR fixes a `QueueService` lifecycle race that caused `test_concurrency_emits_events` and `test_does_not_include_related_resources_from_run_context_for_lineage_events` to fail on `main` in https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/35639456544 (commit adfd5ab).

Both tests ran on the same xdist worker and got the **same** `EventsWorker` object (`0x7f8b10df72f0`) from the `asserting_events_worker` fixture, and every `emit_event` raised `RuntimeError: Cannot put items in a stopped service instance.` The worker's `_client` existed but had no `events` attribute, i.e. its `_lifespan` never reached `__aenter__`.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

`_QueueServiceBase.instance()` does

```python
if key not in cls._instances:
    cls._instances[key] = cls._new_instance(*args)   # starts the service, then caches it
```

`_new_instance` starts the service on the global loop thread *before* the instance is written into `_instances`. If the service's `_run` task exits during that window (e.g. `_lifespan` raises immediately — for `EventsWorker` that's the client/`get_client()` setup), `_run`'s cleanup does `_remove_instance()` (a no-op, nothing cached yet) and sets `_stopped = True`. `instance()` then caches the already-stopped object. Nothing ever evicts it: `_stop()` returns early when `_stopped` is set, so `drain()` from the fixture does not remove it either. Every later `instance()` call for that key on that worker returns the dead service, and every `send()` fails.

`_remove_instance()` also popped by key without checking identity, so a finishing old instance could evict a newer one cached under the same key.

Reproduced locally with a `QueueService` whose `_lifespan` raises: 45–48 of 50 `instance()` calls left a stopped instance cached and returned it on the next call.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Fix</summary>

- `_new_instance()` caches the instance *before* starting it, so a service that stops during startup evicts itself from the cache instead of being cached after it has stopped. If `start()` raises, the instance is evicted and the error propagates.
- `instance()` additionally treats a cached instance with `_stopped` set as absent and creates a new one.
- `_remove_instance()` only removes the entry if it is `self`, so an old instance cannot evict its replacement.

Production semantics are unchanged: `drain()` still permanently stops a service, and a caller whose service fails during startup still gets an error from `send()`; only the poisoned cache is fixed.

Two regression tests in `tests/_internal/concurrency/test_services.py`; both fail on `main`.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- new tests x20 (`--flake-finder`), full `tests/_internal/concurrency/`
- the two originally failing tests x20; `tests/events/client/test_events_worker.py` + `tests/concurrency/test_concurrency_asyncio.py` + `tests/_internal/concurrency/` under `--numprocesses auto --maxprocesses 6`

+def test_instance_returns_new_instance_when_cached_instance_is_stopped():
+    failures = iter([True])
+
+    class FailingLifespanService(MockService):
+        @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
+        async def _lifespan(self):
+            if next(failures, False):
+                raise ValueError("Oh no")
+            yield
+
+    # A lifespan that fails as soon as the service starts stops it while
+    # `instance()` is still creating it; it must not remain cached
+    instance = FailingLifespanService.instance()
+    instance.drain()
+    assert instance._stopped
+    assert QueueService._instances.get(instance._key) is not instance
+
+    # Even if a stopped instance is cached, it must not be returned
+    QueueService._instances[instance._key] = instance
+    new_instance = FailingLifespanService.instance()
+    assert new_instance is not instance
+    assert not new_instance._stopped
+
+    new_instance.send(1)
+    new_instance.drain()
+    new_instance.mock.assert_called_once_with(new_instance, 1)

+def test_stopped_instance_does_not_evict_newer_instance_with_same_key():
+    instance = MockService.instance()
+    instance._stop()
+    new_instance = MockService.instance()
+    assert new_instance is not instance

+    instance._remove_instance()
+
+    assert MockService.instance() is new_instance
+

+def test_concurrent_cleanup_does_not_evict_replacement(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):
+    instance = MockService.instance()
+    checked = threading.Event()
+    advanced = threading.Event()
+    cleanup_thread_id: int | None = None
+    lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    class CacheLock:
+        def __enter__(self) -> None:
+            # Let the paused cleanup continue once its competitor either blocks
+            # on this lock (fixed) or publishes a replacement (broken).
+            if not lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+                advanced.set()
+                lock.acquire()
+
+        def __exit__(self, *args: object) -> None:
+            lock.release()
+
+    class PausingInstances(dict[int, MockService]):
+        def get(
+            self, key: int, default: MockService | None = None
+        ) -> MockService | None:
+            cached = super().get(key, default)
+            if threading.get_ident() == cleanup_thread_id and cached is instance:
+                checked.set()
+                assert advanced.wait(5)
+            return cached
+
+    # Pause cleanup after it reads the old instance, while another thread drains
+    # that instance and requests its replacement.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        MockService, "_instances", PausingInstances(MockService._instances)
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(MockService, "_instance_cache_lock", CacheLock(), raising=False)
+
+    def cleanup() -> None:
+        nonlocal cleanup_thread_id
+        cleanup_thread_id = threading.get_ident()
+        instance._remove_instance()
+
+    def replace() -> MockService:
+        try:
+            instance.drain()
+            return MockService.instance()
+        finally:
+            advanced.set()
+
+    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
+        cleanup_future = executor.submit(cleanup)
+        try:
+            assert checked.wait(5)
+            replacement_future = executor.submit(replace)
+            replacement = replacement_future.result(timeout=10)
+            cleanup_future.result(timeout=10)
+        finally:
+            advanced.set()
+
+    current = MockService.instance()
+    try:
+        assert current is replacement
+        replacement.send(1)
+        replacement.drain()
+        replacement.mock.assert_called_once_with(replacement, 1)
+    finally:
+        replacement.drain()
+        current.drain()
+
+
+def test_instance_cache_lock_is_reset_after_fork(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):
+    class ForkedService(MockService):
+        _instance_cache_lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ForkedService, "_instances", {})
+    # A child process can inherit the cache lock while another thread holds it.
+    with ForkedService._instance_cache_lock:
+        ForkedService.reset_instances_for_fork()
+        assert ForkedService._instance_cache_lock.acquire(blocking=False)
+        ForkedService._instance_cache_lock.release()
+        instance = ForkedService.instance()
+
+    instance.send(1)
+    instance.drain()
+    instance.mock.assert_called_once_with(instance, 1)
+

title: Make Azure bundle uploads idempotent for reused sidecar keys
body:
closes #23169

this PR makes `upload_bundle_to_azure_blob_storage` pass `overwrite=True` so repeated and concurrent uploads of a content-addressed `include_files` sidecar (`files/<sha256>.zip`) no longer fail with `ResourceExistsError`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `ZipBuilder` intentionally reuses the same key for identical included content, but the Azure uploader used Azure's default no-overwrite `upload_blob`, so a second (or concurrent) submission with the same files failed before the flow ran. The S3 and GCS uploaders already overwrite by default, as do the other Azure upload paths in this package (`deployments/steps.py`, `AzureBlobStorageContainer.write_path`).
- Fixing it at the uploader means both the generic `.submit_to_work_pool()` path and the direct Docker path from #22858 get the same behavior.
- Tests: added a `FakeContainerClient` that enforces Azure's no-overwrite default, with coverage for a repeated upload and 5 concurrent uploads to the same key. The existing upload-error test now uses `ClientAuthenticationError` so it still verifies that unrelated failures propagate as `RuntimeError`.

Not reproduced against a live Azure account; verified with unit tests.

</details>

title: Run Biome from node_modules in UI v2 lint job
body:
The UI v2 Checks `Lint` job [failed on main](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/35618769476/job/106396339007) not because of a test, but because `biomejs/setup-biome@v2` couldn't download the Biome binary — it got repeated `HTTP 504` responses from the GitHub API while resolving the release, and the action gave up after three retries.

`@biomejs/biome` is already a locked devDependency in `ui-v2/package-lock.json` and is installed by the preceding `npm ci` (or restored from the node_modules cache), so the separate download is redundant and an extra point of failure. This drops the `setup-biome` step and runs `npx biome ci` from `node_modules` instead, so the lint job depends only on the same install step as the rest of the workflow, and uses the exact locked version (`2.5.12` currently) rather than whatever `setup-biome` resolves.

Verified locally in `ui-v2`: `npm ci && npx biome ci` runs and checks 1523 files.

**Mermaid 12.0.0** ships ELK as the bundled default layout engine, a new `redux-color` / `neo` default appearance, and two new diagram types: [UML use case diagrams](https://mermaid.ai/open-source/syntax/usecase.html).

This is a breaking release (ES2024, Safari 17.4+, Node 22.12+). Existing flowcharts, state and class diagrams will re-lay out and recolour; add `layout: dagre`, `theme: default` and `look: classic` to your config to keep the old look. Full changelog below.

##### Major Changes

- [#​8213](https://redirect.github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/8213) [`33442fd`](https://redirect.github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/commit/33442fddbf91852417ac2805afbd35aba0facbe1) Thanks [@​aloisklink](https://redirect.github.com/aloisklink)! - chore!: require ES2024, Safari 17.4+, Node.JS v22.12+

  Mermaid is now built to target Safari 17.4+ and ES2024. If you need to support
  older browsers, you may need to polyfill or transpile mermaid.

  Safari 17.4+ has been chosen as the floor, as unlike Firefox/Chrome,
  older iOS devices don't get major Safari updates.

  Node.JS v22.12+ is also declared as requirement in our `package.json` files,
  but as mermaid requires a browser, this is mainly so we can use dependencies that
  also declare a Node.JS v22.12+ requirement, without causing issues for users when
  running `npm install`.

- [#​8155](https://redirect.github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/8155) [`810893c`](https://redirect.github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/commit/810893c660ada9e223297a38adcf65d4f4e211a7) Thanks [@​ashishjain0512](https://redirect.github.com/ashishjain0512)! - feat!: **ELK is now bundled with mermaid and is the default layout algorithm.**

  ELK previously shipped as a separate `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` package that sites had to install and register. It is now part of mermaid itself and registered automatically, so `layout: elk` — and the `elk.stress`, `elk.force`, `elk.mrtree`, `elk.sporeOverlap`, `elk.box` and `elk.rectpacking` variants — work with no setup.

  **This changes how existing diagrams look.** Flowchart, state, class, entity-relationship, requirement, use-case diagrams that do not specify a `layout` are

title: prefect-dbt: shut down dbt worker threads when a task times out or is cancelled
body:
closes #23161

this PR makes `PrefectDbtRunner.invoke()` (and `DbtCoreExecutor`) actually stop dbt when the enclosing Prefect task times out or is cancelled, so a retry never runs over a still-executing previous attempt.

**Why it happened:** `dbtRunner.invoke()` runs on the calling thread and only tears down its worker pool / cancels open connections for `KeyboardInterrupt`, `SystemExit` and `FailFastError`. Prefect delivers timeouts/cancellation as its own `CancelledError` (a `BaseException`), which dbt neither recognizes nor propagates: it is swallowed into `dbtRunnerResult.exception` while worker threads and in-flight queries keep running. `PrefectDbtRunner` then wrapped that result in a `ValueError` and the retry started a second dbt run on top of the first.

**Fix:** new private `prefect_dbt.core._invoke.invoke_dbt(runner, args)` runs `runner.invoke(args)` on a dedicated daemon thread (with the caller's contextvars) and waits interruptibly:

```python
try:
    invocation.start()
    while not invocation.wait(0.1): ...
except BaseException:           # Prefect CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt, ...
    inject KeyboardInterrupt into the dbt thread   # dbt's own shutdown path
    cancel_open_adapter_connections()              # adapter.cancel_open_connections() under connection_named("master")
    wait for the dbt thread to exit                # re-cancelling connections every 1s, warning every 30s
    raise                                          # original exception, so TimedOut/retry semantics are unchanged
```

`PrefectDbtRunner.invoke()` on cancellation stops the callback processor *without* draining the queue, fails every node task that was started from a `NodeStart` but never saw its `NodeFinished` (`NodeTaskTracker.fail_incomplete_nodes()` + bounded `join_task_threads()`, so those `execute_dbt_node` threads and task runs terminate instead of waiting forever), resets hook state, then re-raises; the normal completion path is unchanged. A `dbtRunnerResult` whose `exception` is a non-`Exception` `BaseException` is now re-raised as-is instead of being wrapped in `ValueError`. `DbtCoreExecutor` uses the same helper and lets non-`Exception` errors propagate (after reverting the adapter pool).

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

- Liveness is tracked with a `threading.Event` rather than `Thread.join()`: an async exception raised inside `join()` hits CPython's `_wait_for_tstate_lock` except-branch and falsely marks the thread as stopped, which would make the supervisor return while dbt is still running.
- Adapter cancellation looks at every adapter registered in `dbt.adapters.factory.FACTORY` (same as dbt's own Ctrl-C handling); no adapter (cancelled during parse) and non-cancelable adapters are skipped, adapter errors are logged. Verified against dbt-core 1.7.0 and 1.12.5.
- The wait for dbt to exit is not bounded (the thread is a daemon, warnings are logged every 30s): returning while dbt still holds connections is exactly the overlap the i

--- src/integrations/prefect-dbt/prefect_dbt/core/_invoke.py (+167/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,167 @@
+"""Supervised in-process dbt invocation.
+
+`dbtRunner.invoke()` runs dbt on the calling thread and only cleans up its
+worker pool and open database connections for `KeyboardInterrupt`,
+`SystemExit` and `FailFastError`. Prefect signals timeouts and cancellation
+with its own `CancelledError`, which dbt neither recognizes nor propagates: it
+is swallowed into the returned `dbtRunnerResult` while worker threads and
+in-flight queries keep running.
+
+`invoke_dbt` runs dbt on a dedicated thread so that a cancellation delivered
+to the caller can be translated into dbt's own shutdown path: a
+`KeyboardInterrupt` is injected into the dbt thread and open connections are
+cancelled on every registered adapter (repeatedly, since dbt's main thread
+only observes the interrupt between blocking waits and may keep dispatching
+queued nodes until then). The caller waits for the dbt thread to exit before
+the cancellation propagates, so a task retry never overlaps a previous
+attempt.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextvars
+import ctypes
+import threading
+import time
+from typing import Any
+
+from dbt.adapters.factory import FACTORY
+from dbt.cli.main import dbtRunner, dbtRunnerResult
+
+from prefect.logging import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger(__name__)
+
+_WAIT_POLL_INTERVAL = 0.1
+_CANCEL_RETRY_INTERVAL = 1.0
+_SHUTDOWN_WARNING_INTERVAL = 30.0
+
+
+def _inject_keyboard_interrupt(thread: threading.Thread) -> None:
+    if thread.ident is None:
+        return
+    # Returns 0 (no-op) if the thread has already exited.
+    ctypes.pythonapi.PyThreadState_SetAsyncExc(
+        ctypes.c_ulong(thread.ident), ctypes.py_object(KeyboardInterrupt)
+    )
+
+
+class _Invocation:
+    """A dbt invocation running on its own thread.
+
+    Liveness is tracked with an `Event` rather than `Thread.join()`: an
+    asynchronous exception (which is how Prefect delivers timeouts and
+    cancellation to a synchronous caller) raised inside `join()` makes CPython
+    mark the thread as stopped even though it is still running.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, runner: dbtRunner, args: list[str]) -> None:
+        self._runner = runner
+        self._args = args
+        self._context = contextvars.copy_context()
+        self._outcome: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        self.done = threading.Event()
+        self.thread = threading.Thread(
+            target=self._run, name="prefect-dbt-invoke", daemon=True
+        )
+
+    def _run(self) -> None:
+        try:
+            self._outcome["result"] = self._context.run(self._runner.invoke, self._args)
+        except BaseException as exc:
+            self._outcome["error"] = exc
+        finally:
+            self.done.set()
+
+    def start(self) -> None:
+        self.thread.start()
+
+    def wait(self, timeout: float) -> bool:
+        return self.done.wait(timeout)
+
+    def result(self) -> dbtRunnerResult:
+        if "error" in self._outcome:
+            raise self._outcome["error"]
+        return self._outcome["result"]
+
+
+def cancel_open_adapter_connections() -> None:
+    """Cancel in-flight queries on every registered dbt adapter.
+
+    Mirrors dbt-core's `GraphRunnableTask._cancel_connections`, which is only
+    reached by dbt for `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`. Adapters that are not
+    yet registered (cancellation during parsing) or not cancelable are skipped.
+    """
+    with FACTORY.lock:
+        adapters: list[Any] = list(FACTORY.adapters.values())
+
+    if not adapters:
+        logger.debug("No dbt adapter registered; nothing to cancel")
+        return
+
+    for adapter in adapters:
+        if not adapter.is_cancelable():
+            logger.debug(
+                "dbt adapter %r does not support cancelling open connections; "
+                "in-flight queries continue until they finish",
+                adapter.type(),
+            )
+            continue
+        try:
+            with adapter.connection_named("master"):
+                adapter.cancel_open_connections()
+        except Exception as exc:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Failed to cancel open connections for dbt adapter %r: %s",
+                adapter.type(),
+                exc,
+            )
+
+
+def invoke_dbt(runner: dbtRunner, args: list[str]) -> dbtRunnerResult:
+    """Run `runner.invoke(args)` on a supervised thread.
+
+    Returns dbt's result on normal completion. If the calling thread receives
+    any `BaseException` while waiting (Prefect timeout/cancellation,
+    `KeyboardInterrupt`, ...), dbt is shut down before it is re-raised.
+    """
+    invocation = _Invocation(runner, args)
+
+    try:
+        invocation.start()
+        while not invocation.wait(_WAIT_POLL_INTERVAL):
+            pass
+    except BaseException:
+        if invocation.thread.ident is not None:
+            logger.info("dbt invocation cancelled; shutting down dbt worker threads")
+            _inject_keyboard_interrupt(invocation.thread)
+            cancel_open_adapter_connections()
+            _wait_for_shutdown(invocation)
+        raise
+
+    result = invocation.result()
+    # dbt encodes cancellation in its result; preserve it as control flow so
+    # every caller performs exception cleanup rather than normal completion.
+    if (
+        not result.success
+        and isinstance(result.exception, BaseException)
+        and not isinstance(result.exception, Exception)
+    ):
+        raise result.exception
+    return result
+
+
+def _wait_for_shutdown(invocation: _Invocation) -> None:
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    last_cancel = last_warning = started
+    while not invocation.wait(_WAIT_POLL_INTERVAL):
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        if now - last_cancel >= _CANCEL_RETRY_INTERVAL:
+            last_cancel = now
+            cancel_open_adapter_connections()
+        if now - last_warning >= _SHUTDOWN_WARNING_INTERVAL:
+            last_warning = now
+            logger.warning(
+                "Still waiting for dbt to shut down after cancellation (%.0fs)",
+                now - started,
+            )

title: Persist failed task exceptions according to `persist_result` in both task engines
body:
closes #23159

this PR makes both task engines write a failed task's exception to result storage only when `should_persist_result()` is true.

Before this change, the two engines did not agree:

```diff
 # SyncTaskRunEngine.handle_exception
 exception_to_failed_state_sync(exc, ..., result_store=get_result_store(),
-    write_result=True)          # always writes, even with persist_result=False
+    write_result=should_persist_result())

 # AsyncTaskRunEngine.handle_exception
 await exception_to_failed_state(exc, ..., result_store=get_result_store(),
+    write_result=should_persist_result())   # was omitted -> defaulted to False
```

The async omission is the reported bug: `to_state_create` still attached `ResultRecordMetadata` to the Failed state (because `persist_result=True`), so the API-reloaded state pointed at a file that was never written and `aresult()` raised `ValueError("Path ... does not exist.")` instead of the original exception.

This matches what `flow_engine.py` already does for `handle_exception` in both engines.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

Added two parametrized (`sync`/`async`) tests in `tests/results/test_task_results.py`:

- `test_failed_task_exception_is_persisted`: with `persist_result=True`, the original exception is raised from the API-reloaded state.
- `test_failed_task_exception_is_not_persisted_when_disabled`: with `persist_result=False`, nothing is written to storage and the API state has no result data.

Without the fix, `is_persisted[async]` and `is_not_persisted_when_disabled[sync]` fail; with it, `tests/results/` and `tests/test_task_engine.py` pass (387 passed).

</details>

title: Accept `None` values in `find_placeholders`
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23157

this PR makes `find_placeholders` treat `None` as a value with no placeholders, so `CustomWebhookNotificationBlock` accepts `json_data` payloads that contain JSON `null` (nested object fields or list items).

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `find_placeholders` returned early for `int`/`float`/`bool` but raised `ValueError: Unexpected type: <class 'NoneType'>` for `None`. It now returns an empty set for `None`. Other unsupported types (e.g. tuples) still raise.
- `apply_values` already preserved `None`, so the notification payload is sent with `null` intact after placeholder substitution.
- Tests: `find_placeholders` with `None` at the top level and nested in dicts/lists; `CustomWebhookNotificationBlock` sends `{"text":"test","metadata":{"optional":null},"items":[null,"test name"]}` and still rejects unknown placeholders.
