title: Render `data:image/*` URIs in ui-v2 markdown
body:
closes #23155 this PR makes `LazyMarkdown` keep inline `data:image/*` sources on `` elements, so markdown artifacts with base64-encoded figures render in ui-v2 like they do in the Vue UI.
Details Two layers dropped the `src` attribute, which left only the alt text: 1. `react-markdown`'s `defaultUrlTransform` only allows `http(s)`, `irc(s)`, `mailto` and `xmpp`. 2. The `rehype-sanitize` default schema only allows `http`/`https` for `src`. Changes in `ui-v2/src/components/ui/lazy-markdown.tsx`: - Add `"data"` to `protocols.src` in the sanitize schema. - Pass a `urlTransform` that keeps the URL only when `node.tagName === "img" && key === "src" && /^data:image\//i.test(url)`; everything else goes to `defaultUrlTransform`. This keeps `data:text/html` (and any non-image data URL) out of `href` and `src`. - `defaultUrlTransform` is taken from the dynamic `import("react-markdown")` so the module stays lazy-loaded. - A caller-supplied `urlTransform` prop still takes precedence (spread after the default). Tests added to `lazy-markdown.test.tsx`: markdown and raw-HTML `data:image/png` images keep `src`; a `data:text/html` link loses `href` and a `data:text/html` `` loses `src`. Since all ui-v2 markdown goes through `LazyMarkdown`, this also applies to deployment descriptions, block docs, and task run descriptions. Related to #15512

title: Fix retry budget for completed subflows on parent retry
body:
closes #23152

this PR gives a completed inline subflow a fresh run when its parent retries and the previous child has no persisted result. the child receives its configured retries, and the previous Completed run keeps its state and history.

previously, a child could succeed once, fail during the parent retry, and skip its own `retries=1` because both executions shared a cumulative attempt count. the MRE now completes with child runs and counts `A:1 → B:1 → B:2`.

<details>
<summary>behavior and compatibility</summary>

the sync and async engines inspect the latest child's stored state. completed children with persisted results still reuse those results; unsuccessful children still get fresh runs; in-progress children still reattach after process restarts. no server change or counter reset is needed.

the completed child's replacement has a new flow-run ID. nested task caches keyed by flow-run ID therefore do not carry over, consistent with existing failed-child recreation. the retry guide documents this behavior.

this also preserves the tracking-task identity for nested direct calls inside a task context, regardless of whether a result was actually persisted. the regression test covers both persistence modes.

related: #12913, #9152, #21951, #22286.

</details>

<details>
<summary>validation</summary>

- before the fix: four new regression cases failed; two persisted-result controls passed.
- after the fix: sync and async cases cover a successful child retry, exhausted child retries, persisted-result reuse, and preserved original Completed history.
- the standalone MRE failed before the fix and completes afterward with three child calls.
- focused retry, reattachment, and tracking-key tests: 29 passed, 1 existing expected failure.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_flow_engine.py -n4 --tb=short`: 287 passed, 3 existing expected failures.
- pre-commit hooks passed; Vale reported no errors or warnings for the updated retry guide.

</details>

title: Add `container_wait_timeout` to `DockerWorkerJobConfiguration`
body:
closes #23150

this PR adds a `container_wait_timeout` job variable to the Docker worker and passes it to `container.wait()`.

`DockerWorker._watch_container` called `container.wait()` with no arguments. docker-py forwards `timeout=None` to `requests`, so `DOCKER_CLIENT_TIMEOUT` did not apply and `POST /containers/{id}/wait` could block forever. A hung Docker API left the worker attached to the run and held its concurrency slot.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- New field `DockerWorkerJobConfiguration.container_wait_timeout: Optional[int]` (`gt=0`, default `None`).
- `_watch_container` now calls `container.wait(timeout=configuration.container_wait_timeout)`.
- Default behavior does not change: with no value set, the worker waits without a limit. The issue notes there is no correct default for container lifetime, so the value is opt-in.
- The timeout bounds the worker's wait request only; it does not stop the container. If the timeout expires, docker-py raises `requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout`. Because the run was already reported as started, `BaseWorker._submit_run_and_capture_errors` logs "Lost connection to flow run infrastructure", releases the concurrency slot, and leaves the final state to the engine inside the container. No `Crashed` state is proposed.
- Log streaming (`stream_output=True`) is not bounded by this setting; only the `/wait` request is, matching the scope of the issue.
- Tests: timeout is forwarded to the Docker API, default is `None`, `ReadTimeout` propagates out of `run()`, and non-positive values are rejected.

Docs: the field description is exposed through the work pool base job template and the generated API reference; no manual docs change is needed.

Linear: OSS-8226
</details>

title: Fix flaky test_multiple_workers_receive_distinct_messages
body:
This PR fixes the flaky `test_multiple_workers_receive_distinct_messages` test (failed on `main` in [this run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/35370764103)).

### Root cause

The `test_client` fixture returns a `TestClient` that is not entered as a context manager. In that mode, starlette starts a new blocking portal, and so a new event loop in a new thread, for each `websocket_connect`. The two concurrent worker channels in the test therefore run on two different event loops, but they share the process-wide `WORKER_CLEANUP_CONNECTION_REGISTRY` and its `asyncio.Lock`s.

When the second connection tried to acquire `WorkerCleanupConnectionRegistry._lock` while the first loop held it, asyncio raised:

```
RuntimeError: <asyncio.locks.Lock ...> is bound to a different event loop
```

The dispatch failed, the fallback dispatcher then delivered the message from the first loop into the second connection's websocket session, which lives on another loop, and `second_websocket.receive_json()` never returned. The test hit the 90 s `pytest-timeout`.

The server never runs this way: one process has one event loop, so the registry does not need to be loop-safe. The fix keeps the test on one event loop, like the server.

### Fix

Add a `_shared_event_loop(test_client)` context manager to the test module. It starts one blocking portal and sets `test_client.portal` so all websockets opened during the test use the same event loop. It is applied to the two tests in the module that open two worker channels at the same time (`test_idle_cleanup_workers_share_one_dispatcher` and `test_multiple_workers_receive_distinct_messages`).

Using `with test_client:` was not used because it also runs the app lifespan (migrations, services, Docket worker), which the rest of these tests do not do.

### Verification

- `test_worker_channel_cleanup_dispatcher.py`: 10 sequential runs, all 13 tests pass each time.
- `test_worker_channel_cleanup_dispatcher.py` + `test_worker_channel_cleanup_registry.py` with `-n 4`: 29 passed.
- `ruff format --check` passes. `ruff check` reports two pre-existing `PLC0414` findings in this file that are not changed by this PR.

title: Add browser-local pinned deployments to the React UI
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb5fc1fd-58ef-4e13-b754-bc3d70d2886f



this PR adds pinned deployments to the React UI: pin a deployment from its table row or its details page, and it sorts to the top of the deployments list. Pins live in the browser's `localStorage`, not on the server — an open source server has no users, so server-side pins would be shared by everyone pointing at it.

Related to #15512

<details>
<summary>How it works</summary>

- `usePinnedDeployments` (`src/components/deployments/pinned-deployments/`, alongside the button) is a small `useSyncExternalStore` store over the `prefect-pinned-deployments` localStorage key. Every pin button and the list route read the same state, and other tabs pick up changes through the `storage` event. Stored values are parsed with zod; anything malformed is treated as no pins.
- `PinDeploymentButton` is a ghost icon button with `aria-pressed` and a tooltip. In table rows it is hidden until the row is hovered or the button is keyboard-focused; it stays visible for pinned deployments and on devices without hover (`@media (hover: none)`), so it works on touch screens. On the details page it is always visible.
- Pinned deployments sort first across pages, not only within the current page. `usePinnedFirstDeployments` (`src/api/deployments/use-pinned-first-deployments/`, next to `useListDeploymentsWithFlows`) reads the pinned deployments that match the current search/tag filters (`deployments.id.any_`), then fills the rest of the page from everything else (`deployments.id.not_any_`) using an offset that accounts for the pinned rows. Page sizes stay constant and no deployment repeats or is skipped. Within each group the selected sort order applies. No API changes.
- The pinned and unpinned reads resolve at different times, so the hook only swaps the list once they agree. Otherwise a deployment shows twice (or not at all) for a frame while it moves.
- Rows slide to their new position when pinning reorders the list. There is no animation library in ui-v2, so this is a small FLIP hook (`useAnimatedReorder`) on the Web Animations API using the UI's usual 200ms timing, skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`. `DataTable` gains an opt-in `animateRowReorder` prop, and the deployments table now sets `getRowId` so rows keep their identity when they move.
- The deployment details header now wraps. It already overflowed a 360px-wide screen before this PR, and the pin button would have pushed Run and the actions menu further off-screen.
- The route loader warms the same cache through one `prefetchPinnedFirstDeployments` function from the same module, so the query keys the loader and the hook use cannot drift apart; a test checks the hook renders from the prefetched cache without refetching.
- This means the list now uses `/deployments/filter` + `/deployments/count` instead of `/deployments/paginate`, with or without pins, so there is one code path.
- The pinned read sends no `limi

title: Fix two tests that do not check what their names say
body:
closes #23140

this PR fixes two tests that did not check the behavior that their names describe.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**`test_compound_automation_all_double_nested_trigger_any_all_does_not_act`** (`tests/events/server/triggers/test_composite_triggers.py`)

The fixture is `all(all(Failed, Completed), any(Completed, NonExistent))`. The event stream contains both `Completed` and `Failed`, so the nested `all` and the nested `any` both fire and the outer trigger acts one time. The old body had a no-op `act.call_count == 2` and then read `act.call_args` as if the trigger fired. The name and docstring were wrong, not the trigger. The test is renamed to `..._all_and_any_acts`, the docstring is corrected, and `act.assert_called_once()` replaces the no-op comparison. The sibling `..._all_all_does_not_act` test still covers the "does not act" case.

**`TestPausingFlows::test_can_not_nonblocking_pause_subflows`** (`tests/server/orchestration/test_core_policy.py`)

`ctx.run.parent_task_run_id == uuid4()` was a comparison, so the run stayed a top-level flow and the test passed only because top-level runs with no deployment are also aborted by `HandlePausingFlows`. The test now uses the `task_run` fixture and assigns `ctx.run.parent_task_run_id = task_run.id`, so the foreign key is valid and the run is a real subflow.

Verified locally: both test files pass, `pre-commit run --files ...` passes.

title: Make no-op comparisons in tests actually assert
body:
Several tests evaluate a comparison and throw the result away, so the check can never fail. This adds the missing `assert`s and fixes the one expectation that was wrong.

| File | Check that never ran |
|---|---|
| `tests/blocks/test_abstract.py` | both `caplog.records[...].message == ...` checks |
| `tests/cli/test_deploy.py` | `automation.name` / `automation.description` |
| `tests/events/server/triggers/test_composite_triggers.py` | two `act.call_count == N` checks |
| `tests/server/models/test_block_documents.py` | `fly_block_documents_count == 3` |
| `tests/utilities/test_asyncutils.py` | `await bar() == 42` |
| `tests/cli/test_work_queues.py` | `assert "Work pool with name: 'bad-pool' not found."` (always true). Now checked through `invoke_and_assert(..., expected_output_contains=...)` |
| `tests/utilities/test_collections.py` | `json.dumps(Color.RED) == "RED"`. With the `assert` added this fails, because `json.dumps` returns `'"RED"'`, so the expectation is corrected. |

Every changed test passes: `pytest tests/blocks/test_abstract.py tests/server/models/test_block_documents.py tests/utilities/test_asyncutils.py tests/utilities/test_collections.py tests/events/server/triggers/test_composite_triggers.py tests/cli/test_work_queues.py` gives 337 passed, and `TestDeploymentTrigger::TestDeploymentTriggerSyncing::test_automation_creation` passes. Changing an expectation (e.g. `'"RED"'` to `'"BLUE"'`) makes the corresponding test fail, as it should. `ruff check` / `ruff format` are clean.

Two more comparisons of this kind turned out to hide real questions about what the test should check (a `does_not_act` trigger test that acts once, and a subflow pause test whose subflow setup is a no-op). They're left untouched and described in #23140.

title: Omit inferred securityGroups so ECS tasks use the VPC default security group
body:
closes #13026

This PR removes the `securityGroups: []` entry from the network configuration that `ECSWorker._load_network_configuration` infers from a VPC.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The AWS `AwsVpcConfiguration` contract says: if you omit `securityGroups`, ECS uses the default security group of the VPC. An explicit empty list is not the same as an omitted field. Botocore keeps the empty list on the wire, so ECS does not fall back to the default security group.

Change:

```diff
 "awsvpcConfiguration": {
     "subnets": [s["SubnetId"] for s in subnets],
     "assignPublicIp": "ENABLED",
-    "securityGroups": [],
 }
```

Explicit `securityGroups` in a custom `network_configuration` are not changed.

Tests: `test_network_config_from_vpc_id` and `test_network_config_from_default_vpc` now assert that the field is absent. Moto does not emulate the AWS default and raises `KeyError: 'securityGroups'` when the field is omitted. The two tests above mock `_create_task_run` at the outgoing-request boundary while they still run the full `worker.run` path. For all other tests that use the `ecs_mocks` fixture (which already patches Moto internals), the fixture now patches `moto.ecs.models.Task.__init__` to set a default empty `securityGroups` on a copy of the network configuration, so the request Prefect sends stays unchanged.

Links:
- AWS `AwsVpcConfiguration`: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/API_AwsVpcConfiguration.html

</details>

title: Only write deployments that a poll actually changes
body:
closes #23129

This PR reduces deployment writes from queue polling while preserving poll freshness, queue events, and direct model calls.

Each polling API request records the polled queues' heartbeats in a short, write-only transaction before submitting background tasks. This keeps later polls from disappearing when Docket deduplicates pending or running work. The queue status/event task and deployment task run independently; a deployment enqueue or execution failure cannot replay or suppress queue-ready events.

The queue model function has its original queue-only interface again, with no Docket dependency. Deployment write coalescing is opt-in: the polling APIs enable it only after committing their heartbeats. Direct model calls and older task payloads retain unconditional refreshes, and explicit deployment IDs always refresh.

For opted-in queue polls, only non-READY deployments or deployments with missing/older timestamps are written. The refresh interval remains half the configured deployment timeout. Queue timestamps remain monotonic. Queue heartbeat writes and queue-event reads are batched under the database bind limit. The deployment read still locks rows in ID order before reading the clock and batching updates.

Trade-off: polling requests now wait for a short transaction that updates the polled queue rows in batches. Warm queues do not need a background queue-status task. Deployment updates remain in the background, and `DeploymentResponse.last_polled` can lag queue polls because it is refreshed periodically.

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

- Rebased on October 6, 2026 onto `main` at `85cbd1f13c`; new head `495a1b3b58`. `git range-diff` confirms the reviewed patch is unchanged.
- Current validation on Python 3.13.12 across all seven affected suites: **502 passed, 2 dialect-specific skips on SQLite** and **499 passed, 5 dialect-specific skips on PostgreSQL 18.6**.
- Current pre-commit lint, formatting, spelling, and type checks pass. The pre-push OpenAPI hook reports generated-file drift; the regenerated OpenAPI schema and TypeScript are byte-for-byte identical to regeneration from current `main`. Those unrelated generated changes are excluded.

Previous validation:

- Earlier full validation on Python 3.12, seven affected suites: **582 passed on SQLite**, **579 passed on PostgreSQL 18.6**; remaining cases are dialect-specific skips.
- After the latest fix and rebase: **302 tests passed on each of SQLite and PostgreSQL 18.6** across the work-queue model, both polling API suites, and Docket tests. The three new bind-limit cases failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- Regression tests cover polls at 0 and 25 seconds with background workers stopped, a deployment task finishing at 26 seconds, and Foreman checks at 65 and 86 seconds.
- Real Docket tests cover repeated deployment-enqueue failures, exhausted deployment-write retries, queue-event failures, and recovery on a later poll.
- UI-only requests still do not record po

title: Add flow_run(state_type, coalesce(start_time, expected_start_time)) index
body:
closes #23127

this PR adds a composite index on `flow_run (state_type, coalesce(start_time, expected_start_time))` so that state-filtered flow run queries sorted by start time do not time out on large PostgreSQL tables.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`POST /flow_runs/filter` with a `state.type` filter, a `start_time` bound, and `sort=START_TIME_ASC` compiles to:

```sql
WHERE state_type IN (...) AND coalesce(start_time, expected_start_time) <= :cutoff
ORDER BY coalesce(start_time, expected_start_time) ASC LIMIT :limit
```

The existing `ix_flow_run__coalesce_start_time_expected_start_time_{asc,desc}` indexes do not contain `state_type`. On a 6M-row table the planner walks the ordered expression index and removes ~5.5M rows with a filter, which exceeds the statement timeout.

Changes:
- `orm_models.py`: add `ix_flow_run__state_type_coalesce_start_time` to `FlowRun.__table_args__`.
- PostgreSQL migration `d4a7e1c93f52`: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, with the `pg_index.indisvalid` check + `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY` repair pattern from `c8d5f2a71b3e`. Rejects offline (`--sql`) generation because it must inspect the catalog.
- SQLite migration `a3b9c7d2e5f1`: plain `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`.
- `MIGRATION-NOTES.md` entry.

Verified locally against PostgreSQL 16: after `prefect server database upgrade`, the ticket's query shape plans as

```
Limit
  -> Index Scan using ix_flow_run__state_type_coalesce_start_time on flow_run
       Index Cond: ((state_type = 'RUNNING'::state_type) AND (COALESCE(start_time, expected_start_time) <= now()))
```

with no separate sort. `tests/server/database/test_migrations.py` passes in full on both SQLite and PostgreSQL.

</details>

title: Fix date-dependent failure in interval schedule form test
body:
This PR fixes the `IntervalScheduleForm > keeps the selected time when picking another day` test in ui-v2. The test failed on `main` on 2026-09-15: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/34975837424

**Root cause:** the test always clicks the calendar button for the 15th of the current month and finds it by its accessible name (`format(date, "EEEE, MMMM do, yyyy")`). `react-day-picker` adds a `Today, ` prefix to the label of the current day. On the 15th of each month, the button name is `Today, Tuesday, September 15th, 2026`, so `getByRole` finds no match and the test fails. The test is not random; it fails every time it runs on the 15th.

**Fix:** select the 15th, or the 14th when today is the 15th, so the target day is never today.

Verified locally on the 15th (the failing condition): all 7 tests in the file pass.

title: Omit UI source maps and nightly source distributions
body:
This PR reduces release uploads by disabling source maps in both bundled UIs and building only wheels for nightly `prefect` releases (`X.Y.Z.devN`). This limits future PyPI storage growth after the [3.8.6 publication failure](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/34854806040/job/104012320935).

Stable releases, release candidates, other prereleases, and manual builds retain both wheels and source archives. The versioning docs now explain that new nightlies require wheel-based installation. Browser debugging of production bundles no longer has the generated source maps.

<details>
<summary>Build results and checks</summary>

- Local artifacts are approximately 6.0 MiB for the wheel and 5.4 MiB for the source archive, with both UIs present and no `.map` files. The nightly build produces only the wheel.
- Both UI production builds passed, along with focused Biome/ESLint checks and 9 UI tests.
- The release workflow, UI build validation, and CLI build tests passed: 22 tests. The new nightly cases failed before the workflow change.
- Both the direct wheel and a wheel rebuilt from the source archive served both UI pages and their referenced JavaScript/CSS assets in isolated installations.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed. The documentation style check reported no errors.

</details>

Related to #15512.

title: ui-v2: show tag names inline and make tag overflow focusable
body:
closes #23107

This PR makes `TagBadgeGroup` show tag names inline and makes the tag overflow control accessible.

Before this change, the group replaced all tag names with one `N tags` badge when a run had more than two tags. The badge was a `span`, so keyboard users could not reach it.

Now the group:

- Shows as many tag names as fit in the width of its container. It measures the tags with `ResizeObserver` and shows more names when the container gets wider.
- Moves only the tags that do not fit behind a `+N` `<button>`. The button opens a `Popover` that lists the hidden tags. The button works with the keyboard, a pointer, and touch. Its `title` shows the hidden names on hover.
- Keeps `onTagClick` and `onTagsChange` (remove) for the tags in the popover.
- Keeps `title={tag}` on each `TagBadge`, so truncated labels still show the full name.

`maxTagsDisplayed` is now an optional hard cap. It has no default of `2`. Callers that set it (`3` or `5`) get the same cap as before, but only when the tags do not fit first.

`FlowRunCard` and `TaskRunsListItem` set `min-w-0` on the tag column so the group can measure the space it has.

The `MoreVertical` action-menu buttons on the flow run and task run details pages get an `sr-only` "Open menu" label (matching the other action menus in ui-v2). Their tests previously selected the menu with `getByRole("button", { expanded: false })`, which now also matches the `+N` overflow trigger; they select by name instead.

Tags that do not fit stay in the DOM on an absolutely positioned, invisible, `inert`/`aria-hidden` row so the group can measure them. The group sets its own `width` to the sum of every tag it may show plus the counter (capped by `max-w-full`). This width does not depend on how many tags currently fit, so the fit calculation cannot change the size it measures. Without this, a run with many tags could wrap the `+N` counter to a second line at narrow widths. `FlowRunCard` gives the tag column `flex-1` so the run name keeps its width and the tags take the space that is left.

Review follow-ups:

- Repeated tag values get per-occurrence keys and the measurement refs are keyed by index, so duplicates do not overwrite each other.
- New `overflow="badge"` prop renders `+N` as a plain badge (hidden names in `title`/`aria-label`). `TagsSelect` uses it because its `ComboboxTrigger` is already a `<button>`; a nested button is not valid.
- The `FlowRunHeader` tag wrapper can shrink (`min-w-12 flex` instead of `shrink-0`), so the fit calculation sees the real remaining width and the action menu stays on-screen on narrow viewports.
- Tag keys are `<occurrence>:<tag>`, so a literal tag cannot equal a generated key.
- The fit calculation measures a hidden sizer badge that shows the widest possible counter (`+{tags.length}`, `tabular-nums`) instead of the live `+N` control. The counter cannot wrap when the hidden count gets an extra digit, and the layout cannot oscillate.
- The `TagsInput` text field gets `basis-32

title: Restore deployment, work pool, and work queue links on V2 flow-run cards
body:
closes #23106

this PR restores the deployment, work pool, and work queue links on the flow-run cards of the flow "Runs" tab in the React UI.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `FlowRunCard`: the third row now shows `FlowRunDeployment`, `WorkPoolLink`, and `WorkQueueIconText` when the run has the related data. The row is not rendered when the run has no deployment and no work pool. The queue status dot is hidden for runs in a terminal state (same as the Vue UI).
- `routes/flows/flow.$id.tsx`: a new `buildFlowRunDeploymentsFilter(flowRuns)` collects the unique `deployment_id` values of the visible page and loads them with `buildFilterDeploymentsQuery`. The query is not enabled when no run has a deployment. The same filter is prefetched in the route loader and in the hover pagination prefetch, so the cards do not suspend. The Deployments tab data is not used because it has its own filter and pagination.
- `FlowDetail`: accepts `flowRunDeployments` and attaches the matching `deployment` to each `FlowRunCardData`.
- `WorkQueueIconText`: renders the queue name and link from its props and only fetches queue details (with `useQuery`, `retry: false`) when `showStatus` is set. A deleted or inaccessible queue on a historical run no longer throws to the route error boundary; the status dot is simply omitted.
- Tests: `flow-run-card.test.tsx` checks the three link `href` values and checks that no relationship row is rendered for a run without associations. `work-queue-icon-text.test.tsx` adds a 404 regression case. A `WithWorkPoolAndQueue` story is added.

title: Format deployment Created/Updated timestamps in ui-v2 metadata
body:
closes #23111

this PR formats the Created and Updated values in the ui-v2 deployment metadata sidebar with the existing `FormattedDate` component (`format="absolute"`, for example `Sep 14, 2026 at 2:57 PM`) instead of the raw API string. The raw ISO timestamp stays available in the tooltip. Missing values still show `None`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `deployment-metadata.tsx`: Created and Updated render `<FieldValue><FormattedDate date={...} format="absolute" /></FieldValue>`, the same pattern used in `flow-details.tsx`. The existing `None` fallback is unchanged.
- `deployment-metadata.test.tsx`: the render helper now accepts `Partial<Deployment>` overrides. New tests check the formatted text, the tooltip content, and the `None` fallback. Tests run with `TZ=UTC` (see `vite.config.ts`), so the expected strings are literals.

Related to #15512
</details>

title: Fix race between `WatcherThreadCancelScope` timeout injection and scope exit
body:
This PR fixes a flaky xdist worker crash in `tests/test_futures.py` (failed run: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/34644362193, also https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/34232387401).

### Root cause

`as_completed(..., timeout=...)` on a worker thread uses `WatcherThreadCancelScope`. The enforcer thread waits for the timeout, then injects `CancelledError` into the supervised thread with `PyThreadState_SetAsyncExc`. Nothing stopped the enforcer from doing this after the supervised thread had already left the scope. When the timeout expired at the same moment the scope was exiting, the exception landed at an arbitrary instruction outside the scope (in the failing run: inside a logging handler while it held a lock). The worker thread in `test_as_completed_with_timeout_from_worker_thread` never finished, and the next test on the xdist worker (`test_as_completed_with_zero_timeout_yields_completed_future`) was reported as the crash.

I reproduced this locally with a stress script (CPU contention + `PREFECT_LOGGING_INTERNAL_LEVEL=DEBUG`): the supervised thread was blocked in `__exit__` joining the enforcer while the enforcer was injecting the exception.

### Fix

Add `_exit_lock` and an `_exited` flag to `WatcherThreadCancelScope`. The enforcer still marks the scope cancelled (and runs cancel callbacks) as soon as the timeout elapses, without holding any lock. Only the exception delivery is serialized with scope exit, and it is skipped when the supervised thread has already left the scope:

```python
# supervised thread
def __exit__(...):
    try:
        with self._exit_lock:
            self._exited = True
            retval = super().__exit__(*_)
    finally:
        self._event.set()
        self._enforcer_thread.join()

# enforcer thread
if self.cancel(throw=False):          # state + callbacks, no locks held
    self._send_cancelled_error()

def _send_cancelled_error(self):
    with _get_thread_shield(self._supervised_thread), self._exit_lock:
        if self._exited:
            return                    # never inject into a thread outside the scope
        _send_exception_to_thread(self._supervised_thread, CancelledError)
```

The shield is taken before `_exit_lock`, so the enforcer never holds `_exit_lock` while it waits on a shield that the exiting thread holds.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- New test `test_watcher_thread_cancel_scope_does_not_inject_into_exiting_thread` fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- Stress reproducer: 1000+ iterations pass (failed at iteration ~29 before the fix).
- `tests/_internal/concurrency/test_cancellation.py` and `tests/test_futures.py`: all pass; the two affected `as_completed` tests pass 200x with `--flake-finder`.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the changed files: no new findings.
</details>

### Checklist

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
  - If no issue exists and your change is not

--- src/prefect/_internal/concurrency/cancellation.py (+16/-4)
@@ -410,6 +410,11 @@ class WatcherThreadCancelScope(CancelScope):

         super().__enter__()
         self._event = threading.Event()
+        # Serializes exception delivery with the supervised thread's exit, so the
+        # exception is never injected into a thread that has already left the scope
+        # and is running arbitrary code.
+        self._exit_lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._exited = False
         self._enforcer_thread = None
         self._supervised_thread = threading.current_thread()
 
@@ -428,7 +433,9 @@ def __exit__(self, *_: Any) -> Optional[bool]:
         # this frame, so the event must be set from a `finally` to guarantee the
         # enforcer is always released.
         try:
-            retval = super().__exit__(*_)
+            with self._exit_lock:
+                self._exited = True
+                retval = super().__exit__(*_)
         finally:
             self._event.set()
             if self._enforcer_thread:
@@ -448,7 +455,13 @@ def _send_cancelled_error(self):
                 self,
                 self._supervised_thread,
             )
-            with _get_thread_shield(self._supervised_thread):
+            # The shield is acquired before the exit lock: the supervised thread may
+            # exit the scope while shielded and must not wait on a lock held by a
+            # thread that is waiting for that shield.
+            with _get_thread_shield(self._supervised_thread), self._exit_lock:
+                if self._exited:
+                    logger.debug("%r already exited; not sending exception", self)
+                    return
                 try:
                     _send_exception_to_thread(self._supervised_thread, CancelledError)
                 except ValueError:
@@ -462,8 +475,7 @@ def _timeout_enforcer(self):
         if not self._event.wait(self.timeout):
             logger.debug("%r enforcer detected timeout!", self)
             if self.cancel(throw=False):
-                with _get_thread_shield(self._supervised_thread):
-                    self._send_cancelled_error()
+                self._send_cancelled_error()
 
     def cancel(self, throw: bool = True):

--- tests/_internal/concurrency/test_cancellation.py (+56/-0)
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@
 import anyio
 import pytest
 
+from prefect._internal.concurrency import cancellation
 from prefect._internal.concurrency.cancellation import (
     AlarmCancelScope,
     AsyncCancelScope,
@@ -172,6 +173,61 @@ def interrupted_exit(self: CancelScope, *exc_info: object) -> None:
         scope._enforcer_thread.join()
 
 
+def test_watcher_thread_cancel_scope_does_not_inject_into_exiting_thread(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+):
+    """
+    If the timeout elapses while the supervised thread is already exiting the scope,
+    the scope is still marked as cancelled but the enforcer must not inject an
+    exception: it would land at an arbitrary instruction outside the scope (e.g.
+    inside a logging handler) and can leave locks held forever.
+    """
+    exiting = threading.Event()
+    enforcer_ready = threading.Event()
+    original_exit = CancelScope.__exit__
+    original_enforcer = WatcherThreadCancelScope._timeout_enforcer
+    original_get_shield = cancellation._get_thread_shield
+
+    def synchronized_exit(self: CancelScope, *exc_info: object) -> bool | None:
+        exiting.set()
+        assert enforcer_ready.wait(5), "Enforcer did not reach the cancellation check"
+        return original_exit(self, *exc_info)
+
+    def synchronized_enforcer(self: WatcherThreadCancelScope) -> None:
+        assert exiting.wait(5), "Supervised thread did not start exiting"
+        original_enforcer(self)
+
+    def notify_enforcer_ready(thread: threading.Thread) -> cancellation.ThreadShield:
+        thread_shield = original_get_shield(thread)
+        # The enforcer obtains the shield before it checks, under the exit lock,
+        # whether the supervised thread has already left the scope.
+        enforcer_ready.set()
+        return thread_shield
+
+    send_exception_to_thread = MagicMock()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(CancelScope, "__exit__", synchronized_exit)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        WatcherThreadCancelScope, "_timeout_enforcer", synchronized_enforcer
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(cancellation, "_get_thread_shield", notify_enforcer_ready)
+    # Observe injection without risking an asynchronous exception in test cleanup.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        cancellation, "_send_exception_to_thread", send_exception_to_thread
+    )
+
+    def on_worker_thread() -> WatcherThreadCancelScope:
+        with WatcherThreadCancelScope(timeout=0) as scope:
+            pass
+        return scope
+
+    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
+        scope = executor.submit(on_worker_thread).result(timeout=10)
+
+    assert scope.cancelled()
+    assert not scope.completed()
+    send_exception_to_thread.assert_not_called()

title: docs: state when a deployment concurrency slot is acquired and released
body:
this PR documents when a flow run takes and releases a deployment concurrency slot, and how worker prefetch interacts with `CANCEL_NEW`.

The concepts page listed the concurrency fields and collision strategies but did not say that a run takes its slot on the `Scheduled -> Pending` transition (worker submission, up to `PREFECT_WORKER_PREFETCH_SECONDS` before the scheduled start) and keeps it until it leaves `Pending`, `Running`, or `Cancelling`. Users with a short schedule interval, a limit of 1, and `CANCEL_NEW` saw every other run cancelled with "Deployment concurrency limit reached" and read it as a bug.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `docs/v3/concepts/deployments.mdx` (Concurrency limiting): new paragraphs that state when the slot is acquired and released (including the in-process retry exception), link to prefetch, and give the interval guidance for `CANCEL_NEW` with a limit of 1 (interval > max(prefetch window, infrastructure startup) + run time). They also note that a run must reach `Running` within `grace_period_seconds` for the slot to stay held, and that `flow.serve()` uses the runner's `prefetch_seconds` argument instead of the worker setting.
- `docs/v3/concepts/workers.mdx` (Configure prefetch): one sentence that says a waiting run holds its deployment slot as long as it reaches `Running` within the grace period, with a link back.
- `docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployments/prefect-yaml.mdx`: `collision_strategy` table row now links to the concepts section.

Source of truth: `SecureFlowConcurrencySlots` and `ReleaseFlowConcurrencySlots` in `src/prefect/server/orchestration/core_policy.py`; `Runner.__init__` in `src/prefect/runner/runner.py` for the serve prefetch default.

Linear: [OSS-8208](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/OSS-8208/docs-state-when-a-deployment-concurrency-slot-is-acquired-and-released) (internal; no public GitHub issue)
</details>

title: Handle abstract container annotations for nested blocks
body:
closes #14282

this PR changes how Prefect detects `Block` types that are nested inside container field annotations.

`Block` schema generation and registration only traversed annotations whose origin is `list`, `dict`, `tuple`, or a union type. Pydantic keeps abstract container types (for example `collections.abc.Sequence[Child]`) as the field origin, so a field like `children: collections.abc.Sequence[Child]` was left out of `block_schema_references`, and `register_type_and_schema` did not register `Child` transitively.

The change replaces the fixed `NestedTypes` list with one shared rule, `_is_nested_type`, and applies it to every code path that walks field annotations:

- `schema_extra` (`block_schema_references` and `secret_fields` collection)
- `aregister_type_and_schema` and `register_type_and_schema` (transitive nested block registration)
- `_walk_annotation_for_blocks` (nested block type collection for schema position metadata)
- `Block.annotation_refers_to_block_class`, which now uses the same rule recursively for consistency

The rule returns true for union origins and for parameterized annotations whose origin is a subclass of `collections.abc.Iterable`. It does not recurse into non-container generics such as `Literal` or `type`, which could otherwise be misclassified.

<details>
<summary>notes</summary>

- checking `issubclass(origin, collections.abc.Iterable)` also covers `set`, `frozenset`, `collections.deque`, `collections.abc.Mapping`, `Iterator`, and other iterable container origins, not only `Sequence`
- `tests/blocks/test_core.py` has a schema-level regression test for `Sequence` fields with `Literal` and `type` fields as non-container controls, plus sync and async `register_type_and_schema` regression tests for transitive child registration
- no documentation changes: the set of supported annotations for nested blocks is not documented in hand-authored docs
</details>

title: Scan orphaned logs/artifacts by flow_run_id cursor instead of anti-join per batch
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23079

this PR changes the orphaned log and artifact vacuum so that it does not scan the full table for each delete batch.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**Problem.** `vacuum_orphaned_logs` deleted rows with this condition, 200 rows at a time:

```sql
DELETE FROM log WHERE id IN (
  SELECT id FROM log
  WHERE flow_run_id IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flow_run WHERE flow_run.id = log.flow_run_id)
  LIMIT 200
)
```

Postgres runs this as a hash anti-join with a sequential scan of the full `log` table. The scan repeats for each batch. On a 357M-row table, this keeps the database at 100% read IOPS for hours and the cleanup does not finish. An index on `(flow_run_id, id)` does not correct this: the anti-join must still visit every row of the child table for each batch.

**Change.** `_delete_orphaned_by_flow_run` replaces the anti-join with a keyset scan over the distinct `flow_run_id` values, then deletes by `flow_run_id`:

```
cursor = None
loop:
    ids = SELECT DISTINCT flow_run_id FROM log
          WHERE flow_run_id IS NOT NULL AND flow_run_id > cursor
          ORDER BY flow_run_id LIMIT batch_size
    stop if ids is empty
    existing = SELECT id FROM flow_run WHERE id IN (ids)
    cursor = ids[-1]
    for each orphaned id in (ids - existing):
        _batch_delete(model, model.flow_run_id IN (orphaned_ids), batch_size)
```

Each query reads one bounded slice of the existing `ix_log__flow_run_id` index. A full pass reads the index one time instead of one time per batch. Deletes use the same index, in the same way as the `vacuum_old_flow_runs` child cleanup. No new index or migration is required.

Plans on Postgres 17 (400k rows, 8k distinct runs):

```
Limit
  -> Unique
      -> Index Only Scan using ix_log__flow_run_id on log
           Index Cond: ((flow_run_id IS NOT NULL) AND (flow_run_id > $1))
```

```
Delete on log
  -> Nested Loop
      -> HashAggregate
          -> Limit
              -> Index Scan using ix_log__flow_run_id on log log_1
                   Index Cond: (flow_run_id = ANY ($1))
      -> Index Scan using pk_log on log
```

The same helper is used for `vacuum_orphaned_artifacts` (`ix_artifact__flow_run_id`).

**Tests.** Added `test_scans_all_flow_runs_across_multiple_batches`: `batch_size=2`, three live runs and three orphaned runs interleaved with three logs each plus one `NULL` log. It checks that only orphaned rows are removed across several cursor pages. Ran `tests/server/services/test_db_vacuum.py` against SQLite and Postgres 17.

</details>

--- docs/v3/advanced/transactions.mdx (+92/-0)
@@ -127,6 +127,98 @@ def confirmation(transaction):
 ```
 </Tip>
 
+## Configure commit timing
+
+The `commit_mode` parameter controls when a transaction commits its staged result and runs its
+`on_commit` hooks. Import `CommitMode` from `prefect.transactions` to choose a mode:
+
+| Mode | Behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| `CommitMode.LAZY` | Defers committing to the parent transaction. Without a parent, commits on successful context exit. |
+| `CommitMode.EAGER` | Commits on successful context exit, even if a parent transaction is still active. |
+| `CommitMode.OFF` | Does not automatically commit on context exit. A parent can still commit it, or you can call `txn.commit()` explicitly. Without a parent, an uncommitted transaction rolls back on exit. |
+
+When you omit `commit_mode`, a transaction inherits its parent's mode, or uses `LAZY` if it has no parent.
+This also applies to the transactions created by task runs. An explicit mode on a nested transaction
+overrides the inherited mode.
+
+### Reuse cached results with eager commits
+
+With `LAZY`, tasks inside a transaction stage their results until the outer transaction commits.
+With `EAGER`, each task commits when its own transaction exits, making its persisted result available
+to subsequent calls before the outer block finishes.
+
+The following example uses a cache policy based on task inputs and enables result persistence:
+
+```python
+from prefect import flow, task
+from prefect.cache_policies import INPUTS
+from prefect.transactions import CommitMode, transaction
+
+
+@task(cache_policy=INPUTS, persist_result=True)
+def sub_task(x: int):
+    print(f"Computing {x}")
+    return x * 2
+
+
+@flow
+def compare_commit_modes():
+    with transaction(commit_mode=CommitMode.LAZY):
+        sub_task(2)  # Executes and stages its result
+        sub_task(2)  # Executes again: the first result is not committed yet
+    # Both results commit when the block exits
+
+    with transaction(commit_mode=CommitMode.EAGER):
+        sub_task(3)  # Executes and commits its result immediately
+        sub_task(3)  # Reuses the committed result without executing the task body
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    compare_commit_modes()
+```
+
+Starting with an empty cache, this prints `Computing 2` twice and `Computing 3` once.
+The blocks use different inputs so the lazy block's results do not populate the eager block's cache.
+On subsequent runs, both blocks can reuse previously committed results.
+
+Eager commits do not enable caching on their own. Reuse requires a matching cache key and an
+unexpired, persisted result accessible to the next task run. See [caching](/v3/concepts/caching)
+for configuration details. Concurrent task calls can both start before either commits, so `EAGER`
+alone does not guarantee that a task body executes only once.
+
+### Understand rollback behavior
+
+Once a task's transaction commits, it cannot be rolled back. With `EAGER`, a later failure in the
+outer transaction does not run rollback hooks for tasks that have already committed, and their
+persisted results remain available. Their commit hooks have already run as well.
+
+For example, changing the earlier `pipeline` to use `transaction(commit_mode=CommitMode.EAGER)`
+would commit `write_file` before `quality_test` runs. If `quality_test` fails, `del_file` would not
+run and the file would remain. With the default `LAZY` mode, `write_file` remains staged and
+its rollback hook deletes the file when `quality_test` fails.
+
+Use `LAZY` when completed tasks should remain eligible for rollback until the group succeeds.
+Use `EAGER` when tasks should commit independently and make their results available sooner.
+In either mode, rollback hooks must implement cleanup of external side effects, such as file writes
+or API calls; Prefect does not automatically undo those operations.
+
+### Commit manually
+
+Use `OFF` to control the commit explicitly:
+
+```python
+from prefect.transactions import CommitMode, transaction
+
+with transaction(commit_mode=CommitMode.OFF) as txn:
+    txn.stage("result")
+    txn.commit()
+```
+
+If you omit `txn.commit()` in this example, the transaction rolls back when the block exits.
+Calling `commit()` also commits child transactions. As with eager commits, a later exception
+cannot roll back a transaction that you have already committed manually.
+

title: ci: resolve integration dependency overrides with `uv lock` instead of post-hoc `uv pip install`
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23071

this PR changes the "Pin dependency override" step of the integration package tests so the override is applied during resolution, not after it.

Before, the step did `uv sync` and then `uv pip install "dbt-core==1.8.0"`. The second command downgraded `protobuf` to 4.x but kept `googleapis-common-protos>=1.75.1`, which is compiled against protobuf 6.x. The import of `google.api` then failed with a protobuf `VersionError`.

Now the step does:

```diff
-uv sync
-uv pip install "${{ matrix.dependency-override }}"
+uv lock --upgrade-package "${{ matrix.dependency-override }}"
+uv sync --locked
```

`uv lock --upgrade-package` accepts a full specifier (`dbt-core==1.8.0`) and uses it as a constraint for the whole resolution. The resolver selects a compatible set for all packages (for `dbt-core==1.8.0`: `googleapis-common-protos==1.75.0`, `protobuf==4.25.9`, `dbt-postgres==1.9.1`, `dbt-snowflake==1.8.4`). If a compatible set does not exist, the job fails at the lock step with a resolver error instead of at import time.

<details>
<summary>Local verification</summary>

In `src/integrations/prefect-dbt`:

- `uv lock --upgrade-package "dbt-core==1.8.0" && uv sync --locked` resolves `dbt-core 1.8.0`, `protobuf 4.25.9`, `googleapis-common-protos 1.75.0`.
- `uv run --no-sync pytest -m "not integration" tests/cli`: 71 passed.
- `uv lock --upgrade-package "dbt-core==1.7.0"` also resolves.

</details>

title: fix(settings): default local_storage_path to PREFECT_HOME/storage (#23046)
body:
### Summary
Fixes #23046 where `local_storage_path` (and other home-dependent settings like `memo_store_path` and `logging_config_path`) failed to default to `$PREFECT_HOME/...` when `PREFECT_HOME` was customized and the respective setting environment variables/kwargs were left unset.

### Root Cause
`local_storage_path` is defined on `ResultsSettings`, `memo_store_path` on `ServerSettings`, and `config_path` on `LoggingSettings`. When Pydantic settings constructs these sub-settings models, `values` only contains fields for that specific nested model (not `home`, which lives on the root `Settings` model). Consequently, default factories fall back to `~/.prefect` instead of using `settings.home`.

### Fix
Added home-dependent default resolution to `Settings.post_hoc_settings` (`@model_validator(mode="after")`). If a path setting (`local_storage_path`, `profiles_path`, `memo_store_path`, `config_path`) was not explicitly set during initialization, `post_hoc_settings` resolves it using `self.home`.

### Verification
- Added `TestHomeDependentDefaults` in `tests/test_settings.py` verifying that custom `PREFECT_HOME` correctly sets `local_storage_path`, `profiles_path`, `memo_store_path`, and `config_path`.
- Verified explicit overrides continue to take precedence.
- All new tests pass green.
author: Tyagiquamar
diff:
--- src/prefect/settings/models/root.py (+13/-0)
@@ -279,6 +279,19 @@ def post_hoc_settings(self) -> Self:
         to use default_factory. The remaining items here require access to the full Settings instance
         or have complex interdependencies that will be migrated in future PRs.
         """
+        if "profiles_path" not in self.model_fields_set:
+            self.profiles_path = self.home / "profiles.toml"
+            self.__pydantic_fields_set__.remove("profiles_path")
+        if "local_storage_path" not in self.results.model_fields_set:
+            self.results.local_storage_path = self.home / "storage"
+            self.results.__pydantic_fields_set__.remove("local_storage_path")
+        if "config_path" not in self.logging.model_fields_set:
+            self.logging.config_path = self.home / "logging.yml"
+            self.logging.__pydantic_fields_set__.remove("config_path")
+        if "memo_store_path" not in self.server.model_fields_set:
+            self.server.memo_store_path = self.home / "memo_store.toml"
+            self.server.__pydantic_fields_set__.remove("memo_store_path")
+
         if self.ui_url is None:
             self.ui_url = default_ui_url(self)
             self.__pydantic_fields_set__.remove("ui_url")

         with temporary_settings({PREFECT_DEBUG_MODE: True}):

             assert "PREFECT_DEBUG_MODE" in env
+
+
+class TestHomeDependentDefaults:
+    def test_copy_with_update_recomputes_home_dependent_defaults(
+        self, tmp_path: Path
+    ) -> None:
+        settings = Settings(home=tmp_path / "old")
+        new_home = tmp_path / "new"
+
+        updated = settings.copy_with_update(updates={PREFECT_HOME: new_home})

+        monkeypatch.setenv("PREFECT_RESULTS_LOCAL_STORAGE_PATH", str(override_path))
+        settings = Settings()
+        assert settings.home == custom_home
+        assert settings.results.local_storage_path == override_path

title: Fix Docker work pool editing and block/env serialization in UI v2
body:
closes #23066

Related to #15512

this PR fixes three regressions in the UI v2 schema form that break Docker work pool editing and block/environment serialization.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

**1. `Definition not found for #/definitions/DockerRegistryCredentials`**

The Docker worker schema stores its definitions under `$defs` (Pydantic output), but refs are rewritten to `#/definitions/...`. `getSchemaDefinition` only looked in one container, chosen from the schema shape. It now checks the container named in the ref first and falls back to the other one.

**2. Block document references**

`SchemaFormInputBlockDocument` emitted `{ $ref: "<id>" }`. The server (and the legacy Vue UI) expect:

```json
{ "$ref": { "block_document_id": "<id>" } }
```

The input now emits and reads this shape, and reuses the `BlockDocumentReferenceValue` type from `types/block-document-value.ts` instead of a local string-ref type.

**3. Environment variables and custom block dictionaries saved as escaped JSON strings**

The schema form edits free-form objects with a JSON editor, which stores `{ "__prefect_kind": "json", "value": "<string>" }` in the form values. These wrappers were written directly into work pool base job template `default`s and block document `data`, so the server received:

```json
{ "value": "{\"CDWH_ENVIRONMENT\":\"dev\"}", "__prefect_kind": "json" }
```

New `removePrefectKindValues` utility parses the wrappers back to native JSON (recursively; other `__prefect_kind` values such as `jinja` and `workspace_variable` are left alone). Empty or invalid JSON text becomes `undefined` and is removed from arrays, so malformed editor text is never saved as a string. The block document edit page now stops when `validateForm` reports the form invalid (the server reports malformed JSON as a validation error), so invalid JSON does not remove a saved field through `merge_existing_data: false`. It is applied in `BaseJobTemplateFormSection` and in the block document create/edit/dialog submissions, so the server now receives `{ "CDWH_ENVIRONMENT": "dev" }`.

`SchemaFormInputObject` also now hands existing dictionary values to the JSON editor (previously an existing value made the nested open object render nothing), so saved environment variables are visible and editable on the work pool edit page.

**Tests**

- `mergeSchemaPropertyDefinition.test.ts`: mixed `$defs` / `definitions` resolution and ref-prefix precedence
- `schema-form-input-block-document.test.tsx`: nested `$ref` shape
- `removePrefectKindValues.test.ts`: wrapper removal, nesting, string literals, empty/invalid input, cleared array entries
- `base-job-template-form-section.test.tsx`: environment default is written as a plain object, never as a `__prefect_kind` wrapper
- `block-document-edit-page.test.tsx`: no update request when validation fails

`npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and `npm test run` pass. `ui-v2/src/components/AGENTS.md` documents the schema form / API contrac

title: Allow cancelling a blocking paused flow run after its pause timeout elapses
body:
Follow-up to #23039 (merged as 4fa7c8b9be).

This PR makes an explicit cancel win over an elapsed pause deadline. #23039 added `is_cancelling()` to the allowed destinations in `HandleResumingPausedFlows`, but the later `pause_timeout` check still rejected the transition and wrote `Failed` when the pause had expired. A blocking pause keeps the flow process alive, so the worker must receive `Cancelling` to tear the process down (see #7807).

```diff
 class HandleResumingPausedFlows(FlowRunOrchestrationRule):
     async def before_transition(...):
         ...
+        if proposed_state.is_cancelling():
+            return
         pause_timeout = initial_state.state_details.pause_timeout
         if pause_timeout and pause_timeout < now("UTC"):
             await self.reject_transition(state=states.Failed(...), ...)
```

Unchanged behavior:
- Resume or reschedule attempts on an expired pause are still rejected and rewritten to `Failed`.
- Suspended runs (`pause_reschedule=True`) are still converted directly to `Cancelled` by `BypassCancellingFlowRunsWithNoInfra`, which runs before this rule.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- `tests/server/orchestration/test_core_policy.py`: the focused rule test from #23039 (which duplicated the parametrized happy path) is converted into an expired-pause regression: `test_allows_cancelling_a_paused_flow_run_after_pause_has_timed_out`.
- `tests/server/orchestration/api/test_flow_runs.py`: new `test_cancelling_a_paused_flow_run_with_expired_timeout_is_accepted` proves the API accepts `CANCELLING` for an expired blocking pause and persists `CANCELLING`.

Both new tests fail without the source change. Ran `TestResumingFlows`, `TestBypassCancellingFlowRunsWithNoInfra`, and `TestSetFlowRunState` (56 passed) plus Ruff on the touched files.

title: fix(ci): move old-sqlite.Dockerfile UI builders from bullseye to bookworm
body:
This PR changes the two Node UI-builder stages in `.github/docker/old-sqlite.Dockerfile` from `node:*-bullseye-slim` to `node:*-bookworm-slim`, and adds that Dockerfile to the path triggers of the Integration tests workflow.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The `Test SQLite 3.24.0 Compatibility` and `Test SQLite 3.31.1 Compatibility` jobs in the Integration tests workflow fail on `main` (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/34233246261). This is not a flaky test. The `docker build` step fails in `apt-get update`:

```
E: Release file for http://deb.debian.org/debian-security/dists/bullseye-security/InRelease is expired (invalid since 16h 26min 4s).
```

Debian 11 (bullseye) reached the end of LTS support, and the `bullseye-security` repository is no longer refreshed. Every build that uses a bullseye base image now fails in the same way, so this job will not recover on its own.

The root `Dockerfile` already uses `node:20.20.2-bookworm-slim` and `node:22.23.2-bookworm-slim` for the same UI-builder stages, so this change makes the CI Dockerfile match the production Dockerfile. `chromium` is available in bookworm, so the `apt-get install` step does not change.

The workflow did not run for changes to `.github/docker/old-sqlite.Dockerfile`, so a PR that changed only that file could not verify the SQLite jobs. The path is now in the `pull_request` and `push` triggers, and both SQLite jobs pass on this PR.

No tests are needed: the change is CI infrastructure only.

</details>

title: fix: schedule automation cache update on the event loop for SQLite
body:
closes #23055

This PR fixes a deadlock that freezes the event loop of a Prefect server on SQLite.

### Summary

On SQLite, `_notify()` in `src/prefect/server/events/models/automations.py` registers an `after_commit` listener that calls `run_coro_as_sync(automation_changed(...))`. The listener runs on the event-loop thread inside `session.commit()`, and `run_coro_as_sync` blocks that thread until the coroutine completes on the run-sync loop. `automation_changed()` waits on the module-global automations lock, which `reconcile_automations()` (and other coroutines on the same loop) can hold across awaits. If the lock is held when a commit lands, the lock holder can never resume because the loop is blocked: a permanent deadlock. The server then accepts TCP connections but never answers any request.

This change schedules `automation_changed()` as a task on the running loop instead of blocking on the run-sync loop. A held lock now only delays the cache refresh. When the committing thread has no running loop, the code falls back to `run_coro_as_sync` as before. The PostgreSQL path is not changed; it uses `NOTIFY` and has no `after_commit` listener.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

- Reproduced the reported minimal reproduction (`repros/23055.py`, which runs a real uvicorn server and holds `_automations_lock` on its loop): before this change `POST /automations/` never answers and `GET /health` hangs; after this change the POST returns `201`, the cache update completes after the lock is released, and `/health` keeps answering.
- Added `test_automation_commit_does_not_block_event_loop_while_lock_held` in `tests/events/server/models/test_automation_notifications.py`: it holds the automations lock on the test's event loop and commits an automation. On the unfixed code the test deadlocks (pytest-timeout fires); with this change it passes and the cache update lands once the lock is released.
- `tests/events/server/models/` and `tests/events/server/` (automation/trigger/reconcile tests) pass locally on SQLite.
</details>

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/uv (ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv)</summary>

### [`v0.12.10`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#01210)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/compare/0.12.9...0.12.10)

Released on 2026-09-04.

##### Enhancements

- Attempt to revoke short-lived PyPI trusted-publishing tokens after `uv publish` completes, including when publishing fails ([#​21423](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21423))

##### Preview features

- Omit `exclude-newer-package` settings for packages outside the resolution from `uv.lock` with the `missing-exclude-newer-package-lock` preview feature ([#​21455](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21455))
- Show terminal dependency cycles in `uv tree --invert` output ([#​21404](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21404))

##### Performance

- Speed up locking large workspaces with conflicts by excluding unrelated extras and dependency groups from conflict simplification ([#​21399](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21399))
- Speed up `uv publish` by hashing each artifact in a single blocking task and reusing the buffer across reads ([#​21389](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21389))

##### Bug fixes

- Prevent `--locked` from failing when `exclude-newer-package` settings differ only for packages outside the resolution ([#​21454](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21454))
- Allow `uv lock --check` to reuse a lockfile when an absolute `exclude-newer` cutoff is moved later ([#​19571](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/19571))
- Allow `uv lock --check` to reuse a lockfile when a package-specific `exclude-newer` cutoff is disabled ([#​21450](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21450))
- Require an explicit `--name` when `uv init` would infer a project name reserved for a Python interpreter ([#​21395](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21395))
- Write package-specific `exclude-newer` cutoffs to `uv.lock` in a deterministic order ([#​21453](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21453))

### [`v0.12.9`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0129)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/compare/0.12.8...0.12.9)

title: fix(server): begin SQLite write transaction before reading in `mark_deployments_ready`
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23051

this PR makes `mark_deployments_ready` and `mark_deployments_not_ready` open their transaction with `with_for_update=True`, so SQLite starts with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and holds the write lock before the read.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Both functions read the deployment rows and then update them in one transaction. On SQLite the transaction started as `BEGIN DEFERRED`. When a concurrent worker poll committed a write between the read and the update, SQLite could not upgrade the read transaction to a write transaction. It failed at once with `database is locked` (`SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT`). The busy timeout does not apply to this case, so `PREFECT_SERVER_DATABASE_TIMEOUT` did not help.

```diff
 async with db.session_context(
     begin_transaction=True,
+    with_for_update=True,
 ) as session:
```

`with_for_update` is a no-op on PostgreSQL, where the `.with_for_update()` on the query already locks the rows.

The new test `test_sqlite_write_lock_is_held_before_reading` injects a committed write from a second `sqlite3` connection between the read and the update. Without the fix, the test fails with the same `database is locked` error that the issue reports. With the fix, the second connection is blocked and the update completes.

</details>

title: fix(prefect-dbt): raise on skipped dbt nodes in PrefectDbtRunner
body:
<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://docs.prefect.io/contribute/index
-->

<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
<!-- Whether or not AI tools helped draft this PR, you are responsible for understanding the change, keeping it scoped, validating it locally, and explaining the approach. -->
<!-- Maintainers may close PRs that appear low-effort, likely AI-generated, and substantially far from the expected implementation. -->

### Checklist
<!-- These boxes may be checked after opening the pull request. -->

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
  - If no issue exists and your change is not a small fix, please [create an issue](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/new/choose) first.
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.
- [x] If this pull request removes docs files, it includes redirect settings in `mint.json`.
- [x] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings.

This PR fixes PrefectDbtRunner incorrectly marking dbt nodes as successful when they were actually skipped due to upstream failure.
I didn't create issue, because AI bot creates a duplicate PR and noise.
   
**What was happening**

In strict static analysis mode, dbt's task graph splits node execution into phases (Render → Analyze → Run). Downstream nodes can complete their Render and Analyze phases before an upstream node's Run phase finishes. This means dbt emits NodeStart for a downstream node before it knows the upstream will fail.

When the upstream fails (e.g. in a pre-hook), dbt propagates the skip and emits NodeFinished for the downstream node with node_status = "skipped".

PrefectDbtRunner correctly creates a Prefect task on NodeStart. But execute_dbt_node only checked FAILURE_STATUSES when the node finished — it never checked SKIPPED_STATUSES. So the task function returned normally and Prefect recorded it as success, even though the node never executed.

**The fix**

Added a SKIPPED_STATUSES check in execute_dbt_node. When a node finishes with a skipped status, the task now raises an exception with a clear message, so Prefect marks the task as failed rather than succeeded.

Prefect has no SKIPPED task state (the terminal states are COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, CRASHED), so FAILED is the most accurate representation of "this node did not run because something upstream broke."

+        if node_status in SKIPPED_STATUSES:
+            raise Exception(

title: Allow flow names with surrounding whitespace to complete
body:
A flow name with a leading or trailing space can prevent final-state reporting and leave the run in `Running`. This PR trims spaces and tabs from optional attribution headers so these flows complete, while preserving their names.

Values that become empty are omitted. The same normalization serves sync and async clients, including environment-sourced flow, deployment, and worker attribution.

<details>
<summary>Validation and contribution checklist</summary>

The regression tests exercise real HTTP serialization and flow completion, without mocking orchestration. They cover sync and async flows, surrounding spaces and tabs, and whitespace-only names. All 34 attribution tests pass. Repository hooks pass.

The test file also passes without database clearing, so its unnecessary `clear_db` marker is removed per `tests/AGENTS.md`.

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`". No matching issue was found; this is a small fix.
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue. Not applicable.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed. This restores accepted flow names; no configuration or usage change requires documentation.
- [ ] If this pull request removes docs files, it includes redirect settings in `mint.json`. Not applicable.
- [x] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Session context</summary>

An async flow called through `asyncio.run` reproduced the reported `LocalProtocolError` after its body completed. Removing the trailing space avoided the failure. The regression tests failed before the fix, and the original reproduction completes after it. Attribution headers were introduced in [#20508](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/20508).

</details>

title: Reduce task run recorder INSERT compilation CPU
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23040

This PR applies the [PostgreSQL event-persister pattern from #22961](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/22961/changes) to task-run upserts: rows are passed as execution parameters instead of embedded in each `INSERT`. This avoids constructing a row-expanded SQLAlchemy expression while retaining bulk `insertmanyvalues` execution.

<summary>Details</summary>

- Preserves explicit NULL values, the existing upsert and stale-state behavior, conflict-key ordering, and segment boundaries.
- Leaves SQLite and single-row PostgreSQL segments on the existing path for compatibility and to avoid overhead at the default batch size.
- Adds regression coverage for mixed stale, updated, and newly inserted rows in one bulk upsert.

Validated against the PostgreSQL and SQLite task-run recorder tests and with pre-commit.

title: docs: warn future migrations about INVALID CONCURRENTLY index repair
body:
Automated AGENTS.md update triggered by commit ef3967a78cfedac6353e728e5a8aea304fb0ca03. This PR was generated by Claude Code analyzing the diff from the latest push to main and updating any stale AGENTS.md files.
Why this belongs in AGENTS.md 
Path: src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md

Proposed text: "**`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS` migrations can leave an `INVALID` index behind if the build is interrupted** (statement timeout, pod restart, racing replicas) — a later `IF NOT EXISTS` retry then silently skips repairing it, so the migration records as applied but the planner never uses the index. New concurrent-index migrations should check `pg_index.indisvalid` and `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY` if invalid; see `c8d5f2a71b3e` for the pattern."

Non-obvious evidence: The failure mode is invisible from reading any single migration file — `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS` looks idempotent and safe, but Postgres records the migration as applied while leaving an unusable `INVALID` index, silently degrading query plans (seq scan instead of index) with no error anywhere in the migration log. This is not stated in any docstring, comment, or test name outside the one new migration file that happens to fix it.

Cross-cutting scope: Applies to any future migration that creates a Postgres index with `CONCURRENTLY` — confirmed 15 existing migrations in `database/_migrations/versions/postgresql/` already use this pattern, so it is a recurring construct, not a one-off. The guidance is a reusable checklist item ("check indisvalid, REINDEX CONCURRENTLY if not") for whoever writes the 16th one.

Why not code comment/docstring: The new migration file (`c8d5f2a71b3e...py`) already has this explanation in its own docstring, but that only helps someone already reading that specific repair migration after the fact. A future author writing an unrelated new concurrent-index migration would have no reason to open this file and would repeat the same mistake unless the AGENTS.md Database Migrations section flags the pattern up front.

Durability: This is a structural fact about how Postgres CONCURRENTLY builds interact with Alembic's IF NOT EXISTS idiom — it doesn't depend on this specific table/column and will remain true and relevant long after this migration and its triggering incident are forgotten.

Counter-evidence checked: Read src/prefect/server/AGENTS.md's existing "Database Migrations" section (only stated the SQLite/PostgreSQL parity requirement, nothing about CONCURRENTLY or INVALID indexes). Checked MIGRATION-NOTES.md (per-migration changelog, not a durable operating manual — appropriately left alone). Grepped all migrations using CONCURRENTLY to confirm this is a recurring pattern (15 hits) rather than a one-off. No existing AGENTS.md in src/prefect/server/database/ to house this closer to the code.
Changed files in triggering pus

title: Treat ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED as alive in Windows `_is_pid_alive`
body:
closes #23036

this PR makes the Windows branch of `_is_pid_alive` report a process as alive when `OpenProcess` fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (5). This matches the POSIX branch, which returns `True` for `PermissionError`.

Before this change, a null handle from `OpenProcess` was always reported as dead. A null handle occurs for a missing process (`ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`, 87) and also for a live process that we cannot open (another user, higher integrity, protected process). `FileSystemLockManager` then removed a live lock as stale and a second holder could acquire it.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

```diff
-handle = ctypes.windll.kernel32.OpenProcess(...)
+kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
+handle = kernel32.OpenProcess(...)
 if handle:
     ...
     return True
-return False
+return ctypes.get_last_error() == ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED
```

Tests:
- `@pytest.mark.windows` test: PID 4 (`System`) is reported alive. Runs in the Windows CI job.

CI: `src/prefect/locking/**` and `tests/locking/**` are added to the `paths` filter of `windows-tests.yaml`, so the Windows job runs for changes to this module.

</details>

title: Resolve the Azure CLI executable through PATH in AzureCLI.run_command
body:
closes #15048

This PR makes `AzureCLI.run_command` resolve the command executable through `shutil.which` before it starts the process.

On Windows, the Azure CLI launcher is `az.cmd`. A bare `az` as `argv[0]` is not found by `subprocess` when no shell is used, so every Azure Container Instance provisioning step fails with `FileNotFoundError` (`Errno 2`), even when the launcher is on `PATH`. All Azure provisioning calls go through this one boundary.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

```diff
-result = await run_process(shlex.split(command), check=False)
+args = shlex.split(command)
+if args:
+    args[0] = shutil.which(args[0]) or args[0]
+result = await run_process(args, check=False)
```

- Only `argv[0]` changes. The argument list, `check=False`, and the error handling stay the same.
- If `shutil.which` does not find the command, the original name is passed through so the existing error path is not changed.
- No `shell=True` and no new dependency.
- Tests: `TestAzureCLIRunCommand` covers `az` resolving to an `az.CMD` path with successful output, and an unresolved command passing through unchanged.
- No documentation change is needed: this is a bug fix with no change to the user-facing interface.

</details>

title: Rebuild invalid ix_event_resources__occurred left by an interrupted build
body:
closes #23032

this PR adds a PostgreSQL migration `c8d5f2a71b3e` that repairs an `INVALID` `ix_event_resources__occurred` index.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Migration `bad1e352c597` runs `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS`. When PostgreSQL cancels that build (statement timeout, lock timeout, restart, two replicas that migrate at the same time), it leaves an `INVALID` index with that name. On the next upgrade `IF NOT EXISTS` sees the name and skips the build. Alembic records the revision, and the planner never uses the index. The `db_vacuum` delete on `event_resources.occurred` then falls back to a sequential scan.

The new migration uses the same guard as `50737cdaee36` and `9e9dadc36797`:

```
if not pg_index.indisvalid for ix_event_resources__occurred:
    DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS ix_event_resources__occurred
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS ix_event_resources__occurred ON event_resources (occurred)
```

- The catalog check is skipped in `--sql` (offline) mode, same as the two earlier migrations.
- `downgrade()` is a no-op. The index belongs to `bad1e352c597`, and that revision drops it.
- There is no SQLite counterpart. SQLite does not build indexes concurrently and cannot leave an invalid index.

Verification against PostgreSQL 16 in Docker, with the procedure from the issue (invalid index at `7218aad17905`, then upgrade):

```
before upgrade:                            ix_event_resources__occurred|f
after upgrade to 9e9dadc36797 (main head): ix_event_resources__occurred|f
after upgrade to head (c8d5f2a71b3e):      ix_event_resources__occurred|t
```

Tests: unit tests for the invalid and valid paths of `upgrade()`, and a dry-run test for the offline SQL output, both in `tests/server/database/test_migrations.py`.

</details>

+
+`bad1e352c597` used a plain `IF NOT EXISTS`, so an `INVALID` index left by an
+interrupted build was skipped and never repaired. This rebuilds an invalid
+`ix_event_resources__occurred` with `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, preserving the
+old index until its replacement is valid. Offline SQL generation is rejected
+because it cannot safely inspect the catalog. Downgrading is a no-op; the index
