--- src/prefect/server/database/_migrations/versions/postgresql/2026_09_04_000000_c8d5f2a71b3e_rebuild_invalid_event_resources_occurred_index.py (+66/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+"""Rebuild an invalid event_resources(occurred) index
+
+Revision ID: c8d5f2a71b3e
+Revises: 9e9dadc36797
+Create Date: 2026-09-04 00:00:00.000000
+
+Revision `bad1e352c597` creates `ix_event_resources__occurred` with
+`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS`. A build that is cancelled or
+interrupted (statement timeout, lock timeout, pod restart, two replicas racing
+to migrate) leaves an `INVALID` index behind. On the next upgrade
+`IF NOT EXISTS` sees the name, skips the build, and the revision is recorded as
+applied, so the planner never uses the index and the `db_vacuum` delete on
+`event_resources.occurred` falls back to a sequential scan.
+
+This migration rebuilds an invalid leftover with `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY`,
+which preserves the existing index until its replacement is valid. When the
+index is already valid it is a no-op; when it does not exist it is created.
+Catalog lookups anchor the index to the resolved `event_resources` table so an
+identically named index in another schema cannot be inspected or rebuilt.
+"""
+
+from alembic import op
+
+# revision identifiers, used by Alembic.
+revision = "c8d5f2a71b3e"
+down_revision = "9e9dadc36797"
+branch_labels = None
+depends_on = None
+
+
+def upgrade():
+    migration_context = op.get_context()
+    with migration_context.autocommit_block():
+        if migration_context.as_sql:
+            raise RuntimeError("c8d5f2a71b3e requires an online PostgreSQL migration")
+
+        index_query = """
+            SELECT format('%I.%I', n.nspname, c.relname), i.indisvalid
+            FROM pg_index i
+            JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid
+            JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
+            WHERE i.indrelid = to_regclass('event_resources')
+              AND c.relname = 'ix_event_resources__occurred'
+            """
+        index = op.get_bind().exec_driver_sql(index_query).first()
+        if index is None:
+            op.execute(
+                """
+                CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS
+                ix_event_resources__occurred
+                ON event_resources (occurred)
+                """
+            )
+        elif not index[1]:
+            op.execute(f"REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY {index[0]}")
+
+        index = op.get_bind().exec_driver_sql(index_query).first()
+        if index is None or not index[1]:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "ix_event_resources__occurred is missing or invalid after creation"
+            )
+
+

title: Add TLA+ model for deployment concurrency leases
body:
Adds a bounded [TLA+](https://lamport.azurewebsites.net/tla/tla.html) model of deployment-concurrency release authority and durable repository guidance for keeping future models mapped to production contracts.

- Checks an abstract SQL-authoritative claim protocol against stale expiry work, duplicate delivery, PENDING reacquisition, and competing release paths.
- Preserves seven unsafe current-code traces as deterministic strict-`xfail` regressions.
- Documents model selection, non-vacuity, model-to-code mapping, implementation tests, ownership, and removal criteria in `AGENTS.md`.
- Adds a path-filtered GitHub Actions workflow that checks the target protocol and verifies all seven intentional counterexamples.

The target model does not specify a production schema, migration, or replay protocol, and a green TLC run is not evidence that Prefect's Python implementation conforms.

Related to https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22935

<details>
<summary>Checks and scope</summary>

The CI job uses Temurin 21 and checksum-verified TLA+ Tools `v1.7.4`. The target explores 55,915 distinct states with no invariant violation. The unsafe configurations fail with their expected `RenewWinsAgainstStaleScan` or `NoForeignRelease` invariant.

</details>
author: desertaxle
diff:
--- .github/workflows/tla-plus.yaml (+124/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,124 @@
+name: TLA+ model check
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - .github/workflows/tla-plus.yaml
+      - "formal/tla/**"
+
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+    paths:
+      - .github/workflows/tla-plus.yaml
+      - "formal/tla/**"
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
+  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
+
+env:
+  TLA_TOOLS_VERSION: "1.7.4"
+  TLA_MODEL_DIR: formal/tla/deployment-concurrency
+
+jobs:
+  check-deployment-concurrency:
+    name: Deployment concurrency
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Set up Java
+        uses: actions/setup-java@v5
+        with:
+          distribution: temurin
+          java-version: "21"
+
+      - name: Download TLA+ tools
+        run: |
+          tla_tools_url="https://github.com/tlaplus/tlaplus/releases/download/"
+          tla_tools_url+="v${TLA_TOOLS_VERSION}/tla2tools.jar"
+          tla_tools_sha256="936a262061c914694dfd669a543be2457"
+          tla_tools_sha256+="3c45d5aa0ff20a8b96b23d01e050e88"
+          curl --fail --location --silent --show-error \
+            "$tla_tools_url" \
+            --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/tla2tools.jar"
+          printf '%s  %s\n' \
+            "$tla_tools_sha256" \
+            "$RUNNER_TEMP/tla2tools.jar" \
+            | sha256sum --check -
+
+      - name: Check target protocol
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/tlc/target"
+          java -XX:+UseParallelGC \
+            -jar "$RUNNER_TEMP/tla2tools.jar" \
+            -workers 1 \
+            -metadir "$RUNNER_TEMP/tlc/target" \
+            -config "$TLA_MODEL_DIR/DeploymentConcurrency.cfg" \
+            "$TLA_MODEL_DIR/DeploymentConcurrency.tla"
+
+      - name: Check expected counterexamples
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+
+          check_counterexample() {
+            local config="$1"
+            local invariant="$2"
+            local name="${config%.cfg}"
+            local output="$RUNNER_TEMP/tlc/${name}.log"
+
+            mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/tlc/$name"
+            set +e
+            java -XX:+UseParallelGC \
+              -jar "$RUNNER_TEMP/tla2tools.jar" \
+              -workers 1 \
+              -metadir "$RUNNER_TEMP/tlc/$name" \
+              -config "$TLA_MODEL_DIR/$config" \
+              "$TLA_MODEL_DIR/DeploymentConcurrency.tla" \
+              2>&1 | tee "$output"
+            local status="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
+            set -e
+
+            if [[ "$status" -ne 12 ]]; then
+              echo "Expected TLC exit 12 for $config, got $status" >&2
+              return 1
+            fi
+
+            if ! grep -Fq "Invariant $invariant is violated." "$output"; then
+              echo "Expected $config to violate $invariant" >&2
+              return 1
+            fi
+          }
+
+          check_counterexample \
+            CounterexampleStaleReap.cfg \
+            RenewWinsAgainstStaleScan
+          check_counterexample \
+            CounterexampleFallbackRelease.cfg \
+            NoForeignRelease
+          check_counterexample \
+            CounterexampleReadPresentRelease.cfg \
+            NoForeignRelease
+          check_counterexample \
+            CounterexampleFlowRunDeletion.cfg \
+            NoForeignRelease
+          check_counterexample \
+            CounterexampleDuplicateReap.cfg \
+            NoForeignRelease
+          check_counterexample \
+            CounterexampleAcquireAbort.cfg \
+            NoForeignRelease
+          check_counterexample \
+            CounterexampleReacquireNullification.cfg \
+            NoForeignRelease

+## Formal Protocol Models
+
+- Use TLA+ selectively for bounded concurrent or distributed protocols whose correctness depends on interleavings, retries, duplication, time, or ownership. Prefer ordinary tests for local or sequential behavior.
+- Treat each `formal/tla/<protocol>/README.md` as the authority for its scope, configurations, action-to-code mapping, owner, and review triggers.
+- Before changing mapped behavior, review the model and its deterministic regressions. Update them when the abstraction changes; otherwise state in the PR why it remains valid.
+- A green model validates only its documented abstraction, not Prefect's implementation. Implementation evidence comes from mapped behavior and contract tests.
+
 ## Working on Issues
 
 - Read the GitHub issue/PR and comments (`gh issue view`, `gh pr view`) before writing code
--- formal/tla/AGENTS.md (+37/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+# TLA+ Protocol Models
+
+Add a model only when a bounded concurrency question can change a design or
+preserve a regression that cheaper tests cannot establish.
+
+## Model contract
+
+- Label each configuration as current, target, or intentionally unsafe. Model
+  or isolate current failure behavior before a repair; a target remains a
+  proposal until mapped production tests pass.
+- Keep independently durable stores, queues, transactions, and clocks distinct
+  unless production makes them atomic. State fairness and availability
+  assumptions; never infer liveness from a safety-only run.
+- For each design-critical safety claim, include an unsafe configuration that
+  violates the exact named invariant, with bounds that admit the contested
+  trace and make critical actions reachable.
+
+Each model README records its question, owner, bounds, assumptions and
+exclusions, configuration status, invariants, commands and expected results,
+action/state-to-production mapping, and review triggers. Every production
+writer of modeled state must map to an action or be explicitly out of scope.
+
+Translate relevant counterexamples into deterministic behavior tests using
+explicit barriers, not sleeps. A target is implemented only when mapped
+contract tests pass; check database locking or serialization against
+PostgreSQL. Keep the model and its test oracle independent of production code.
+
+## CI and lifecycle
+
+- Fix the JDK distribution and major version in CI and document the matching
+  local major. Pin and checksum the TLA+ tool release. Run targets as
+  expected-green and verify each unsafe configuration's exact exit and named
+  invariant. Do not commit tool JARs or TLC metadata.
+- Keep a new check advisory until its owner accepts the scope, invariants,
+  runtime, and diagnostics.
+- Remove an unowned, unmappable, or obsolete model and its dedicated CI;
+  preserve useful production regressions.

title: docs: document Backoff Limit and PREFECT_FLOW_RUN_EXECUTE_SIGTERM_BEHAVIOR in the Kubernetes guide
body:
this PR adds a **Backoff Limit** entry to the "Configure work pool options" list in the Kubernetes how-to guide (`docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployment_infra/kubernetes.mdx`), after **Finished Job TTL** to match the base job template order.

The entry documents behavior that was not in the docs before:

- With `backoffLimit=0` (default), the worker injects `PREFECT_FLOW_RUN_EXECUTE_SIGTERM_BEHAVIOR=reschedule` into the pod, so a `SIGTERM` (eviction, node drain, spot reclaim) reschedules the run in a new pod.
- The accepted values `reschedule`, `relinquish`, and `crash` (any other value), and what each does on `SIGTERM`.
- How to opt out: set the variable in **Environment Variables** (the worker only injects when unset); deployments can override through `job_variables`.
- `OOMKilled` does not reach the `SIGTERM` handler, so the run ends `Crashed` regardless.
- With `backoffLimit>0`, the worker forces `relinquish`.

Version note: the ticket said `reschedule` injection began in prefect-kubernetes 0.6.x, but `git tag --contains` for #17412 shows it shipped in prefect-kubernetes 0.5.9, so the doc says 0.5.9. Opt-out (#19223) is 0.6.6 and `relinquish` (#22622) is Prefect 3.8.1 / prefect-kubernetes 0.7.12, both confirmed the same way.

Source: `_configure_eviction_handling` in `src/integrations/prefect-kubernetes/prefect_kubernetes/worker.py` and `_termination_intent` in `src/prefect/cli/flow_run.py`.

 Set to 60 so completed flow runs are cleaned up after a minute.
 
+**Backoff Limit**
+
+Number of times Kubernetes retries a job after its pod is terminated. Defaults to 0.
+
+When set to 0, Kubernetes does not retry the job. Instead, the worker sets
+`PREFECT_FLOW_RUN_EXECUTE_SIGTERM_BEHAVIOR=reschedule` in the pod's environment, so a
+flow run whose pod receives a `SIGTERM` (for example, from an eviction, node drain, or
+spot instance reclaim) moves to `AwaitingRetry` and starts again in a new pod.
+An abrupt termination such as `OOMKilled` never reaches the `SIGTERM` handler, so with a
+backoff limit of 0 the run ends as `Crashed` regardless of the variable's value.
+Kubernetes still retries the job when the backoff limit is greater than 0.
+
+`PREFECT_FLOW_RUN_EXECUTE_SIGTERM_BEHAVIOR` accepts the following values:
+
+| Value | Behavior on `SIGTERM` |
+| --- | --- |
+| `reschedule` | The run is rescheduled and the worker starts a new pod. |
+| `relinquish` | Prefect leaves the run state unchanged so a Kubernetes-retried pod can resume it. Requires Prefect 3.8.1 or later. |
+| `crash` (or any other value) | The run ends as `Crashed` and no new pod starts. |
+
+To keep the backoff limit at 0 but stop Prefect from rescheduling terminated runs, set
+the variable yourself in **Environment Variables**:
+
+```json
+{"PREFECT_FLOW_RUN_EXECUTE_SIGTERM_BEHAVIOR": "crash"}
+```
+
+The worker only injects its own value when the variable is unset.
+You can override this on each deployment through `job_variables`.
+
+When set to a value greater than 0, Kubernetes owns retries. The worker sets the
+variable to `relinquish` and Prefect leaves the run state unchanged so the retried pod
+can pick it up.
+
+<Note>
+The worker began injecting `reschedule` in prefect-kubernetes 0.5.9 and started
+respecting a preset `PREFECT_FLOW_RUN_EXECUTE_SIGTERM_BEHAVIOR` in prefect-kubernetes
+0.6.6. The `relinquish` value and its use when the backoff limit is greater than 0
+require Prefect 3.8.1 and prefect-kubernetes 0.7.12 or later.
+</Note>
+
 **Pod Watch Timeout Seconds**
 
 Number of seconds for pod creation to complete before timing out.

title: Do not overwrite a final flow run state with Crashed on a post-completion SIGTERM
body:
related to #23025

this PR stops the flow engine from overwriting an already-reported final state with `Crashed` when a `SIGTERM` arrives during post-completion teardown.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

On Cloud Run push work pools, the control plane deletes the execution shortly after it sees `Completed`. The resulting `SIGTERM` can land while the engine is still in its cleanup path (for example, `observe_flow_run_suspension` joining its thread). The `except TerminationSignal` branch in `initialize_run` called `handle_crash` without a check of the current state, so `Crashed` was forced over `Completed`.

Change in both `FlowRunEngine.initialize_run` and `AsyncFlowRunEngine.initialize_run`:

```
except TerminationSignal as exc:
    cancel_all_tasks()
    if intent == "cancel": handle_cancellation(exc); raise
    if intent in _SUPERVISOR_OWNED_INTENTS: raise
    if intent is not None: log unknown-intent error   # unchanged
-   handle_crash(exc); raise
+   if flow_run.state.is_final(): log debug, do not re-raise
+   else: handle_crash(exc); raise
```

This mirrors the existing `except BaseException` branch, which already ignores exceptions raised after the run reached a final state. Runner-driven `cancel` and supervisor-owned intents are not affected.

Tests: `test_termination_signal_after_user_code_finishes_does_not_crash_{sync,async}` in `tests/test_flow_engine.py`.

Linear: [OSS-8191](https://linear.app/prefect/issue/OSS-8191)
</details>

body:
Bumps [@xmldom/xmldom](https://github.com/xmldom/xmldom) from 0.8.13 to 0.8.15.
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.8.15

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: trimming trailing whitespace from an XML end tag (ETag) is now anchored so it runs in linear time instead of backtracking quadratically on a long whitespace run, preventing a ReDoS reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString. Trimmed output is byte-identical. GHSA-x4fp-j954-r2f4
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9
  • Security: XMLSerializer.serializeToString() under { requireWellFormed: true } now rejects a DocType name that is not a valid XML Name, throwing InvalidStateError — matching the sibling publicId/systemId/internalSubset checks and preventing XML injection via Doc

title: Add 2.x Docker release recovery path
body:
Updates the 2.x Docker workflow to use `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN_RW` and allows maintainers to publish images for an existing stable release tag. The recovery path checks out the immutable tag and publishes the same version, minor, and `2-latest` aliases as a normal stable release.

Disables matrix fail-fast so one image failure does not cancel the remaining variants. Normal release events and development dispatches retain their existing behavior.

### Example

```bash
gh workflow run docker-images.yaml --repo PrefectHQ/prefect --ref 2.x -f tag=2.20.26
```

For documentation changes:

For new functions or classes in the Python SDK:

+      publish_minor: ${{ steps.recovery.outputs.publish_minor }}
+      publish_2_latest: ${{ steps.recovery.outputs.publish_2_latest }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Resolve release recovery aliases
+        id: recovery
+        if: ${{ inputs.tag != '' }}
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+
+          if [[ ! "$TAG" =~ ^2\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+            echo "Release recovery requires a stable 2.x tag, got: $TAG" >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          stable_tags="$(
+            gh api --paginate \
+              "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases?per_page=100" \
+              --jq '.[] | select(.draft == false and .prerelease == false) | .tag_name' \
+            | grep -E '^2\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' \
+            | sort -V
+          )"
+
+          if ! grep -Fxq "$TAG" <<< "$stable_tags"; then
+            echo "Release recovery requires a published stable 2.x release, got: $TAG" >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          IFS=. read -r major minor _ <<< "$TAG"
+          latest_minor="$(grep -E "^${major}\\.${minor}\\.[0-9]+$" <<< "$stable_tags" | tail -n 1)"
+          latest_2x="$(tail -n 1 <<< "$stable_tags")"
+
+          [[ "$TAG" == "$latest_minor" ]] && publish_minor=true || publish_minor=false
+          [[ "$TAG" == "$latest_2x" ]] && publish_2_latest=true || publish_2_latest=false
+
+          echo "publish_minor=$publish_minor" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "publish_2_latest=$publish_2_latest" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

title: Docs: Disable logging
body: Adds a new section on disabling logs to the adv config guide
author: znicholasbrown
diff:
--- docs/v3/advanced/logging-customization.mdx (+115/-2)
@@ -1,7 +1,7 @@

-keywords: ["logging", "custom handler", "log level", "log format", "structured logging"]
+keywords: ["logging", "custom handler", "log level", "log format", "structured logging", "disable logging", "opt out", "PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_ENABLED", "send_to_api"]
 ---
 
 Prefect relies on [the standard Python implementation of logging configuration](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.config.html).
@@ -211,4 +211,117 @@ and SciPy logging statements with your flow and task run logs, use:
 `PREFECT_LOGGING_EXTRA_LOGGERS=dask,scipy`
 
 Configure this setting as an environment variable or in a profile. See
-[Settings](/v3/develop/settings-and-profiles/) for more details about how to use settings.
\ No newline at end of file
+[Settings](/v3/develop/settings-and-profiles/) for more details about how to use settings.
+
+## Disable logging
+
+Prefect prints run logs to the console and sends them to the API.
+Use the settings in this section to turn off one or both outputs.
+
+### Stop sending logs to the API
+
+Set `PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_ENABLED` to `false` to keep logs out of the API.
+This setting works with Prefect Cloud and with a self-hosted Prefect server.
+
+<CodeGroup>
+```bash Environment variable
+export PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_ENABLED=false
+```
+
+```bash Profile
+prefect config set PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_ENABLED=false
+```
+
+```toml prefect.toml
+[logging.to_api]
+enabled = false
+```
+</CodeGroup>
+
+When this setting is `false`:
+
+- Flow run logs, task run logs, Prefect Cloud worker logs, and logs from [extra loggers](#include-logs-from-other-libraries) are not sent to the API.
+- Logs still print to the console.
+- States, events, artifacts, and other run data are still sent to the API. Only log records are affected.
+
+#### Where to set it
+
+Prefect reads this setting in the process that runs your flow.
+Set it at the scope that matches how you run your flows:
+
+| Scope | How to set it |
+|---|---|
+| A local run, or a flow served with `.serve()` | An environment variable, your active profile, or a `prefect.toml` file. See [Settings and profiles](/v3/concepts/settings-and-profiles). The process that calls `.serve()` passes its settings to each flow run it starts. |
+| Every flow run started by a worker | The environment or profile of the worker process. A worker passes each setting that is explicitly set in its own configuration to every flow run it starts. |
+| Every deployment in a work pool | The `env` field in the work pool's base job template. |
+| One deployment | The `env` job variable in `prefect.yaml` or in `.deploy()`. See [Customize job variables](/v3/how-to-guides/deployments/customize-job-variables). |
+| One flow run | The `env` job variable on the custom run form in the UI, or the `--job-variable` option on the CLI. |
+
+Environment variables from these scopes are merged key by key, and the most specific scope wins.
+A flow run's `env` overrides the deployment's, the deployment's overrides the work pool's, and all of them override the worker's own settings.
+
+### Silence a logger
+
+To stop a logger from writing to the console and to the API, raise its level or disable it.
+
+To keep only `WARNING` and higher records from task runs, raise the level of the task run logger:
+
+```bash
+prefect config set PREFECT_LOGGING_LOGGERS_PREFECT_TASK_RUNS_LEVEL="WARNING"
+```
+
+To disable the flow run and task run loggers for a block of code, use `disable_run_logger`.
+Inside the block, `get_run_logger()` returns a logger that discards every record, even outside of a run.
+This is useful when you call a task's function directly in a test:
+
+```python
+from prefect import task
+from prefect.logging import disable_run_logger, get_run_logger
+
+
+@task
+def process_order(order_id: int) -> int:
+    get_run_logger().info(f"Processing order {order_id}")
+    return order_id
+
+
+with disable_run_logger():
+    assert process_order.fn(42) == 42
+```
+
+See [Test workflows](/v3/how-to-guides/workflows/test-workflows) for more testing patterns.
+
+### Keep one message out of the API
+
+To print a single log record to the console without sending it to the API, pass `send_to_api=False` in the `extra` argument of the log call:
+
+```python
+from prefect import flow
+from prefect.logging import get_run_logger
+
+
+@flow
+def sync_customers():
+    logger = get_run_logger()
+    logger.info("Starting customer sync")
+    logger.info("Local debug detail", extra={"send_to_api": False})
+
+
+sync_customers()
+```
+
+The second message prints to the console but is not sent to the API.
+
+### Silence the warning for logs outside of a run
+
+Prefect can only send a log record to the API when the record belongs to a flow run.
+If a logger that is attached to the API handler is used outside of a run, Prefect drops the record and prints a warning.
+This happens, for example, when a library listed in `PREFECT_LOGGING_EXTRA_LOGGERS` logs outside of a flow run.
+
+To turn the warning off:
+
+```bash
+prefect config set PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_WHEN_MISSING_FLOW=ignore
+```
+
+The default value is `warn`. Set the value to `error` to raise an exception instead.
--- docs/v3/how-to-guides/workflows/add-logging.mdx (+2/-0)
@@ -37,6 +37,8 @@ def logger_flow():

Any logs emitted by the logger will be associated with the flow run or task run they are emitted from and sent to the Prefect backend. Logs sent to the Prefect backend are visible in the Prefect UI.
 
+To keep logs out of the Prefect backend, see [Disable logging](/v3/advanced/logging-customization#disable-logging).

title: fix(ui-v2): keep flow run tooltip on the hovered run while moving into it
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23011

this PR makes the flow run activity bar chart tooltip stay on the run the user hovered first, so the user can move the cursor into the tooltip and click its links.

Before this change, the tooltip showed the live Recharts payload. When the cursor crossed a neighbor bar on the way to the tooltip, the tooltip changed to that run at once. When the cursor left the plot area, Recharts hid the tooltip wrapper and the card disappeared.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

New hook `useStickyHoverTarget(candidate, getKey, { switchDelay = 150, enabled = true })` in `use-sticky-hover-target.ts`:

- The first candidate is shown at once.
- A different candidate (or no candidate) is applied only after `switchDelay` ms. If the original candidate comes back before that, no switch happens. Re-renders of the same candidate do not restart the timer.
- `enabled: false` clears the target at once, with no delay and even while pinned. `FlowRunTooltip` passes `active !== false`, so when another chart in the same `FlowRunActivityBarGraphTooltipProvider` takes ownership the displaced tooltip disappears immediately and two cards are never shown.
- `pin()` / `unpin()` freeze the current target. `FlowRunTooltip` pins on `onMouseEnter` of the card and unpins on `onMouseLeave`.

`FlowRunTooltip` now renders from the sticky `target` (flow run + coordinate at the time it was adopted) instead of the live `payload`/`coordinate`. The card sets `visibility: visible` so the Recharts wrapper (which becomes `hidden` when the pointer leaves the plot area) does not hide the card while the pointer is inside it.

Tests: `use-sticky-hover-target.test.ts` covers the hook timing and pin rules. `flow-run-activity-bar-graph.test.tsx` renders the chart and drives Recharts pointer events to check that the tooltip stays on the first run while the cursor crosses a neighbor, stays while the cursor is inside the card and the link keeps its href, and that two charts never show two cards.

Browser verification: with a local server and 30 flow runs on `/dashboard`, a Playwright script hovered a bar, swept the cursor across neighbor bars into the card, and clicked the flow run link. Before the change, the card was gone (`null`) after entering it; after the change, the card stayed on the original run and the link navigated to the flow run page. Pausing on a different bar still switches the tooltip after the delay.

![tooltip pinned while the pointer is over a different bar](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..AcugA_JPuYiVWbfQDz12pyDn_Lgx27Y

title: Handle Podman missing-container responses when auto-removing containers
body:
closes #8421

This PR makes the Docker worker accept the missing-container responses that Docker-compatible APIs give when a container was auto-removed.

The Docker Engine gives a 404 (`docker.errors.NotFound`) for a container that no longer exists. Podman gives a 500 (`docker.errors.APIError`) with the explanation `container <id> does not exist in database: no such container`. The worker handled only the 404, so with `auto_remove` set, the 500 came out of `DockerWorker.run` and the flow run was not monitored to completion.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`_is_missing_container_error` in `prefect_docker/worker.py` tells if a Docker API error says that the container does not exist. It is true for `docker.errors.NotFound` and for any `APIError` whose message contains `no such container`.

The worker uses this classification at the two points in the issue:

- log retrieval in `_watch_container`, which now logs the same style of warning it already logs for a container that is marked for removal.
- `container.reload()` and `container.wait()`, which are caught in `_watch_container_safe`.

The new behavior applies only when `configuration.auto_remove` is true, because a container that disappears without `auto_remove` is not expected. All other error paths keep their current behavior:

- a 500 that is not a missing-container response comes out of `run` as before.
- a missing-container 500 comes out of `run` as before when `auto_remove` is false.
- a 404 continues to give a warning, with or without `auto_remove`.

Tests go through `DockerWorker.run` with the Docker API mocked at the client boundary. They cover the Podman 500 and the native Docker 404 at log retrieval, `reload`, and `wait`, plus the two negative controls above.

</details>

- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.

- [x] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings.

title: Do not import pandas when prefect.cache_policies is imported
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22998

`prefect.cache_policies` called `_register_stable_transforms()` at import time. That function imported pandas. Therefore every `import prefect` imported pandas if pandas was installed, and the process used approximately 45 MiB more memory.

This PR registers the stable transforms only for modules that the user imported:

```python
def _register_stable_transforms() -> None:
    if "pandas" in sys.modules:
        import pandas as pd
        STABLE_TRANSFORMS[pd.DataFrame] = ...
```

The call moved from module import to `Inputs.compute_key`. A value of type `pd.DataFrame` cannot exist before the user imports pandas, so the transform is always registered before a `DataFrame` input is hashed. The `sys.modules` check makes the import a dictionary lookup, so `compute_key` stays cheap.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- `test_importing_module_does_not_import_optional_dependencies` imports `prefect.cache_policies` in a subprocess and asserts that pandas is not in `sys.modules`.
- `test_key_registers_transforms_for_already_imported_modules` puts a stub pandas module in `sys.modules` and asserts that the `DataFrame` transform makes the cache key independent of column order.

Both tests fail without the change.
</details>

- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed. Behavior of cache keys does not change, so documentation is not needed.

title: Bump snowflake-connector-python from 4.4.0 to 4.7.1
body:
Bumps [snowflake-connector-python](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-python) from 4.4.0 to 4.7.1.
Release notes

Sourced from snowflake-connector-python's releases.

4.7.1

  • v4.7.1(Jul 15,2026)
    • Added support for Python 3.14t (free-threaded).
      • Note: Python 3.14t CI testing excludes win_arm64 (no cryptography wheels available) and mitmproxy proxy tests on all platforms (transitive dependencies aioquic/pylsqpack lack free-threaded-compatible wheels).
    • Improved verification of TLS connections (SNOW-3675579).
    • Fixed python-connector.log not rotating on Windows, and every record being logged twice, when easy logging is enabled via config.toml (SNOW-3680325).
      • Note: As part of this fix, easy logging no longer calls logging.basicConfig() and therefore no longer configures the root logger. python-connector.log now captures only the snowflake.connector, botocore, and boto3.
    • Improved URL validation reliability by replacing the hand-rolled regex in is_valid_url() with urllib.parse.urlparse (SNOW-3392651).
    • Fixed OAuth infinite loop when tokens expire by ensuring reauthenticate() calls _request_tokens() directly instead of looping through prepare(). Token cache is now read exactly once per connection, and _store_tokens() preserves macOS Keychain ACL by never calling remove(). The async OAuth reauthenticate() now runs the synchronous OAuth flow on a worker thread instead of blocking the event loop.
    • Fixed OAuth scope handling for Snowflake custom OAuth: when refresh tokens are enabled, the connector no longer appends the OIDC offline_access scope for token endpoints on *.snowflakecomputing.com or *.snowflakecomputing.cn, which caused invalid_scope errors. Snowflake custom OAuth expects refresh_token in scope instead. External IdP behavior is unchanged.
    • Fixed input validation for scale metadata in Arrow result set processing for TIME, TIMESTAMP_NTZ, TIMESTAMP_LTZ, and TIMESTAMP_TZ columns (SNOW-3388299).

title: fix(prefect-dbt) Route source freshness logs to enclosing task
body:
<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://docs.prefect.io/contribute/index
-->

<!-- Include an overview of the proposed changes here -->
<!-- Whether or not AI tools helped draft this PR, you are responsible for understanding the change, keeping it scoped, validating it locally, and explaining the approach. -->
<!-- Maintainers may close PRs that appear low-effort, likely AI-generated, and substantially far from the expected implementation. -->

### Checklist
<!-- These boxes may be checked after opening the pull request. -->

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
  - If no issue exists and your change is not a small fix, please [create an issue](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/new/choose) first.
- [x] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.
- [x] If this pull request removes docs files, it includes redirect settings in `mint.json`.
- [x] If this pull request adds functions or classes, it includes helpful docstrings.

closes #22990

When `PrefectDbtRunner.invoke(['source', 'freshness', ...])` is called inside a Prefect task, logs from source node events were routed to the **flow run** instead of the enclosing task.

Root cause:

`_process_logging_sync` always called `task_state.get_task_logger(node_id, ...)` for any event with `node_info`. For `dbt build` this works fine — a Prefect task is registered per model node via `_process_node_started_sync`. But `_get_manifest_node_and_config` only looks in `manifest.nodes`, not `manifest.sources`, so source nodes during `source freshness` never get a task registered. `get_task_run_id(node_id)` returns `None`, the logger is created with `task_run_id=None`, and Prefect routes those logs to the flow.

Meanwhile events *without* `node_info` (e.g. dbt startup lines) already fell back to `hydrated_context(context) + get_run_logger()`, which correctly restores the caller's task run context — that's why `dbt deps` logs appeared in the task but `source freshness` per-source logs did not.

`PREFECT_HOME` is a single temp directory created once per test session (`pytest_sessionstart`), not reset between tests. A test that writes a file directly into it (e.g. a PID file) must delete it in fixture teardown, or later tests in the same session can see it as real state.

Non-obvious evidence: Nothing in the test files themselves states that PREFECT_HOME is session-scoped rather than per-test. Confirmed by reading tests/conftest.py:321-341 (`pytest_sessionstart` sets `TEST_PREFECT_HOME = tempfile.mkdtemp()` once as a module-level global, applied via a session-scoped settings profile). A developer reading an individual test file (e.g. tests/cli/test_start_server.py) would have no reason to suspect the directory persists and is shared across the whole suite unless they went and read conftest.py.

Cross-cutting scope: Applies to any test anywhere in the suite that writes a file directly into PREFECT_HOME (PID files, config files, ad hoc artifacts) rather than going through a fixture that already manages cleanup (e.g. tmp_path). This is a session-wide shared-mutable-state invariant, not specific to the CLI server tests that triggered this observation — the same bug class could recur in any subsystem's tests.

Why not code comment/docstring: The invariant lives in tests/conftest.py (session setup) but the risk surfaces in unrelated test files elsewhere in the tree that write into PREFECT_HOME without knowing it's shared. A comment in conftest.py wouldn't be seen by an agent writing a new test in tests/cli/ or tests/events/. AGENTS.md is the right place because it's loaded ambiently for anyone editing under tests/.

Durability: This will remain true and relevant as long as the test suite sets PREFECT_HOME once per session (a deliberate performance/isolation tradeoff, not a bug to be fixed) — unrelated to the specific PR that surfaced it. Any future test that pokes a file directly into PREFECT_HOME needs this warning.

Counter-evidence checked: Read tests/AGENTS.md in full — no existing mention of PREFECT_HOME or this invariant. Read tests/conftest.py:310-450 to confirm the directory is created once in pytest_sessionstart and torn down only at session end (line 407-408), not per-test. Checked tests/fixtures/AGENTS.md — no overlap. The existing "Database isolation" section documents an analogous but separate shared-state gotcha (DB not reset per test) using the same pattern, supporting that this is a recognized category of pitfall in this file rather than a one-off.

title: Apply jitter around the backed off interval in critical_service_loop
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22979

This PR draws the jittered sleep in `critical_service_loop` around the backed off interval (`interval * 2**backoff_count`) instead of around the base `interval`.

The two sleep branches were mutually exclusive, so any caller passing `jitter_range` lost the doubling the loop's docstring promises ("On each backoff, the interval will be doubled") — while still printing the increased interval it wasn't using. Every caller in the repo passes `jitter_range=0.3` (`workers/base.py`, `runner/_scheduled_run_poller.py`, `_internal/observers.py`), so a worker that can't reach the API kept polling at ~10s rather than easing off toward the ~1 minute the comment in `workers/base.py` intends.

<details>
<summary>Before and after</summary>

Using the reproduction from the issue (`interval=1, consecutive=3, backoff=6`, 15 consecutive failures, `anyio.sleep` recorded):

Before:

```
jitter_range=None: [1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8, 16, 16, 16, 32]
jitter_range=0.3:  [0.99, 0.94, 1.05, 1.18, 1.01, 0.78, 0.79, 0.96, 1.01, 1.03, 1.27, 0.99, 0.75, 0.84, 0.94]
```

After:

```
jitter_range=None: [1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8, 16, 16, 16, 32]
jitter_range=0.3:  [1.19, 1.27, 1.53, 1.76, 2.59, 5.17, 3.06, 3.06, 9.65, 7.41, 8.3, 18.57, 15.21, 17.57, 27.6]
```

Behavior without `jitter_range` is unchanged, and with `backoff_count == 0` the jittered interval is identical to before.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

Added `test_backoff_increases_interval_when_jittered`, which asserts each sleep falls within the jitter band of the expected doubled interval. It fails on `main` and passes with the change:

```
$ uv run pytest tests/utilities/test_services.py -q -k backoff   # without the src change
FAILED tests/utilities/test_services.py::test_backoff_increases_interval_when_jittered
1 failed, 4 passed, 16 deselected

$ uv run pytest tests/utilities/test_services.py -q -k "backoff or jitter"   # with the src change
6 passed, 15 deselected
```

The existing suite missed this because `test_jittered_sleeps_between_loops` uses a workload that never fails (so `backoff_count` stays 0) and `test_backoff_increases_interval_on_each_consecutive_group` never passes `jitter_range`.

Other runs (Windows, Python 3.12.10):

- `uv run pytest tests/utilities/test_services.py -q` — 19 passed, 2 failed. The two failures are `test_stopping_metrics_server` and `test_stopping_and_starting_from_async`; both fail identically on an unmodified `main` in this environment.
- `uv run pytest tests/workers/test_base_worker.py -q -n4` — 152 passed, 2 failed (`TestSubmit::test_basic`, `TestSubmit::test_basic_uses_execution_launcher_override`), both also failing on unmodified `main` here.
- `uv run pytest tests/runner/test__scheduled_run_poller.py tests/utilities/test_math.py -q` — 44 passed.
- `uv run ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the two changed files — no new findings (the pre-existing `UP035`/`UP045`/`SIM117`/`ASYNC210` re

title: Fix two flaky tests found in Unit tests on main
body:
Both tests failed in https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/33271162813 (commit a8e3039).

### `TestPrestartCheck::test_choose_when_multiple_profiles_have_same_api_url`

`TestBackgroundServer::test_start_port_in_use_by_background_server` writes a fake PID (`99999`) into `$PREFECT_HOME/server.pid` and never removes it. `PREFECT_HOME` is one temporary directory for the whole session, so any later test in the same worker sees a server that does not exist: `prefect server start --background` fails with "A server is already running in the background" (exit code 1), and the `stop_server` fixture prints "Cleaning up stale PID file." instead of "Server stopped!". With `--dist worksteal` the order changes per run, so the failure is intermittent.

The fake PID file now comes from a `stale_pid_file` fixture that deletes it after the test. `test_stop_stale_pid_file` uses the same fixture.

Reproduced before the fix:

```
uv run pytest -p no:randomly \
  "tests/cli/test_start_server.py::TestBackgroundServer::test_start_port_in_use_by_background_server" \
  "tests/cli/test_start_server.py::TestPrestartCheck::test_choose_when_multiple_profiles_have_same_api_url"
```

### `test_periodic_evaluation_continues_event_if_it_raises`

The test started `evaluate_periodically(0.01s)`, slept `0.1s`, and asserted more than one evaluation. On a loaded runner the loop only ran once in that window, so `await_count` was 1. The mock now sets an `asyncio.Event` on the second evaluation and the test waits for that event instead of a fixed sleep.

title: Make the test storage_document_id fixture and block data encryption deterministic
body:
This PR makes two test-infrastructure changes that remove setup errors in the server test jobs.

**1. The `storage_document_id` fixture writes through the test database session.**

The fixture saved a `LocalFileSystem` block through `prefect_client`, so the hosted API server subprocess wrote the block type, the block schema, and the block document in its own transactions. The test session then referenced those rows. When another test process cleared the database between the write and the read, setup failed with `Block type <id> not found` (404) and with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` while the `deployment` fixture inserted its row. The fixture now registers the block type and the block schema and creates the block document with the server models in the test session, so the deployment and the document it references are written by the same connection. This also keeps server tests free of the full client fixture, as `tests/AGENTS.md` requires.

**2. The tests use a fixed server encryption key.**

Block document data is encrypted with a Fernet key. Without `PREFECT_SERVER_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in the environment, each process generates a key and keeps it in the `configuration` table, and caches it in memory. The database clearing removes that row, so a process that later reads the key generates a different one. The test process and the hosted API server subprocess then encrypt and decrypt with different keys, and any read of the block document fails with `cryptography.fernet.InvalidToken` and a 500 response. A fixed key in the pytest environment makes both processes agree, independently of the database clearing.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

The second failure mode is reproducible: a test that starts the hosted server and writes a block document, then a `clear_db` test, then a test that creates a deployment with `storage_document_id`. With the fixed key the sequence passes; without it the deployment request fails with a 500 caused by `InvalidToken`.

Also run locally: `tests/client/test_prefect_client.py` (251 passed), `tests/blocks` and `tests/server/orchestration/api/test_block_documents.py` (only pre-existing failures that need a local Redis), and repeated parallel runs of `tests/server/services/test_cancellation_cleanup.py` and `tests/server/models/test_work_queues.py`.

</details>

title: Deduplicate Kubernetes observer state checks and diagnosis logs for unchanged Pending pods
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22964

This PR stops the Kubernetes observer from repeating flow run state checks and diagnosis logs when a pod stays in the `Pending` phase.

Kubernetes sends many watch events for a pod that does not change. Before this change, each event caused a new `read_flow_run` call, a new `propose_state` call, and a possible duplicate flow run log. This PR makes these operations occur one time for each unchanged condition:

- The observer deduplicates diagnoses by normalized cause. For `Unschedulable` diagnoses, it normalizes only complete, recognized Kubernetes scheduler formats. Supported filter counts and reason ordering, the Kubernetes v1.35 NodeDeclaredFeatures requirement list, and default-preemption summaries are canonicalized while general post-filter text remains exact. Unknown or malformed scheduler output uses the exact original detail, so upstream format changes can produce an extra log instead of suppressing a meaningfully changed diagnosis.
- One lifecycle-state owner retains each pod's completed state check and last diagnosis key together. Completed checks are cleared when a pod leaves `Pending`, diagnosis keys are cleared on recovery, and empty records are removed. Deletion and shutdown release the whole record. A periodic, paginated Kubernetes listing also releases state for pods whose deletion event was missed, but only after the full watched namespace and label scope is listed successfully. Live pods and UIDs observed concurrently with reconciliation remain retained.
- The observer records a completed flow run state check for each pod while the pod stays in the `Pending` phase. Transient failures, timeouts, and rejected proposals are not retained, so the observer retries them on the next event.
- The observer inspects the state that `propose_state()` returns. It records the check as completed only when the returned state is `InfrastructurePending` or is running, final, paused, or cancelling. Any other replacement state, such as a `Scheduled` state after a rejected proposal, is retried on the next event.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- `diagnostics.py`: adds `InfrastructureDiagnosis._dedupe_key()`. Recognized `Unschedulable*` scheduler messages use a namespaced normalized key; unfamiliar or malformed messages use a namespaced exact key. The parser requires the expected scheduler scaffold, fully consumes counted reason histograms, and accepts only the Kubernetes reason shapes covered by the observer's scheduler-message corpus. It tags scheduler stages, preserves arbitrary post-filter text, validates nested default-preemption summaries independently, and sorts NodeDeclaredFeatures requirements only when that complete reason matches. All other diagnosis categories remain exact.
- `observer.py`:
  - `_PodLifecycleStates` owns one record per relevant pod UID, containing the completed Pending-state check and last successfully handed-off diagnosis key.
  - Lifecycle obs

+def _split_default_preemption(post_filter: str) -> tuple[str | None, str] | None:
+    """Separate a default-preemption summary from earlier post-filter output."""
+    prefix = f"{_DEFAULT_PREEMPTION_PREFIX} "
+    if post_filter.startswith(prefix):
+        general_post_filter = None
+        preemption_detail = post_filter.removeprefix(prefix)
+    else:
+        marker = f", {_DEFAULT_PREEMPTION_PREFIX} "
+        marker_index = post_filter.find(marker)
+        if marker_index <= 0:
+            return None
+        if post_filter.find(marker, marker_index + len(marker)) != -1:
+            return None
+        general_post_filter = post_filter[:marker_index]
+        preemption_detail = post_filter[marker_index + len(marker) :]

+    return general_post_filter, preemption_detail
+
+
+def _normalize_post_filter(post_filter: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]] | None:
+    """Preserve post-filter output, normalizing default-preemption summaries."""
+    preemption = _split_default_preemption(post_filter)
+    if preemption is None:
+        if _DEFAULT_PREEMPTION_PREFIX in post_filter:
+            return None
+        return [("postfilter", post_filter)]
+
+    general_post_filter, preemption_detail = preemption
+    parsed_preemption = _parse_scheduler_message(preemption_detail)
+    if not parsed_preemption or any(
+        section != "filter" for section, _ in parsed_preemption
+    ):

+    normalized = []
+    if general_post_filter:
+        normalized.append(("postfilter", general_post_filter))

+        (f"postfilter/preemption/{section}", reason)
+        for section, reason in parsed_preemption
+    )
+    return normalized
+
+
+def _parse_scheduler_message(message: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]] | None:
+    """Parse one complete, recognized Kubernetes scheduler message."""
+    node_summary = _NODE_SUMMARY_PATTERN.match(message)
+    if node_summary is None:
+        return None
+
+    remainder = message[node_summary.end() :]
+    if not remainder:

+    if not remainder.startswith(" ") or remainder.startswith("  "):

+    payload = remainder.removeprefix(" ")

+        if not payload.startswith(f"{_DEFAULT_PREEMPTION_PREFIX} "):
+            return None
+        return _normalize_post_filter(payload)
+
+    if ". " in payload:
+        first_section, post_filter = payload.split(". ", 1)
+        if not post_filter:
+            return None
+    elif payload.endswith("."):
+        first_section = payload.removesuffix(".")
+        post_filter = None
+    else:
+        return None
+
+    if not first_section:
+        return None
+
+    normalized: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
+    if first_section[0].isdigit():
+        for part in _REASON_BOUNDARY_PATTERN.split(first_section):
+            counted_reason = _COUNTED_REASON_PATTERN.fullmatch(part)
+            if counted_reason is None:
+                return None
+            reason = _normalize_scheduler_reason(counted_reason.group("reason"))
+            if reason is None:
+                return None
+            normalized.append(("filter", reason))
+    elif _PREFILTER_PATTERN.fullmatch(first_section):
+        normalized.append(("prefilter", first_section))
+    else:
+        return None
+
+    if post_filter is not None:
+        normalized_post_filter = _normalize_post_filter(post_filter)
+        if normalized_post_filter is None:
+            return None
+        normalized.extend(normalized_post_filter)
+    return normalized
+
+
+def _scheduler_dedupe_key(detail: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:

+

title: Fix the four pyright errors that fail static analysis on main
body:
The `Type Checks` job fails on `main` ([run 33094495447](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/33094495447/job/98595728553)) because #22827 made the CI pyright check analyze the source tree again. This PR makes `uv run pyright -p pyrightconfig-ci.json --level error` report 0 errors again.

One error is a real defect; the other three are type-level only:

- `runner/_workspace_runtime_bootstrap.py`: `_run_sync` did `import anyio` and then used `anyio.to_thread.run_sync`. `anyio` declares a module-level `__getattr__` that returns `type[BrokenWorkerInterpreter]`, so pyright resolved `anyio.to_thread` through that fallback. The import is now `import anyio.to_thread`, which also makes the submodule import explicit at runtime.
- `runner/_workspace_supervisor.py`: the saved-handler dict was typed `dict[int, signal.Handlers]`, but `signal.getsignal` returns a callable, an `int`, a `signal.Handlers`, or `None`. A `_SignalHandler` type alias now holds that union.
- `runner/_workspace_supervisor.py`: `# pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]` on the `_workspace_command` import from the sibling private module.
- `_internal/attempt_control.py`: `# pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryIsInstance]` on the runtime disposition guard, which stays because receipts are also built from wire data.

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

- `uv run pyright -p pyrightconfig-ci.json --level error` → `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations`
- `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check` are clean on the changed files
- `uv run pytest tests/runner/test__workspace_starter.py tests/runner/test__workspace_supervisor.py` → 19 passed

title: Make prefect_test_harness settings visible in isolated asyncio test cases
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/15818

This PR makes `prefect_test_harness` expose its settings as the process-global settings context while the harness is active, and restore the prior global context when the harness exits.

`unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase` copies the current `contextvars` context when the test case is constructed, which happens during collection. A session-scoped fixture enters `prefect_test_harness` after collection, so the copied context has no `SettingsContext`. Test methods run in that copied context, `SettingsContext.get()` falls back to the import-time `GLOBAL_SETTINGS_CONTEXT`, and `get_client()` fails with "No Prefect API URL provided".

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- `prefect.context._temporary_global_settings_context` is a new internal context manager. It replaces `GLOBAL_SETTINGS_CONTEXT` and restores the prior value on exit.
- `prefect_test_harness` enters it last on its `ExitStack`, with the settings context that holds the harness database and API URL settings plus any settings the caller applied around the harness. Because it is entered last, it unwinds first, before the temporary settings.
- Contexts that hold their own `SettingsContext` keep it, so normal context isolation does not change. Only contexts without a settings context, which already read the process-global fallback, see the harness settings.

Tests cover the reported pattern with an `IsolatedAsyncioTestCase` that is constructed in an empty context, restoration of the global context after the harness exits, and restoration of the enclosing harness settings for nested harnesses.

</details>

closes #22954

title: Cache Redis messaging URL lookup
body:
closes #22951

this PR caches the Redis messaging URL used by `cluster_key_prefix`, avoiding expensive settings construction for every event.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Rebuilding `RedisMessagingSettings` accounted for roughly 80% of publish-path CPU per event. Caching the URL lookup removes nearly all of that overhead, cutting overall publish CPU per event by about 80%. This improves publish throughput by nearly 5x and trigger throughput by about 1.6x.

The cache is refreshed when Redis clients are cleared and isolated between tests.

The full `prefect-redis` suite and applicable pre-commit hooks pass. No documentation changes are needed because public behavior is unchanged.

This PR adds the release notes for `3.8.4` and refreshes the generated API reference docs.

The notes come from `just prepare-release 3.8.4`. Then this PR does the cleanup:

## Missing coverage recommendations

The following new features have no documentation yet and may need new pages or sections:

Missing documentation coverage — recommendations only (no new pages created)

This PR (Fix ProcessWorker auto-uv after pull steps, #22857) is almost entirely an
internal refactor of `src/prefect/runner/` private modules (prefixed with `_`):
- New POSIX/Windows process termination scope abstraction (`ProcessTerminationScope`),
  including a genuinely new capability: Windows Job Object-based process-group-equivalent
  kill-on-close semantics (previously only POSIX had real process-group isolation).
- A new out-of-process "workspace supervisor" (`_workspace_supervisor.py`) and bootstrap
  entrypoint (`_workspace_runtime_bootstrap.py`) that prepares the workspace (running pull
  steps) and launches the engine/hooks as a child, replacing the old in-process
  `resolve_workspace_in_subprocess` flow.
- `on_cancellation`/`on_crashed` hooks for workspace-resolved runs now execute via a new
  `WorkspaceHookRunner` subprocess rather than in-process, using a `Protocol`
  (`FlowRunHookRunner`) shared with `HookRunner`.

None of these are public API — no recommendation to document them directly.

One existing doc paragraph was stale and has been fixed in this pass:
- `docs/v3/how-to-guides/deployments/store-flow-code.mdx` ("Python project dependencies
  in custom images" section) said process workers use "the flow run's working directory"
  as the project root. After this fix, process workers detect the project root using the
  same workspace resolution as other execution paths, which runs *after* deployment pull
  steps complete — this was the actual bug being fixed (previously a `pyproject.toml`
  added by a pull step, e.g. `git_clone`, wouldn't be found). Updated the paragraph to
  describe pull-step-aware detection.

No new page is warranted for this change — it's a bug fix restoring already-documented
behavior (the auto-`uv run` launcher described in that same section) to work correctly
with pull steps, not a new user-facing feature.

title: Suggest existing deployment tags in the V2 deployments filter
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22938

The tags filter on the V2 deployments page was a plain text input. Users had to type each tag from memory. The V1 UI shows the tags that exist. This PR gives the V2 filter a combobox that suggests the tags of the existing deployments, and that also accepts new tags that you type.

The tag combobox already existed in `FlowRunTagsSelect`. This PR moves that interaction into a shared `TagsSelect` component in `components/ui`, then uses it for both the flow run filter and the new `DeploymentTagsSelect`.

### Changes

- `components/ui/tags-select`: new presentational combobox. The caller gives the suggestions. It keeps the behavior of the flow run filter: search, select a suggestion, add a tag with `Enter` or with a trailing comma, remove the last tag with `Backspace`, remove one tag, and clear all tags.
- `components/deployments/deployment-tags-select.tsx`: gets the suggestions from `POST /deployments/filter` with `useQuery`, then makes the list of tags unique and sorts it.
- `components/flow-runs/flow-run-tags-select.tsx`: keeps its query, but shows `TagsSelect`.
- `components/deployments/data-table`: shows `DeploymentTagsSelect` in place of `TagsInput`. The selected tags go to the same column filter, so the URL state of the route does not change.

- The suggestion query asks for a maximum of 200 deployments. This keeps the request small. If a tag is not in that set, you can still type it.

title: Prevent revocation of live filesystem concurrency leases
body:
closes #22935

This PR prevents stale filesystem expiration-index entries from causing live concurrency leases to be revoked. Index updates now use Prefect's existing file lock across server processes, and expiration scans verify candidates against the authoritative lease file before reporting them.

<details>
<summary>Implementation and tests</summary>

- Serializes index updates, removals, and batched repairs with `FileLock`, releasing it on errors and cancellation. A repair rewrites an entry only while it still holds the value the scan read, so a renewal that lands during the scan is never undone, whether it lengthened or shortened the lease, and an entry removed during the scan is not recreated.
- Rechecks expiration before repossession and updates the memory backend's stored expiration on renewal so that check works across built-in backends.
- Gives revocation tasks a per-lease Docket key to suppress duplicate scheduling while a task is queued or running.
- Replaces timing-based concurrency tests with controlled process interleavings for creation, renewal, and revocation. The concurrent-creation regression fails on the previous implementation with two lease files but only one index entry.
- Makes the existing stale-expiry-scan regression pass and updates the formal-model mapping. The model remains valid because filesystem locking does not combine lease storage with SQL accounting; the target claim protocol remains unimplemented.

`uv run pytest tests/server/concurrency tests/server/services/test_repossessor.py -x -q`: **74 passed, 1 xfailed** on Python 3.14 with SQLite. The expected failure covers the preexisting duplicate-reaper accounting race. The repository's pinned pre-commit checks pass for the changed files.

Two preexisting limitations stay open. Renewal can still race with revocation after the repossessor's expiration check, while database work is in progress. And because `renew_lease` writes the lease file and the index separately, a renewal that shortens a lease can leave the index later than the lease file, which delays reclamation until the index deadline passes; the scan does not read lease files for entries that the index reports as live. Closing either one requires a separate protocol change that coordinates both writes, and lease removal with SQL slot accounting.

</details>

title: docs: add new Prefect Managed outbound IPs
body:
Prefect Managed infrastructure now uses six possible outbound IP addresses. The docs list only three, so firewall allowlists based on the docs can reject runs scheduled in the new availability zones.

This adds the three new addresses and tells readers to allowlist the full set because the address may vary between flow runs.

Related infrastructure change: [PrefectHQ/platform#12350](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/platform/pull/12350)

Validation: `vale v3/how-to-guides/deployment_infra/managed.mdx`

title: fix(e2e): re-verify work pool state after navigation in empty-state test
body:
this PR fixes a flaky E2E test that failed on `main`: [UI v2 E2E Tests run 32777297433](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/32777297433) (commit 465bb66).

**Root cause**: The test `Work Pools List Page › Empty state when no work pools exist` does one API check before navigation. It skips the test if work pools exist. Tests run with `fullyParallel: true` and 2 workers in CI. A parallel test can create a work pool in the time between the API check and the page render. The page then shows the work pool list, not the empty state. The assertion for the empty-state heading fails.

**Fix**: Add a second API check after the page loads. Skip the test if work pools appeared from a parallel worker. This is the same pattern that `e2e/artifacts/artifacts.spec.ts` uses, and the pattern that `e2e/AGENTS.md` recommends ("Re-verify global state after navigation").

<details>

Verified locally with a Prefect server on `localhost:4200`:
- The test passes when it runs alone with an empty database.
- The test skips (does not fail) when parallel tests in the same file create work pools (3 consecutive full-file runs with `--workers=2`: 8 passed, 1 skipped each time).
- `npm run check` and `npm run lint` show no errors.

</details>

title: docs: point ui-v2 AGENTS.md at seconds-native duration formatter
body:
Automated AGENTS.md update triggered by commit cd45b58343715d8d198a9f5047c51c3351ac2eca.

This PR was generated by Claude Code analyzing the diff from the latest push to main and updating any stale AGENTS.md files.

<details>
<summary>Why this belongs in AGENTS.md</summary>

<pre>
Path: ui-v2/AGENTS.md

Proposed text: Updated the existing "Duration fields" bullet under API Integration from:
"...`humanizeDuration` and similar JS libraries expect milliseconds — always multiply by 1000 before passing to them"
to:
"...Prefer `secondsToApproximateString`/`secondsToString` from `@/utils/seconds` for display — they take raw seconds directly. `humanizeDuration` and similar JS libraries expect milliseconds instead, so multiply by 1000 before passing to them"

Non-obvious evidence: The prior bullet was a blanket instruction to multiply seconds by 1000 before formatting durations, which is now actively wrong guidance for the preferred path. The diff (commit cd45b58, "Fix readable run durations in the V2 UI") migrated four call sites (flow-runs-accordion via flow-run-duration.tsx, task-run-details.tsx, run-card.tsx) off `humanizeDuration` and onto `secondsToApproximateString`/`secondsToString`, which take raw seconds and must NOT be multiplied by 1000. A future agent following the old AGENTS.md bullet verbatim when adding a new duration display would re-introduce the exact inconsistency this PR fixed (mixing millisecond-multiplied humanizeDuration calls with the new seconds-native helpers), since the codebase still has other unmigrated `humanizeDuration` call sites (activity-chart/popover.tsx, flow-runs-scatter-plot.tsx, task-runs-list-item.tsx, schedule-badge, flow-run-section.tsx, get-schedule-title.ts) that make the old advice look complete when read in isolation.

Cross-cutting scope: Duration formatting is used across multiple unrelated component families (dashboard flow-run accordion, flow-run cards, task-run details, generic run cards), all of which read the same `estimated_run_time`/`total_run_time` seconds fields from the API. This is a repo-wide display convention, not a detail of one component's control flow.

Why not code comment/docstring: The risk isn't in any single function's implementation — `secondsToApproximateString` and `secondsToString` are already documented with JSDoc examples. The risk is a future agent choosing the wrong utility (`humanizeDuration` + ×1000) for a *new* duration display because that's what the root AGENTS.md currently prescribes as the only pattern. No single file's comments can prevent that misdirection; it has to be corrected where the convention is asserted.

Durability: This is a lasting API/display contract (seconds-in, formatted-string-out) that will keep applying to any future component showing run/task durations, well after this specific PR is forgotten. It's not tied to the specific bug or test changes in the diff.

Counter-evidence checke

title: chore(deps): Update astral-sh/setup-uv action to v10
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [astral-sh/setup-uv](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv) | action | major | `v9.0.0` → `v10.0.1` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/setup-uv (astral-sh/setup-uv)</summary>

### [`v10.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v10.0.1): 🌈 Tolerate transient manifest timeouts

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v10.0.0...v10.0.1)

##### Changes

Thank you [@​arguile-](https://redirect.github.com/arguile-) for making this action more resilient.

##### 🐛 Bug fixes

- Tolerate transient manifest timeouts [@​arguile-](https://redirect.github.com/arguile-) ([#​1016](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/1016))

##### 🧰 Maintenance

- chore: update known checksums for 0.12.4 @​[github-actions\[bot\]](https://redirect.github.com/apps/github-actions) ([#​1017](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/1017))

##### 📚 Documentation

- docs: update version references to v10.0.0 @​[github-actions\[bot\]](https://redirect.github.com/apps/github-actions) ([#​1014](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/1014))

### [`v10.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v10.0.0): 🌈 Disable automatic caching for sensitive events and new QOL features

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v9.0.0...v10.0.0)

##### Changes

Another breaking release, directly after v9.0.0 but we think the added security justifies that.

##### Extra security by default

If you use the default `enable-cache: auto` this will now **DISABLE THE CACHE** to protect against cache poisoning for the following events:

- `pull_request_target`
- `workflow_run`
- `release`

You can read the full reasoning in [#​984](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/984)

##### `version: latest-known`

```yaml
- name: Install the latest version of uv known to setup-uv
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.0
  with:
    version: "latest-known"
```

This will now install the latest version with a checksum that is known by this action. The [known `uv` checksums](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/4f6036f71cec78afb113b323f220c9185d983c12/src/download/checksum/known-checksums.ts) are automatically updated but will take a release of this action to take effect. You won't be always using the latest & greatest but you will have an extra level of security.

##### Read python version from `.tool-versions`

```yaml
- name: Install uv based on the version defined in .tool-versions and also set python
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.0
  with:
    version-file: "pyproject.toml"
```

Will now also set the python version if it is defined in `.tool-versions`. You can read the details [in the docs](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/main/docs/advanced-versi

title: chore(ci): Follow CodeQL v4 releases
body:
this PR switches CodeQL analysis from exact patch tags to the floating `v4` tag. CodeQL will stay current within v4 without a Renovate PR for each release.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

GitHub recommends using the major-version tag for advanced CodeQL setups. Renovate preserves the shortest compatible GitHub Actions tag, so the next workflow version change should be `v4` to `v5`.

This intentionally trades exact patch reproducibility and the repository's seven-day Renovate cooldown for automatic updates within the supported CodeQL major version.

No tests are needed because this only changes the action version selector. Focused pre-commit checks pass for `.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml`.
</details>

- [ ] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"

@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+---
+title: Prefect scope of support
+sidebarTitle: Scope of support
+description: Understand what Prefect support covers and where to find help for requests outside its scope.
+keywords: ["service boundaries", "shared responsibility", "customer assistance", "ticket eligibility"]
+---
+
+This page describes what Prefect's Solutions Engineering team can help with, what falls outside its scope,
+and where to go for everything else. Clear boundaries help resolve issues quickly. When a request is out of
+scope, the team directs you to the appropriate resource.
+
+## Support entitlement
+
+| Offering | Support tiers | Channel |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Prefect Open Source, FastMCP, and the Prefect Cloud free tier | — | [Prefect Community Slack](https://prefect.io/slack), [GitHub](https://github.com/PrefectHQ), [Prefect documentation](/v3/get-started/index), and [FastMCP documentation](https://gofastmcp.com/) |
+| Prefect Cloud | Starter / Team | Ticketed support with no response-time commitments |
+| Prefect Cloud | Bronze / Silver / Gold | Email; support portal at Silver and above; response times and coverage hours per your agreement |
+| Prefect Horizon | Bronze / Silver | Email; support portal at Silver; response times per your agreement |
+| Prefect Customer-Managed | Priority / Premier | [support@prefect.io](mailto:support@prefect.io); see the [Customer-Managed scope of support](https://docs-customer-managed.prefect.io/support/) |
+
+Bug reports and feature requests are always welcome on GitHub, on any plan.
+
+## In scope
+
+Solutions Engineering assists with:
+
+- **Prefect product usage and configuration.** Documented features of Prefect Cloud, Prefect Open Source,
+  Horizon, and FastMCP, including work pools, deployments, automations, role-based access control (RBAC),
+  and single sign-on (SSO).
+- **Troubleshooting Prefect-owned components.** The Cloud control plane, Prefect server, workers, SDK,
+  Horizon platform, FastMCP framework, and Prefect-maintained integrations.
+- **Best-practice guidance.** Documented patterns for flows, deployments, work pools, and upgrade paths;
+  the recommended way to configure Prefect for your execution environment; and technical onboarding and
+  implementation planning sessions when included in your support tier.
+- **Defect escalation.** Reproducing suspected bugs, triaging reported security vulnerabilities, and
+  escalating confirmed defects and critical incidents to Engineering.
+- **Billing and account administration.**
+
+Issues on unsupported versions may require an upgrade as the first troubleshooting step.
+
+## Out of scope
+
+Solutions Engineering does not provide assistance with:
+
+- **Your infrastructure.** Prefect helps you configure Prefect to communicate with your infrastructure,
+  but does not provision, debug, or tune it. This includes compute platforms such as Kubernetes, Amazon ECS,
+  serverless platforms, and virtual machines; networking such as virtual private clouds, firewall rules, proxies,
+  DNS, and TLS; and cloud accounts and identity and access management (IAM). Self-hosting customers on every
+  plan remain responsible for operating their Prefect environment, including its database, scaling, and
+  backups.
+- **Your code.** Writing, debugging, or optimizing your flows, tasks, business logic, or custom MCP servers
+  and tools. Errors raised by your code or its dependencies are the author's responsibility; Prefect reports
+  those errors.
+- **Third-party software.** Tools, libraries, databases, and services not owned by Prefect;
+  community-maintained integrations; and modified or forked builds of Prefect software.
+- **Deep architectural consultation.** Best-practice guidance is in scope, but deep consultative engagements
+  or guidance on sizing, design, or the operational architecture of your infrastructure are not. A question
+  that can be answered from documented patterns in a support ticket or onboarding session is support. A
+  request that requires discovery of your environment, a design deliverable, or ongoing ownership of an
+  outcome is consultation and project work.
+
+For design, implementation, migrations, security work, training, or end-user support, Prefect Customer
+Engineering may be able to help. Contact your account team or customer success manager.
+
+## Shared responsibility model
+
+| Component | Prefect Open Source | Prefect Cloud (hybrid work pools) | Prefect Cloud ([push work pools](/v3/how-to-guides/deployment_infra/serverless)) | Prefect Cloud ([managed work pools](/v3/how-to-guides/deployment_infra/managed)) | Prefect Horizon | FastMCP |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Control plane / API | You | **Prefect** | **Prefect** | **Prefect** | **Prefect** | — |
+| Execution infrastructure | You | You | You | **Prefect** | **Prefect** | You |
+| Your code (flows, tasks, and MCP tools) | You | You | You | You | You | You |
+| Networking from your environment | You | You | You | You | You | You |
+| Third-party services | You | You | You | You | You | You |
+
+Support covers the cells marked **Prefect**, plus the documented behavior of Prefect software running in
+your environment.
+
+Prefect Customer-Managed deployments follow a dedicated boundary. See the
+[Customer-Managed scope of support](https://docs-customer-managed.prefect.io/support/).
+
+## Get help effectively
+
+Tickets that include the expected and actual behavior, exact errors and logs, product versions, execution
+environment, and steps already tried are resolved faster.
+
+For requests outside the support scope, use the following resources:
+
+| Issue | Where to go |
+| --- | --- |
+| Your infrastructure or third-party tools | The vendor's documentation and support, or your platform team |
+| Code patterns and approaches | [Prefect Community Slack](https://prefect.io/slack) |
+| Design and implementation work | Prefect Customer Engineering, through your account team |
+| Bug reports and feature requests | [Prefect](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect) and [FastMCP](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp) on GitHub |
+
+For common product issues, see [How to troubleshoot Prefect Cloud](/v3/how-to-guides/cloud/troubleshoot-cloud).
+
+<Note>
+This page describes Prefect's standard support offering. Contractual terms, including service-level
+agreements, are defined in your agreement with Prefect and control if there is a conflict.
+</Note>
