title: fix(prefect-slack): include subject in SlackWebhook notifications
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/13120

`prefect_slack.SlackWebhook.notify`/`notify_async` accept a `subject` and silently drop it — the Slack incoming-webhook payload only has a `text` field, and both paths sent `text=body`. Since Prefect's core apprise-backed `SlackWebhook` renders the subject as a header above the body, this prepends it here too:

```python
text = f"{subject}\n{body}" if subject else body
```

Omitted, `None`, and empty subjects keep the existing body-only payload, so no existing notification changes shape.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.
  - No docs change: the documented signature already advertised `subject`; this makes the behavior match.

<details>
<summary>Validation</summary>

- Reproduced on clean `main` with a script driving both paths against a mocked webhook client: each sent `text='Hello, world!'` with `subject="Nice Subject Line Here"` supplied.
- New parametrized sync + async tests (`subject`, `None`, `""`) fail before the fix (2 failed) and pass after.
- `uv run pytest` in `src/integrations/prefect-slack`: 41 passed, 5 skipped.
- `uv run ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.

</details>

+    @staticmethod

         """
         client = self.get_client()
-        response = await client.send(text=body)
+        response = await client.send(text=self._format_text(body, subject))

title: ci: drop unused global mintlify-scrape install from static analysis
body:
this PR removes the `Install mintlify-scrape` step from the `pre-commit-checks` job in `.github/workflows/static-analysis.yaml` and adds `timeout-minutes: 10` to that job.

The step ran an unpinned `npm install -g @mintlify/scraping`, which now enters an npm peer-resolution loop and can burn the six-hour GitHub Actions job limit. title: Merge Prefect secrets into existing ECS container secrets
body:
Related to #13035 but I think that issue is no longer relevant?

The ECS worker wipes out any `secrets` defined in the task definition when it injects the Prefect API key / auth string secret ARNs. This PR makes it update rather than overwrite.

`_prepare_task_definition` built a fresh list containing only Prefect's secrets and then did `container["secrets"] = secrets`, so a user whose task definition template declared, say, a database password secret lost it as soon as `prefect_api_key_secret_arn` was set on the work pool.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Now the Prefect secrets are merged into whatever is already on the container:

- Existing secrets are preserved, in their original order.
- A configured ARN takes precedence over a task-definition secret of the same name (`PREFECT_API_KEY` / `PREFECT_API_AUTH_STRING`), so the work pool setting still wins and no duplicate entry is produced — ECS rejects duplicate secret names.
- Behaviour is unchanged when neither secret ARN is configured.

The environment-variable removal for `PREFECT_API_KEY` / `PREFECT_API_AUTH_STRING` is unchanged, just deduplicated into one loop.

Three tests added to `tests/workers/test_ecs_worker.py`:

- `test_secrets_in_task_definition_are_preserved` — user secrets survive alongside both Prefect secrets
- `test_secrets_in_task_definition_are_preserved_without_prefect_secrets` — no regression when no ARNs are configured
- `test_secret_arn_replaces_matching_secret_in_task_definition` — configured ARN overrides a same-named task-definition secret without duplicating it

`uv run --project ./src/integrations/prefect-aws pytest src/integrations/prefect-aws/tests/workers/test_ecs_worker.py` → 123 passed.

Note: the new tests use `construct_configuration_with_job_template` rather than `construct_configuration(task_definition=...)`, because `task_definition` is not a field on `ECSVariables` and is silently dropped by that helper. A couple of existing tests pass `task_definition=` to `construct_configuration` and are therefore not exercising what they appear to; not touched here.

</details>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: peterbygrave

--- src/integrations/prefect-aws/prefect_aws/workers/ecs_worker.py (+21/-19)

-        secrets = []
+        prefect_secrets: dict[str, str] = {}
         if configuration.prefect_api_key_secret_arn:
-            secrets.append(
-                {
-                    "name": "PREFECT_API_KEY",
-                    "valueFrom": configuration.prefect_api_key_secret_arn,
-                }
+            prefect_secrets["PREFECT_API_KEY"] = (
+                configuration.prefect_api_key_secret_arn
             )
-            # Remove the PREFECT_API_KEY from the environment variables
-            for item in tuple(container.get("environment", [])):
-                if item["name"] == "PREFECT_API_KEY":
-                    container["environment"].remove(item)  # type: ignore
-
         if configuration.prefect_api_auth_string_secret_arn:
-            secrets.append(
-                {
-                    "name": "PREFECT_API_AUTH_STRING",
-                    "valueFrom": configuration.prefect_api_auth_string_secret_arn,
-                }
+            prefect_secrets["PREFECT_API_AUTH_STRING"] = (
+                configuration.prefect_api_auth_string_secret_arn
             )
-            # Remove the PREFECT_API_AUTH_STRING from the environment variables
+
+        if prefect_secrets:
+            # Remove the corresponding environment variables because the values will
+            # be provided via secrets instead
             for item in tuple(container.get("environment", [])):
-                if item["name"] == "PREFECT_API_AUTH_STRING":
+                if item["name"] in prefect_secrets:
                     container["environment"].remove(item)  # type: ignore
 
-        if secrets:
+            # Merge into any secrets already defined on the container rather than
+            # replacing them. A secret configured here takes precedence over one of
+            # the same name in the task definition.
+            secrets = list(container.get("secrets") or [])
+            for secret in secrets:
+                if secret.get("name") in prefect_secrets:
+                    secret["valueFrom"] = prefect_secrets.pop(secret["name"])
+            secrets.extend(
+                {"name": name, "valueFrom": value_from}
+                for name, value_from in prefect_secrets.items()
+            )

         return task_definition

Release notes

Sourced from ruff's releases.

0.16.0

Release Notes

Released on 2026-07-23.

Check out the blog post for a migration guide and overview of the changes!

Breaking changes

  • Ruff now enables a much larger set of rules by default (413, up from 59). See the blog post for more details and the new Default Rules page for a full listing of the enabled rules. Note that this is primarily an expansion, but 18 of the more opinionated pycodestyle (E) and pyflakes (F) rules have been removed from the default set: E401, E402, E701, E702, E703, E711, E712, E713, E714, E721, E731, E741, E742, E743, F403, F405, F406, and F722.

  • Ruff can now format Python code blocks in Markdown files and will do this by default. See the documentation for more details.

  • Ruff now supports ruff: ignore comments at the ends of lines, like noqa comments, or on the line preceding a diagnostic. For example, these both suppress an unused-import (F401) diagnostic:

    import math  # ruff: ignore[F401]

    ruff: ignore[F401]
    

    import os

  • Fixes are now shown in check and format --check output:

    ❯ ruff format --check .
unformatted: File would be reformatted
 --> try.md:1:1

  - import   math
2 + import math
3 | ```
  |

  • format --check now supports the same output formats as the linter, including the github and gitlab outputs for rendering annotations in CI:

::error title=ruff (unformatted),file=try.md,line=2,col=8,endLine=2,endColumn=10::try.md:2:8: unformatted: File would be reformatted

title: docs: document Submitting and InfrastructurePending states
body:
This PR documents the two `PENDING` sub-states added in #20964 on the states concept page: `Submitting` (proposed by `BaseWorker`/runner while submitting to infrastructure) and `InfrastructurePending` (proposed by observers, e.g. `prefect-kubernetes` for a pod still in `Pending` phase).

Adds them to the state table, the state transitions table (`Pending -> Submitting -> InfrastructurePending -> Running`, matching `PreventPendingTransitions` which allows PENDING→PENDING when the name changes), and the mermaid diagram.

Docs-only.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes `<link to issue>`"
- [x] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.

title: Reject unknown fields for FlowRunFilter and its nested criteria
body:
closes #13057

This PR makes `FlowRunFilter` and every nested flow-run criterion model reject unknown fields instead of silently ignoring them. Previously, a typo such as `FlowRunFilter(type=state_filter)` (the public field is `state`) was dropped by the base model's `extra="ignore"` config, producing an empty filter that broadens `read_flow_runs` results rather than narrowing them.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`PrefectBaseModel` uses `extra="ignore"`, so extra keys passed to any filter are silently discarded. For flow-run filters this is a footgun: an empty filter matches everything, so a mistyped criterion quietly returns unrelated runs.

A private strict base is introduced in `client/schemas/filters.py`:

```python
class _FlowRunFilterBaseModel(PrefectBaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
```

`FlowRunFilter` and all of its nested criterion models (`FlowRunFilterId`, `FlowRunFilterState`, `FlowRunFilterStateType`, `FlowRunFilterStateName`, time filters, etc.) now inherit from this base, so both top-level and nested unknown fields raise a `ValidationError` (`type == "extra_forbidden"`).

The change is deliberately scoped: `FlowFilter`, `TaskRunFilter`, other filter families, and `FilterSet` keep their existing permissive `extra="ignore"` behavior, so adding new server-side fields to those payloads remains non-breaking.

Regression tests in `tests/client/schemas/test_filters.py` cover top-level and nested unknown fields, confirm known fields still validate, and assert the other filter families stay permissive.

</details>

title: Clear stale expiration entries when a repossessed lease is missing
body:
`test_sync_concurrency_with_leases` and `test_async_concurrency_with_leases` both timed out on main (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/30457912336). Server access logs show each test's child process renewed its lease a handful of times and then stopped (i.e. `process.kill()` ran), so both tests were stuck in their last loop:

```python
while (await lease_storage.read_expired_lease_ids()) != []:
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
```

Two problems, both fixed here:

1. **The repossessor can leak a permanently-expired index entry.** `revoke_expired_lease` returns early when `read_lease()` comes back `None`, without touching the storage's expiration index. The filesystem lease storage keeps expirations in a shared `expirations.json` that every process read-modify-writes without locking, so a concurrent write can resurrect an entry for a lease whose file was already deleted. That entry then expires and stays expired forever: `monitor_expired_leases` reschedules it every second and `read_expired_lease_ids()` never returns `[]`. The missing-lease branch now revokes the lease, which clears the orphaned index entry.

2. **The tests waited on global state.** `read_expired_lease_ids()` covers every lease in the shared storage, including leases owned by the other tests running in parallel. Each test now waits for its own lease to disappear (`read_lease(active_lease.id) is None`).

Validated by running `integration-tests/test_concurrency_leases.py -n 4` 20x against a local server (all green), plus `tests/server/services/test_repossessor.py`.

title: fix(ui-v2): render ANSI color escape codes in flow run logs
body:
closes #22652

The `ui-v2` run-logs component rendered log messages as a plain text node, so ANSI SGR escape sequences (from `rich`, `colorama`, captured colorized subprocess output, etc.) showed up literally in the row (`<ESC>[32mgreen<ESC>[0m ...`). The legacy Vue UI tokenizes those codes into colored text; this restores parity.

### What changed

- New `ui-v2/src/lib/ansi.tsx` with `renderLogMessage(message)`, which walks the message splitting on the SGR regex, tracks active SGR classes, and maps codes to Tailwind classes (ported from the V1 `ansiToTailwind` map, including `dark:` variants). Unrecognized codes are stripped rather than printed.
- `linkify(text, className?)` gained an optional `className` so ANSI color classes carry through to the linkified text/anchor segments without an extra wrapper element.
- `run-logs` now renders `renderLogMessage(log.message)` instead of `linkify(log.message)`.
- Added a `RunLogs (ANSI colors)` Storybook story.

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

- Hardcoded color classes (e.g. `text-green-600 dark:text-green-500`) trigger the repo's `no-restricted-syntax` lint *warnings* (not errors). They're intentional here: ANSI colors map to specific terminal colors with no semantic-token equivalent, and each carries an explicit `dark:` variant for dark mode — matching the V1 implementation.
- The escape regex is built from `String.fromCharCode(27)` to avoid embedding a control character in source (and the `no-control-regex` lint rule) without an eslint-disable comment.

</details>

title: Confirm the exact suspension transition reported by a suspension event
body:
Fixes the flaky `integration-tests/test_flow_suspension.py::test_external_suspension_stops_flow_run_at_next_task_boundary` (timeout on main: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/30364502074).

### Root cause

`FlowRunSuspendingObserver` read the flow run once when a `prefect.flow-run.Suspended` event arrived and silently dropped the notification if that read did not report a suspended state. The event can be delivered before the state change that produced it is readable, and the subscription never sends that event again, so the suspension is lost and the run keeps executing.

State-change events use the validated state ID as the event ID, allowing the observer to confirm the exact transition instead of reading mutable current state.

### Change

- A private `_SuspensionWatch` owns one flow run's server-derived replay checkpoint, exact-state confirmation, deduplication, retry, and task cleanup.
- Events received during the initial state read wait behind an initialization gate, then reconcile against that server checkpoint; replay filtering no longer depends on the worker clock.
- `PrefectClient.read_flow_run_state(state_id)` uses the existing exact-state endpoint instead of repeatedly fetching and scanning the run's complete state history. Sync and async clients are both covered.
- Confirmation remains asynchronous and retries until the watch closes. After 30 seconds it warns once and backs off, so a temporarily unreadable state is not permanently lost or polled aggressively.
- The websocket-primary and polling-fallback design is unchanged.

The producer-side ordering issue is tracked separately in #22654.

Tests: `tests/test_observers.py` (37 passed); targeted async and sync client state-read tests (3 passed); Ruff and source Pyright checks passed.

title: fix(prefect-aws): scope pull_from_s3 listing to the requested folder
body:
closes #13025

`pull_from_s3(bucket, "my-folder")` also matched sibling folders like `my-folder-2/`, because the raw `folder` was used as the `list_objects_v2` prefix. The pull step then crashed with `ValueError: 'my-folder-2/my-flow.py' is not in the subpath of 'my-folder'`. Users had to write `folder: "my-folder/"` to work around it; now both forms behave the same.

<details>
<summary>Change</summary>

```python
prefix = f"{folder}/" if folder and not folder.endswith("/") else folder
...
paginator.paginate(Bucket=bucket, Prefix=prefix)
...
relative_path_to_current_platform(remote_key).relative_to(prefix)
```

The delimiter is appended only when `folder` is non-empty and not already delimited, so pulling from the bucket root (`folder=""`) and already-delimited input are unchanged, as is the `folder` value in the returned output.

</details>

title: fix(ui-v2): allow any float precision on schema number inputs
body:
closes PrefectHQ/prefect#19416

This PR fixes deployment edit forms blocking on high-precision float defaults in the React UI (`ui-v2`).

## Summary

* Redirected from [PrefectHQ/prefect-ui-library#3132](<https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect-ui-library/pull/3132#issuecomment-5095430941>) per @znicholasbrown — the OSS schema UI now lives in `ui-v2`, not the legacy Vue library.
* `SchemaFormInputNumber` renders `<Input type="number">` without an explicit `step`, so browsers default to `step=1` and reject values like `0.001` via HTML constraint validation — even when editing unrelated fields.
* Set `step="any"` so arbitrary float precision is accepted.

- [ ] Edit an unrelated field and save — form should submit successfully
- [ ] Confirm the float field still accepts values like `0.001` and `1.234567`

title: Keep worker startup alive when the Prefect API is unreachable
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22638

`prefect worker start` died with an unhandled `httpx.ConnectError` (exit 1) when the API was unreachable, before the worker reached its retrying service loops. Three pre-loop API calls were fatal; this PR makes the recoverable ones non-fatal.

1. **CLI paused-pool / paused-queue preflights** (`cli/_worker_utils.py`) only caught `ObjectNotFound`. They are informational, so they now also swallow `httpx.HTTPError` and report "not paused".
2. **`BaseWorker.setup()`** called `sync_with_backend()` unguarded. It now tolerates transient errors (transport errors and 5xx) and lets the `critical_service_loop` sync loop keep retrying; non-transient errors (auth/4xx, missing `PREFECT_API_URL`) still fail fast:
   ```python
   try:
       await self.sync_with_backend()
   except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
       if not _is_transient_api_error(exc):
           raise
       self._logger.warning("Unable to reach the Prefect API while starting up; ...")
   ```
   Because the work pool is unknown when that sync fails, cancellation-observer setup moved out of `setup()` into `_setup_cancellation_observer()`, called from `sync_with_backend()` — so cancellation handling starts as soon as the pool is known instead of being silently disabled for the process lifetime.
3. **`ProcessWorker.start()`** was a verbatim copy of `BaseWorker.start()` plus a redundant `await worker.sync_with_backend()` ("wait for an initial heartbeat"), left over from #14611 when worker-side cancellation was removed. `setup()` already syncs, so the override is deleted rather than patched.

Worker type discovery (`--type` omitted) genuinely needs the API, so it still exits — but with an actionable message pointing at `--type` instead of a traceback.

<details>
<summary>Manual verification</summary>

```shell
PREFECT_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1/api PREFECT_CLIENT_MAX_RETRIES=0 \
  prefect worker start --pool unavailable-api-repro --type process --run-once
# before: httpx.ConnectError traceback, exit 1
# after:  "Unable to reach the Prefect API while starting up; the worker will keep
#          attempting to connect", worker starts, exit 0
```

Recovery: started a worker against a down `127.0.0.1:4299`, then started the server. The worker logged the warning, stayed alive, created `recovery-test` on reconnect, and reported `WorkerStatus.ONLINE`.
</details>

title: fix(futures): make PrefectFutureList.result timeout message reachable
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22633

This PR makes `PrefectFutureList.result(timeout=...)` actually raise `TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for all futures to complete within N seconds`, by branching on exception type instead of message text.

The guard in `result()` tested for the non-f-string literal `"Scope timed out after {timeout} second(s)."`, so it never matched; and even with the missing `f`, `as_completed` had already relabelled every `TimeoutError` as `"N (of M) futures unfinished"`. Both are fixed by giving Prefect's own waiting a private `TimeoutError` subclass:

```python
class _WaitTimeoutError(TimeoutError): ...

# as_completed
with timeout_context(timeout, timeout_exc_type=_WaitTimeoutError): ...
except _WaitTimeoutError:
    raise _WaitTimeoutError("%d (of %d) futures unfinished" % ...)  # message unchanged

# PrefectFutureList.result
except _WaitTimeoutError as exc:
    raise TimeoutError(f"Timed out waiting for all futures to complete within {timeout} seconds") from exc
```

A `TimeoutError` raised inside a task is not a `_WaitTimeoutError`, so it propagates unchanged by construction — narrowing the `except` in `as_completed` also stops such an error from being mislabelled "futures unfinished". `as_completed`'s own message and public exception type (`_WaitTimeoutError` is a `TimeoutError`) are unchanged.

`result()` also drops its own `timeout_context`: it armed a second enforcer for the same deadline as the one `as_completed` already arms. In worker threads both fire at once, and the loser injects a `CancelledError` after its scope has exited, so it surfaces in unrelated later work (it was wedging xdist workers on this PR's CI).

That leaves the retrieval half of the deadline, [raised in review](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/22634#issuecomment-5094626416), which `result()` now handles itself:

```python
for future in as_completed(list(self), timeout=timeout):
    ...
    if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline:
        raise TimeoutError(timeout_message)
except CancelledError as exc:
    if deadline is None or time.monotonic() < deadline:
        raise
    raise TimeoutError(timeout_message) from exc
```

A cancel scope delivers cancellation into the frame the supervised thread is *currently* in; while `as_completed` is suspended at its `yield` that frame is `result()`, so `timeout_context` cannot convert it and a bare `CancelledError` — a `BaseException`, so it also walks past a caller's `except Exception` — escaped. `result()` claims it only once its own deadline has passed, leaving cancellation from an enclosing scope such as a flow run timeout to propagate. And where no scope arms at all (`cancel_sync_after` returns a `NullCancelScope` on win32) the explicit deadline check still enforces the timeout.

<summary>Verification</summary>

Repro from the issue now prints `TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for all futures to complete within 0.5 seconds`. `test_result_timeou

Bumps [ray](https://github.com/ray-project/ray) from 2.55.0 to 2.56.0.
Release notes

Sourced from ray's releases.

Ray-2.56.0

Highlights

  • Ray Data Stability: In this Ray release, we've added a variety of stability improvements, including running multiple datasets in a cluster, adding automatic batch size selection to CPU-based map-batches, and default logical memory configuration to prevent OOMs. We've also tightened iter_batches stability by reducing hidden buffering and shutting down the executor when consumers exit early (#63660, #63682, #62949). This reduces object-store spilling for common training workloads
  • Ray Serve: We re-architected Ray Serve LLM by decoupling request handling from token streaming response path (#62667, #62680, #62668, #62669, #63167), resulting in significant LLM serving performance improvements. We've also introduced new routing policies such as session-sticky routing via consistent hashing with ConsistentHashRouter (#62905, #63096, #62906) and CapacityQueueRouter (#62323) which is beneficial for supply-constrained workloads.
  • Ray Core: We've added GPU-domain-aware placement groups using label locality (#61442, #61614, #62487, #62533). This enables placement groups to pack bundles onto nodes that share a ray.io/gpu-domain label instead of only packing at the single-node level. We've also added initial Kubernetes in-place pod resizing support for Autoscaler v2 (#55961, #62369,

title: Relinquish evicted flow runs to infrastructure retry
body:
closes #22620

### The bug
On a Kubernetes pool with `backoffLimit > 0`, an evicted pod gets a SIGTERM and the engine marks the run `Crashed`. Kubernetes then starts a fresh pod for the same Job and runs the flow again, so a run that was already terminal comes back and runs twice.

### The fix
Implements @desertaxle's suggestion. `prefect flow-run execute` now takes a termination behavior (`crash`, `reschedule` or `relinquish`, via `PREFECT_FLOW_RUN_EXECUTE_SIGTERM_BEHAVIOR`) and delivers it to the engine as an intent over the control channel that already connects them. On SIGTERM the supervisor signals the intent, proposes `AwaitingRetry` only for `reschedule`, and exits non-zero for `relinquish` so Kubernetes counts the attempt and retries.

The engine dispatches on intent alone and no longer reads Kubernetes-specific config. Ordinary cancellations carry no intent and still crash the run. The worker sets `relinquish` whenever `backoffLimit` is not 0, keeping Prefect's reschedule and Kubernetes Job retries mutually exclusive.

### Worth noting
- The engine child now starts in its own process group on POSIX, matching Windows, so an external SIGTERM cannot reach it before the supervisor signals intent.
- An unset `backoffLimit` now relinquishes rather than crashes. Kubernetes defaults it to 6, so retries really do happen.
- The second commit de-flakes two tests that fail on `main` regardless of this change.

title: fix(concurrency): release leases granted to callers that were cancelled mid-acquire
body:
Fixes the flake in `tests/concurrency/test_context.py::test_concurrency_context_releases_slots_async` seen on main (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/30122656936): the limit was left with `active_slots == 1` after the context exited.

### Root cause

`aacquire_concurrency_slots_with_lease` awaits `asyncio.wrap_future(future)` on a `concurrent.futures.Future` that the acquisition service fulfills from the global event loop thread. When the caller's cancel scope fires while the increment request is in flight, `wrap_future` cancels that future. The request then succeeds server-side, but:

```python
future.set_result(response)   # InvalidStateError: CANCELLED
```

so the service crashed handling the item and the lease id was never returned to anyone — the caller couldn't record it on `ConcurrencyContext.cleanup_lease_ids`, so the slots stayed occupied until lease expiry. Exactly this sequence is in the CI log (`increment-with-lease` 200 at `39.998`, `InvalidStateError` at `40.000`, read of `active_slots == 1` at `40.001`).

### Fix

Two orderings of "caller goes away while the acquisition is in flight" are now both handled:

1. **Cancelled before the result is delivered.** `FutureQueueService._handle` transitions the future to running before delivering the result, which closes the cancel/set race atomically and lets the service see that the caller gave up:

   ```python
   if future.set_running_or_notify_cancel():
       future.set_result(response)
   else:
       await self._discard(response)   # no-op by default
   ```

   `ConcurrencySlotAcquisitionWithLeaseService._discard` releases the orphaned lease.

2. **Cancelled after the future is running**, where `wrap_future` cancels only its wrapper and the delivered result is dropped: `aacquire_concurrency_slots_with_lease` catches `CancelledError` and attaches a done callback that releases the lease if one ends up being granted (off the cancelled caller, on a short-lived daemon thread).

Regression tests added for both paths; each fails on main and passes here.

- [x] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.

+    reaches a caller that is already gone.
+    """
+    response = Response(
+        200,
+        json={
+            "lease_id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
+            "limits": [
+                MinimalConcurrencyLimitResponse(
+                    id=uuid.uuid4(), name="test", limit=1
+                ).model_dump(mode="json")
+            ],
+        },
+    )

+    future: Future[Response] = Future()
+    sent = asyncio.Event()
+
+    def send(item: tuple[object, ...]) -> Future[Response]:
+        sent.set()
+        return future
+
+    service = mock.MagicMock(spec=ConcurrencySlotAcquisitionWithLeaseService)
+    service.send = send

+    with mock.patch.object(
+        ConcurrencySlotAcquisitionWithLeaseService, "instance", return_value=service
+    ):

+            aacquire_concurrency_slots_with_lease(names=["test"], slots=1)
+        )
+        # Once the request has been sent, the caller is suspended on the future.
+        await sent.wait()
+
+        assert future.set_running_or_notify_cancel()
+        acquire.cancel()
+        with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+            await acquire
+
+        future.set_result(response)
+
+    service.release_orphaned_lease.assert_called_once_with(response)
+
+

+async def test_does_not_release_when_no_lease_was_granted(outcome: str):
+    """Only a granted lease needs releasing; a dead acquisition has nothing to clean up."""

+
+    def send(item: tuple[object, ...]) -> Future[Response]:

title: Make ConcurrencyContext exit cleanup best-effort
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22615

`ConcurrencyContext.__exit__` released its fallback `cleanup_lease_ids` in a bare loop, so a single transient failure stranded every remaining lease (holding slots until TTL expiry) and skipped `super().__exit__()`. This PR guards each release individually, logs a warning on failure, and always runs the context teardown. The same fix is applied to the v1 context's `cleanup_slots` loop, which had the identical pattern.

```python
for lease_id in self.cleanup_lease_ids:
    try:
        client.release_concurrency_slots_with_lease(lease_id=lease_id)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to release concurrency lease %s during cleanup", lease_id, exc_info=True)
```

The outer `get_client(...)` block is also guarded so client construction/teardown errors don't bypass `super().__exit__()`.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

`tests/concurrency/test_context.py` and `tests/concurrency/v1/test_context.py` each get a test where the first cleanup release raises: the remaining IDs are still attempted and the context var is reset.
</details>

title: docs: note event/log subscriber reconnect logic must stay in sync
body:
Automated AGENTS.md update triggered by commit 4692edad00c9342144eb7e29e8115bf64c655801.

This PR was generated by Claude Code analyzing the diff from the latest push to main and updating any stale AGENTS.md files.

<details>
<summary>Why this belongs in AGENTS.md</summary>

<pre>
Path: src/prefect/AGENTS.md

Proposed text: Added bullet under "Key Contracts":
> - **Event and log WebSocket subscribers are parallel implementations.** `events/clients.py::PrefectEventSubscriber` and `logging/clients.py::PrefectLogsSubscriber` duplicate the same reconnect/backoff/dedup logic, including the `reconnect_on_clean_close` option (used by `events/subscribers.py::FlowRunSubscriber` so a clean disconnect doesn't hide a terminal event). Mirror any reconnection-behavior change across both.

Non-obvious evidence: The diff adds an identical `reconnect_on_clean_close` parameter, with near line-for-line identical retry/backoff/`ConnectionClosedOK` handling, to both `PrefectEventSubscriber.__anext__` (src/prefect/events/clients.py) and `PrefectLogsSubscriber.__anext__` (src/prefect/logging/clients.py) in the same commit. Nothing in either file's docstring, comments, or the events/logging AGENTS.md files states that these two classes are meant to be kept behaviorally in lockstep — a contributor fixing a reconnect bug in one is unlikely to discover the sibling copy in the other subsystem's directory without already knowing to look.

Cross-cutting scope: Applies to the whole reconnection/backoff contract shared by the events and logging subscriber subsystems (spans two sibling directories: `events/` and `logging/`), not just this diff's single new parameter.

Why not code comment/docstring: The duplication is invisible from either file in isolation — a comment in one file wouldn't inform an editor working in the other. This is the same class of cross-file "must stay in lockstep" invariant already captured for the sync/async engines one bullet above it, so it belongs at the same shared-ancestor level (src/prefect/AGENTS.md), not duplicated into both `events/AGENTS.md` and `logging/AGENTS.md`.

Durability: The parallel-implementation relationship (and the risk of the two drifting) persists regardless of this specific PR; it will matter for any future change to reconnect/backoff/dedup behavior in either subscriber, long after `reconnect_on_clean_close` itself is old news.

Counter-evidence checked: Read src/prefect/events/AGENTS.md and src/prefect/logging/AGENTS.md in full — neither mentions the other subscriber implementation or a lockstep requirement. Grepped both files and src/prefect/AGENTS.md for "PrefectLogsSubscriber", "PrefectEventSubscriber", and "reconnect_on_clean_close" — no existing mentions. Confirmed via the diff that both `__anext__` implementations were edited with matching logic in the same commit, supporting that they are intentionally parallel rather than coincidentally simila

Explicitly timezone-aware stdlib calls such as `datetime.now(ZoneInfo("UTC"))` are allowed when needed to preserve timezone information. title: Fix as_completed timeout enforcement in worker threads and on Windows
body:
Fixes an issue where `as_completed(..., timeout=...)` could hang indefinitely in worker threads and on Windows because `Event.wait()` was unbounded and Prefect's synchronous timeout context cannot interrupt blocking waits in those environments (Windows uses `NullCancelScope`; worker threads use `WatcherThreadCancelScope`).

### Changes

- In `src/prefect/futures.py::as_completed`, establish a monotonic deadline when iteration begins and wait on `finished_event` using only the remaining time.
- Preserve the existing outer `TimeoutError` handler so the exception message remains `N (of M) futures unfinished`.
- Keep `timeout=None` behavior unchanged (unbounded `Event.wait()`).
- Add `test_as_completed_with_timeout_from_worker_thread` in `tests/test_futures.py`: consumes `as_completed` from a real worker thread with a never-completing `PrefectConcurrentFuture`, verifies the worker raises `TimeoutError` with the expected message, and self-cleans if the implementation is broken.
- Update `.github/workflows/windows-tests.yaml`:
  - Add `src/prefect/futures.py` and `tests/test_futures.py` to the `pull_request.paths` filter.
  - Add a separate step that runs the complete `tests/test_futures.py` module on Windows alongside the existing `@pytest.mark.windows` step.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request adds or changes functionality and includes tests.
- [x] This pull request changes internal timeout behavior but does not change public signatures or exception types; no documentation update needed.

title: fix(ui-v2): guard deployment Parameters tab against missing schema properties
body:
closes #22603

This PR fixes the deployment Parameters tab crashing with `Something went wrong / Cannot convert undefined or null to object` in the Updated (React) UI.

### Bug 1 — Parameters tab crash (fixed)

`useDeploymentParametersToTable` only guarded that `parameter_openapi_schema` was truthy, then called `Object.keys(schema.properties)`. When the schema object exists but has no `properties` key (or `properties` is `null`), `Object.keys(undefined | null)` throws exactly `Cannot convert undefined or null to object`. Because the throw happens during render, the route's `errorComponent` replaces the **entire** deployment page (header + all tabs + toolbars) with the error card — matching the reporter's screenshot.

Fix (`deployment-parameters-table.tsx`):

```ts
const parameterOpenApiSchema = deployment.parameter_openapi_schema
  ?.properties as Record<string, ParameterOpenApiSchema> | undefined;
if (!parameterOpenApiSchema) {
  return [];
}
const parameters = (deployment.parameters ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
```

Now a parameter-less deployment renders the empty ("No results.") table instead of throwing. Also defaults `parameters` to `{}` to avoid a latent `parameters[key]` crash when `properties` exist but `parameters` is null.

<details>
<summary>Bug 2 — filtered-empty state hiding the filter/search box</summary>

Could **not** be reproduced on `main`. All filterable tabs on the deployment detail page keep their toolbar/search visible when a filter returns zero results:

- **Runs / Upcoming tabs** (`deployment-details-runs-tab.tsx`, `deployment-details-upcoming-tab.tsx`): `FlowRunsRowCount` + `FlowRunsFilters` render unconditionally above `FlowRunsList`, which shows a "No runs found" empty state with a "Clear Filters" button.
- **Parameters tab**: the `SearchInput` renders unconditionally above the table; there's already a passing `filters no results` test asserting the search box stays and "No results." shows.

The reporter's only screenshot shows the crash, and their note "the page has to be reloaded to recover" matches the crash's page-level error boundary wiping the toolbar. The most likely explanation is that Bug 2's "search box disappears" is the downstream effect of the Bug 1 crash replacing the whole page — resolved by this fix. Left as draft in case the reporter has a distinct repro; no separate code change made since the behavior can't be reproduced.
</details>

### Checklist

- [x] References the related issue by including "closes #22603"
- [x] Adds tests: covers schema with no `properties`, `properties: null`, missing schema, and missing `parameters`
- [x] No user-facing docs needed (bug fix)

title: Add composable worker initializer to ProcessPoolTaskRunner
body:
closes #22589

Adds optional `initializer` / `initargs` constructor parameters to `ProcessPoolTaskRunner`, giving a supported way to run per-worker setup before task code executes.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

`ProcessPoolTaskRunner` hardcoded the `initializer` it passed to `ProcessPoolExecutor` (Prefect's `_initialize_process_pool_worker`, which forwards events/logs to the parent). Under `"spawn"`, workers are fresh interpreters that unpickle task payloads — triggering imports — before any task code runs, so there was nowhere to do per-worker bootstrap like adjusting `sys.path`.

The new params mirror `ProcessPoolExecutor`'s `initializer` / `initargs` but **compose** with Prefect's setup rather than replacing it: Prefect's runs first, then the user callable, so forwarding is in place when user setup runs. Threaded through `__init__`, `duplicate()`, and `__enter__`; read via `getattr` for pickle-safety. The callable and `initargs` must be picklable.

```python
runner = ProcessPoolTaskRunner(initializer=add_to_path, initargs=("/opt/my_app/libs",))
```

Additive and backward compatible.

</details>

     the parent process.
+
+    If a user `initializer` is provided, it runs after Prefect's own setup so that
+    it can rely on event/log forwarding already being in place.
     """
     if message_queue is None:
         EventsWorker.set_client_override(None)
         set_api_log_sink(None)
-        return
+    else:
+        EventsWorker.set_client_override(
+            ProcessPoolForwardingEventsClient,
+            event_queue=message_queue,

Bumps [pyasn1](https://github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1) from 0.6.3 to 0.6.4.
Release notes

Sourced from pyasn1's releases.

Release 0.6.4

This is a security release.

  • CVE-2026-59885 (GHSA-8ppf-4f7h-5ppj): Fixed quadratic time complexity in the OBJECT IDENTIFIER and RELATIVE-OID decoders. A small crafted substrate encoding many arcs could consume excessive CPU.
  • CVE-2026-59884 (GHSA-m4p7-r5rc-7g4j): Limited BER long-form tag IDs to 20 octets (140 bits). Unbounded tag IDs allowed a crafted substrate to consume excessive CPU and memory.
  • CVE-2026-59886 (GHSA-hm4w-wwcw-mr6r): Fixed excessive memory and CPU consumption in Real.__float__() for values with large base-10 exponents.
  • Pinned PyPI publish GitHub Action to an immutable commit.

All changes are noted in the CHANGELOG.

Changelog

Sourced from pyasn1's changelog.

Revision 0.6.4, released 08-07-2026

  • CVE-2026-59885 (GHSA-8ppf-4f7h-5ppj): Fixed quadratic time complexity in the OBJECT IDENTIFIER and RELATIVE-OID decoders. A small crafted substrate encoding many arcs could consume excessive CPU. Arcs are now accumulated in linear time; decoded values are unchanged (thanks for reporting, tynus2)
  • CVE-2026-59884 (GHSA-m4p7-r5rc-7g4j): Limited BER long-form tag IDs to 20 octets (140 bits), matching the OID arc limit introduced in 0.6.2. Unbounded tag IDs allowed a crafted substrate to consume excessive CPU and memory; longer tag IDs are now rejected with PyAsn1Error. Also fixed Tag and TagSet repr() failing on huge tag (thanks for reporting, mikeappsec) IDs due to the integer-to-string conversion limit (Python 3.11+)
  • CVE-2026-59886 (GHSA-hm4w-wwcw-mr6r): Fixed excessive memory and CPU consumption in Real.float() for values with large base-10 exponents. Conversion no longer materializes huge intermediate integers; values too large to represent as a Python float raise OverflowError promptly, and prettyPrint() renders them as '' as before. Also fixed base-10 mantissa normalization to use exact integer arithmetic; mantissas larger than 2**53 could previously lose precision through float division (thanks for reporting, gvozdila)

title: Expose Kubernetes pod-failure diagnosis as a matchable event label
body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22575

The `prefect-kubernetes` observer already classifies pod failures with `diagnose_k8s_pod`, but the result was only written to a flow-run log — the replicated pod events carried nothing an automation could match on to tell one failure mode from another (only `kubernetes.reason` on evictions). This is most limiting for pods that never start: an `Unschedulable` pod never heartbeats, so the zombie-flow automation can't apply, leaving only a coarse "no `Running` within N minutes" timer that can't distinguish a genuinely stuck pod from a slow-to-schedule one.

This PR exposes the diagnosis on the events as a stable, matchable label.

<details>
<summary>What changed</summary>

- **`prefect_kubernetes/diagnostics.py`**
  - Added a `DiagnosisCategory(str, Enum)` with stable string values: `ImagePullError`, `CrashLoopBackOff`, `OOMKilled`, `Evicted`, and `Unschedulable` split by cause — `Unschedulable.InsufficientResources`, `Unschedulable.NodeAffinity`, `Unschedulable.Taint`, plus a generic `Unschedulable` fallback. These values are an automation-matching contract and should stay stable.
  - Added a `category: DiagnosisCategory` field to `InfrastructureDiagnosis` and set it in every `_check_*` branch.
  - Added `_categorize_unschedulable(message)` which maps the scheduler condition message (the only place the cause appears) to a category via tolerant substring matching, falling back to generic `Unschedulable` when the cause is unknown or the message is empty.

- **`prefect_kubernetes/observer.py`**
  - In `_replicate_pod_event`, when a diagnosis is produced, add `resource["kubernetes.diagnosis"] = diagnosis.category.value` to the emitted event's resource labels — mirroring the existing `kubernetes.reason` pattern. The label is emitted whenever a diagnosis exists (not gated on `flow_run_id` the way the log is).

- **Tests**
  - `tests/test_diagnostics.py`: assert `category` on each per-category test; parametrized `Unschedulable`-by-cause coverage (insufficient resources, node affinity/selector, taint, unknown fallback).
  - `tests/test_observer.py`: assert `kubernetes.diagnosis` on the emitted event for unschedulable/OOM pods, and its absence for healthy pods.
</details>

Scoped to the `prefect-kubernetes` integration. `prefect-aws` has a parallel `InfrastructureDiagnosis`/`diagnose_ecs_task` that could get the same treatment as a follow-up, but it is out of scope here.

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22575"
- [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue.
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed.
  - The new `kubernetes.diagnosis` label is additive

+
+    These values are emitted as the `kubernetes.diagnosis` label on
+    replicated pod events, so automations can match on a specific failure
+    mode. Treat the values as a stable contract — do not rename them.
+    """

+def _categorize_unschedulable(message: str) -> DiagnosisCategory:

 ) -> InfrastructureDiagnosis | None:

+            category=DiagnosisCategory.EVICTED,

title: Preserve subprocesses after output stream errors
body:
this PR keeps subprocesses running to completion when stdout or stderr forwarding fails, restoring compatibility with AnyIO 4.14.2 and removing its temporary dependency exclusion.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

AnyIO 4.14.2 closes underlying subprocess pipe transports during cleanup. When Prefect's output consumer raises, that cleanup can terminate the flow process before it records a final state.

`run_process` now drains both pipes without forwarding their output and waits for the process to exit before re-raising the original streaming error. Cancellation continues through the existing termination path because the fallback handles only ordinary exceptions.

The dependency constraints in `pyproject.toml` and `client/pyproject.toml` now permit AnyIO 4.14.2 again, and the lockfile resolves to 4.14.2.

The regression emits one megabyte to each output stream after forcing a forwarding failure and verifies that the child still reaches completion. The focused process utility suite passes against AnyIO 4.14.2.
</details>

title: fix(tests): stabilize flaky cleanup renewal and flow-discovery log tests
body:
Two tests failed on `main` in the "Runner, Worker, Settings, Input, and CLI Tests - python:3.14" job (workflow run [29848647580](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/29848647580), commit 1144d63). Both are timing/ordering-dependent flakes, not real regressions — the triggering commit only touched pagination endpoints.

### `tests/workers/test_cleanup.py::test_executor_keeps_renewing_until_ack_resolves` — `TimeoutError`

The test built a cleanup message with only a **0.1s lease** (`lease_renewal_buffer_seconds=0.05`). On a loaded runner, more than 0.1s can elapse between message creation and when `WorkerCleanupExecutor.execute` evaluates the lease, so `execute` hits its `_lease_expired` guard and skips the message entirely — no ack and no renew is ever sent, and the test hangs on `await renew_sent.wait()` until `fail_after(1)` fires.

Reproduced deterministically by sleeping ~0.3–0.5s before scheduling `execute`: the message is skipped and the test raises `TimeoutError` (matching CI).

Fix: use a generous lease window with a buffer that still fires the first renewal immediately.

```diff
-    lease_renewal_buffer_seconds=0.05,
-    operation_result_timeout_seconds=1,
- message = _message_frame(lease_expires_at=now("UTC") + timedelta(seconds=0.1))
+    lease_renewal_buffer_seconds=5,
+    operation_result_timeout_seconds=5,
+ message = _message_frame(lease_expires_at=now("UTC") + timedelta(seconds=5))
```

The `[Ack, Renew]` ordering assertion is preserved: the ack frame is appended synchronously (the handler returns without yielding) before the ack future yields control to the renewal task.

### `tests/cli/test_prompts.py::...test_find_flow_functions_in_file_returns_empty_list_on_file_error` — `assert 'Could not open foo.py' in ''`

The message is logged at `DEBUG` on the `prefect` logger. `caplog` only captures it if the `prefect` logger's effective level is `DEBUG`. `temporary_settings({PREFECT_DEBUG_MODE: True})` only changes the *setting* (gating whether `logger.debug(...)` is called) — it does not re-run `setup_logging()`, so the actual logger level depends on ambient state left by earlier tests. When another test leaves it at `INFO`, the record is filtered and `caplog.text` is empty.

Reproduced by setting the `prefect` logger to `INFO` before the assertion → exact CI failure.

Fix: pin the level in the test.

```python
caplog.set_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="prefect")
```

### Verification

- Both root causes reproduced locally, then confirmed fixed under the same load/ordering simulation.
- `uv run pytest tests/workers/test_cleanup.py tests/cli/test_prompts.py --numprocesses auto --maxprocesses 6 --dist worksteal` → 38 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.

### Checklist

- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed. (test-only change)

title: Guard non-thread-safe TTLCache in `_read_toml_file` with a lock
body:
This PR makes the TOML file cache in `prefect.settings.sources` thread-safe.

`_read_toml_file` reads and writes a module-level `cachetools.TTLCache` (`_file_cache`) with no locking. `TTLCache` is not thread-safe: `__setitem__` calls `expire()`, which walks the cache's internal linked list. When another thread mutates the cache concurrently, that list is corrupted and `expire()` raises a spurious `KeyError` on a key that was just present.

Settings are loaded whenever a `PrefectBaseSettings` subclass is instantiated, so any path that constructs settings from multiple threads at once (e.g. a worker submitting runs) can trigger this as an intermittent `KeyError` originating from `_read_toml_file` -> `cachetools`.

Fix: guard all `_file_cache` access with a module-level `threading.Lock`.

<details>
<summary>Change</summary>

```python
_file_cache_lock = threading.Lock()

def _read_toml_file(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ...
    with _file_cache_lock:
        if value := _file_cache.get(cache_key):
            return value
    data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    with _file_cache_lock:
        _file_cache[cache_key] = data
    return data
```

The file read stays outside the lock so concurrent readers of distinct files don't serialize on I/O.
</details>

Added a regression test that hammers `_read_toml_file` from many threads. It uses a near-zero TTL (so `expire()` actually deletes links on every access) and a tiny `sys.setswitchinterval` (so the GIL hands off inside those walks); the test fails with a `KeyError` on `main` and passes with the lock.

title: Fix saved block parameters in deployments
body:
closes #13122

this PR serializes saved `Block` instances in deployment parameters as block-document references. Deployments now resolve the persisted block instead of storing an inline copy with masked secret values.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The deployment model previously passed arbitrary parameter objects through normal Pydantic JSON serialization. For secret-bearing blocks, that persisted `**********` and block metadata instead of a usable value.

This change:

- adds an opt-in reference mode to `Block` serialization without changing ordinary block dumps;
- uses that mode for `RunnerDeployment` parameters in create and update operations;
- keeps sync and async deployment paths consistent;
- rejects unsaved blocks with actionable `.save()` guidance; and
- covers nested collections and Pydantic models, API round trips, updates, runtime hydration, and sync dispatch.

Checks run:

- `uv run pytest tests/blocks/test_block_reference.py tests/runner/test_runner.py::TestRunnerDeployment tests/runner/test_runner.py::TestAsyncDispatch -q` (`97 passed`)
- focused regression tests (`4 passed`)
- Ruff check and format check for the changed files
- the original `DatabricksCredentials` reproduction against the worktree source

</details>

title: fix(server/api): consistent zero-limit behavior for core pagination endpoints
body:
<!--
Thanks for opening a pull request to Prefect!
If this is your first contribution, please make sure to review our contribution guidelines: https://docs.prefect.io/contribute/index
-->

`limit=0` is accepted by `LimitBody` but the `flow`, `deployment`, `flow_run`, and `task_run` `/paginate` endpoints computed `pages=(count + limit - 1) // limit`, which raised `ZeroDivisionError` and returned HTTP 500.

This change applies the existing `work_queues`/`workers` pattern:

```python
pages=(count + limit - 1) // limit if limit > 0 else 0
```

With `limit=0`:
- `results=[]`
- `count` is still the full filtered count
- `limit=0`
- `pages=0`
- `page` is the requested page (default 1)

title: Add "Copy to new run" to flow run menu in ui-v2
body:
closes #22564

The legacy Vue UI exposes a "Copy to new run" option in the flow run detail page's three-dots menu, but ui-v2 (React) did not. This restores parity.

When a flow run has a `deployment_id`, the menu now shows a "Copy to new run" item that links to the deployment's custom run page pre-populated with the run's parameters — matching the legacy behavior (`routes.deploymentFlowRunCreate(deploymentId, parameters)`).

- Added tests covering the link (correct href with encoded parameters) and its absence when the run has no deployment.

The linked issue also references OSS-6084 ("copy everything") as a follow-up enhancement; that broader scope is intentionally out of scope here.

title: Make Redis concurrency leases cluster-slot safe
body:
this PR makes Redis-backed concurrency lease storage hash-slot safe for Redis Cluster while preserving existing standalone Redis key names.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- hash-tags lease records, expiration indexes, and holder indexes under one `prefect:concurrency` Cluster slot
- makes revoke's Lua-generated holder keys use the same cluster-aware prefix
- adds exact key compatibility coverage for Cluster and standalone configurations
- adds an opt-in real Redis Cluster test covering create, read, renew, active/expired lookup, holder indexing, and revoke cleanup

This is the next incremental Cluster-support slice after #22211, #22448, and #22453. Redis Cluster client activation remains intentionally gated until the cleanup queue's multi-key transactions are made hash-slot safe.

</details>

title: docs: fix stale lease-cleanup invariant in concurrency AGENTS.md
body:
Automated AGENTS.md update triggered by commit 22aad393a32b87a24124fc5b221bcaca0d5855ca.

This PR was generated by Claude Code analyzing the diff from the latest push to main and updating any stale AGENTS.md files.

<details>
<summary>Why this belongs in AGENTS.md</summary>

<pre>
Path: src/prefect/concurrency/AGENTS.md

Proposed text: Replaced the "Cancellation during acquire or release" Pitfalls bullet with:
"Cleanup leases are recorded at acquisition, not reactively on cancellation. `ConcurrencyContext.cleanup_lease_ids` gets the lease ID the moment a lease is granted, and it's discarded again after a successful release. This closes a race where cancellation fires the instant the lease is granted — before the release call is even reached — which would otherwise leak the slot. `ConcurrencyContext.__exit__` releases any leases still in the list via a sync client; if `ConcurrencyContext` is not active, those leases are abandoned until server-side expiry."

Non-obvious evidence: The prior AGENTS.md text described the cleanup-list population as reactive — only added to `cleanup_lease_ids` when a `CancelledError` was caught around acquisition or release. The merged diff (commit 22aad39) changes this mechanism: `aacquire_concurrency_slots_with_lease` now appends the lease id to `ctx.cleanup_lease_ids` unconditionally the moment the lease is granted, and a new `_discard_cleanup_lease` helper removes it after a successful release. The old description is no longer an accurate account of how the list is populated, and this isn't obvious from a quick read of either `_asyncio.py` or `_sync.py` in isolation — you have to trace both the acquire path and the release path in both modules to see that recording is now eager, not exception-triggered.

Cross-cutting scope: This is a cross-file contract spanning `_asyncio.py` and `_sync.py` (the documented sync/async lockstep invariant) and directly concerns the cleanup-on-cancellation invariant that the "Pitfalls" section exists to capture — the exact kind of undocumented-invariant/parallel-implementation risk the sync skill prioritizes.

Why not code comment/docstring: The new code already has inline comments explaining the eager-recording rationale locally in `_asyncio.py`, but AGENTS.md is the place a future agent reads before touching either the sync or async cleanup path — it needs to state the invariant as a fact about the subsystem's contract (what's guaranteed to be in `cleanup_lease_ids` and when), not just the rationale for one call site.

Durability: The eager-record/discard-on-release mechanism is now the permanent design of lease cleanup, not a one-off fix detail — any future change to acquire/release ordering in either module must preserve it, so the guidance stays relevant long after this PR is old news.

Counter-evidence checked: Re-read the full diff in both `_asyncio.py` and `_sync.py`, the current AGENTS.md Pitfalls/Architecture sections, and con

body:
closes #22553

This PR wraps the `propose_state(Crashed)` call in the Kubernetes observer's `_mark_flow_run_as_crashed` handler in a `try/except (Abort, Exception)`, mirroring the existing pod `InfrastructurePending` path in the same file.

Under multi-replica / high-concurrency bursts there is a TOCTOU race: the flow run can transition to a terminal state (`COMPLETED`/`CRASHED`) between the handler's early `is_final()` check and the later `propose_state(Crashed)` call (after the 30s reschedule-wait loop). The server then rejects the transition with `prefect.exceptions.Abort`, which escaped the kopf handler and caused kopf to stop the Jobs watcher for that worker process — leaving subsequent Job failures unreconciled and flow runs stuck Running in the UI.

<details>

```diff
     if not has_other_active_job:
         logger.warning(...)
-        result_state = await propose_state(
-            client=orchestration_client,
-            state=Crashed(message="No active or succeeded pods found for any job"),
-            flow_run_id=uuid.UUID(flow_run_id),
-        )
+        try:
+            result_state = await propose_state(
+                client=orchestration_client,
+                state=Crashed(message="No active or succeeded pods found for any job"),
+                flow_run_id=uuid.UUID(flow_run_id),
+            )
+        except (Abort, Exception):
+            logger.debug(f"Failed to propose Crashed for flow run {flow_run_id}", exc_info=True)
+            return
         if captured_pod_logs and result_state.is_crashed():
             _send_crashed_pod_logs(...)
```

Added `test_abort_on_crash_proposal_is_noop`: simulates the race (running run, no other active jobs, `propose_state` raises `Abort`) and asserts the handler returns without raising and does not forward crash logs.

</details>

### Checklist

- [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes #22553"
- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
- [x] If this pull request changes user-facing behavior, it updates documentation or explains why documentation is not needed. (internal reliability fix; no user-facing docs)

v1.18.1 — June 21, 2026

This release focuses on Node HTTP adapter fixes, safer AxiosError serialisation, runtime/type correctness fixes, documentation updates, and dependency maintenance.

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • AxiosError Serialisation: Made AxiosError#cause non-enumerable to prevent circular JSON serialisation failures when errors include nested causes. (#10913)
  • Node HTTP Adapter: Guarded socket.setKeepAlive for proxy agent streams, accepted path-only URLs when socketPath is configured, deferred environment proxy handling to Node, and explicitly passed maxBodyLength through to follow-redirects. (#10917, #10930, #10942, #10993)
  • Runtime and Type Correctness: Fixed several runtime crashes, type definition mismatches, and incorrect error handling paths. (#10959, #11021)
  • AxiosURLSearchParams: Switched the encoder callback to an arrow function so encoder.call(this) receives the AxiosURLSearchParams instance correctly. (#11019)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Documentation: Documented sensitive headers and status transition behaviour, prepared cleaned-up docs, added Deno install instructions, and clarified that request data is request-specific (#11007, #11010, #11023, #11025)

  • Dependencies: Bumped vite, rollup, form-data, js-yaml, and multer across the root project, docs, smoke tests, and module test workspaces. (#11011, #11012, #11013, #11014, #11015, #11016, #11017<

title: Redact API key from lazy logging args in ObfuscateApiKeyFilter
body:
Redacts the configured `PREFECT_API_KEY` from lazy logging arguments before any handler formats the record.

`ObfuscateApiKeyFilter.filter` previously only redacted `record.msg`, so calls like `logger.info("api_key=%s", api_key)` left the plaintext key in `record.args` and it could be shipped to API/Cloud logs during `APILogHandler.prepare()`.

Changes:
- Read the current API key once and apply `redact_substr` to both `record.msg` and `record.args`.
- Preserve positional tuple and mapping shapes so `LogRecord.getMessage()` continues to format correctly.

Added tests under `TestObfuscateApiKeyFilter` for:
- positional formatting: `"api_key=%s"` with `(test_api_key,)`
- mapping formatting: `"api_key=%(api_key)s"` with `({"api_key": test_api_key},)`

Validation:
- `uv run pytest tests/test_logging.py -k TestObfuscateApiKeyFilter -q` → 10 passed
- `uv run pytest tests/test_logging.py -q` → 145 passed
- `uv run ruff check src/prefect/logging/filters.py tests/test_logging.py` → All checks passed
- `uv run ruff format --check src/prefect/logging/filters.py tests/test_logging.py` → 2 files already formatted
- `git diff --check` → clean

--- src/prefect/logging/filters.py (+73/-9)
@@ -1,29 +1,90 @@
 import logging
+from collections.abc import Mapping
 from typing import Any
 
-from prefect.utilities.collections import visit_collection
 from prefect.utilities.names import obfuscate
 
 
+class _RedactedString(str):
+    """
+    A `str` subclass that stores a separate `repr` value.
+
+    This allows logging's `%r` and `%a` conversions to use a redacted
+    representation while `%s` and JSON serialization use the redacted
+    `str` value.
+    """
+
+    __slots__ = ("_repr",)
+
+    def __new__(cls, str_value: str, repr_value: str) -> "_RedactedString":
+        instance = super().__new__(cls, str_value)
+        instance._repr = repr_value
+        return instance
+
+    def __repr__(self) -> str:
+        return self._repr
+
+    def __reduce__(self) -> tuple[type, tuple[str, str]]:
+        return (type(self), (str(self), self._repr))
+
+
 def redact_substr(obj: Any, substr: str) -> Any:
     """
     Redact a string from a potentially nested object.
 
+    Standard collections (list, tuple, set, dict, and other `Mapping`
+    instances) are traversed recursively and have their string values redacted
+    while preserving shape. Non-container objects are redacted by replacing
+    their `str` and `repr` values with obfuscated versions, avoiding the
+    need to reconstruct arbitrary user objects (e.g. dataclasses with
+    `init=False` fields or Pydantic models).
+
     Args:
         obj: The object to redact the string from
         substr: The string to redact.
 
     Returns:
         Any: The object with the API key redacted.
     """
+    if isinstance(obj, str):
+        return obj.replace(substr, obfuscate(substr))
+
+    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple, set)):
+        seq = obj
+        items = [redact_substr(item, substr) for item in seq]
+        if all(item is orig for item, orig in zip(items, seq)):
+            return obj
+        # Preserve namedtuple types.
+        if hasattr(type(seq), "_make"):
+            return type(seq)._make(items)
+        return type(seq)(items)
+
+    if isinstance(obj, Mapping):
+        mapping = obj
+        items = [
+            (redact_substr(key, substr), redact_substr(value, substr))
+            for key, value in mapping.items()
+        ]
+        if all(
+            k1 is k2 and v1 is v2 for (k1, v1), (k2, v2) in zip(items, mapping.items())
+        ):
+            return obj
+        # Return a plain dict so that arbitrary Mapping types (e.g. ChainMap)
+        # can still be formatted by logging's `%` operator and serialized as
+        # JSON without reconstructing the original mapping type.
+        return dict(items)
 
-    def redact_item(item: Any) -> Any:
-        if isinstance(item, str):
-            return item.replace(substr, obfuscate(substr))
-        return item
+    # For opaque objects, redact their rendered string representations.  This
+    # handles exceptions, dataclasses, Pydantic models, and other lazy logging
+    # arguments whose `__str__` or `__repr__` may contain the secret.
+    str_value = str(obj)
+    repr_value = repr(obj)
+    redacted_str = str_value.replace(substr, obfuscate(substr))
+    redacted_repr = repr_value.replace(substr, obfuscate(substr))
+    if redacted_str is not str_value or redacted_repr is not repr_value:
+        return _RedactedString(redacted_str, redacted_repr)
 
-    redacted_obj = visit_collection(obj, visit_fn=redact_item, return_data=True)
-    return redacted_obj
+    return obj
 
 
 class ObfuscateApiKeyFilter(logging.Filter):
@@ -35,7 +96,10 @@ def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:
         # Need to import here to avoid circular imports
         from prefect.settings import PREFECT_API_KEY
 
-        if PREFECT_API_KEY:
-            record.msg = redact_substr(record.msg, PREFECT_API_KEY.value())
+        api_key = PREFECT_API_KEY.value()
+        if api_key:
+            record.msg = redact_substr(record.msg, api_key)
+            if record.args is not None:
+                record.args = redact_substr(record.args, api_key)
 
         return True

title: Keep flow run watch alive across stream disconnects
body:
closes #22549

this PR keeps flow-run watching active across recoverable event and log WebSocket disconnects and prevents non-terminal flow runs from being reported as finished.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

- Keeps clean WebSocket closure as normal iterator completion for existing event and log subscriber consumers.
- Adds an explicit lower-level `reconnect_on_clean_close` policy and enables it for `FlowRunSubscriber`, where a clean load-balancer closure should not end an active flow-run watch.
- Bounds consecutive clean-close reconnect cycles so repeated successful handshakes without delivered data cannot reconnect indefinitely.
- Retains event continuity through the existing server backfill and event-ID deduplication behavior.
- Reconnects logs as a live stream while documenting that logs emitted during a disconnect cannot be replayed because the OSS logs endpoint is live-only.
- Keeps `FlowRunSubscriber` focused on multiplexing events and logs, propagating only exhausted or non-retryable subscriber failures.
- Re-reads the flow run after streaming stops so a terminal server state wins, while a non-terminal state produces `FlowRunWatchError` instead of false success.
- Adds regression coverage for default clean-close completion, opt-in reconnects, bounded clean-close retries, failure propagation, final-state reconciliation, and CLI watch behavior.

</details>

title: fix(concurrency): record lease at acquisition so a cancelled acquire can't leak a slot
body:
Fixes the flaky `tests/concurrency/test_context.py::test_concurrency_context_releases_slots_sync` that failed on `main` ([workflow run](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/29749432456), commit d70bb7692f70a071654c4ffecc1d962c0f246e9d) with `AssertionError: assert 1 == 0` — the slot was never released after the timeout.

### Root cause

The sync `concurrency()` path acquires the lease via `run_coro_as_sync(...)`, which runs the acquisition coroutine on a **separate** event-loop thread and blocks the calling thread in `call.result()`. `timeout()` cancels by injecting a `CancelledError` into the calling thread, which (for the watcher-thread mechanism) only fires once the blocking wait returns.

Under load, acquisition takes longer than the 0.5s timeout, so the sequence is:

1. server grants the slot + lease (coroutine completes on the run-sync thread),
2. `call.result()` returns the value to the calling thread,
3. the pending `CancelledError` fires **while unwinding out of the acquire call**, before the lease id is ever assigned to a local.

The lease id is lost: it is never released and never recorded in `ConcurrencyContext.cleanup_lease_ids`, so the slot leaks until server-side lease expiry → `active_slots == 1`.

### Fix

Record the lease on the active `ConcurrencyContext` the **moment it is granted**, inside `aacquire_concurrency_slots_with_lease`:

```python
retval = ConcurrencyLimitWithLeaseResponse.model_validate(response.json())
...
elif ctx := ConcurrencyContext.get():
    ctx.cleanup_lease_ids.append(retval.lease_id)
return retval
```

In the sync path this runs to completion on the un-cancelled run-sync thread, so a cancellation firing in the calling thread can no longer lose the lease. The normal release path removes it again (`_discard_cleanup_lease` after a successful release); anything left over — release cancelled, or the acquire itself cancelled — is released idempotently by `ConcurrencyContext.__exit__` (the server's `decrement-with-lease` is a no-op when the lease is already gone).

Crucially, **the acquisition wait is not shielded**, so an enclosing timeout can still interrupt a wait on a saturated limit — addressing the Codex review note on the earlier revision of this PR. Mirrored across `_sync.py`/`_asyncio.py` per the lockstep invariant in `concurrency/AGENTS.md`. No sleeps/retries/manual timeouts added.

### Verification

- Reproduced deterministically under 8-core CPU saturation: the sync test failed ~20/20 before, passes **25/25** after (sync + async together).
- Confirmed a saturated-limit acquire under an outer `timeout()` still raises `TimeoutError` at the deadline (no hang) — the interruptibility Codex flagged is preserved.
- Full `tests/concurrency/` suite: **111 passed**.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `pyright --level error` / pre-commit `mypy` all clean.

### Checklist

- [x] If this pull request adds or changes functionality, it includes tests or explains why tests are not needed.
  - No ne

title: Prevent recurring UI dependency PR failures
body:
This PR addresses the recurring Dependabot UI-v2 update failures seen in #22378, #22425, #22464, and #22530. Changes: - In `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, switch `check-ui-v2` and `service-sync-ui-v2-openapi` from `npm i --no-upgrade` to `npm ci`. This makes validation consume the committed lockfile and stops npm from rewriting `package-lock.json` (and stripping `libc` metadata) during the pre-commit clean-tree check. - In `.github/dependabot.yml`: - Group ESLint/TypeScript toolchain updates (`@eslint*`, `eslint*`, `typescript`, `typescript-eslint`, `@tanstack/eslint-plugin-*`) so the compiler and lint plugins move together. - Add a separate `@biomejs/biome` group so formatting-related changes can be reviewed deliberately. - Restrict the catch-all `ui-v2-dependencies` group to minor/patch updates and exclude toolchain packages, so major non-toolchain updates are not hidden in routine batches. - Ignore `typescript` versions `>=6.1.0` until `typescript-eslint` supports that peer range.
Why use npm ci instead of npm i --no-upgrade? `npm i --no-upgrade` can still mutate `package-lock.json` based on the local npm version, even when the lockfile is valid. `npm ci` installs exactly from the committed lockfile and never rewrites it, which is the correct contract for validation hooks.
### Checklist - [x] This change is config-only and does not modify UI source, `package.json`, or `package-lock.json`. - [ ] I have run the relevant local checks (pre-commit config validation, Dependabot YAML parsing, `npm ci` / `npm run lint` / `npm run build` in `ui-v2`, and both affected pre-commit hooks). closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/22535

### Overview

`vacuum_events_with_retention_overrides` deletes `event_resources` rows via an `event_id` subquery:

```python
db.EventResource.event_id.in_(
    sa.select(db.Event.id).where(db.Event.event == event_type, db.Event.occurred < cutoff)
)
```

But `event_resources` had **no index on `event_id`**, so PostgreSQL fell back to a sequential scan of the whole (potentially tens-of-millions-of-rows) table on every `_batch_delete` batch. On busy servers this blows past `PREFECT_API_DATABASE_TIMEOUT` (default 10s), raising `TimeoutError` and pruning nothing — letting `events`/`event_resources` grow unbounded.

### Changes

1. **Add `ix_event_resources__event_id`** to the `EventResource` ORM model and the SQLite + PostgreSQL migrations (PostgreSQL uses `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, matching the existing `event_resources` occurred-index migration). This makes the retention-override delete an index lookup instead of a full scan.

2. **Add `server.database.migration_timeout`** (`PREFECT_SERVER_DATABASE_MIGRATION_TIMEOUT`), applied to the migration engine in `_migrations/env.py` instead of the application default `server.database.timeout`. Concurrent index builds on large tables can far exceed the 10s API statement timeout, which would fail startup migrations and can leave an invalid index behind. Defaults to `None` (no timeout); configurable to bound migration duration. This addresses the review concern and applies to all `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` migrations, not just this one.

### Note on the default heartbeat override

An earlier revision of this PR also dropped the default `event_retention_overrides = {"prefect.flow-run.heartbeat": 7d}`. That was reverted (Codex review): because `retention = min(type_retention, global_retention)`, the default caps heartbeat events at 7d even when `server.events.retention_period` is longer, so removing it would make long-retention deployments keep far more high-volume heartbeat data. With the index added the per-type path is cheap, so the default is kept unchanged.

- [x] References the related issue via "closes"
- [x] Includes tests (`tests/server/database/test_migrations.py` exercises the new migration-engine path; `tests/test_settings.py` covers the new setting; existing `test_db_vacuum.py` covers the retention-override delete)
- [x] No user-facing runtime behavior change — no docs update needed
- [ ] Does not remove docs files
- [x] N/A — no new public functions/classes

title: docs: clarify active gcl setup for concurrency context manager examples
body:
## Summary
Adds a note to the global concurrency limits how-to guide explaining that examples require an active limit created with \prefect gcl create\ before the context manager will block execution.

Fixes #11787
author: br413
diff:
--- docs/v3/how-to-guides/workflows/global-concurrency-limits.mdx (+14/-2)
@@ -143,17 +143,29 @@ if __name__ == "__main__":
 
 In both examples, the `concurrency` context manager occupies one slot on the `database` concurrency limit. If no slots are available, execution blocks until a slot becomes available.
 
+<Note>
+Before running these examples, create an **active** global concurrency limit that matches the name used in code:
+
+```bash
+prefect gcl create database --limit 1
+```
+
+If the limit does not exist, the default behavior is to log a warning and continue execution without blocking. Use `strict=True` when you need concurrency enforcement to fail fast when the specified limit does not exist instead of silently proceeding.
+
+`strict=True` does not enforce limits that exist but are inactive — ensure the limit is active (the default for `prefect gcl create`) before expecting tasks to block.
+</Note>
+
 ### Using strict mode
 
-Enable strict mode to ensure errors are raised if the limit doesn't exist or if lease renewal fails:
+Enable strict mode to ensure errors are raised if the limit doesn't exist (not if it is merely inactive) or if lease renewal fails:
 
 ```python
 from prefect import flow, task
 from prefect.concurrency.sync import concurrency
 
 @task
 def process_critical_data(x, y):
-    # strict=True ensures this task fails fast if concurrency can't be enforced
+    # strict=True fails fast when the limit is missing, not when it is inactive
     with concurrency("database", occupy=1, strict=True):
         return x + y

body:
## Description

`prefect.utilities.text` has two helpers, but the test suite only covered
`fuzzy_match_string`, leaving `truncated_to` untested.

`truncated_to(length, value)` shortens a long string to
`<start>...<N> additional characters...<end>`, but only when that placeholder
form is actually shorter than the original.

This extends `tests/utilities/test_text.py` with coverage for `truncated_to`:

- empty / `None` values returning `""`
- a value within `length` returned unchanged
- a long value being truncated with the "N additional characters" placeholder
- the original value being kept when the placeholder would be longer than the
  small amount trimmed

No source changes.

## Verification

Assertions verified against the real `prefect.utilities.text` module (4/4
pass); `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.
